processes.title: From Police Questioning to the Indictment Decision (Suspects)
processes.summary: The steps from the day you are asked to appear until the prosecutor decides whether to indict. Based on the amended Criminal Procedure Act in force from October 2, 2026

steps.title: The day you are contacted: check the case
steps.desc: Write down the case number, the department and investigator in charge, what you are accused of, and whether you are a suspect (피의자) or a witness (참고인). If the call came from an unfamiliar number, call the police station's main number back to confirm. You don't need to explain the case at length on the phone; it is enough to set a date.
steps.period: The request to appear (출석요구서) must state the gist of the alleged facts (Investigation Rules (수사준칙) Article 19(3))
steps.tip: The call itself can be written up in an investigation report, so it is fine to say you will explain the details when you come in.

steps.title: Consultation and organizing materials
steps.desc: The managing partner consults with you in person and sets the direction: dispute the allegations, or admit them and ask for leniency. We put the materials you already have, such as messages, transfer records and photos, in date order, and first secure CCTV and dashcam footage that could be erased.
steps.period: CCTV at shops and parking lots is usually overwritten within two weeks to a month
steps.tip: Exporting and saving the whole chat is better than screenshots cropped to the favorable parts.

steps.title: Adjusting the date to appear
steps.desc: If you don't have enough time to prepare, we ask the investigator to postpone. The investigator must discuss the date and time of questioning with the suspect and, if there is one, with the lawyer. Get the new date confirmed again by text.
steps.period: If a postponement is requested, the date must be adjusted unless there are special circumstances (Investigation Rules Article 19(1)3 and (2))
steps.tip: If you repeatedly fail to appear without contacting them, an arrest warrant may be requested (Criminal Procedure Act Article 200-2).

steps.title: Mock questioning
steps.desc: We pick out likely questions and you answer them as in real questioning. We find and fix in advance the places where you fill in dates and amounts with guesses or where your story changes. At this stage we also decide how much to say and which questions to decline to answer.
steps.tip: You also need to practice saying "I don't remember" when you don't remember.

steps.title: Questioning of the suspect (sitting in)
steps.desc: Before questioning, the investigator must inform you of your right to remain silent and your right to a lawyer's assistance. The lawyer can sit next to you, advise you and take notes, and objects on the spot to improper questioning methods. If you are tired, you can ask for a break.
steps.period: In principle, total time is within 12 hours and actual questioning within 8 hours, and there is in principle no questioning from 9 p.m. to 6 a.m. (Investigation Rules Articles 21 and 22)
steps.tip: Jisan Law objects on the spot to leading or improper questions and makes sure the objection is written in the statement record.

steps.title: Reading and signing the statement record
steps.desc: When questioning ends, you read the statement record (조서) and sign it. You can ask for corrections or state an objection where it does not match what you said, and the investigator must add this to the record (Criminal Procedure Act Article 244). Pay particular attention to times, amounts and sentences about what you knew, such as "I was aware that."
steps.tip: You can later apply to inspect and copy the record containing your own statement (Investigation Rules Article 69(1)).

steps.title: Defense written opinion and additional materials
steps.desc: We submit a written opinion (의견서) covering what you could not fully explain during questioning and materials found later. If you dispute the allegations, it addresses the facts and the law. If you admit them, it presents making up for the harm, remorse and efforts to prevent reoffending, with supporting materials.
steps.period: For complaint cases, the police must decide whether to refer the case within 3 months of accepting the complaint (Criminal Procedure Act Article 238, for complaints accepted on or after October 2, 2026)
steps.tip: A written opinion is reflected only if submitted before the police decide whether to refer the case.

steps.title: Decision to refer or not to refer
steps.desc: If the police find the suspicion supported, they refer (송치) the case to a prosecutor at the Public Prosecution Service (공소청). If not, they send the prosecutor a written statement of reasons and the records. Even after a decision not to refer (불송치), the case goes to the prosecutor if the complainant files an objection.
steps.period: A prosecutor who receives the records of a non-referred case returns them to the police within 90 days (Criminal Procedure Act Article 245-5)
steps.tip: Even if you receive a notice of non-referral, keep your materials rather than throwing them away.

steps.title: The prosecutor's indictment decision
steps.desc: The prosecutor does not investigate directly but reviews the records and decides on indictment, a request for a summary order (약식명령), or non-indictment (불기소) such as a suspended indictment (기소유예) or no charge due to lack of suspicion (혐의없음). If more is needed, the prosecutor requests supplementary investigation by the police, and when hearing the suspect's views, must allow the lawyer to take part (Criminal Procedure Act Article 245-13(5)).
steps.period: Police who receive a request for supplementary investigation must report the results within 1 month (Article 197-2(4)), and for complaint cases, whether to indict must be decided within 3 months of referral (Article 257)
steps.tip: Until the decision, written opinions and settlement agreements can be submitted to the Public Prosecution Service.

processes.title: From Arrest to the Detention Decision
processes.summary: Whether to request a detention warrant is decided within 48 hours of the arrest. Here are the steps and deadlines families need to know.

steps.title: Arrest and notice to the family
steps.desc: The procedure differs slightly depending on whether it is an arrest with a warrant, an emergency arrest (긴급체포) or an arrest in the act (현행범 체포). If there is no lawyer, the police must notify a family member or other person chosen by the suspect in writing of the case name, the date, time and place of arrest, the gist of the alleged crime and the reason for the arrest.
steps.period: Written notice within 24 hours of the arrest (Investigation Rules (수사준칙) Article 33)
steps.tip: Be sure to write down the time of the arrest. The 48 hours are counted from then.

steps.title: Appointing a lawyer and visits
steps.desc: An arrested person cannot use a phone, so the family has to act first. A spouse, lineal relatives and siblings can independently appoint a lawyer (Criminal Procedure Act Article 30(2)), and the lawyer can visit the arrested person (Article 34).
steps.tip: Family visits at the police holding cell are often restricted or short, so it is quicker to hear about the case through a lawyer's visit.

steps.title: Questioning while under arrest
steps.desc: Questioning starts right after the arrest and can continue several times. Statements made then become material for the warrant request and the pre-detention hearing (영장실질심사). The lawyer sits in on this questioning too.
steps.period: If unavoidable for deciding whether to request a detention warrant, late-night questioning is allowed within 48 hours of the arrest (Investigation Rules Article 21(2)1)
steps.tip: At the visit, we first set the direction of your statement so you don't answer with guesses while shaken.

steps.title: Applying for and requesting a detention warrant
steps.desc: If the police think detention is necessary, they apply to the prosecutor for a warrant, and the prosecutor requests it from the court. If the police do not apply or the prosecutor does not request it, the person is released right away.
steps.period: Immediate release if not requested within 48 hours of the arrest (Criminal Procedure Act Articles 200-2(5) and 200-4)
steps.tip: Documents on residence, work and family need to be gathered within this time.

steps.title: Pre-detention hearing
steps.desc: A judge calls the suspect in person and questions them on whether detention is necessary. The judge looks at whether there is substantial reason to suspect the crime, whether the person has a fixed residence, and whether there is a risk of destroying evidence or fleeing. The lawyer attends and states an opinion, and if there is no lawyer, the court appoints a court-appointed defense counsel (국선변호인).
steps.period: An arrested suspect is questioned by the day after the warrant is requested unless there are special circumstances (Criminal Procedure Act Article 201-2(1)). The result usually comes out that night or early the next morning
steps.tip: Jisan Law attends the pre-detention hearing and submits the documents the family gathered together with a written opinion.

steps.title: Investigation after detention
steps.desc: If the warrant is issued, the person stays in the police station holding cell and is moved to a detention center once the case is referred. Questioning continues during detention, and the lawyer sits in.
steps.period: 10 days with the police, 10 days with the prosecutor, extendable once by up to 10 days with a judge's permission (Criminal Procedure Act Articles 202, 203 and 205)
steps.tip: The detention period is short, so written opinions and settlement attempts must be timed to fit within it.

steps.title: Review of the legality of detention
steps.desc: If the detention is unjust or circumstances have changed, you can ask the court to review whether detention is appropriate (구속적부심사). The suspect, the lawyer, family members, people living with the suspect and the employer can all file the request. The court may also order release on condition of paying a bail deposit.
steps.period: Questioning within 48 hours of the request being filed (Criminal Procedure Act Article 214-2(4))
steps.tip: If a settlement has been reached or new materials have come up, it is time to consider this review.

steps.title: Bail after indictment
steps.desc: After indictment, you can request bail (보석). The court must grant bail unless, for example, the crime carries death, life imprisonment or a maximum of more than 10 years, the person is a repeat or habitual offender, or there is a risk of destroying evidence or fleeing (Criminal Procedure Act Article 95). Conditions such as a deposit, residence restrictions and a pledge to appear are attached (Article 98).
steps.period: Can be requested until the judgment becomes final
steps.tip: The court can allow the deposit to be replaced with a surety bond (보증서) submitted by someone other than the defendant (Article 100(3)).

processes.title: From Receiving the Indictment to Trial
processes.summary: The steps from the day the court sends you a copy of the indictment to the first-instance sentencing and appeal.

steps.title: Service of a copy of the indictment
steps.desc: When the prosecutor indicts, the court sends a copy of the indictment (공소장). Write down the date you received it, read the offense, the applicable provisions and the alleged facts line by line, and mark anything that differs from what happened.
steps.period: Served at least 5 days before the first trial date (Criminal Procedure Act Article 266)
steps.tip: If your address has changed, tell the court right away so you don't miss a summons.

steps.title: Submitting a written opinion
steps.desc: You submit to the court a written opinion stating whether you admit the alleged facts and your views on the pretrial preparation procedure. The opinion is also passed to the prosecutor, so don't rush to decide whether to admit anything before seeing the records.
steps.period: Within 7 days of receiving the copy of the indictment (Criminal Procedure Act Article 266-2)
steps.tip: The deadline is short, so it is a good idea to contact us as soon as you receive the indictment.

steps.title: Court-appointed defense counsel or appointing a lawyer
steps.desc: In cases such as when the defendant is detained, is a minor or is 70 or older, or the offense carries a minimum of 3 years' imprisonment, the court appoints a court-appointed defense counsel (국선변호인) on its own if there is no lawyer. In other cases, you can request one if you cannot hire a lawyer because of poverty or similar reasons.
steps.period: Criminal Procedure Act Article 33
steps.tip: If the lawyer who handled the investigation stage continues, the line of the statement records and written opinions stays consistent.

steps.title: Inspecting and copying the investigation records
steps.desc: We apply to the Public Prosecution Service to inspect and copy the documents the prosecutor will submit as evidence, the list of witnesses, documents that may favor the defendant and so on. If the defendant has a lawyer, the defendant personally can apply only to inspect.
steps.period: Criminal Procedure Act Article 266-3
steps.tip: Only after seeing the records can you decide whether to consent to each piece of evidence and whom to call as witnesses.

steps.title: First trial date
steps.desc: After you are informed of the right to remain silent and your identity is confirmed, the prosecutor reads the alleged facts, and the defendant and lawyer state whether they admit them. Then they give their views on the evidence. In principle, a criminal trial can be held only if the defendant appears (Criminal Procedure Act Article 276).
steps.period: The time until the first trial date is not set by law and depends on the court
steps.tip: In cases you admit, it is better to have the settlement agreement and sentencing materials ready before the first trial date.

steps.title: Examination of evidence and witnesses
steps.desc: In contested cases, the people who made statement records you did not consent to appear as witnesses, and cross-examination points out the weaknesses in their statements. In cases you admit, we submit materials on making up for the harm, remorse and efforts to prevent reoffending, and your family and work situation.
steps.tip: A settlement is taken into account right up to sentencing, so efforts to make up for the harm continue during the trial.

steps.title: Closing and final statement
steps.desc: When the examination of evidence is over, the prosecutor states the sentence it seeks (구형), the lawyer makes the closing argument, and the defendant makes a final statement. If you write your final statement briefly in advance and practice it, you won't be flustered.
steps.tip: The sentence the prosecutor seeks is only the prosecutor's opinion. The court decides the sentence.

steps.title: Sentencing and appeal
steps.desc: If you disagree with the judgment, you appeal. After appealing, once you are notified that the records have reached the appellate court, you must submit a statement of grounds for appeal.
steps.period: Appeal within 7 days of the sentencing date (Criminal Procedure Act Article 358); statement of grounds for appeal within 20 days of receiving the notice (Article 361-3)
steps.tip: If you miss the deadline for the statement of grounds, the appeal can be dismissed, so write the date down separately.

processes.title: From Filing a Complaint to Notice of the Outcome (Victims)
processes.summary: The steps for those who were harmed and want to file a criminal complaint. From October 2, 2026, complaints are filed with the police, and the law sets deadlines for police decisions and ways for complainants to challenge them.

steps.title: Organizing the harm and securing evidence
steps.desc: First gather materials that disappear over time, such as chat records, transaction history, medical certificates, photos and CCTV. Write down in date order when, where, who did what and how.
steps.period: CCTV is usually erased within two weeks to a month
steps.tip: A complaint that does not meet the legal elements can lead to a counter-complaint, so we first examine whether it is a crime.

steps.title: Writing and filing the complaint
steps.desc: Attach to the criminal complaint (고소장) the facts for which you want punishment and a list of evidence. File it at the civil affairs office of the police station with jurisdiction over the other party's address or the place where it happened, and get a receipt.
steps.period: A complaint is made to a judicial police officer in writing or orally (Criminal Procedure Act Article 237, in force from October 2, 2026)
steps.tip: Complaints are not filed with the Public Prosecution Service (공소청).

steps.title: Questioning of the complainant
steps.desc: The police ask you again about the complaint and hear your response to the other party's claims. A lawyer can take part and assist in the complainant's questioning too (Investigation Rules (수사준칙) Article 13(3)), and Jisan Law goes with you and helps with your statement.
steps.tip: Reread your complaint before questioning so your statement doesn't contradict it.

steps.title: Checking the progress of the investigation
steps.desc: Check the progress by asking the investigator in charge or through notification texts. If more than 6 months have passed since the investigation began with no real investigation and no good reason, you can raise an objection with the head of the investigating agency.
steps.period: Notice of action within 14 days of the objection; if there is no action or you are dissatisfied, a request for review by the higher agency within 14 days (Criminal Procedure Act Article 245-11)
steps.tip: This applies to cases where the investigation began on or after October 2, 2026

steps.title: The police decision on referral
steps.desc: If the police find the suspicion supported, they refer the case to the Public Prosecution Service; if not, they decide not to refer it (불송치). In that case, they notify you in writing of the decision and reasons, and send the decision along with guidance and a form for filing an objection.
steps.period: Decision within 3 months of accepting the complaint (Article 238); notice of non-referral within 7 days of sending the records (Article 245-6)
steps.tip: Look at whether you can rebut, line by line, the reasons for non-referral written in the notice.

steps.title: Objection to non-referral
steps.desc: If you file an objection, the police refer the case to the prosecutor. To prepare the objection, you can apply to inspect and copy the investigation records, and this is in principle granted if found necessary (Article 245-12).
steps.period: Within 3 months of receiving the notice (Article 245-7(3), for notices on or after October 2, 2026)
steps.tip: Check the deadline first so you don't miss the 3 months while waiting for the records.

steps.title: The prosecutor's decision and meeting
steps.desc: A prosecutor at the Public Prosecution Service reviews the records of the referred case and decides. The complainant can request a meeting with the prosecutor to give their views, and the prosecutor decides whether to accept after considering whether it is needed (Article 245-13(2)).
steps.period: For complaint cases, whether to indict is decided within 3 months of referral (Article 257)
steps.tip: Submit a written opinion saying you want strict punishment, along with evidence of the harm, before the decision.

steps.title: Appeal and application for a ruling against non-indictment
steps.desc: If the prosecutor decides not to indict (불기소), you can appeal (항고) to the head of the regional public prosecution office through the district public prosecution office the prosecutor belongs to. If the appeal is dismissed, you can file an application for a ruling (재정신청) with the high court.
steps.period: Appeal within 30 days of receiving notice of non-indictment (Public Prosecution Service Act (공소청법) Article 57); application for a ruling within 10 days of receiving notice that the appeal was dismissed (Criminal Procedure Act Article 260)
steps.tip: First get the statement of reasons for non-indictment and check what was considered lacking.

areaPages.areaName: Fraud, Embezzlement and Breach of Trust
areaPages.title: Fraud, Embezzlement and Breach of Trust
areaPages.lead: Whether a money dispute becomes a criminal case depends on whether you intended and were able to repay when you received the money, and whether you used money entrusted to you beyond your authority. That is judged from the contracts, transfer records and conversations at the time.

seo.title: Fraud and Embezzlement Charges in Korea: Responding and Penalties | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: Accused of fraud in Korea for failing to repay a loan, or of embezzlement for spending company money? Start by separating the issues. We cover the fraud penalty amended in December 2025, the KRW 500 million threshold under the Specific Economic Crimes Act, complaint requirements for property crimes between family members, and filing complaints for victims.

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: You couldn't repay money borrowed from an acquaintance on time, and they say they will accuse you of fraud
A business you raised investment for did poorly, and an investor claims it was fraud
After you left your job, your former company accused you of occupational embezzlement
Your business partner disputed the settlement of accounts and accused you of embezzlement and breach of trust
You received payment in a secondhand sale, sent the item late and were reported
A family member spent money you had entrusted to them as they pleased
You were the victim of investment fraud and want to file a criminal complaint

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 347 (Fraud)
items.text: A person who deceives another and receives property or obtains a financial benefit is punished by up to 20 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 50 million. The statutory penalty was raised by the amendment of December 23, 2025, and since punishment follows the law in force at the time of the act (Criminal Act Article 1), the previous statutory penalty applies to acts before that date.

items.name: Criminal Act Article 355 (Embezzlement and Breach of Trust)
items.text: A person who holds another's property and embezzles it or refuses to return it, or a person who handles another's affairs and, in breach of their duty, obtains a financial benefit and causes loss to that person, is punished by up to 5 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 15 million.

items.name: Criminal Act Article 356 (Occupational Embezzlement and Breach of Trust)
items.text: Embezzlement or breach of trust in violation of occupational duties is punished by up to 10 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 30 million.

items.name: Act on the Aggravated Punishment of Specific Economic Crimes (특정경제범죄 가중처벌 등에 관한 법률) Article 3
items.text: If the gain from fraud, embezzlement or breach of trust is KRW 500 million or more but less than KRW 5 billion, the punishment is imprisonment for a fixed term of 3 years or more; if it is KRW 5 billion or more, life imprisonment or imprisonment of 5 years or more. A fine up to the amount of the gain can also be imposed.

table.title: Statutory Penalties by Offense

table.note: Based on current laws on the National Law Information Center (국가법령정보센터, the government's official law database) as of October 2026. Habitual fraud is punished by up to one and a half times the penalty (Criminal Act Article 351).

sections.title: Whether it is fraud or a civil matter is judged at the time you received the money
body: Fraud requires an unbroken chain: deception, a mistaken belief caused by it, a handover of property based on that mistake, and a resulting gain. The mere fact that you did not repay is not enough; it must be shown that you had no intention or ability to repay when you received the money.

So investigators look at the day you received the money: your income and assets, other debts, what you said the money was for, and what you actually used it for. If you used the money for the stated purpose and have repaid even part of it, those records are your most important defense materials. On the other hand, if you described the purpose differently or overstated your financial situation, that becomes the issue.

sections.title: Embezzlement and breach of trust turn on your position and authority
body: Embezzlement (횡령) is using property entrusted to you as if it were your own or refusing to return it. Breach of trust (배임) is when someone handling another's affairs neglects their duty and causes a loss. In cases involving company funds, investment money or settling accounts between business partners, both crimes are often alleged together.

Disputes usually arise over whether you were in a position of holding the money, whether you had authority or approval to spend it, and whether you intended to put it back later. An explanation that it was a long-standing company practice is accepted only with materials such as approval documents, accounting records and past examples. Even when a CEO uses corporate money, the company and the individual are treated as separate, so embezzlement can be an issue.

sections.title: A gain of KRW 500 million is the threshold
body: If the gain is KRW 500 million or more, the Specific Economic Crimes Act applies instead of the Criminal Act, and there is no longer a path to a fine-only sentence. The amount of the gain changes depending on whether several transactions are grouped together or treated separately, so we calculate amounts and dates for each transaction.

If you are convicted under Article 3 of the Specific Economic Crimes Act, for a certain period you cannot work at financial institutions or at companies closely related to the crime, and cannot obtain related licenses or permits (Article 14 of the same Act). Because the career consequences are serious, we check from the start of the investigation whether the calculation of the gain can be disputed.

sections.title: Property crimes between family members require a complaint
body: With the amendment of Criminal Act Article 328 on December 31, 2025, fraud, embezzlement and breach of trust between relatives are no longer exempt from punishment; instead, they became crimes that can be prosecuted only on the victim's complaint (applied through Criminal Act Articles 354 and 361). In these cases, you can also file a complaint against your own or your spouse's lineal ascendants, such as parents.

For crimes that require a complaint, you cannot file once 6 months have passed from the day you learned who the offender was (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 230). This special rule does not apply to accomplices who are not relatives. If you are considering a complaint over a money issue within the family, first write down the date you found out.

Under the addendum, the amended provision applies to crimes committed on or after June 27, 2024. For acts between family members from June 27, 2024 until the amended law took effect (December 31, 2025), there was a special rule allowing a complaint within 6 months of the effective date, so you must check the dates for each case to see whether the complaint period is still open.

sections.title: How settlement and repayment affect the outcome
body: Fraud, embezzlement and breach of trust can be punished even if the victim does not want punishment. However, how much of the loss has been made up for weighs heavily in whether you are indicted and in the sentence. If it is hard to repay the full amount at once, we submit a repayment plan together with records of actual partial repayment.

If you are the victim, Jisan Law writes the criminal complaint and goes with you to your questioning as the complainant, and separately from the criminal complaint, we also consider a provisional attachment (가압류) or a claim for damages. Criminal proceedings exist to punish, not to collect money for you. Whether you take steps to preserve assets before the other side hides them affects recovery.

factors.title: Factors That Affect the Outcome and Sentence
plus: Multiple victims or the same method used repeatedly
A large loss that has not been made up for
Lying about the purpose or your financial situation from the start
Siphoning off money over a long period using a work position
A prior record for a similar offense
minus: Records showing the money was used for the stated purpose
A history of steady repayment, even if partial
Making up for the harm and a settlement
Materials showing the spending followed company approval or practice
A minor role and little gain
No criminal record

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Criminal Law Center Responds

items.title: Consultation with the managing partner
items.desc: We check the allegations in the complaint or the text asking you to appear, and separate what to dispute from what to admit.

items.title: Organizing materials in time order
items.desc: We line up contracts, transfer records and chat records by date to show the circumstances at the time you received the money.

items.title: Mock questioning and sitting in
items.desc: We practice in advance with likely questions about the flow of money, go into the interview room with you, and object on the spot to improper questions.

items.title: Defense written opinion
items.desc: We submit a written opinion, with supporting materials, showing there was no intent to defraud (편취 고의) or intent of unlawful appropriation (불법영득의사), and pointing out problems in calculating the gain.

items.title: Considering restitution
items.desc: If there are parts you admit, we set a repayment plan and the direction for settlement, and Jisan Law handles settlement contact with the victim's side on your behalf. In cases involving investment contracts or company funds, Bonwoo Koo also works on the case.

checklist.title: Helpful Materials to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: Contracts, IOUs, investment agreements
Bank transaction records of money given and received
Chat records from the time, such as KakaoTalk and text messages
Records of your income and assets around the time you received the money
Records of repayments made so far
For company cases, approval documents and accounting records
A copy of the complaint or the text asking you to appear

faqs.q: Can it still be fraud if I repaid part of the money?
faqs.a: Yes. Fraud is judged as of the time you received the money, so later partial repayment does not by itself mean there was no fraud. However, a record of steady repayment suggests you did not intend to deceive from the start, and it also counts as making up for the harm.

faqs.q: An investor accused me of fraud because they lost their investment.
faqs.a: A business failing and causing a loss is not fraud in itself. The issues are whether you misrepresented the business or its revenue structure when raising the investment, and whether you used the money where you promised. We start by comparing the business plan with records of how the investment was spent.

faqs.q: I run a one-person company. Is it embezzlement if I used company money personally?
faqs.a: It can be. The company and you as its CEO are legally different persons, so using company funds for personal purposes can amount to embezzlement of company property. The judgment depends on whether it was booked as a provisional payment, whether it was later settled, and whether the spending was for the company, so the accounting records need to be reviewed too.

faqs.q: I'm a fraud victim. If I file a complaint, can I get my money back?
faqs.a: Filing a complaint alone does not get your money back. Sometimes the offender repays during the investigation to reach a settlement, but to recover money you should also consider a provisional attachment and a claim for damages. It is important to act while the other side still has assets.

faqs.q: It happened a long time ago. Can I still file a complaint?
faqs.a: Yes, if the statute of limitations has not run out. It is set by the maximum statutory penalty: 10 years for fraud and occupational embezzlement or breach of trust, and 7 years for simple embezzlement or breach of trust (Criminal Procedure Act Article 249). If the gain is large enough for the Specific Economic Crimes Act to apply, the period may differ, so organize the dates and amounts and check.

faqs.q: A family member took out a loan in my name and took the money. Can't they be punished because we're family?
faqs.a: With the amendment to the Criminal Act on December 31, 2025, fraud, embezzlement and breach of trust between family members are no longer exempt from punishment and can be punished if the victim files a complaint. However, because these crimes require a complaint, you must file within 6 months of learning who the offender is, and if it happened before the amended law took effect on December 31, 2025, whether it applies and the complaint period must be checked separately. You can also file a complaint against your parents or your spouse's parents.

areaPages.title: Involvement in Voice Phishing (Cash Collectors, Couriers and Withdrawers)
areaPages.summary: If you collected and passed on cash for a high-paying part-time job, the circumstances at the time decide the outcome more than saying you didn't know.
areaPages.cardLaw: Criminal Act Article 347; Telecommunications Fraud Refund Act Article 15-2
areaPages.lead: Even if all you did was receive and pass on cash or withdraw and send it, you will be investigated as an accomplice in voice phishing fraud. The issue is less whether you knew from the start than whether you kept going even though there were signs that should have made you suspicious.

seo.title: Voice Phishing Cash Collector or Courier Charges in Korea: Penalties and Response | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: Questioned in Korea as a voice phishing accomplice after collecting or delivering cash for a high-paying part-time job? Conditional intent, meaning you went ahead while suspecting it might be a crime, is the issue. We cover the applicable laws and penalties, materials to keep and gather before questioning, and the sentence reduction provision introduced in September 2026.

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: You took a field or collection job you saw on a job site, received and passed on cash, and the police contacted you
You followed instructions to split the cash you received and deposit it into several accounts at an ATM
You were told to introduce yourself as a financial institution employee and collect money
You withdrew money that came into your account, or converted it to crypto and sent it on
A family member was arrested on the spot, and you were told a detention warrant may be requested

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 347 (Fraud)
items.text: A person who deceives another and obtains property or a financial benefit is punished by up to 20 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 50 million (amended December 23, 2025). A person who received and passed on the money can also be punished as a co-principal (공동정범, Article 30) or an accessory (방조범, Article 32), and an accessory's sentence is lighter than the principal's.

items.name: Special Act on the Prevention of Telecommunications Financial Fraud and Refund of Damaged Assets (전기통신금융사기 피해 방지 및 피해자산 환급에 관한 특별법) Article 15-2
items.text: Using telecommunications to deceive or frighten people into sending or transferring money, handing it over directly or withdrawing it is punished by imprisonment for a fixed term of 1 year or more or a fine of 3 to 5 times the criminal proceeds, and both can be imposed together. Attempts are also punished.

items.name: Article 17-2 of the same Act (Reduction or Exemption of Punishment)
items.text: If you provide statements or materials during the investigation or trial that reveal others' crimes, or give information leading to the capture of offenders or on criminal proceeds, the sentence can be reduced or waived. This was introduced on September 8, 2026, and also applies to cases under investigation or on trial at that time.

sections.title: Saying you didn't know is not enough
body: Even if you did not know for certain it was voice phishing, courts find intent if you thought it might be illegal and kept doing the work anyway. So rather than repeating that you didn't know, you need to show with materials why you believed it was a legitimate job at the time.

The circumstances investigators look at are generally similar. They ask whether you were hired only through a messenger app without an interview or employment contract, whether the pay was far too high for the work, whether you were told to pose as someone else or delete chat rooms, and whether you split the cash into ATM deposits.

sections.title: Even one time does not end lightly
body: Cash collectors meet victims in person, so they are identified first, and if they went out several times or the amounts were large, a detention warrant may be requested after arrest. If the scope of the conspiracy is read broadly, the charges may include losses you never received yourself, so you must dispute precisely what you did and from when to when.

Making up for the harm weighs heavily in sentencing. If there are several victims, we consider a settlement or a criminal deposit (형사공탁) for each victim, and if you have statements or materials that help capture members of the ring or trace criminal proceeds, we also look at the sentence reduction provision.

sections.title: Leave your phone and chat records as they are
body: If you get scared and delete Telegram chats or reset your phone, you will be suspected of trying to destroy evidence, which can become grounds for detention. Job ad screenshots, company introduction materials, instruction messages and records of pay deposits, if kept, can actually show that you were used.
If your phone was seized, you can request to take part in the forensic examination and check what data is extracted.

factors.title: Factors That Affect the Outcome and Sentence
plus: Collected cash many times, in large amounts
Posed as a financial institution employee or investigator
Deleted chat records or reset the phone
Shared in the profits, such as commission in proportion to amounts collected
Kept going despite reasons to be suspicious
minus: Records of being hired through a legitimate job platform and receiving company materials
Only once or over a short period
Pay at the level of a daily wage or travel expenses
Quit or reported it on your own after sensing something was wrong
Making up for the harm or a criminal deposit
Cooperating with the investigation and providing information about the ring

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Criminal Law Center Responds

items.title: Consultation with the managing partner
items.desc: We hear everything in date order, from how you were recruited to the last collection, and separate what to dispute from what to admit.

items.title: Preserving and organizing materials
items.desc: We secure the job ads, messenger chats and deposit and withdrawal records in their original form, and make a table of the period and number of times you worked.

items.title: Mock questioning and sitting in
items.desc: We practice in advance with questions about intent, go into the interview room with you, and object on the spot to leading questions.

items.title: Responding to arrest and detention
items.desc: If you were arrested, we visit to check the situation, attend the pre-detention hearing (영장실질심사) and explain that there is no risk of flight or destroying evidence.

items.title: Written opinion and restitution
items.desc: We submit a written opinion disputing the scope of involvement and intent, and for the parts you admit, consider a settlement or criminal deposit for each victim.

checklist.title: Helpful Materials to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: Screenshots of the job ad and records of how you applied
The full messenger chats in which you received work instructions
Notes of the dates, places and amounts of cash you received
Records of the account where you received pay
Documents you received, such as a company profile or letter of authorization
The text asking you to appear or a list of seized items

faqs.q: I only received money and passed it on. Can I be an accomplice to fraud?
faqs.a: Yes. Collecting and delivering is the stage where the victims' money is actually obtained, so it is often treated as co-principal liability, and if your role is found to be minor, you may be judged an accessory. Either way, to avoid punishment you need to show with materials that you had no intent.

faqs.q: If I return the money to the victims, will the punishment be reduced?
faqs.a: Making up for the harm weighs heavily in the decision and sentence. However, this is not a crime where the case ends just because the victim does not want punishment. If you cannot reach the victim, you can consider a criminal deposit.

faqs.q: I've been asked to appear, but they keep contacting me.
faqs.a: Stop following their instructions, and keep the messages instead of deleting them. The contact itself can be material showing that the ring exists and that you were used. It is better to decide with your lawyer before questioning which materials to submit and when.

areaPages.areaName: Handing Over or Lending Bank Accounts and Debit Cards
areaPages.title: Handing Over or Lending Bank Accounts and Debit Cards (Electronic Financial Transactions Act Violations)
areaPages.summary: Even if you sent your card to get a loan, you can be punished for lending an access medium if the loan opportunity is treated as payment.
areaPages.cardLaw: Electronic Financial Transactions Act Articles 6(3) and 49(4)
areaPages.lead: If you hand over the means of operating an account, such as a debit card, password, certificate or OTP, you can be punished whether or not the account was used in a crime. What you handed over, why, and what you were promised in return decide the case.

seo.title: Lending a Bank Account or Debit Card in Korea: Electronic Financial Transactions Act Violations | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: Sent your debit card and password to someone who promised a loan, and now your account is frozen and the Korean police want you to appear? Payment and awareness of the crime are the issues. We cover the statutory penalty, Supreme Court rulings, account freezes and restrictions on financial transactions.
keywords: Electronic Financial Transactions Act violation Korea

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: You sent your debit card and password by courier after being told you would get a loan
Someone asked to borrow your account to build up a transaction record, and you agreed
You were offered a certain amount per day to lend your card
Your account was suddenly frozen, and you were told to appear for violating the Electronic Financial Transactions Act
You handed over your certificate and OTP at an acquaintance's request

items.name: Electronic Financial Transactions Act (전자금융거래법) Article 6(3)
items.text: Prohibits transferring or receiving access media (접근매체), lending, keeping or delivering them while giving, receiving, demanding or promising payment, lending them knowing they will be used in a crime, and arranging or advertising such acts.

items.name: Electronic Financial Transactions Act Article 49(4)
items.text: A person who, in violation of Article 6(3), transfers, receives, lends, keeps, delivers or circulates access media, or provides account information knowing it will be used in a crime, is punished by up to 5 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 30 million, and imprisonment and a fine can be imposed together (paragraph 8 of the same Article).

items.name: Telecommunications Fraud Refund Act (통신사기피해환급법) Article 13-2
items.text: If the holder of a frozen account receives a fine for transferring or lending access media in connection with voice phishing, the Financial Supervisory Service designates them as a person subject to electronic financial transaction restrictions for 3 years; for imprisonment (including a suspended sentence), for 5 years.

sections.title: What matters is the card and the password
body: People often say they lent their bank account, but what the law punishes is the access medium. This covers the means and information used to give transaction instructions or verify your identity, such as debit or cash cards, certificates, user IDs and passwords. Even without handing over anything physical, giving out the information can count if it let the other person move money through your account.

Transferring means handing the account over entirely; lending means letting someone use it for a period without your control. Transferring is punished even without payment, but lending is punished only if payment was promised or you knew it would be used in a crime, so what was said and the messages exchanged when you handed it over matter.

sections.title: A loan opportunity can also count as payment
body: Many people say they never received a single won and were only trying to get a loan. In a case where a person who would normally struggle to get a loan sent a debit card to build a transaction record and get a chance at a loan, the Supreme Court held that the opportunity could be payment for the lending (Supreme Court Decision 2017도16946, June 27, 2019).

That does not mean everyone is found guilty. The judgment differs depending on whether the other person convincingly posed as a financial company so that you could believe it was a normal procedure, whether you were to get the card back, and whether you reported it right after sensing something was wrong.

sections.title: If the account was used for voice phishing
body: If victims' money comes into the account you handed over, the account is frozen (지급정지), and you may also be investigated for aiding fraud or as an accomplice. If you withdrew or sent money yourself, the allegations become much more serious.

There is an objection procedure for account freezes, but it has a deadline (Telecommunications Fraud Refund Act Article 7), and it is not accepted if the account holder is found to have known the account would be used for fraud or failed to know through gross negligence. Check right away when you receive the notice.

factors.title: Factors That Affect the Outcome and Sentence
plus: Received or agreed to receive money in return
Handed over several accounts or cards
Was also involved in withdrawals or transfers afterward
Large losses and many victims
A previous record for the same offense
minus: Materials showing you could believe it was a loan process (impersonation documents, consultation records)
Signs you were to get the card back
Reported the card lost or went to the police as soon as you realized something was wrong
No actual gain
Making up for the harm

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Criminal Law Center Responds

items.title: Checking how it was handed over
items.desc: We check with chat records and courier waybills who asked for what and under what pretext.

items.title: Sorting out the scope of the allegations
items.desc: Using the request to appear, we determine whether only the Electronic Financial Transactions Act violation is at issue or aiding fraud as well.

items.title: Mock questioning and sitting in
items.desc: We practice in advance for questions about why you sent it and what you were to receive, and go into the questioning with you.

items.title: Submitting a written opinion
items.desc: We submit a written opinion, with supporting materials, showing there was no payment arrangement or awareness of the crime, and the circumstances to consider in the decision.

checklist.title: Helpful Materials to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: The courier waybill or quick-delivery record for sending the card
Loan consultation texts, KakaoTalk messages and call records
Materials the other person sent, such as a business registration certificate or business card
The account freeze notification text
Your account's transaction history
The text asking you to appear

faqs.q: I only sent the card. I never received any money.
faqs.a: Payment includes not only money actually received but also a promise to receive it, and a chance to get a loan can also count. On the other hand, if there was no promise of payment and you did not know it would be used in a crime, it is hard to punish it as lending. What the other person said they would do for you at the time matters most.

faqs.q: Is lending my card to a family member a problem too?
faqs.a: If you let them use it briefly without any payment and did not know it would be used in a crime, the lending itself is not punished. However, transferring it outright is prohibited even without payment, and if the card is used in a crime, you will be investigated.

faqs.q: If I'm fined, will my banking be blocked?
faqs.a: In cases connected to voice phishing, you can be designated as a person subject to electronic financial transaction restrictions for 3 years from sentencing for a fine, or 5 years for imprisonment. If non-face-to-face transactions such as internet banking are blocked, daily life becomes very inconvenient, so we take this into account from the decision stage.

areaPages.areaName: Secondhand Sale, Investment and Romance Fraud
areaPages.title: Secondhand Sale Fraud, Investment "Leading Room" Fraud and Romance Scams
areaPages.summary: Online fraud victims are spread across the country, so calls come from several police stations. The first step is bringing the cases together.
areaPages.lead: These are cases where you took payment in a secondhand sale but couldn't send the item, or where money changed hands with someone you met in an investment chat room (리딩방) or on social media and it turned into a fraud case. Even under the same crime of fraud, the materials investigators look at and the way cases grow differ by type.

seo.title: Secondhand Sale, Investment Chat Room and Romance Scam Fraud in Korea | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: Accused by several buyers in Korea after taking payment and failing to ship, or questioned for involvement in an investment chat room or romance scam? The issues differ. We cover combining cases, habitual fraud, the scope of accomplice liability and how victims can recover money.

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: You took payment on a secondhand trading app, couldn't send the items, and several people filed complaints
You agreed to sell concert tickets, something came up, and your refund was delayed
You worked as a consultant under an investment chat room operator and are being questioned as an accomplice to fraud
You borrowed money from someone you met on social media and were reported for a romance scam
The person who encouraged you to invest has cut off contact, and you want to file a complaint

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 347 (Fraud)
items.text: A person who deceives another and obtains property or a financial benefit is punished by up to 20 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 50 million. For acts before the amendment of December 23, 2025, the statutory penalty in force at the time of the act applies.

items.name: Criminal Act Article 351 (Habitual Offenders)
items.text: Habitual fraud is punished by the penalty for that crime increased by up to one half.

items.name: Telecommunications Fraud Refund Act (통신사기피해환급법) Article 2, item 2
items.text: Acts disguised as selling goods or providing services are excluded from telecommunications financial fraud under this Act. So for losses from secondhand sale fraud, it is hard to use the account freeze and refund procedures under this Act that apply to voice phishing.

sections.title: Secondhand sale fraud looks at when the listing was posted
body: The key questions are whether you actually had the item, whether you sold the same item to several people, and what you did after receiving the money to ship it or refund the buyer. If you couldn't send it because a parcel was lost or something suddenly came up, there is room to treat it as a civil matter of failing to keep the contract.

On the other hand, if you kept posting new listings to raise money to refund earlier buyers, robbing Peter to pay Paul, it is easy to conclude you never intended to ship, and the penalty may be increased for habitual fraud.

sections.title: Bringing cases from several police stations into one place
body: Buyers file complaints where they each live, so at first you get separate calls from several police stations. If you keep failing to appear, an arrest warrant may be requested, so the first step is to ask the investigators in charge to combine the cases in one place.
Make your own list of victims using the trading app chats and deposit records. You need to know the full scale, including buyers who haven't filed complaints yet, to make a repayment plan.

sections.title: If you were involved in an investment chat room or romance scam
body: Chat room consultants, people who lent their accounts and people who converted received money into crypto and sent it on are also investigated as accomplices. The issues are whether you thought it was legitimate investment consulting, whether you were given scripts promising assured returns, and when you quit. When investigated as an organization, joining a criminal group may also be considered, so narrowing down the period you worked and the role you played directly affects the sentence.

sections.title: If you are a victim, look at criminal and civil steps together
body: Filing a complaint alone does not bring your money back. If you know the other person's account, also consider a provisional attachment (가압류). Fraud disguised as selling goods, such as secondhand sale fraud, is not covered by the voice phishing account freeze system, so it has to be approached through the investigation and civil proceedings.

factors.title: Factors That Affect the Outcome and Sentence
plus: Kept posting listings to pay off earlier buyers
Many victims
Used fake-name accounts or other people's bank accounts
Did not respond to requests to appear
A large role within the organization
minus: Records showing you actually had the item when you listed it
Records of efforts to ship or refund
Repayment and settlement with all victims
A short period of involvement and little gain
No criminal record

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Criminal Law Center Responds

items.title: Consultation with the managing partner
items.desc: We look at the listings, chats and deposit records and separate what may be seen as fraud from what is a trading dispute.

items.title: Victim list and combining cases
items.desc: We make a table of amounts and refund status for each transaction, and consider how to bring cases from several police stations into one place.

items.title: Mock questioning and sitting in
items.desc: We prepare for questions about your circumstances when you sold and why you couldn't ship, and go into the questioning with you.

items.title: Repayment plan and written opinion
items.desc: We set a repayment plan you can actually keep and submit a written opinion summarizing your progress.

checklist.title: Helpful Materials to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: The original listings and photos of the items
The full chat rooms with buyers
Deposit records, waybills and refund records
Texts from each police station asking you to appear
For involvement cases, records of how you were recruited and your work instructions

faqs.q: Each case is only tens of thousands of won. Can I still be detained?
faqs.a: Even if each amount is small, arrest or detention may be considered if there are many victims or you are seen as a flight risk for not appearing. It is important to bring the cases together, appear faithfully and show that you are actually repaying.

faqs.q: I only sent the item late. Is that fraud?
faqs.a: If you eventually shipped it or gave a refund, that suggests you did not intend to deceive from the start. Show with your chat records whether you had the item when you sold it and whether you explained the delay to the buyer.

faqs.q: I only received a salary as a consultant in an investment chat room.
faqs.a: Even if you only received a salary, if your consulting was used to deceive investors, you will be investigated as an accomplice. You can dispute the scope of your involvement by organizing whether you had materials that made the company seem legitimate, what the scripts said, and when you quit after becoming suspicious.

areaPages.title: Occupational Embezzlement (Company Money, Client Payments, Company Goods)
areaPages.summary: Don't accept the embezzlement amount your company wrote down as it is. Each transaction needs to be sorted into business spending or personal use.
areaPages.lead: These are cases where an employee is accused of using company money, payments received from clients or company goods for personal purposes. Complaints often come after a conflict around the time of leaving the company, when the company goes back over its accounting records.

seo.title: Occupational Embezzlement Accusations in Korea: Company Money and Client Payments | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: Did your former employer in Korea accuse you of occupational embezzlement after you left, or question collected payments or corporate card use? Start by breaking the amount down by transaction. We cover the statutory penalty, the statute of limitations, how to respond to demands for a signed admission, and the effect of repayment and settlement.

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: A few months after you left, your former company accused you of occupational embezzlement
The company is taking issue with you depositing part of the payments collected from clients late
You used a corporate card for both business and personal purposes
The company wants you to sign a statement admitting embezzlement along with your resignation letter
You were reported for taking inventory and materials that were going to be thrown away
You took part of the sales proceeds in place of unpaid wages

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 355(1) (Embezzlement)
items.text: A person who holds another's property and embezzles it or refuses to return it is punished by up to 5 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 15 million.

items.name: Criminal Act Article 356 (Occupational Embezzlement and Breach of Trust)
items.text: Embezzling property held in the course of one's work is punished by up to 10 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 30 million. The statute of limitations is 10 years (Criminal Procedure Act Article 249(1)3).

items.name: Act on the Aggravated Punishment of Specific Economic Crimes (특정경제범죄 가중처벌 등에 관한 법률) Article 3
items.text: If the gain from embezzlement is KRW 500 million or more but less than KRW 5 billion, the punishment is imprisonment for a fixed term of 3 years or more; if it is KRW 5 billion or more, life imprisonment or imprisonment of 5 years or more.

sections.title: Breaking the company's figure down by transaction
body: The amount in the complaint often mixes money actually spent on business, provisional payments the company knew about and allowed, and amounts settled later. The first task is to split bank transfers, corporate card charges and cash collections into individual transactions and match each to where it was spent and whether it was approved.
A smaller embezzlement amount changes the decision and sentence, and whether it exceeds KRW 500 million changes the applicable law itself.

sections.title: Were you the custodian, and did you mean to treat it as your own?
body: Occupational embezzlement (업무상횡령) requires that a person who held and managed money or goods for the company disposed of them as if they were their own. If you had no transfer authority or only carried out your superior's instructions, you can dispute whether you were a custodian or had intent.

Saying you meant to put it back later is not enough on its own, but if there are materials suggesting you were allowed to use it, such as the company's settlement practice or an agreement to deduct it from your pay, there is room to dispute. Taking company money because of unpaid wages can also raise embezzlement issues, so it is safer to claim wages separately.

sections.title: Don't rush into signing admissions or settlement agreements
body: Sometimes a company demands a signed statement or confirmation admitting embezzlement before filing a complaint. If you sign before the amount is sorted out, that document is used like a confession in the investigation, so sign only after checking the amount and wording.

If there are parts you admit, repayment weighs heavily in the decision. However, embezzlement is a crime where the investigation continues even after a settlement, so the settlement agreement should set out both the amount to be repaid and a statement that the company does not want punishment.

factors.title: Factors That Affect the Outcome and Sentence
plus: Siphoned off money many times over a long period
Altered the books or created false supporting documents
Large losses with no recovery
A previous record for the same offense
minus: Materials showing business use or approval
Company practice and settlement records
Returned or repaid the money voluntarily
Little personal gain
No criminal record

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Criminal Law Center Responds

items.title: Consultation with the managing partner
items.desc: We check the period and amount at issue in the complaint or the materials the company sent.

items.title: Transaction-by-transaction breakdown
items.desc: We make a table sorting transfers, card charges and collections into business use, approved spending and personal use.

items.title: Mock questioning and sitting in
items.desc: We practice with likely questions about the flow of funds and go into the interview room with you.

items.title: Written opinion and repayment approach
items.desc: For disputed amounts, we submit a written opinion with supporting evidence; for amounts you admit, we set the approach to repayment and settlement.

checklist.title: Helpful Materials to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: Employment contract, job description and delegation of authority rules
Transfer records and corporate card statements for the period in question
Approval documents and messages with instructions from superiors
Records of settlements or returns
Signed statements and certified letters exchanged with the company
Records of unpaid wages and severance pay

faqs.q: I left the company a long time ago. Can they still file a complaint now?
faqs.a: Regardless of when you left, a complaint can be filed within the statute of limitations, which is 10 years for occupational embezzlement. The older the matter, the more often the records from that time remain only with the company, so we also consider asking investigators to check the accounting records.

faqs.q: If I repay everything, will the complaint be withdrawn?
faqs.a: Even if the company withdraws the complaint, occupational embezzlement is a crime where the investigation and trial can continue. However, full repayment and a settlement weigh heavily when deciding the outcome, such as a suspended indictment (기소유예) or a fine.

faqs.q: I handled it because the CEO told me to, but I'm the only one accused.
faqs.a: If you only carried out instructions and gained nothing personally, you can dispute intent or the intent of unlawful appropriation (불법영득의사). Instruction messages, approval records and materials showing where the money actually went are important.

areaPages.areaName: Theft and Embezzlement of Lost Property
areaPages.title: Theft, Nighttime Burglary and Embezzlement of Lost Property
areaPages.summary: The charge and sentence vary greatly depending on whether the item was in someone's possession or lost, and whether you entered a home at night.
areaPages.lead: This covers taking items from a supermarket or unstaffed store, entering someone's home or building at night and taking things, and not returning a wallet you found. Which crime applies depends on what you took, where and how.

seo.title: Theft, Nighttime Burglary and Keeping Lost Property in Korea | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: Contacted by the Korean police over shoplifting at an unstaffed store or supermarket, entering a home at night, or a wallet you found or money sent to you by mistake? First pin down the exact charge. We cover the differences in statutory penalties, complaint requirements for theft between family members and what to prepare before the decision.

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: You took items from an unstaffed store without paying and the police contacted you
You left a supermarket without paying for some items and were identified on CCTV
You are accused of entering a house with an open door at night and taking things
You did not immediately return a phone or wallet you found on the street or subway
You spent money sent to you by mistake and were asked to return it
A family member says they will file a complaint because you took their belongings

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 329 (Theft)
items.text: Stealing another's property is punished by up to 6 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 10 million. Attempts are also punished (Article 342).

items.name: Criminal Act Article 330 (Nighttime Burglary) and Article 331 (Special Theft)
items.text: Breaking into a person's residence or a managed building at night and stealing is punished by up to 10 years' imprisonment, with no fine option. Breaking a door or wall at night to enter and steal, or stealing while carrying a weapon or jointly with two or more people, is punished by 1 to 10 years' imprisonment.

items.name: Criminal Act Article 360 (Embezzlement of Lost Property)
items.text: Keeping property that has left another's possession, such as a lost item, is punished by up to 1 year's imprisonment, a fine of up to KRW 3 million or a petty fine.

sections.title: Nighttime burglary has no fine option
body: For simple theft, a fine can be chosen, but stealing after entering an inhabited home or a managed building at night carries only imprisonment, so it cannot end with a fine through a summary order (약식명령). That is why disputes start with whether you entered after sunset and whether the place was a residence or a managed building.

If the place you entered at night was open to anyone, such as a shop doing business, there may be room to dispute whether it counts as breaking in at all. We check materials showing the time you entered and whether the business was open.

sections.title: Found items and money that arrived by mistake
body: Keeping an item the owner lost is not theft but embezzlement of lost property (점유이탈물횡령). However, an item the owner left briefly, such as on a shop table, is considered still in the possession of the owner or the shop, so taking it can be theft.

Spending money sent to you by mistake instead of returning it is treated as embezzlement, not embezzlement of lost property (Supreme Court Decision 2010도891, December 9, 2010). If you also paid with a card you found, fraudulent use of a credit card is a separate issue.

sections.title: Even for first offenses and small amounts, get the record straight first
body: Unstaffed store and supermarket cases are mostly identified through CCTV and payment records, so denying facts that are true actually works against you. Check exactly which items, how many times and what amounts, and for what you admit, making up for the harm quickly helps the outcome.

With the amendment on December 31, 2025, theft between family members became a crime that can be prosecuted only on the victim's complaint (Criminal Act Articles 344 and 328). A complaint cannot be filed once 6 months have passed from the day the victim learned who the offender was.

factors.title: Factors That Affect the Outcome and Sentence
plus: Broke into a residence at night
Repeated it many times (habitual)
Carried a weapon or acted with others
Sold off the stolen items
A previous record for the same offense
minus: A first offense involving a small amount
Returned the items or paid compensation
Impulsive, spur-of-the-moment circumstances
Started treatment for impulse control problems
The victim does not want punishment

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Criminal Law Center Responds

items.title: Consultation with the managing partner
items.desc: We check what you are accused of taking, when and where, and determine which crime applies.

items.title: Organizing the facts
items.desc: We match payment records and visit records to separate what to admit from what to dispute.

items.title: Mock questioning and sitting in
items.desc: We practice in advance for questions about how it happened and your motive, and go into the questioning with you.

items.title: Restitution and written opinion
items.desc: We gather records of compensation and materials showing remorse and treatment, and submit a written opinion before the decision.

checklist.title: Helpful Materials to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: The text asking you to appear
A list of the items taken and their value
Payment records or receipts from the same day
Receipts for returning items or paying compensation
If you found the item, notes on where you found it and what you did afterward
Treatment or counseling records, if any

faqs.q: I paid for everything. Will I still be punished?
faqs.a: Theft is a crime where the investigation continues even if you pay compensation or the victim does not want punishment. However, for a first offense involving a small amount where the harm has been made up for, the chances of a light outcome such as a suspended indictment (기소유예) increase.

faqs.q: I only picked up a wallet and kept it for a few days.
faqs.a: If you meant to return it to the owner, it is not embezzlement of lost property. Materials showing that intention matter, so organize any records of trying to contact the owner or signs that you meant to hand it in to the police or a lost and found center.

faqs.q: The shop owner is demanding a large sum to settle.
faqs.a: Settling is not mandatory, and the amount is set by looking at the actual loss and circumstances. If the demand is so excessive that settling is difficult, you can also make a criminal deposit (형사공탁) of an amount equal to the loss.

areaPages.title: Property Damage and Special Property Damage
areaPages.summary: Not every broken item is property damage. The first question is whether you intentionally destroyed its usefulness.
areaPages.lead: Breaking, hiding or making someone else's property unusable is property damage (재물손괴). Breaking something by accident is not a criminal matter; it remains a matter of compensation for damages.

seo.title: Property Damage Accusations in Korea: Response and Penalties | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: Accused of property damage in Korea for throwing a phone during an argument or scratching a car? Intent and impairing the item's usefulness are the issues. We cover the statutory penalty, special and joint property damage, the difference when assault is also alleged, and disputes over repair costs.

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: You threw the other person's phone during an argument and cracked the screen
You were accused of scratching a car during a parking dispute
You were reported for throwing away an ex-partner's belongings
You are accused of breaking a shop's fixtures together with others
A neighbor deliberately damaged your belongings and you want to file a complaint

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 366 (Property Damage, etc.)
items.text: Destroying or hiding another's property, documents or electronic records, or otherwise impairing their usefulness, is punished by up to 3 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 7 million. Attempts are also punished (Article 371).

items.name: Criminal Act Article 369(1) (Special Property Damage)
items.text: Damaging property by displaying the force of a group or crowd or while carrying a dangerous object is punished by up to 5 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 10 million.

items.name: Punishment of Violences, etc. Act (폭력행위 등 처벌에 관한 법률) Article 2(2)
items.text: If two or more people jointly commit property damage, the penalty set in the Criminal Act is increased by up to one half.

sections.title: It can be property damage even without breaking anything
body: Impairing usefulness means making an item unusable for its intended purpose. Splashing filth on a car so it can't be driven as is, or hiding documents so they can't be used, can also count.

On the other hand, if you dropped and broke something by accident, there is no intent, so it is not property damage. It is important to check with video and witnesses whether it was deliberate, thrown in anger, or knocked off by bumping into it.

sections.title: When assault is also alleged, a settlement has a different effect
body: When something is broken during an argument, assault or threats are often alleged as well. Assault and threats cannot be prosecuted if the victim does not want punishment, but property damage is not that kind of crime, so the case remains even after a settlement. If the settlement agreement states that the victim does not want punishment, it is taken into account in the decision.

If several people broke things together or someone was holding a dangerous object, the penalty becomes heavier as special property damage or joint property damage under the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act. This is why each person's actions need to be described separately in statements.

sections.title: Check that repair costs have a basis
body: Check whether the amount the other person demands matches an actual repair estimate and does not include scratches that were already there. If you pay compensation after matching the scope with estimates and photos, it is reflected in the criminal decision and settles the civil dispute as well.

If you are the one filing a complaint, you need materials showing the damage was deliberate. Submitting before-and-after photos, video or messages capturing what the other person said in anger, and a repair estimate together makes it easier to rebut a claim that it was an accident. Jisan Law writes the criminal complaint with these materials attached and goes with you to your questioning as the complainant.

factors.title: Factors That Affect the Outcome and Sentence
plus: Held a dangerous object or acted with others
A large amount of damage
Repeated it against the same person
Assault or threats also occurred
minus: Spur-of-the-moment circumstances
Paid repair costs and settled
Minor damage
No criminal record
