items.title: Consultation with the managing partner
items.desc: We hear what happened and decide whether to dispute intent or admit it and make up for the harm.

items.title: Securing materials from the scene
items.desc: We put CCTV, dashcam footage, witnesses and before-and-after photos in time order.

items.title: Sitting in on questioning
items.desc: We go into the questioning with you and object on the spot to improper questions.

items.title: Submitting a written opinion
items.desc: We submit a written opinion before the decision, attaching the scope of repairs and records of compensation.

checklist.title: Helpful Materials to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: Photos and video of the scene
The repair estimate the other person sent
Messages exchanged at the time
Witnesses' contact details
The text asking you to appear

faqs.q: I threw something in anger, and the other person's belongings broke too.
faqs.a: If you meant to break the other person's belongings, or threw it knowing they could break, intent may be found. The direction and distance of the throw and the surroundings are the basis for the judgment, so secure any video first.

faqs.q: I threw away my ex-partner's belongings. Is that a problem?
faqs.a: If the items belong to the other person, throwing them away or hiding them can be treated as impairing their usefulness. It is safer to set a deadline for them to collect their things, tell them, and keep a record that you stored the items in the meantime.

faqs.q: I want to file a complaint against someone who deliberately damaged my belongings.
faqs.a: You need materials showing it was deliberate. Gather video, messages exchanged before and after, and a repair estimate when filing, and you can claim repair costs as damages separately from the criminal case.

areaPages.title: Acquiring and Keeping Stolen Goods
areaPages.summary: You can be punished even if you didn't know for sure the goods were stolen, as long as you had reason to suspect it, and secondhand buyers in the trade can be liable for negligence too.
areaPages.lead: Buying, keeping or moving items obtained by theft or deception is a stolen goods crime (장물죄). Many people are contacted over secondhand phones, luxury goods or precious metals they bought below market price.

seo.title: Acquiring Stolen Goods and Negligent Acquisition in Korea | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: Contacted by the Korean police for acquiring stolen goods because a phone you bought on a secondhand app or jewelry you purchased turned out to be stolen? Whether you had reason to suspect it at the time is the issue. We cover the statutory penalty, the awareness standard courts apply, buyers' duty of care and the special rule for relatives.
keywords: negligent acquisition of stolen goods Korea

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: A phone you bought below market price on a secondhand app turned out to be stolen
You run a used phone buying business and bought unopened phones purchased with a stolen card
The police contacted you because items an acquaintance left with you were stolen
You sold items a family member brought you on their behalf
Jewelry your shop bought turned out to come from a fraud

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 362 (Acquisition of Stolen Goods, Brokering, etc.)
items.text: Acquiring, transferring, transporting or keeping stolen goods, or brokering such acts, is punished by up to 7 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 15 million. If habitual, the punishment is 1 to 10 years' imprisonment (Article 363).

items.name: Criminal Act Article 364 (Occupational or Gross Negligence)
items.text: Acquiring stolen goods or similar acts through occupational negligence or gross negligence is punished by imprisonment without labor for up to 1 year or a fine of up to KRW 5 million.

items.name: Criminal Act Article 365 (Crimes Between Relatives)
items.text: If you are related to the victim, prosecution requires the victim's complaint. If you are the spouse, a lineal blood relative or a relative living together with the original offender who obtained the stolen goods, or the spouse of such a person, the sentence can be reduced or waived (amended December 31, 2025).

sections.title: Being aware enough to suspect is sufficient
body: You don't need to know for certain that the goods were stolen. Courts hold that awareness at the level of suspecting they might be stolen is enough, considering the seller's identity, the nature of the goods and the price and manner of the deal (Supreme Court Decision 2004도6084, October 13, 2006).

A price far below market, new products without a receipt or warranty, and seller accounts and deposit accounts that keep changing are unfavorable signs. If you paid the market price and checked the seller's identity, those records are your strongest materials.

sections.title: If suspicion arose after you bought it
body: The same ruling holds that if you did not know when you received the item and only later came to suspect it was stolen, it is not the crime of acquiring stolen goods. However, reselling or moving it after you found out can create a separate problem, so if you become suspicious, it is safer to leave it as is and inform the investigators.

sections.title: If buying is your business, the duty of care is heavier
body: In trades where stolen goods easily slip in, such as buying phones, precious metals or luxury goods, there is considered to be a duty of care to check how the goods were obtained and who the seller is. If you neglected to check, you can be punished for occupational negligence in acquiring stolen goods (업무상과실장물취득) even if you didn't know they were stolen.
If you routinely kept records of checking ID, a purchase ledger and market price lookups, those become materials showing there was no negligence.

Occupational negligence in acquiring stolen goods applies even if you did not know the goods were stolen, but its statutory penalty is much lighter. The outcome depends greatly on which crime you are charged with, so we first argue that there was no reason to suspect anything at the time of the deal.

factors.title: Factors That Affect the Outcome and Sentence
plus: Traded at a price far from market value
Repeatedly bought and resold
Did not check the seller's identity
A previous record for the same offense
minus: Records showing you paid the market price
Records of checking the seller's ID and transaction history
Reported it and handed over the item as soon as you became suspicious
Returned the item to the victim
No criminal record

items.title: Consultation with the managing partner
items.desc: We hear how you bought the item, the price and your relationship with the seller, and identify where awareness may be an issue.

items.title: Organizing transaction materials
items.desc: We gather chats, transfer records, market price data and purchase ledgers to reconstruct the circumstances of the deal.

items.title: Mock questioning and sitting in
items.desc: We practice in advance for questions about the price and the seller, and go into the questioning with you.

items.title: Submitting a written opinion
items.desc: We submit a written opinion, with supporting materials, showing there was no reason for suspicion or that you fulfilled your duty of care.

checklist.title: Helpful Materials to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: Chat records with the seller
Transfer records
Materials showing the market price at the time of the deal
Purchase ledgers and ID check records (if you are a dealer)
Records of handing over or returning the item

faqs.q: If I return the item, will I avoid punishment?
faqs.a: Returning it counts in your favor in the decision, but it does not by itself clear the allegation. Stolen goods crimes look at whether you had reason to suspect the goods were stolen at the time of the deal.

faqs.q: The seller was a friend, so I didn't suspect anything.
faqs.a: Knowing the seller can be a reason you didn't suspect, but if the item was expensive for your friend's circumstances or the explanation of where it came from was sketchy, it may count against you. Keep the chat records of how your friend explained it.

faqs.q: I sold items a family member brought me on their behalf.
faqs.a: There is a provision allowing the sentence to be reduced or waived if you are the spouse, a lineal blood relative or a relative living together with the person who obtained the stolen goods. However, a waiver is not automatic, and it does not apply to accomplices who are not family.

areaPages.title: Extortion and Special Extortion
areaPages.summary: Even if you were owed money, it becomes extortion if the way you frightened the other person goes beyond what society accepts. The case remains even after a settlement.
areaPages.lead: Frightening someone into handing over money or a financial benefit is extortion (공갈). Demands for settlement money or compensation backed by threats to expose or report someone are often met with extortion complaints.

seo.title: Extortion and Special Extortion Accusations in Korea | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: Accused of extortion in Korea after demanding settlement money or compensation, or of special extortion after going with others to collect money? How you made the demand is the issue. We cover the statutory penalty, the line between extortion and legitimately exercising your rights, attempts and the effect of a settlement.

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: You demanded compensation for an accident, said you would tell the other person's company, and were accused of extortion
You are accused of taking money after threatening to tell someone's family about their private life
You went with several people to pressure someone into repaying money you lent
You demanded compensation over a foreign object in your restaurant food and were reported
Someone is using your weak spot to demand money, and you want to file a complaint

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 350 (Extortion)
items.text: Obtaining property or a financial benefit by extorting a person is punished by up to 10 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 20 million. Attempts are also punished (Article 352).

items.name: Criminal Act Article 350-2 (Special Extortion)
items.text: Extortion committed by displaying the force of a group or crowd or while carrying a dangerous object is punished by 1 to 15 years' imprisonment, with no fine option.

items.name: Punishment of Violences, etc. Act (폭력행위 등 처벌에 관한 법률) Article 2(2)
items.text: If two or more people jointly commit extortion, the penalty set in the Criminal Act is increased by up to one half.

sections.title: It can be extortion even if you were owed money
body: Courts hold that even with a legitimate claim, collecting money through threats that society would find hard to accept is extortion (Supreme Court Decision 99도4305, February 25, 2000). The problem is less what you demanded than how you demanded it.

Calculating your loss, claiming compensation and saying you will sue if they don't pay is generally seen as exercising your rights. On the other hand, demanding more than your actual loss while saying you will tell their workplace or family, or post it online, makes it more likely to be seen as extortion.

sections.title: It is punished as an attempt even if you got no money
body: Even if the other person was not frightened or did not send money, once you began the extortion it is attempted extortion. If you made the demand by text or messenger, those records are direct evidence, so to explain the context you need to check the full conversation in time order.

If the other side submitted only part of the conversation, you need to submit the messages before and after the demand as well. The same sentence reads differently depending on whether the other person first promised compensation and who first mentioned an amount.

sections.title: The investigation continues even after a settlement
body: Extortion can be prosecuted even if the victim does not want punishment. Returning the money and settling is reflected in the decision and sentence, but it does not end the case. Special extortion carries only imprisonment, so how early you made up for the harm affects whether you get a suspended sentence (집행유예).
If several people went together, the penalty may be increased as joint extortion under the Punishment of Violences, etc. Act. Write down separately what each person who went said and did.

factors.title: Factors That Affect the Outcome and Sentence
plus: Went with several people or showed a dangerous object
Demanded an amount far from the actual loss
Demanded repeatedly or actually exposed the person
A previous record for the same offense
minus: There was an actual loss behind the demand
Returned the money and settled
A single, spur-of-the-moment incident
No criminal record

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Criminal Law Center Responds

items.title: Consultation with the managing partner
items.desc: We check the circumstances behind the demand, what was actually said and any money received.

items.title: Organizing conversation records
items.desc: We put messages and call recordings in time order to build materials showing how the demand was made.

items.title: Mock questioning and sitting in
items.desc: We practice in advance for questions about how you made the demand and the words used, and go into the questioning with you.

items.title: Written opinion and restitution
items.desc: We argue that it was within the scope of exercising your rights, or if you admit it, proceed with returning the money and settling, and submit a written opinion.

checklist.title: Helpful Materials to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: All messages exchanged with the other person
Call recordings
Materials on the loss behind the demand (medical certificates, receipts, etc.)
Records of money given and received
The text asking you to appear

faqs.q: The other person was in the wrong first. Why is asking for compensation extortion?
faqs.a: Even if the other person was clearly at fault, getting money by frightening them can be extortion. What decides it is whether the amount was close to the actual loss, and whether you mentioned a lawsuit or formal procedures or instead threatened to expose them.

faqs.q: If I return the money, does the case end?
faqs.a: The investigation can continue even if you return it. However, returning it early and settling weighs heavily when deciding whether to indict and on the sentence.

faqs.q: I was harmed and want compensation, but I'm worried I'll be accused of extortion.
faqs.a: Document your loss to set the amount, and don't say you will tell their workplace or family. If you make the demand through formal channels, such as a certified letter or civil proceedings, you can avoid an extortion dispute.

areaPages.areaName: Gambling and Running a Gambling Venue
areaPages.title: Gambling, Habitual Gambling and Opening a Gambling Venue
areaPages.summary: Even within online gambling, illegal private sports betting falls under the National Sports Promotion Act and is punished far more heavily than gambling under the Criminal Act.
areaPages.cardLaw: Criminal Act Articles 246 and 247; National Sports Promotion Act Article 48
areaPages.lead: From online casinos and ladder games to private sports betting sites and cash-out services at hold'em pubs, betting money on an outcome decided by chance raises gambling issues. The applicable law depends on whether you were a user or an operator and what kind of game it was.

seo.title: Online Gambling, Illegal Sports Betting and Running a Gambling Venue in Korea | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: Asked by the Korean police to appear for using a gambling site, or accused of opening a gambling venue over cash-outs at a hold'em pub? First sort out the type of game and your role. We cover the statutory penalties under the Criminal Act and the National Sports Promotion Act, habitual gambling and the statute of limitations.

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: The police asked you to appear over a gambling site you used several years ago
You were told records of the account you used to top up a private sports betting site have surfaced
You run a hold'em pub and are accused of exchanging chips for cash or gift certificates
You worked promoting a gambling site or managing its accounts
You were caught playing cards for stakes with acquaintances

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 246 (Gambling and Habitual Gambling)
items.text: Gambling is punished by a fine of up to KRW 10 million, but it is not punished if it is no more than temporary amusement. Habitual gambling is punished by up to 3 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 20 million.

items.name: Criminal Act Article 247 (Opening a Gambling Venue, etc.)
items.text: Opening a place or space for gambling for profit is punished by up to 5 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 30 million, and a fine of up to KRW 10 million can be added (Article 249).

items.name: National Sports Promotion Act (국민체육진흥법) Article 26(1), Article 47 and Article 48
items.text: Issuing, without permission, anything similar to betting tickets that pay out money for correctly predicting sports results is punished by up to 7 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 70 million, and a person who gambles using them is punished by up to 5 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 50 million.

sections.title: Punishment for users depends on the type of game
body: Using sites for online casinos, baccarat, or ladder and odd-even games falls under the crime of gambling in the Criminal Act, which carries only a fine. In contrast, private sports betting (사설 스포츠토토) on the results of real sports matches falls under the National Sports Promotion Act, which carries imprisonment even for users. If you did both on one site, you need to separate how much you bet on each.

If you used the site over a long period with many bets and large amounts, it may be treated as habitual gambling (상습도박), making imprisonment possible. Investigators match top-up and cash-out accounts with server records, so admitting only part of it based on memory undermines the credibility of your statement.

sections.title: For operators and staff, their actual role is examined
body: Even a business where the game itself is not a problem, such as a hold'em pub, can amount to opening a gambling venue if it exchanges chips for cash or gift certificates or connects players with outside money changers. People who served as dealers, did promotion or managed accounts are also investigated as accomplices or accessories depending on their role, and operating profits are subject to confiscation or collection of their value, so how much you actually gained must also be disputed.

sections.title: Whether it was temporary amusement is also considered
body: Games among acquaintances for small stakes may be treated as temporary amusement (일시오락) and not punished. The size of the stakes, the participants' financial circumstances, the time and place of the game and what the winnings were used for are considered together.

When someone borrows money or dips into company funds to finance gambling, fraud or embezzlement often becomes an issue as well. We review the whole situation so that responding only to the gambling case doesn't lead to another case.

factors.title: Factors That Affect the Outcome and Sentence
plus: Long period of use and large amounts (habitual)
Used private sports betting
Involved in operating, promotion or cash-outs
Committed other crimes to fund gambling
A previous record for the same offense
minus: Short period of use and small amounts
Quit on your own and received treatment or counseling
Family has promised to supervise and support you
No criminal record
No or little operating profit

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Criminal Law Center Responds

items.title: Consultation with the managing partner
items.desc: We check the sites used, the type of games, the period and your role to sort out the applicable law.

items.title: Organizing account records
items.desc: We organize top-up and cash-out records by period and match them against the investigators' materials.

items.title: Mock questioning and sitting in
items.desc: We practice in advance for questions about how you came to use the site and how often, and go into the questioning with you.

items.title: Submitting a written opinion
items.desc: We dispute habitual gambling or the scope of involvement, and submit a written opinion with treatment and relapse-prevention materials attached.

checklist.title: Helpful Materials to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: The text asking you to appear
Records of the accounts used to top up and cash out on the site
Notes on the sites used and the types of games
For operator cases, materials on how the business operated and its revenue
Treatment or counseling records

faqs.q: I only lost money. Can I still be punished?
faqs.a: The crime of gambling is committed by betting money and taking part, regardless of whether you won or lost. However, if you only topped up and never actually placed bets, you can dispute it, so check the records.

faqs.q: It happened several years ago. Can I still be punished?
faqs.a: The statute of limitations is 5 years for gambling and habitual gambling under the Criminal Act, and 7 years for using private sports betting (Criminal Procedure Act Article 249). It is counted from the last day you used the site, so the period must be organized precisely.

faqs.q: Does it help to get treatment for a gambling problem?
faqs.a: Records of steady treatment or counseling are reflected in the decision and sentence as efforts to prevent relapse. Records of actually attending matter more than a token registration.

faqs.q: Can I get back the money I put into a gambling site?
faqs.a: Money handed over to gamble is often treated as payment for an illegal cause (불법원인급여), making it hard to claim back. If you report that the site refused to cash out, your use of the site may come to light first, so organize the period and amounts of use and then get advice.

areaPages.areaName: Unauthorized Fundraising and Illegal Multi-Level Marketing
areaPages.title: Unauthorized Fundraising and Illegal Multi-Level Marketing
areaPages.summary: If money was raised by promising to return the principal plus high returns, it is punished as unauthorized fundraising even if it is not fraud, and recruiters are investigated too.
areaPages.cardLaw: Act on the Regulation of Unauthorized Fundraising Articles 3 and 6; Door-to-Door Sales Act Article 58
areaPages.lead: Raising money from many people without authorization while promising to return the principal or more is unauthorized fundraising (유사수신). Many cases involve crypto, mining or investment platforms, and people who recruited downline investors and received commissions are also booked.

seo.title: Unauthorized Fundraising and Illegal Multi-Level Marketing Charges in Korea | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: Questioned in Korea as an accomplice in unauthorized fundraising after recruiting acquaintances to an investment platform that promised to return investors' principal and receiving commissions, or is your investment stuck? First sort out the issues. We cover the statutory penalties under the Unauthorized Fundraising Act and the Door-to-Door Sales Act, and how they differ from fraud.

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: You introduced acquaintances to an investment platform and received commissions, and now you are told you are an accomplice in unauthorized fundraising
You invested in a crypto mining product and withdrawals are blocked
You worked as a ranked member of an MLM company that turned out to be unregistered
You only recommended investments based on the company's presentation materials
You are preparing a criminal complaint to get your investment back

items.name: Act on the Regulation of Unauthorized Fundraising (유사수신행위의 규제에 관한 법률) Articles 2, 3 and 6
items.text: Prohibits, among other things, raising funds (including virtual assets) from unspecified members of the public as a business without authorization, permission, registration or reporting under the law, while promising to pay the principal or more in the future. Violations are punished by up to 5 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 50 million. Advertising for this purpose is punished by up to 2 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 20 million.

items.name: Act on Door-to-Door Sales, etc. (방문판매 등에 관한 법률) Article 24 and Article 58(1)
items.text: Operating a multi-level sales organization without registration, effectively moving only money without any trade in goods, or paying for recruiting downline salespeople itself, among other acts, is punished by up to 7 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 200 million. If three times the total sales amount exceeds KRW 200 million, the fine can be up to that amount.

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 347 (Fraud)
items.text: If investment money was taken while hiding a structure that could not pay the promised returns, fraud is also at issue, and if the gain is KRW 500 million or more, the Specific Economic Crimes Act applies.

sections.title: Unauthorized fundraising and fraud are considered separately
body: Unauthorized fundraising is committed if you made a business of raising money while promising to repay the principal without authorization, regardless of whether anyone was deceived. The mere fact that there was a business genuinely trying to make a profit is hard to use as a defense.

Fraud additionally asks whether the structure could never pay the promised returns from the start and this was hidden. If it was a scheme paying earlier investors with money from later ones, it is easily seen as fraud, and the losses are often large enough for the Specific Economic Crimes Act to apply.

sections.title: For recruiters and ranked members, what they knew is the issue
body: People who trusted the head office's explanation and recommended it to acquaintances are also booked. Many invested themselves and suffered losses while also receiving recruitment commissions, so it is common to be both a victim and a suspect.

The first step is to organize when you learned about the company's revenue structure, what you said when recommending it and how much commission you received. You also need to organize how much you put in and lost to explain your actual gain. Keep records of rank promotion bonuses and referral performance as well.

sections.title: If you are a victim, stop making further deposits first
body: If you are asked to deposit more or pay a fee to withdraw, don't put in any more. Download the investment contract, deposit records, group chats and presentation materials, and consider a provisional attachment (가압류) while the operator still has assets, to give yourself a chance of recovery.

In cases with many victims, people often file complaints together. Even if you gather materials in a group chat, keep your own investment records and how you were recruited separate so that statements don't get mixed up. On the victims' side, Jisan Law writes complaints tailored to each person's investment records and goes with them to their questioning as complainants.

factors.title: Factors That Affect the Outcome and Sentence
plus: Led recruitment from a high rank
Received large commissions
Kept recommending it even after withdrawals were blocked
Many victims and large losses
minus: You are also an investor who suffered heavy losses
Circumstances in which it was reasonable to trust the company's materials
Quit as soon as you learned of the problem
Returned commissions or made up for the harm
No criminal record

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Criminal Law Center Responds

items.title: Consultation with the managing partner
items.desc: We hear about the company's structure, your role, your investment and commissions, and sort out whether unauthorized fundraising, the Door-to-Door Sales Act or fraud is at issue.

items.title: Organizing the flow of funds
items.desc: We put the money you put in, the dividends and commissions received, and your losses into a table.

items.title: Mock questioning and sitting in
items.desc: We practice in advance for questions about how you recruited people and when you became aware, and go into the questioning with you.

items.title: Submitting a written opinion
items.desc: We submit a written opinion with materials on the extent of your involvement, your actual gain and your circumstances as a victim.

checklist.title: Helpful Materials to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: The investment contract and the company's explanatory materials
Account records of deposits, dividends and commissions
Group chats and recruitment messages
Rank charts or commission structure materials
The text asking you to appear

faqs.q: I lost money too. Why am I a suspect?
faqs.a: Because if you were an investor who also brought in others and received commissions, you can be seen as taking part in raising the money. The money you lost is taken into account in the decision and sentence, so organize precisely what you put in and what you received.

faqs.q: I never promised anyone they would get their principal back.
faqs.a: Unauthorized fundraising requires a promise to pay the principal or more, so if there was no such promise, there is room to dispute it. However, if the company's materials or group chat announcements stated fixed returns, merely passing them on can be a problem.

faqs.q: How can I tell whether an MLM company is registered?
faqs.a: Multi-level sales businesses must register with the Fair Trade Commission or the provincial government, and the Fair Trade Commission publishes registration information. Before joining, also check whether the company has a consumer damage compensation insurance contract.

areaPages.title: Computer Fraud and Fraudulent Use of Credit Cards
areaPages.summary: The charge depends on how you used someone else's card or account: a payment, a bank transfer or a cash withdrawal.
areaPages.cardLaw: Criminal Act Article 347-2; Specialized Credit Finance Business Act Article 70
areaPages.lead: These are cases of using a family member's or acquaintance's card, account or mobile payment without permission, or paying with a card you found. Because money moved through machines and computer systems rather than by deceiving a person, they are treated differently from ordinary fraud.

seo.title: Computer Fraud and Fraudulent Credit Card Use in Korea | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: Contacted by the Korean police after secretly transferring money from a family member's account or paying with a card you found? The charge depends on how the money moved. We cover the statutory penalties, Supreme Court rulings distinguishing payments, transfers and cash withdrawals, and complaint issues in cases between family members.
keywords: unauthorized use of family member's card Korea
Specialized Credit Finance Business Act violation

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: You opened the banking app on your parent's phone and transferred money to your own account
You made several payments at a convenience store with a card you found
You were accused of making online payments with the card of a partner you lived with
You are accused of processing points and refunds using your access to the company's computer system
Your child secretly used your card and the police contacted you

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 347-2 (Fraud Using Computers, etc.)
items.text: Obtaining a financial benefit by entering false information or improper commands into a computer or other information processing device, or by entering or changing information without authority, is punished by up to 20 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 50 million (amended December 23, 2025).

items.name: Specialized Credit Finance Business Act (여신전문금융업법) Article 70(1)
items.text: Selling or using a lost or stolen credit or debit card, or a card obtained by robbery, embezzlement or deception, is punished by up to 7 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 50 million.

items.name: Criminal Act Articles 354 and 328 (Crimes Between Relatives)
items.text: Fraud and computer fraud between relatives can be prosecuted only on the victim's complaint. However, this special rule does not apply if the victim is found to be a financial institution.

sections.title: The charge depends on how the money moved
body: Taking a cash advance from an ATM with a stolen card is theft as well as fraudulent use of a credit card (Supreme Court Decision 95도997, July 28, 1995). If you used the same card to transfer money to your own account, the issue is not theft but computer fraud (컴퓨터등사용사기) (Supreme Court Decision 2008도2440, June 12, 2008).

If you bought something by presenting the card at a shop, fraud against the merchant and fraudulent use of a credit card are both considered, and if you found the card, not returning it is assessed separately as well.

sections.title: Even between family members, the case may not end
body: When you used a family member's card or account, if the special rule for relatives applies, the case can be prosecuted only if the family member who is the victim files a complaint. However, in a case where someone used a relative's bankbook to transfer the deposit to their own account at another bank, the Supreme Court treated the financial institution, not the relative, as the victim and did not apply this special rule (Supreme Court Decision 2006도2704, March 15, 2007). This is why the case can continue even if your family does not want you punished.

sections.title: The issue is how far you were permitted
body: If you routinely shared passwords and were trusted to pay household expenses, the dispute is over how far you were permitted. Gather conversations and transaction records showing the permitted purposes and amounts and whether you had used it the same way before. In company system cases, the rules setting the scope of your authority and approval records are the standard.

factors.title: Factors That Affect the Outcome and Sentence
plus: Split payments or transfers into many transactions
Large amounts with no recovery
Threw away or hid the card after paying
A previous record for the same offense
minus: Signs that you had routinely been allowed to use it
Only once and a small amount
Returned the card and paid compensation immediately
No criminal record

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Criminal Law Center Responds

items.title: Consultation with the managing partner
items.desc: For each transaction, we check how you obtained the card or account and how you used it.

items.title: Sorting out the charges
items.desc: We separate payments, transfers and cash withdrawals, and determine which crime is at issue for each and who the victim is.

items.title: Mock questioning and sitting in
items.desc: We practice in advance for questions about the scope of permission and how you used it, and go into the questioning with you.

items.title: Written opinion and restitution
items.desc: We submit a written opinion with records of compensation and materials about permission attached.

checklist.title: Helpful Materials to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: Payment and transfer records
Notes on how you came to have the card
Chat records showing you were routinely allowed to use it
Records of compensation or returning the card
The text asking you to appear

faqs.q: I paid once, a few thousand won, with a card I found. Can I still be punished?
faqs.a: Regardless of the amount, fraudulent use of a credit card and fraud can be at issue. However, if it happened only once, you paid compensation right away and you have no criminal record, those circumstances are considered in the decision. Keep the receipts for compensation paid to the card company or the shop.

faqs.q: My child secretly used my card, and I want to withdraw the report.
faqs.a: If it was used to pay at shops, the special rule for family members comes into play, but if it was a cash withdrawal or transfer and the financial institution is treated as the victim, the case may continue even if you, the parent, don't want it to. If your child is under 14, juvenile protection proceedings, rather than criminal punishment, are at issue.

faqs.q: I had access rights to the company system. Is it still computer fraud?
faqs.a: Even with access rights, it can be computer fraud if you went beyond their scope to enter false information or process things for your own benefit. The first thing to check is how far your authority extended under company rules.

areaPages.title: Assault, Injury and Threats
areaPages.lead: Simple assault and threats cannot be punished if the victim does not want punishment, but once injury or a dangerous object is involved, you can be punished even after a settlement. Which charge the case is framed as is decided early on.

seo.title: Assault, Injury and Threats in Korea: Penalties, Settlement and Self-Defense | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: The outcome depends on whether it was a mutual fight, whether you can claim self-defense and when you settle. We cover the statutory penalties for assault, injury, special assault and threats in Korea, which ones end if the victim does not want punishment, the effect of a statement of no wish to punish, and the evidence to keep before questioning.

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: An argument broke out over drinks and you pushed each other, but only you were accused
You were hit first and only blocked, but the other person submitted a medical certificate for a 2-week injury
You got out of your car during a road rage argument, and they say it is special assault
You were accused of threats because of a text you sent in anger
The other person is demanding an excessive amount to settle
You were assaulted and want to file a criminal complaint

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 260 (Assault, Assault on a Lineal Ascendant)
items.text: Using violence against a person's body is punished by up to 2 years' imprisonment, a fine of up to KRW 5 million, short-term detention or a petty fine. Prosecution cannot be brought against the victim's expressed wishes (paragraph 3).

items.name: Criminal Act Article 257 (Injury)
items.text: Injuring a person's body is punished by up to 7 years' imprisonment, suspension of qualifications for up to 10 years, or a fine of up to KRW 10 million. It can be punished even if the victim does not want punishment.

items.name: Criminal Act Article 261 (Special Assault) and Article 258-2 (Special Injury)
items.text: Assault committed by displaying the force of a group or crowd or while carrying a dangerous object is punished by up to 5 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 10 million; if it causes injury, by 1 to 10 years' imprisonment.

items.name: Criminal Act Article 283 (Threats)
items.text: Threatening a person is punished by up to 3 years' imprisonment, a fine of up to KRW 5 million, short-term detention or a petty fine, and prosecution cannot be brought against the victim's expressed wishes.

table.title: Statutory Penalties and the Effect of a Settlement
columns: If the victim does not want punishment
rows: Up to 2 years' imprisonment, a fine of up to KRW 5 million, short-term detention or a petty fine
Up to 5 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 7 million
Up to 5 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 10 million
Up to 7 years' imprisonment, suspension of qualifications for up to 10 years, or a fine of up to KRW 10 million
Can be punished; no fine option
Up to 3 years' imprisonment, a fine of up to KRW 5 million, short-term detention or a petty fine
Up to 7 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 10 million
table.note: If assault or special assault results in injury or death, it is punished as injury, serious injury or injury resulting in death (Criminal Act Article 262). Based on current laws on the National Law Information Center (국가법령정보센터, the government's official law database) as of October 2026.

sections.title: Assault and injury are not decided by a single medical certificate
body: Assault (폭행) means the use of physical force against a person's body, so pushing or throwing things without hitting can also count. Injury (상해) requires a result in which the person's physical health has worsened. A medical certificate does not automatically make it injury, and a minor wound that would heal on its own is sometimes not recognized as injury.

We check whether the certificate was issued several days after the incident, whether the diagnosis fits what happened, and whether there are actual treatment records. Whether the charge is framed as assault or injury completely changes the effect of a settlement.

sections.title: Mutual fights and self-defense
body: An act to protect yourself or others from a present unjust attack is not punished if there is a reasonable ground for it (Criminal Act Article 21). However, if both sides fought intending to attack each other, the fact that you were hit first is usually not enough for self-defense (정당방위) to be recognized.

The factors are whether you were acting to defend yourself, whether you went beyond what was needed to block, and whether there was another way to avoid it. Even if you went too far, it may not be punished if it was out of fear or panic at night or in an unsettling situation (paragraph 3 of the same Article). So we break the CCTV footage down scene by scene: the order of events, who laid hands first and how many times blows were exchanged.

sections.title: A dangerous object changes the charge
body: Even if it is not a weapon, any object that can make the other person feel endangered depending on how it is used is treated as a dangerous object. Bottles, chairs, umbrellas and sometimes even cars can count. If you are found to have carried a dangerous object, it becomes special assault or special injury, and the rule that the case ends if the victim does not want punishment no longer applies.

Special injury has no fine option, so if you are indicted, the sentence is set within the range of imprisonment. How the object was actually used and whether the situation would make the other person feel endangered can be disputed, so we quickly secure footage from the scene and witness statements.

sections.title: Timing of a settlement and the effect of a statement of no wish to punish
body: For simple assault and threats, once the victim states they do not want punishment, prosecution cannot be brought and the case ends. This can be done until the first-instance judgment is pronounced, and once given, it cannot be taken back to seek punishment again (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 232(3)).

Injury, special assault and similar crimes can be punished even after a settlement, but it weighs heavily in the decision and sentence. If the victim refuses to settle or their contact details are unknown, we consider a criminal deposit (형사공탁) at the trial stage (Deposit Act Article 5-2). Check that the settlement agreement includes, along with the amount, a statement that the victim does not want punishment (처벌불원).

sections.title: Threats can arise from a single text
body: Threats are committed by announcing harm that would frighten the other person, regardless of whether you actually intended to carry it out. Even a message sent in anger can lead to a complaint for threats depending on its content and the surrounding conversation.

On the other hand, if it was a passing expression of emotion, or the conversation as a whole shows it was not an announcement of harm, it may not be a threat. Don't look only at the message in question; save the entire conversation before and after it with screenshots or a backup.

factors.title: Factors That Affect the Outcome and Sentence
plus: Used a dangerous object or assaulted with several people
Serious wounds or a long treatment period
Repeated, one-sided beating
Retaliation or attempts to approach the victim
A record of violent crimes, or an offense during a suspended sentence period
minus: The other person attacked or provoked first
Minor harm and a spur-of-the-moment incident
A settlement with the victim and a statement of no wish to punish
A criminal deposit when a settlement is not possible
No criminal record

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Criminal Law Center Responds

items.title: Consultation with the managing partner
items.desc: At the first consultation, we determine whether it was mutual, whether self-defense can be argued and whether the case needs a settlement.

items.title: Securing footage and records
items.desc: CCTV at shops and on the street is kept only briefly. We secure footage, witnesses and messages first.

items.title: Mock questioning and sitting in
items.desc: We pick out likely questions scene by scene and practice, and in the interview room we object on the spot to leading questions.

items.title: Written opinion and settlement approach
items.desc: We submit a written opinion arguing self-defense or that no injury occurred. In cases you admit, we decide together on the timing and method of a settlement, and Jisan Law handles settlement contact with the victim's side on your behalf.

items.title: Filing complaints for victims
items.desc: If you were the one assaulted, we organize the medical certificate and footage, write the criminal complaint and go with you to your questioning as the complainant.

checklist.title: Helpful Materials to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: Where and when it happened, and who was nearby
Locations of CCTV cameras or footage you have secured
If you were hurt, a medical certificate and photos
All messages exchanged with the other person
The text asking you to appear or a copy of the complaint
The settlement terms the other person has demanded

faqs.q: I was hit too. Should I file a counter-complaint?
faqs.a: If you were actually hit, you can file a complaint, and both of you will be investigated for mutual assault. However, using it only as leverage for a settlement can undermine the credibility of your statement. It is better to first organize evidence of your own injuries and your defensive circumstances, then decide.

faqs.q: What if the settlement agreement doesn't say the victim doesn't want punishment?
faqs.a: In simple assault or threats cases, if only settlement money changes hands and the victim's wish not to punish is not conveyed to the investigators or the court, the case continues. The settlement agreement must clearly state the wish not to punish, and that document must be submitted to the investigators or the court to take effect.

faqs.q: The victim is demanding an outrageous amount to settle.
faqs.a: Settling is not mandatory, and there is no fixed standard for the amount. We propose a reasonable range based on the degree of injury, medical costs and sentencing in similar cases, and if no settlement is reached, you can show your willingness to make up for the harm through a criminal deposit at the trial stage.

faqs.q: If I'm accused of assault, how much will the fine be?
faqs.a: The statutory penalty for simple assault is up to 2 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 5 million, among others. The actual amount depends on the degree of violence, injuries, criminal record and whether a settlement was reached, so it is hard to say in advance. It is a crime that cannot be punished against the victim's wishes (반의사불벌죄), so if a settlement is reached, no punishment is imposed at all.

areaPages.title: Special Assault and Special Injury
areaPages.summary: Whether you were holding the object, and whether it counts as a dangerous object, changes the effect of a settlement and the statutory penalty.
areaPages.lead: The single fact that you were holding a dangerous object turns assault into special assault (특수폭행), and the case does not end even if the victim does not want punishment. How the object was actually used is the first issue deciding the charge and the sentence.

seo.title: Special Assault and Special Injury in Korea: Penalties and What Counts as a Dangerous Object | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: Special assault and special injury depend on whether you carried a dangerous object or acted with others, and you can be punished even after a settlement. We cover the statutory penalties, when cars, bottles or phones count as dangerous objects, joint assault and the materials to secure before questioning.

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: You threw the phone in your hand during an argument, and you were told to come in for questioning for special assault
You only picked up a beer bottle at a drinking session and put it back down, but it became special assault
You are accused of special injury for pushing someone with your car
An argument broke out while you were with friends, and you were accused of several people beating someone
You settled with the victim, but you were told the case is not over

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 261 (Special Assault)
items.text: Assault or assault on a lineal ascendant committed by displaying the force of a group or crowd or while carrying a dangerous object is punished by up to 5 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 10 million. Unlike simple assault, it can be punished regardless of the victim's wishes.

items.name: Criminal Act Article 258-2 (Special Injury)
items.text: Injury or injury to a lineal ascendant committed in the same way is punished by 1 to 10 years' imprisonment, and if it results in serious injury, by 2 to 20 years' imprisonment. There is no fine option, and attempts are also punished.

items.name: Punishment of Violences, etc. Act (폭력행위 등 처벌에 관한 법률) Article 2(2) and (4)
items.text: If two or more people jointly commit assault, threats, injury or similar crimes, the penalty set in the Criminal Act is increased by up to one half. The rule that prosecution cannot be brought if the victim does not want punishment does not apply to joint assault or joint threats.

sections.title: A dangerous object is defined by how it was used, not by what it is
body: Courts decide by asking whether, by common social standards, using the object could make the other person or a third party feel their life or body was in danger. In a case where a driver, after a road rage argument, reversed 4 to 5 meters and hit the other car, the Supreme Court treated the car as a dangerous object (Supreme Court Decision 2010도10256, November 11, 2010).

Even the same phone or umbrella is assessed differently depending on how far it was thrown, where it hit and whether the other person could have avoided it. So we check scene by scene what you were holding and whether you actually hit or threatened someone with it.

sections.title: A settlement doesn't end it, but a change of charge changes things
body: Special assault, special injury and joint assault can be punished even with a statement of no wish to punish (처벌불원서). However, a settlement and making up for the harm weigh heavily in whether you are indicted and on the sentence, so it is better to plan the timing and method in advance.

If a dangerous object is not established during the investigation, the charge may be reframed as simple assault, and then the victim's wish not to punish can end the case. This is why you shouldn't simply accept the charge you were first booked under, but dispute the object and the circumstances first.

sections.title: Special injury has no fine option
body: Special injury carries only imprisonment, so it cannot end with a summary order (약식명령), and if indicted you face a formal trial. A suspended sentence (집행유예) is possible only when the sentence is 3 years' imprisonment or less, so materials on making up for the harm and remorse need to be ready before trial.

In cases where several people were present, what each person did is assessed separately. If even people who tried to stop the fight or just watched were lumped in for joint assault, the extent of each person's involvement must be distinguished using footage from the scene.

factors.title: Factors That Affect the Outcome and Sentence
plus: Actually swung a weapon or aimed at vital areas such as the head or face
Several people surrounded and beat one person
Deep wounds or a long treatment period
A record of violent crimes, or an offense as a repeat offender or during a suspended sentence period
minus: Only held the object and did not use it
The other person attacked or provoked first
A settlement with the victim and payment of medical costs
A criminal deposit when a settlement is not possible

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Criminal Law Center Responds

items.title: Consultation with the managing partner
items.desc: In the consultation, we first sort out which object is at issue and whether there is room to argue it was simple assault.

items.title: Securing footage and materials from the scene
items.desc: We first secure shop CCTV, dashcam footage and witnesses' contact details, and record photos and the size of the object in question.

items.title: Mock questioning and sitting in
items.desc: We practice in advance for questions about why you were holding the object and your movements, and go into the questioning with you.

items.title: Submitting a written opinion
items.desc: We submit a written opinion disputing whether it was a dangerous object and whether there was joint involvement.

items.title: Restitution and sentencing materials
items.desc: We prepare a settlement or criminal deposit (형사공탁), petitions and records of medical costs before trial.

checklist.title: Helpful Materials to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: The text asking you to appear or details of the case filing
CCTV or dashcam footage from the scene, or information on where such footage is
Photos of the object in question
The contents of the other person's medical certificate (if you know them)
If you were hurt, your medical records and photos

faqs.q: I was only holding the object and didn't swing it. Is it still special assault?
faqs.a: The provision punishes assault while carrying a dangerous object, so it is not required that you hit someone with it. However, the judgment depends on whether the situation would make the other person feel endangered by the object and how it related to the assault. Write down specifically the distance at the time, where your hands were and why you were holding it.

faqs.q: If I'm indicted for special injury, is it hard to avoid prison?
faqs.a: There is no fine option, but a suspended prison sentence can still be imposed. The degree of harm, whether there was a settlement, your criminal record and how it happened are the factors, and if a settlement is difficult, we also consider a criminal deposit.

faqs.q: The police said it was special assault. Can that change later?
faqs.a: The charge is reassessed based on the evidence by the prosecutor after referral and by the court after indictment. If a dangerous object is not established, it can change to assault, so you need to state that part accurately from the questioning stage.

areaPages.title: Trespass and Refusal to Leave
areaPages.summary: Shared stairways and hallways in apartment buildings also count as a residence, and whether you entered in a way that disturbed the peace decides whether it is trespass.
areaPages.lead: Trespass (주거침입) does not require going inside the home itself. Entering a shared hallway or stairway of an apartment building can also be a problem, and even if you entered with permission at first, refusing a request to leave is refusal to leave (퇴거불응).

seo.title: Trespass and Refusal to Leave in Korea: Penalties and Rulings on Shared Areas | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: The shared entrance and hallways of an apartment building in Korea can also be the subject of trespass. We explain the standard for entry (disturbing the actual peace of the residence), cases involving co-residents and landlords, when refusal to leave applies, heavier penalties for joint trespass and preparing for questioning.

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: You went as far as the hallway in front of your ex-partner's home and were reported for trespass
You followed another resident through the shared entrance of an apartment building and were reported
The shop owner told you to leave, you stayed to complain, and you were booked for refusal to leave
You opened a lock changed by your separated spouse and entered the home
As the landlord, you couldn't reach the tenant and went inside to check

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 319 (Trespass and Refusal to Leave)
items.text: Breaking into a person's residence, a managed building, a ship or aircraft, or an occupied room is punished by up to 3 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 5 million. The same applies to refusing a request to leave such a place, and attempts are also punished (Article 322).

items.name: Criminal Act Article 320 (Special Trespass)
items.text: Trespass or refusal to leave committed by displaying the force of a group or crowd or while carrying a dangerous object is punished by up to 5 years' imprisonment.

items.name: Punishment of Violences, etc. Act (폭력행위 등 처벌에 관한 법률) Article 2(2)1
items.text: If two or more people jointly commit trespass or refusal to leave, the penalty set in the Criminal Act is increased by up to one half.

sections.title: Shared stairways and hallways count as part of the residence
body: The Supreme Court holds that elevators, shared stairways and hallways inside multi-unit housing such as apartment buildings are, absent special circumstances, a residence protected by the crime of trespass (Supreme Court Decision 2009도4335, September 10, 2009). This means that even without opening the front door, entering as far as the hallway against the residents' wishes can be a problem.

However, whether access was effectively unrestricted and how the building was managed differ from building to building. Photos showing whether the shared entrance was locked and the security situation help the assessment.

sections.title: The standard is whether you entered peacefully
body: Breaking in means entering in a way that disturbs the actual peace the residents enjoy. The Supreme Court held that entering a restaurant in the usual way with the owner's consent is not breaking in, even if the person had another purpose (Supreme Court en banc Decision 2017도18272, March 24, 2022).

Likewise, entering a shared home in the usual way with the consent of a resident who is present is not trespass merely because it is against the wishes of another resident who is away (Supreme Court en banc Decision 2020도12630, September 9, 2021). On the other hand, if you were refused entry or got in secretly, the conclusion is different.

sections.title: A spouse's home or a rented-out home can also be a problem
body: In a case where a spouse who lived in the home blocked entry without good reason and the other spouse went in, the Supreme Court did not find trespass (Supreme Court en banc Decision 2020도6085, September 9, 2021). But if you had already moved out and ended living together, the situation is different, and breaking the lock can be a separate problem.

If you rented out a home, the person who actually occupies it is the tenant. Even a landlord can commit trespass by entering without the tenant's consent, so if you need to check, contact them in advance or ask for someone to be present.

sections.title: Refusal to leave depends on what you did after being asked
body: Even if you entered legitimately at first, staying after the person in charge clearly asked you to leave is refusal to leave. The issues are who made the request, whether it was clear and how long you stayed afterward.

factors.title: Factors That Affect the Outcome and Sentence
plus: Came back after being refused entry
Entered secretly at night or damaged a lock
Occurred together with other crimes (stalking, assault, etc.)
Entered together with several people
minus: A place with open access and a short stay
Consent from some residents, or reasons to believe you had it
A settlement with the victim and a promise not to come back
No criminal record

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Criminal Law Center Responds

items.title: Checking the place and how you entered
items.desc: In the consultation, we first check the building's layout, how access was controlled and who opened the door.

items.title: Securing footage and entry records
items.desc: We check the shared entrance access records and how long CCTV is kept, and secure the footage.

items.title: Mock questioning and sitting in
items.desc: We practice so you can answer consistently about your purpose and how you entered, and go into the questioning with you.

items.title: Written opinion and settlement
items.desc: We submit a written opinion arguing it was not breaking in, or in cases you admit, prepare a settlement with the victim and materials on preventing a recurrence.

checklist.title: Helpful Materials to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: Photos of the building entrance and shared entrance
Texts and call records exchanged at the time of entry
A lease or materials showing you lived there together
Notes on the situation when you were asked to leave

faqs.q: I didn't go inside the home, only up to the front door.
faqs.a: Shared stairways and hallways in multi-unit housing are treated as part of the residence, so going that far against the residents' wishes can be trespass. Circumstances such as whether the shared entrance was open and whether outsiders routinely came in can be disputed.

faqs.q: I went to my ex-partner's door a few times. Is that stalking too?
faqs.a: Waiting or watching near someone's home can be a stalking act, and if it continues or is repeated, it becomes a stalking crime. It is often investigated together with trespass, so stop going there and get advice.

faqs.q: Does a settlement end a trespass case?
faqs.a: Trespass can be prosecuted even if the victim does not want punishment. Even so, a settlement weighs heavily in whether you are indicted and on the sentence.

areaPages.title: Stalking Crimes and Provisional Measures
areaPages.summary: Stalking is committed through repeated contact or approaches and can be punished even after a settlement. Violating a provisional measure is a separate crime.
areaPages.lead: A stalking crime can be punished even if the victim does not want punishment. Violating a no-approach or no-contact order issued right after a report even once is a separate crime, so you first need to know exactly what the decision covers.

seo.title: Stalking Reports, Provisional Measures and Emergency Measures in Korea | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: Stalking in Korea is committed through repeated contact or approaches, and you can be indicted even with a statement of no wish to punish. We cover what emergency measures and provisional measures involve and how long they last, penalties for violations, the deadline to appeal, how to argue there was a legitimate reason, and preparing for questioning.

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: You contacted your ex a few times after breaking up and were reported for stalking
The court issued a provisional measure ordering no approach and no contact
The police notified you of a 100-meter no-approach order as an emergency measure
Calling and visiting several times to get back money you lent has become a problem
You were accused of stalking for knocking on the wall over noise between floors
During a provisional measure, the other person contacted you first and you replied

items.name: Act on the Punishment of Stalking Crimes (스토킹범죄의 처벌 등에 관한 법률) Article 2 (Definitions)
items.text: A stalking act is causing anxiety or fear, against the other person's will and without a legitimate reason, by approaching or following them, waiting or watching near their home or workplace, or sending words or messages by phone, text or messenger, among other acts. Doing this continuously or repeatedly is a stalking crime.

items.name: Article 18 of the same Act (Stalking Crimes)
items.text: A stalking crime is punished by up to 3 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 30 million; if a weapon or other dangerous object is carried or used, by up to 5 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 50 million. The provision barring prosecution against the victim's wishes was deleted by the amendment of July 11, 2023.

items.name: Articles 9 and 20 of the same Act (Provisional Measures and Penalties for Violation)
items.text: The court can order a written warning, no approach within 100 meters, no approach by telecommunications, attachment of an electronic location-tracking device, or confinement in a police holding cell or detention center. Failing to comply with a provisional measure banning approach or contact is punished by up to 2 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 20 million.

table.title: Measures Issued in Stalking Cases
rows: Emergency measure (no approach within 100 meters, no approach by telecommunications)
Judicial police officer, with a judge's approval afterward
Up to 1 year's imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 10 million
Provisional measures No. 2 and 3 (no approach, no approach by telecommunications)
Up to 3 months, extendable twice by 3 months each
Up to 2 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 20 million
Up to 3 months, extendable twice by 3 months each
Impairing the device: up to 3 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 30 million
Provisional measure No. 4 (confinement in a police holding cell or detention center)
table.note: Act on the Punishment of Stalking Crimes Articles 4, 5, 9 and 20. Based on current laws on the National Law Information Center (국가법령정보센터, the government's official law database) as of October 2026.

sections.title: One or two contacts are viewed differently from repeated contact
body: What is punished is carrying out stalking acts continuously or repeatedly. Courts hold that if the conduct, viewed objectively and generally, is enough to cause the other person anxiety or fear, it is a stalking act regardless of whether the person actually felt that way (Supreme Court Decision 2023도6411, September 27, 2023).

A case of repeatedly banging on walls and ceilings over noise between floors was also found to be a stalking crime (Supreme Court Decision 2023도10313, December 14, 2023). Even if the purpose was to get money back or solve a problem, it is hard to be recognized as a legitimate reason if the method went beyond what society considers reasonable.

sections.title: A provisional measure is not a finding of guilt, but violating it creates a new case
body: Texts to apologize, messages offering to return belongings, passing on words through acquaintances, messages from new accounts and social media comments can all be treated as prohibited approaches. Even if the other person contacts you first, don't reply; take screenshots of what they sent.

If the decision violates the law, involves a serious factual error or is clearly unjust, you can appeal within 7 days of being notified (Article 12), and if circumstances change, you can apply to have it cancelled or changed (Article 11). A provisional measure (잠정조치) loses effect if the prosecutor decides not to indict.

sections.title: A settlement affects the outcome and sentence rather than whether you are punished
body: You can be indicted even with a statement of no wish to punish (처벌불원서), but a settlement with the victim is an important factor in deciding on a suspended indictment (기소유예) or the sentence. If approach and contact are prohibited, do not try to settle directly; find a way through a lawyer or the investigators.

If you are found guilty, an order to attend classes or complete a stalking treatment program of up to 200 hours may also be imposed (Article 19). If you start counseling or treatment in advance, those records become materials showing efforts to prevent a recurrence.

factors.title: Factors That Affect the Outcome and Sentence
plus: Kept contacting them with new numbers or accounts after being blocked
Went to their home or workplace and waited
Violated an emergency measure or provisional measure
Carried a weapon or made threats as well
minus: Few contacts over a short period, then stopped
Had a reason to contact them, such as a debt, and the method was not excessive
A settlement with the victim and steps to prevent a recurrence, such as moving or deleting their contact details
Taking part in counseling or a treatment program

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Criminal Law Center Responds

items.title: Checking the decision and notices
items.desc: We check whether it is an emergency measure or a provisional measure, who and where is covered and for how long, and set out exactly what you must comply with.

items.title: Organizing contact records
items.desc: We put messages sent and received in date order so the number of contacts and the circumstances can be shown objectively.

items.title: Mock questioning and sitting in
items.desc: We practice in advance for questions about why and how often you made contact, and go into the questioning with you.

items.title: Challenges and written opinion
items.desc: If there is something to dispute in the decision, we consider an appeal or an application to cancel or change it within 7 days, and submit a written opinion disputing whether there was a legitimate reason or repetition.

items.title: Sentencing materials
items.desc: If indictment is expected, we organize counseling records, materials on preventing a recurrence and the progress of settlement.

checklist.title: Helpful Materials to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: The emergency measure decision or provisional measure decision
All messages and call records exchanged with the other person
Records of the other person contacting you first
Materials showing why contact or a visit was needed (a debt, shared belongings, etc.)
Records of any counseling or treatment

faqs.q: The other person contacted me first. Can't I reply?
faqs.a: A provisional measure prohibits you from contacting or approaching the other person, so even if they contacted you first, replying can be treated as a violation. Don't reply; save what you received.

faqs.q: Can I challenge a provisional measure decision?
faqs.a: You can appeal within 7 days of being notified of the decision. If that period has passed or circumstances have changed, you can apply to the court to have it cancelled or changed.

faqs.q: If I get a settlement agreement, does the case end?
faqs.a: A stalking crime can be prosecuted even if the victim does not want punishment, so a settlement alone does not end the case. However, a settlement is given significant weight in the decision and sentence.

faqs.q: If I've been warned once and then someone else reports me, is it more serious?
faqs.a: If the victim is different, repetition and whether anxiety was caused are assessed separately for each case. However, having been reported several times for similar behavior can count against you when the risk of reoffending is assessed.

areaPages.areaName: Domestic Violence and Domestic Protection Cases
areaPages.title: Domestic Violence and Domestic Protection Cases
areaPages.summary: These cases can go to protective dispositions in family court instead of a criminal trial. Violating a temporary measure is punished separately.
areaPages.cardLaw: Domestic Violence Punishment Act Articles 2, 9, 29 and 40
areaPages.lead: Assault and threats between spouses or between parents and children are handled under the Domestic Violence Punishment Act, and instead of a criminal trial, the prosecutor can send the case as a domestic protection case (가정보호사건) for a protective disposition. How you comply with the temporary measures issued right after the police are called also affects the later outcome.

seo.title: Domestic Violence Reports, Temporary Measures and Domestic Protection Cases in Korea | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: When domestic violence is reported in Korea, emergency and temporary measures come first, and the case then goes either to a criminal trial or as a domestic protection case. We cover who counts as a family member, the types and length of protective dispositions, penalties for violating temporary measures and the effect of the victim not wanting punishment.
keywords: police called over a marital fight Korea

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: The police came during a fight with your spouse and told you to stay out of the house
Your spouse reported you for assault, but you were hit too
You pushed your father during an argument and were booked for assault on a lineal ascendant
You received notice that your case was referred as a domestic protection case
You are under a temporary 100-meter no-approach order but need to make contact about your child
Your spouse says they don't want you punished, but the case is continuing

items.name: Act on Special Cases Concerning the Punishment of Domestic Violence (가정폭력범죄의 처벌 등에 관한 특례법) Article 2
items.text: Domestic violence crimes include assault, injury, threats, arrest and confinement, trespass, coercion, property damage, defamation and insult, among others, between spouses (including common-law spouses) or former spouses, lineal ascendants and descendants, stepparents and children, and relatives living together.

items.name: Articles 9, 40 and 41 of the same Act (Domestic Protection Cases and Protective Dispositions)
items.text: Considering the nature, motive and result of the case and the offender's character and conduct, and respecting the victim's wishes, the prosecutor can handle the case as a domestic protection case. The court can order restrictions on approach, restrictions on approach by telecommunications, restrictions on exercising parental authority, community service or an order to attend classes, probation, entrustment to custodial care, entrustment for treatment and entrustment for counseling. The period cannot exceed 6 months, and community service or classes cannot exceed 200 hours.

items.name: Articles 29 and 63 of the same Act (Temporary Measures and Failure to Comply)
items.text: As temporary measures, a judge can order separation such as removal from the home, no approach within 100 meters, no approach by telecommunications, entrustment to a medical institution, confinement in a police holding cell or detention center, and entrustment for counseling. Failing without good reason to comply with separation, no-approach or no-contact orders is punished by up to 1 year's imprisonment, a fine of up to KRW 10 million or short-term detention.

sections.title: From the police call-out to referral
body: Police who receive a report stop the violence, separate the offender and the victim and, if necessary, arrest the offender in the act. If there is a risk of recurrence and it is urgent, a judicial police officer can directly order emergency temporary measures such as removal from the home or no approach, and in that case temporary measures must be requested from the court within 48 hours (Articles 8-2 and 8-3).

The police promptly investigate domestic violence crimes, refer them to the prosecutor and can give an opinion on whether handling the case as a domestic protection case is appropriate (Article 7). That is why a notice of referral sometimes comes even after the police said the evidence was weak.

sections.title: Domestic protection cases proceed differently from criminal trials
body: If the prosecutor sends the case as a domestic protection case, the family court (or the district court where there is no family court) investigates and holds hearings, then decides on a protective disposition (보호처분) or no disposition. Once a protective disposition becomes final, no prosecution can be brought again for the same facts (Article 16).

A protective disposition is not a criminal punishment, so it does not remain as a criminal record the way a fine or imprisonment does. However, if you fail to carry out a disposition such as community service or entrustment for counseling, it can be cancelled and the case sent back to the prosecutor (Article 46).

sections.title: It may not end even if the victim does not want punishment
body: Simple assault and threats normally cannot be prosecuted if the victim does not want punishment, but even then the prosecutor can handle the case as a domestic protection case (Article 9(2)). Injury and special assault can be indicted regardless of the victim's wishes.

If the assaults were repeated and treated as habitual, the rule barring prosecution against the victim's wishes does not apply. The Supreme Court held that when someone is punished for habitual assault on a lineal ascendant, prosecution can be brought even against the victim's wishes (Supreme Court Decision 2017도10956, April 24, 2018).

sections.title: During a temporary measure, decide on a channel for contact
body: Even if you need to make contact about taking your child to and from school, living expenses or belongings, contacting the person directly by a prohibited method violates the temporary measure (임시조치). First consider going through a lawyer or applying to the court to cancel or change the temporary measure (Article 29(10)). To challenge the decision, you must appeal within 7 days of being notified (Article 49).

factors.title: Factors That Affect the Outcome
plus: Repeated violence or violence in front of children
Use of a weapon or dangerous object
Violated a temporary measure or no-approach order
The victim strongly wants punishment
minus: A one-time fight with circumstances on both sides
Started family counseling or treatment on your own
The victim does not want punishment and there are efforts to restore the relationship
A plan to prevent a recurrence, such as treatment for a drinking problem

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Criminal Law Center Responds

items.title: Checking the measures
items.desc: We check the scope and period of any emergency temporary measure or temporary measure and immediately set out what you must comply with.

items.title: Organizing the circumstances and materials
items.desc: We organize how the fight happened, injuries on both sides, past reports and the time of the 112 emergency call.

items.title: Mock questioning and sitting in
items.desc: We practice in advance for questions that may extend to family relationships and past fights, and go into the questioning with you.

items.title: Opinion on a domestic protection case
items.desc: We submit a written opinion that a domestic protection case is more appropriate than a criminal trial, or one disputing the allegations.

items.title: Preparing for the hearing
items.desc: If the case is referred as a domestic protection case, we gather records of completed counseling and the family's views and submit them at the hearing.

checklist.title: Helpful Materials to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: Documents on temporary or emergency temporary measures received from the police
Photos of injuries and medical records (if you were hurt too)
Messages exchanged on the day
Certificates of any family counseling or treatment
Materials on related proceedings, such as a divorce lawsuit

faqs.q: If it goes as a domestic protection case, will there be no criminal record?
faqs.a: A protective disposition is not a criminal punishment, so it is not recorded as a criminal record the way a fine or prison sentence is.
