However, the record of having been investigated may be kept separately, and if you do not carry out the disposition, it can go back to being a criminal case.

faqs.q: My wife says she doesn't want me punished. Why was the case referred?
faqs.a: The Domestic Violence Punishment Act requires the police to refer the case to the prosecutor, and even if the victim does not want punishment, the prosecutor can handle it as a domestic protection case. The victim's wishes are something the prosecutor and the court must respect when deciding the outcome.

faqs.q: I received a protective disposition. What happens if I can't finish the community service?
faqs.a: The court, on its own or at the request of the prosecutor or others, can cancel the protective disposition and send the case back to the prosecutor or transfer it to the court that referred it. If something comes up, tell the probation office in advance and discuss a change.

areaPages.title: Child Abuse (Parents, Childcare Teachers and Teachers)
areaPages.summary: The issue is how far discipline and student guidance are allowed. For childcare teachers and teachers, the penalty is increased and employment restrictions follow.
areaPages.cardLaw: Child Welfare Act Articles 17 and 71; Child Abuse Punishment Act Article 7
areaPages.lead: Child abuse cases often turn on how far a parent's discipline, childcare at a daycare center or a school's student guidance is allowed. A report alone starts both a local government inquiry and a police investigation, and because childcare teachers and teachers are mandatory reporters, their penalty can be increased by up to one half.

seo.title: Child Abuse Reports in Korea: Parents, Childcare Teachers and Teachers | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: When child abuse is reported in Korea, a local government inquiry and a police investigation proceed together. We explain the standards for physical and emotional abuse, the exception for teachers' legitimate student guidance, heavier penalties for mandatory reporters, conditional suspended indictments, child protection cases and employment restriction orders.

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: You spanked your child as discipline, and the school reported it as child abuse
A parent who saw daycare CCTV footage reported you, a childcare teacher
You were accused of emotional abuse for scolding loudly during class
You are being investigated for child abuse because your child witnessed a fight between you and your spouse
A child abuse officer at the district office contacted you asking you to come in
You received notice that the case was referred as a child protection case

items.name: Child Welfare Act (아동복지법) Article 17 and Article 71(1)
items.text: Physical abuse, emotional abuse (including exposing a child to domestic violence), neglect and similar acts against a child under 18 are punished by up to 5 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 50 million, and sexual abuse by up to 10 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 100 million.

items.name: Act on Special Cases Concerning the Punishment of Child Abuse Crimes (아동학대범죄의 처벌 등에 관한 특례법) Article 2, item 3 and Article 7
items.text: Teachers' legitimate educational activities and student guidance under the Early Childhood Education Act and the Elementary and Secondary Education Act are not considered child abuse. If a mandatory reporter, such as daycare staff, kindergarten or school staff or a private academy instructor, commits a child abuse crime against a child in their care, the penalty for that crime is increased by up to one half.

items.name: Child Welfare Act Article 29-3 (Employment Restrictions)
items.text: When imposing a sentence, including a fine, for a child abuse-related crime, the court also orders that the person may not run or work at child-related institutions for a period of up to 10 years. Exceptions include cases where the risk of reoffending is markedly low.

sections.title: The applicable law depends on who did it
body: Child abuse crimes under the Child Abuse Punishment Act refer to abuse by a guardian. Guardians include not only those with parental authority but also people who protect, raise or educate the child and people who effectively protect and supervise the child through work or employment, so childcare teachers, teachers and private academy instructors are included.

Even if you are not a guardian, the prohibited acts in the Child Welfare Act apply to everyone. Neighbors or adult relatives who hit or insult a child can also be investigated for violating the Child Welfare Act.

sections.title: Emotional abuse looks at the risk of the act rather than the intent
body: The Supreme Court holds that emotional abuse can arise when there is a risk or possibility of harming the child's mental health and normal development, and it is enough that the person was conditionally aware of that risk (Supreme Court Decision 2015도13488, December 23, 2015). Explaining that the purpose was to teach is not enough; the content and intensity of the words, whether it was repeated and the situation at the time are considered together.

For teachers, legitimate educational activities and student guidance are not considered child abuse, and if conduct during educational activities is reported, the superintendent of education with jurisdiction can submit an opinion. The police and prosecutor must file that opinion in the case records and take it into account (Child Abuse Punishment Act Article 17-3).

sections.title: The investigation proceeds on two tracks
body: Once a report is made, a child abuse officer at the city, county or district office can require you to appear, give a statement and submit materials to assess the case (Article 11-2), while the police conduct a criminal investigation. What you say in both places is recorded, so your account of the facts should be consistent from the start.

In cases involving parents, the need to protect the child within the original family is also considered. The prosecutor can give a suspended indictment (기소유예) on condition of counseling, treatment or education (Article 26), or send the case to court as a child protection case (아동보호사건) for a protective disposition (Article 27).

sections.title: How the outcome affects your career
body: Even a fine, in principle, comes with an employment restriction order. If you work at a daycare center, school or private academy, it is important to dispute not only the type of sentence but also an exemption from or the length of the employment restriction. Separately from the criminal outcome, disciplinary or licensing procedures at your institution may follow.

factors.title: Factors That Affect the Outcome and Sentence
plus: Repeated several times against the same child
Targeted young infants or toddlers
Left injuries or the child needed treatment
Told the child or parents to change their statements after the report
minus: A one-time situation with a clear guidance purpose
A situation where the child's behavior was threatening other children's safety
A settlement and apology to the child's side
Efforts to prevent a recurrence, such as completing parenting counseling or education

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Criminal Law Center Responds

items.title: Organizing the situation
items.desc: We set out in time order the context before and after the reported scene, the child's behavior and who else was there.

items.title: Securing footage
items.desc: We check the original CCTV footage from the daycare, classroom or home and how long it is kept, and request access or preservation.

items.title: Mock questioning and sitting in
items.desc: We practice in advance for questions about the purpose and method of guidance, and go into the police questioning with you.

items.title: Submitting a written opinion
items.desc: We submit a written opinion based on the scope of legitimate guidance, the intensity and frequency of the conduct, and the superintendent's opinion, among other things.

items.title: Preparing for the decision
items.desc: We prepare the materials needed for a conditional suspended indictment, a child protection case or an exemption from employment restrictions.

checklist.title: Helpful Materials to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: Details of the report or the text asking you to appear
CCTV footage or information on where it is kept
Guidance records, notices to parents and counseling records concerning the child
Contact details of fellow teachers or others who were present
Written accounts submitted to the education office or institution

faqs.q: Is it enough to say it was for discipline?
faqs.a: The purpose alone does not settle the question. What you said and did and how many times, how the child reacted and whether there was another way are all reviewed, so you need to be ready to explain the specific scenes.

faqs.q: Do I have to say the same thing to the district office and the police?
faqs.a: The two procedures have different purposes, but your statements can be compared. It is important to separate facts you clearly remember from guesses and speak consistently.

faqs.q: If I only get a fine, can I no longer work at a daycare center?
faqs.a: Even when a fine is imposed for a child abuse-related crime, an employment restriction order is in principle imposed with it. If you show circumstances such as a markedly low risk of reoffending, you may be exempted or the period may be shortened.

areaPages.title: Confinement and Coercion
areaPages.summary: These often arise on the spur of the moment between partners or over debts. The issues are how you kept the person from leaving and for how long.
areaPages.lead: Confinement (감금) does not require locking a door. Ignoring a request to be let out of a car and continuing to drive, or blocking someone from leaving an office until they pay, can also be confinement, and if you forced someone to write a signed pledge or apology, coercion (강요) is also at issue.

seo.title: Confinement and Coercion in Korea: When They Apply and the Penalties | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: Not letting someone out of a car or a room can also be confinement in Korea. We explain the statutory penalties for confinement and for confinement resulting in injury or death, confinement through psychological barriers, the standard for coercion when someone is made to write a pledge or resignation letter, and what to organize before questioning.

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: Your partner wanted to get out of the car during an argument, but you kept driving to keep talking
You held someone who wouldn't repay you in your office to talk it out
You made your spouse's affair partner write a pledge never to see them again
You pressed an employee hard to write a resignation letter and were accused of coercion
You are being questioned for confinement resulting in injury because the other person was hurt during the confinement

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 276 (Arrest and Confinement) and Article 280
items.text: Arresting or confining a person is punished by up to 5 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 7 million, or if the victim is a lineal ascendant, by up to 10 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 15 million, and attempts are also punished. Special confinement, such as while carrying a dangerous object, is increased by up to one half (Article 278).

items.name: Criminal Act Article 281 (Arrest or Confinement Resulting in Injury or Death)
items.text: If arrest or confinement causes injury, the punishment is imprisonment for a fixed term of 1 year or more; if it causes death, imprisonment for a fixed term of 3 years or more.

items.name: Criminal Act Article 324 (Coercion)
items.text: Obstructing a person's exercise of their rights or making them do something they have no duty to do by assault or threats is punished by up to 5 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 30 million; if done while carrying a dangerous object or by similar means, by up to 10 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 50 million.

sections.title: The means of keeping someone from leaving are not limited to physical ones
body: The Supreme Court holds that the barrier in confinement can be psychological and intangible as well as physical and tangible. Ignoring a request to get out and continuing to drive elsewhere at 60 to 70 km/h was confinement, and where the victim fell and died trying to escape, confinement resulting in death was found (Supreme Court Decision 99도5286, February 11, 2000).

Confinement is committed even if the person was allowed some freedom of movement within the confined space (Supreme Court Decision 2000도102, March 24, 2000). On the other hand, if the other person could leave at any time and never actually tried to, that makes it hard to see it as confinement.

sections.title: Coercion looks at the means rather than what was demanded
body: Even if you had a right to money or the other person was in the wrong, making them write a pledge by means of assault or threats can be coercion. A threat means announcing harm that would frighten the other person, so even saying you will tell their family or workplace can be a problem depending on the circumstances.

A pledge or settlement agreement obtained by coercion can be cancelled as a declaration of intent made under duress (Civil Act Article 110). If you plan to claim money based on such a pledge, first reconsider whether it is valid.

sections.title: If someone is injured, the statutory penalty changes
body: If the other person is injured during the confinement or while escaping, it becomes confinement resulting in injury, punishable by imprisonment for a fixed term of 1 year or more, with no fine option. You can dispute whether the injury was connected to the confinement and whether such a result was foreseeable.
Confinement and coercion between family members are domestic violence crimes, so temporary measures or domestic protection case procedures may proceed alongside.

factors.title: Factors That Affect the Outcome and Sentence
plus: Long confinement or a remote location
Assault or threats occurred as well
The other person was injured or put in danger trying to escape
Obtained a pledge or money
minus: Released the person on your own after a short time
Circumstances in which the other person could have left
A spur-of-the-moment situation aimed at talking or reconciling
A settlement with the victim

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Criminal Law Center Responds

items.title: Timeline by the minute
items.desc: We set out movements between places and conversations minute by minute, from the time you met to the time you parted.

items.title: Securing objective materials
items.desc: We secure dashcam footage, navigation records, messenger chats and nearby CCTV.

items.title: Mock questioning and sitting in
items.desc: We practice for questions about when you knew the person wanted to leave and why you stopped them, and go into the questioning with you.

items.title: Written opinion and settlement
items.desc: We submit a written opinion disputing the degree of confinement or threats, and for the parts you admit, prepare a settlement and sentencing materials.

checklist.title: Helpful Materials to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: Messages and call records exchanged that day
Dashcam and navigation records
Copies of the pledge or resignation letter in question
Materials showing your relationship with the other person (debt, employment, etc.)

faqs.q: I only held them for a few minutes. Is that still confinement?
faqs.a: Confinement can be committed even for a short time. However, whether it was a very short time, whether the other person actually tried to leave and how you stopped them are reflected in the decision and sentence.

faqs.q: I had a right to the money. Can it still be coercion?
faqs.a: Even if you have a right, forcing performance through assault or threats can raise coercion or extortion. It is safer to collect a debt through procedures such as a payment order or a lawsuit.

faqs.q: Is a pledge written under coercion valid?
faqs.a: A pledge written under duress is a declaration of intent that can be cancelled. If you are the one who received the pledge, check how it was written before making a claim based on it.

areaPages.title: Occupational Negligence Causing Death or Injury and Serious Accidents (Workplace Accidents)
areaPages.summary: Site managers and top management are investigated under different laws. Records of safety measures taken before the accident are key.
areaPages.cardLaw: Criminal Act Article 268; Serious Accidents Punishment Act Article 6; Occupational Safety and Health Act Article 167
areaPages.lead: When a death or injury occurs at work, the site manager is often investigated for occupational negligence causing death or injury (업무상과실치사상) and Occupational Safety and Health Act violations, while top management such as the CEO is investigated for violating the Serious Accidents Punishment Act at the same time. The records and statements made right after the accident set the direction of the investigation.

seo.title: Occupational Negligence Causing Death and Serious Accidents Punishment Act Investigations in Korea | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: Deaths and injuries at Korean workplaces can bring occupational negligence charges, the Occupational Safety and Health Act and the Serious Accidents Punishment Act into play together. We cover who is investigated under which law, the statutory penalties and corporate fines, the exception for workplaces with fewer than 5 workers, and preparing for searches and questioning.
keywords: Occupational Safety and Health Act violation Korea

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: A worker fell to their death at a construction site where you were the site manager
An employee was badly injured when caught in factory equipment, and you, as the manager, were booked
As CEO, you were contacted to come in for questioning over a Serious Accidents Punishment Act violation
The accident involved a subcontractor's worker, but you were told the main contractor's manager is also responsible
A customer was injured at a business such as a shop or private academy

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 268 (Occupational or Gross Negligence Causing Death or Injury)
items.text: Causing death or injury to a person through occupational negligence or gross negligence is punished by imprisonment without labor for up to 5 years or a fine of up to KRW 20 million.

items.name: Occupational Safety and Health Act (산업안전보건법) Articles 167 and 173
items.text: Causing a worker's death by violating safety and health measure obligations, or a contractor's safety and health measure obligations, is punished by up to 7 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 100 million, and the corporation faces a fine of up to KRW 1 billion. A repeat offense within 5 years of the sentence becoming final is increased by up to one half.

items.name: Serious Accidents Punishment Act (중대재해 처벌 등에 관한 법률) Articles 6 and 7
items.text: If a death results from a violation of the duty to ensure safety and health, the business owner or management officer is punished by 1 year or more of imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 1 billion (both can be imposed); where, for example, one accident leaves two or more people injured and needing treatment for 6 months or more, by up to 7 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 100 million. The corporation faces fines of up to KRW 5 billion and KRW 1 billion respectively. It does not apply to workplaces with fewer than 5 regular workers (Article 3).

sections.title: First, sort out who is investigated under which law
body: People who directly managed the work, such as site managers or safety managers, are investigated as offenders for occupational negligence causing death or injury and Occupational Safety and Health Act violations, while the CEO or the executive in overall charge of safety and health is investigated as a management officer under the Serious Accidents Punishment Act. The corporation is subject to fines under the joint penalty provisions.

Occupational negligence causing death or injury is often investigated by the police, while the Occupational Safety and Health Act and the Serious Accidents Punishment Act are investigated by labor inspectors, so you may have to appear before both agencies over the same accident. The company should first organize the facts so that statements to the two agencies don't conflict.

sections.title: The duty of care and causation are the issues
body: Occupational negligence is judged by whether you exercised the care required of someone doing that work, and whether you could have foreseen and avoided the result. Even if the worker was also careless, a manager can be held liable for knowingly leaving a hazard in place; if all necessary measures were taken and an unforeseeable action was the cause, there is room to dispute it.

In Serious Accidents Punishment Act cases, the question is whether the safety and health management system existed only on paper or actually worked. Whether risk assessments, budget spending, site inspections and improvement reports were carried out before the accident is the key material.

sections.title: What to do right after an accident
body: Preserve the scene and secure, as they are, the work logs, pre-work safety check records, training records and records of protective equipment issued. Altering documents or creating new ones after the accident raises suspicion of destroying evidence and actually works against you.

If the accident is serious, the company and the site may be searched. Check the scope of the warrant to see which materials are subject to seizure, and keep copies of materials essential to your work.

sections.title: Relations with the bereaved family and victims
body: Making up for the harm and the bereaved family's wish not to punish weigh heavily in the decision and sentence. Industrial accident compensation and the company's liability for damages proceed separately, and the Serious Accidents Punishment Act provides for liability of up to 5 times the damages where obligations were violated intentionally or through gross negligence (Article 15).

factors.title: Factors That Affect the Outcome and Sentence
plus: The same hazard had been pointed out before but was not fixed
Basic safety facilities (railings, covers, guards) were missing
Altered records or coordinated statements after the accident
A previous record of violating the same law
minus: Risk assessments and improvements were actually carried out before the accident
A worker's unforeseeable departure from procedures
A settlement with the bereaved family or victims and making up for the harm
Measures to prevent a recurrence implemented after the accident

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Criminal Law Center Responds

items.title: Initial consultation and separating roles
items.desc: We set out separately the positions and issues of the company, the site manager and top management.

items.title: Attending searches and seizures
items.desc: If a search takes place, we attend, check the scope of the warrant and put our objections on record.

items.title: Organizing materials
items.desc: We put records of pre-accident safety measures and the reporting system in time order and turn them into evidence.

items.title: Mock questioning and sitting in
items.desc: We practice with likely questions for both the police and labor inspector questioning, and go in with you.

items.title: Written opinion and sentencing materials
items.desc: We submit a written opinion disputing whether the duty of care was breached and causation, and prepare materials on making up for the harm.

checklist.title: Helpful Materials to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: The accident report and photos of the site
Work plans, work logs and pre-work safety check records
Safety training records and records of protective equipment issued
Risk assessment materials and safety and health budget spending records
Contracting and subcontracting agreements and the organization chart

faqs.q: I'm the CEO. Can I be punished even though I wasn't at the site?
faqs.a: The Serious Accidents Punishment Act looks not at whether you were at the site but at whether, as a management officer, you fulfilled your duty to build and run a safety and health management system. A causal link between the breach of duty and the accident must also be proven separately.

faqs.q: Am I responsible even if the accident was caused by the employee's own carelessness?
faqs.a: A worker's fault does not automatically remove the manager's responsibility. The standard is whether the manager could have known of the hazard and whether steps were taken to prevent it.

faqs.q: Does the Serious Accidents Punishment Act apply to a shop with 4 employees?
faqs.a: The provisions on serious industrial accidents in the Serious Accidents Punishment Act do not apply to business owners and management officers of workplaces with fewer than 5 regular workers. However, occupational negligence causing death or injury and the Occupational Safety and Health Act can be at issue regardless of workplace size.

areaPages.areaName: Injury or Assault Resulting in Death
areaPages.title: Injury or Assault Resulting in Death and Other Grave Outcomes
areaPages.summary: Even without intent to kill, the penalty is 3 years' imprisonment or more. The cause of death and whether the result was foreseeable must be disputed.
areaPages.lead: Even if you had no intent to kill, if a person dies as a result of assault or injury, injury resulting in death (상해치사) or assault resulting in death (폭행치사) is at issue, carrying imprisonment for a fixed term of 3 years or more, with no fine option. The causal link between the act and the death, and whether that result was foreseeable, are the key issues.

seo.title: Injury or Assault Resulting in Death in Korea: Penalties and Causation | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: Even if the other person dies after a single blow, injury or assault resulting in death carries 3 years' imprisonment or more in Korea, with no fine option. We cover the difference between murder and these crimes, the cause of death and pre-existing illness, foreseeability of the result, detention and the pre-detention hearing, and relations with the bereaved family.
keywords: assault resulting in death suspended sentence Korea

situations.title: You may need a consultation if
items: You hit someone once, they fell, hit their head and died
A few days after a scuffle, you were told the other person had died
A family member was arrested for assault resulting in death and is about to have a pre-detention hearing
You were told the investigators are even considering a murder charge
You heard the victim had a pre-existing illness

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 259 (Injury Resulting in Death) and Article 262 (Assault Resulting in Death or Injury)
items.text: Injuring a person's body and causing their death is punished by imprisonment for a fixed term of 3 years or more, or if the victim is a lineal ascendant, by life imprisonment or imprisonment of 5 years or more. Causing a person's death through assault or special assault is punished in the same way as injury resulting in death.

items.name: Criminal Act Article 15(2)
items.text: For crimes whose penalty becomes heavier because of a result, the heavier crime is not punished if the occurrence of that result could not have been foreseen.

items.name: Criminal Act Article 250 (Murder)
items.text: Killing a person is punished by death, life imprisonment or imprisonment of 5 years or more. If you are found to have been aware of and accepted the possibility of death, the issue is murder, not a crime resulting in death.

sections.title: Murder and crimes resulting in death are separated by intent
body: If you intended only assault or injury and neither wanted nor expected death, it is injury or assault resulting in death. Investigators look at the tool used, where and how many times the person was struck and your conduct afterward, and may even consider conditional intent (미필적 고의) to kill, so your statement at the first questioning is extremely important.

Even with the same result, if the victim is a lineal ascendant, the statutory penalty rises to life imprisonment or 5 years or more. A death during confinement is confinement resulting in death, carrying imprisonment for a fixed term of 3 years or more.

sections.title: Confirming the cause of death medically
body: Through the autopsy report and medical records, we check the direct cause of death and how it connects to the assault. A pre-existing illness, delayed emergency care or someone else's involvement can be grounds to dispute causation.

Even if causation is established, the crime resulting in death cannot be punished if an ordinary person could not have foreseen that result (Criminal Act Article 15(2)). In that case, you are held responsible only for the assault or injury.

sections.title: Detention is likely in these cases
body: When a person has died, arrest and a request for a detention warrant often move quickly. At the pre-detention hearing (영장실질심사), you need to explain that there is no risk of flight or destroying evidence, pointing to your residence, work, family relationships, whether you turned yourself in and whether you gave aid at the scene.

Because the minimum statutory penalty is 3 years, a sentence of 3 years or less, which allows a suspended sentence (집행유예), requires sufficient mitigating materials such as how the crime happened, making up for the harm and the bereaved family's wishes.

factors.title: Factors That Affect the Outcome and Sentence
plus: Struck repeatedly or kept assaulting after the person fell
Used a weapon or dangerous object
Left the scene without giving aid
A record of violent crimes
minus: A single, spur-of-the-moment act
The victim attacked first, or there were other causes such as a pre-existing illness
Immediately called 119 and gave aid
A settlement with the bereaved family or a criminal deposit

steps.title: How Jisan Law's Criminal Law Center Responds

items.title: Visit right after the arrest
items.desc: We visit the arrested person right away and explain their rights and how to approach their statement.

items.title: Attending the pre-detention hearing
items.desc: We attend the pre-detention hearing and show that there are no grounds for detention.

items.title: Reviewing the cause of death and circumstances
items.desc: We review the autopsy report, medical records and footage from the scene to examine causation and foreseeability.

items.title: Sitting in on questioning and written opinion
items.desc: We also sit in on questioning during detention and submit a written opinion denying intent to kill.

items.title: Preparing for trial
items.desc: We organize relations with the bereaved family, a criminal deposit (형사공탁) and mitigating materials to prepare for trial.

checklist.title: Helpful Materials to Prepare Before a Consultation
items: The notice of arrest or details of any contact about a warrant
Contact details of people who know what happened at the scene
Information on the victim's transfer to hospital and course of treatment
Materials showing the suspect's work and family relationships

faqs.q: I only hit them once. Why is it a crime resulting in death?
faqs.a: Assault resulting in death is committed if there is a causal link between the intentional assault and the death and that result was foreseeable. Even a single blow is a problem if death followed a foreseeable path, such as falling and hitting one's head.

faqs.q: If the victim had a pre-existing illness, is my responsibility reduced?
faqs.a: Even if an illness contributed to the death, causation may not be denied if the assault was one of the causes. However, whether the illness was the main cause and whether you could have known about it at the time of the assault are issues that can be disputed.

faqs.q: Is a suspended sentence possible?
faqs.a: The statutory penalty is 3 years or more, so a suspended sentence is possible only if the sentence imposed is 3 years or less. How the crime happened, a settlement with the bereaved family and efforts to make up for the harm greatly affect the decision.

areaPages.title: Drunk Driving & Traffic Accidents
areaPages.lead: In Korea, the statutory penalty for drunk driving is set by your blood alcohol concentration and any prior offense within the last 10 years. Within that range, the core of your defense is checking how the test was carried out and preparing sentencing materials that courts actually accept.

seo.title: DUI Penalties, Repeat Offenses & Traffic Accidents in Korea | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: Drunk driving penalties in Korea depend on your blood alcohol level and any prior offense within 10 years. Learn about test refusal, drinking after driving, dangerous driving causing injury, the 12 exceptions in the Act on Special Cases Concerning the Settlement of Traffic Accidents, license suspension and revocation, ignition interlock licenses, and what to prepare before questioning.

situations.title: When you may need advice
items: I was caught at a DUI checkpoint, and I already paid a drunk driving fine a few years ago
While waiting for a designated driver, I moved my car a short distance to park it
I blew into the breathalyzer several times, but I was booked for refusing the test
I had a minor collision after drinking, and the other driver went to the hospital
I left the scene of an accident and was later contacted about a hit-and-run
I drive for a living, and losing my license is my biggest worry

items.name: Road Traffic Act (도로교통법) Article 44 (Prohibition of Driving While Intoxicated)
items.text: Driving is prohibited at a blood alcohol concentration of 0.03% or higher. Drivers must comply with a police officer's breath test. If you disagree with the result, you can be tested again, for example by a blood sample taken with your consent. Drinking more alcohol after driving in order to obstruct the test is also prohibited.

items.name: Road Traffic Act Article 148-2 (Penalties)
items.text: The statutory penalty depends on the blood alcohol range. It is increased if you violate the law again within 10 years from the date a sentence of a fine or heavier became final. Refusing the test or obstructing it is punishable by 1 to 5 years in prison or a fine of KRW 5 million to KRW 20 million.

items.name: Act on Special Cases Concerning the Settlement of Traffic Accidents (교통사고처리 특례법) Articles 3 and 4
items.text: Even if a traffic accident causes injury through occupational negligence, prosecution is not allowed if the victim does not want the driver punished or if the driver has comprehensive insurance. However, this does not apply to the 12 exceptions, such as running a red light, crossing the center line and drunk driving, or to fleeing the scene. The insurance exception also does not apply if the victim suffers serious injury.

items.name: Act on the Aggravated Punishment of Specific Crimes (특정범죄 가중처벌 등에 관한 법률) Articles 5-11 and 5-3
items.text: Injuring a person while unable to drive normally because of alcohol is punishable by 1 to 15 years in prison or a fine of KRW 10 million to KRW 30 million. Causing death is punishable by life imprisonment or at least 3 years in prison. If a driver flees without helping the victim and the victim is injured, the statutory penalty is at least 1 year in prison or a fine of KRW 5 million to KRW 30 million.

table.title: Statutory penalties for drunk driving
rows: Up to 1 year in prison or a fine of up to KRW 5 million
1 to 2 years in prison or a fine of KRW 5 million to KRW 10 million
2 to 5 years in prison or a fine of KRW 10 million to KRW 20 million
1 to 5 years in prison or a fine of KRW 5 million to KRW 20 million
Repeat offense within 10 years (0.03% or higher but below 0.2%)
1 to 5 years in prison or a fine of KRW 5 million to KRW 20 million
Repeat offense within 10 years (0.2% or higher)
2 to 6 years in prison or a fine of KRW 10 million to KRW 30 million
Repeat test refusal or obstruction within 10 years
1 to 6 years in prison or a fine of KRW 5 million to KRW 30 million
1 to 15 years in prison or a fine of KRW 10 million to KRW 30 million / life imprisonment or at least 3 years in prison
table.note: Applies to driving a motor vehicle or tram (not personal mobility devices such as e-scooters). The 10 years are counted from the date a sentence of a fine or heavier became final, including sentences that have since expired. Based on current law on the Korea Law Information Center (the government's official law database) as of October 2026.

sections.title: Your level and any offense in the last 10 years set the penalty
body: For a first offense, your blood alcohol range sets the statutory penalty. If you were previously sentenced to a fine or heavier for drunk driving, the first thing to check is whether this offense falls within 10 years from the date that sentence became final. A repeat offense within 10 years falls under a provision with a minimum of 1 year in prison, even if your level is low.

Even if your prior offense was more than 10 years ago, it is still considered at sentencing as a similar prior conviction. If you find the earlier judgment or summary order (약식명령) and note the exact date it became final, we can quickly confirm which provision applies.

sections.title: We check the test timing and circumstances one by one
body: What is punished is your level at the time you were driving. Depending on the gaps between your last drink, when you started driving and when you were tested, and how far the result is from the legal threshold, there may be room to dispute your level at the time of driving. However, the mere possibility that your level was still rising is not enough to decide the case.

We also check whether you were given a chance to rinse your mouth before the breath test, whether you asked for a blood test, and whether the times in the police report on the intoxicated driver (주취운전자 정황진술보고서) match what actually happened. If you were booked for test refusal because you could not complete the test after several attempts, we need to carefully go back over the situation and what the officer told you.
bullets: When you started and stopped drinking, and how much you drank
Where and when you started driving, how far you drove, and why you drove
Designated driver call records and card payment records
The time you were stopped, the time you were tested, and how many tests were taken

sections.title: If there was an accident, different laws apply
body: For an ordinary traffic accident, prosecution is not allowed if you have comprehensive insurance or if the victim does not want you punished. However, an accident while drunk driving is one of the exceptions under the Act on Special Cases Concerning the Settlement of Traffic Accidents, so you can be punished regardless of insurance or a settlement. If you are found to have been unable to drive normally, dangerous driving causing injury under the Aggravated Punishment Act applies.

After an accident, you must stop immediately, help the injured and give your contact details (Road Traffic Act Article 54). If you leave the scene without doing so, failure to take measures after an accident or fleeing after causing injury also becomes an issue, and this part often makes the punishment the heaviest. Write down why you left the scene and how you were contacted afterward, with dates and times.

sections.title: License penalties are handled separately from the criminal case
body: Suspension or revocation of a driver's license is an administrative penalty imposed by the provincial police agency, so it proceeds separately from criminal punishment. The standards are in Attached Table 28 of the Enforcement Rules of the Road Traffic Act. At a blood alcohol level of 0.03% or higher but below 0.08%, you receive 100 penalty points and your license is suspended; as a rule, each point counts as one day of suspension. Your license is revoked if your level was 0.08% or higher, if you caused an accident that injured someone while drinking, or if you refused the test. If you have a prior drunk driving record, a level of just 0.03% or higher leads to revocation. After revocation, you cannot get a new license for a set disqualification period.

If your license was revoked for drunk driving again within 5 years from the date of a previous violation, you must get a conditional license with an ignition interlock device to drive again (Road Traffic Act Article 80-2). If you drive for a living, you can file an objection asking the provincial police agency to reduce the penalty within 60 days from the date of the decision. However, you are not eligible for a reduction if your level exceeded 0.1%, you injured someone, you refused the test, or you have a drunk driving record within 5 years. We also check, within the deadline, whether the decision can be challenged through an administrative appeal. If you decide to challenge it, Jisan Law also handles the administrative appeal and administrative lawsuit.

sections.title: Sentencing materials must be verifiable
body: A letter of apology alone is not enough. What counts are materials that can actually be verified, such as proof that you sold your car or stopped driving, records of alcohol counseling or treatment, and a petition from your family promising that you will not drive again. If you need to drive to make a living, you should support this with a certificate of employment or income records.

If you receive a summary order imposing a fine and feel the amount is too heavy, you can request a formal trial (정식재판) within 7 days of receiving notice (Criminal Procedure Act Article 453). In a formal trial requested by the defendant, the court cannot impose a heavier type of punishment than the summary order, but the fine amount can go up, so think it through before you request one.

factors.title: Factors that affect the outcome and sentence
plus: A similar prior offense within 10 years, especially several
A high blood alcohol level
Someone was injured in an accident, or you left the scene without helping the victim
Driving without a license or while your license was suspended
Fleeing from the checkpoint or obstructing the test
minus: A short driving distance and understandable circumstances
A settlement with the victim and compensation for the harm
Efforts to prevent reoffending, such as selling the car or alcohol treatment
Dependent family and financial circumstances supported by documents
No prior record

items.title: Review the test process

items.desc: We rehearse with the questions the traffic investigation unit asks and attend the questioning with you.

checklist.title: Helpful documents to prepare before your consultation
items: Documents or photos you received at the checkpoint
Any earlier drunk driving judgment or summary order
Payment records from where you drank
Designated driver call and phone records
Original dashcam footage
