faqs.q: Is it drunk driving if I only moved my car a few meters in a parking lot while waiting for a designated driver?
faqs.a: The Road Traffic Act also punishes drunk driving in places other than roads, so a short distance alone does not clear you. However, why you moved the car, how far and where can be taken into account at sentencing, so keep a record of these together with your designated driver call history.

faqs.q: Is it test refusal if I could not blow properly a few times?
faqs.a: Test refusal applies when a person who there is good reason to believe is drunk does not comply with the test. A few failed attempts alone do not automatically count as refusal; the decision looks at the officer's request and warnings and your attitude at the time as a whole. It is important to write down what happened at the scene in time order.

faqs.q: If I drink more after being stopped, can I dispute my level?
faqs.a: No. That itself is punishable. Drinking more in order to obstruct the test is prohibited under the Road Traffic Act and carries the same statutory penalty as test refusal.

faqs.q: If I have insurance, am I free from criminal punishment after an accident?
faqs.a: For an ordinary accident causing injury through occupational negligence, prosecution is not allowed if you have comprehensive insurance. But if the accident falls under one of the 12 exceptions, such as drunk driving, running a red light or crossing the center line, or if the victim was seriously injured or you left the scene, you can be punished regardless of insurance.

areaPages.areaName: Hit-and-Run & Failure to Take Measures After an Accident
areaPages.title: Hit-and-Run (Fleeing After Causing Injury) & Failure to Take Measures After an Accident
areaPages.summary: Even if you gave your contact details, leaving without helping the injured can count as fleeing. Fleeing after causing injury is a serious crime with a minimum fine.
areaPages.cardLaw: Aggravated Punishment Act Article 5-3, Road Traffic Act Articles 54 and 148
areaPages.lead: If someone is injured in an accident and you leave the scene without helping them, you can be charged with fleeing after causing injury (도주치상) under the Act on the Aggravated Punishment of Specific Crimes. Depending on the circumstances, this can apply even if you handed over your contact details. Even when only property was damaged, failing to take the required measures is punishable as failure to take measures after an accident (사고후미조치).

seo.title: Hit-and-Run and Leaving the Scene of an Accident in Korea: Penalties and Defense | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: If you left the scene after a traffic accident in Korea, first check whether it is fleeing after causing injury or failure to take measures after an accident. Court rulings on leaving after only giving your contact details, the claim that you did not notice the accident, penalties by outcome, license disqualification periods, and how insurance relates to criminal punishment.
keywords: leaving the scene of an accident Korea
property damage hit and run Korea

situations.title: When you may need advice
items: After a minor collision, the other person said they were fine so I left, but I was reported for hit-and-run
I did not realize I scratched a car in a parking lot, but the police contacted me
I only handed over my business card and left first because of something urgent
I did not know there was an accident, but I am told my dashcam recorded the sound of an impact
I had been drinking, so I panicked and left the scene

items.name: Act on the Aggravated Punishment of Specific Crimes (특정범죄 가중처벌 등에 관한 법률) Article 5-3
items.text: A driver who injures a person in a traffic accident and flees without helping them or taking other required measures is punishable by at least 1 year in prison or a fine of KRW 5 million to KRW 30 million. If the victim dies and the driver flees, or the victim dies after the driver flees, the penalty is life imprisonment or at least 5 years in prison. Moving the victim away from the scene, abandoning them and fleeing is punished more heavily.

items.name: Road Traffic Act (도로교통법) Articles 54(1) and 148
items.text: A driver who causes a traffic accident must stop immediately, help anyone injured, take other required measures, and give the victim personal details such as name, phone number and address. Failing to do so is punishable by up to 5 years in prison or a fine of up to KRW 15 million.

items.name: Road Traffic Act Article 156, Item 10
items.text: In an accident that clearly only damaged a parked or stopped vehicle, failing to give your personal details to the victim is punishable by a fine of up to KRW 200,000, short-term detention or a petty fine.

table.title: Provisions that apply when you leave the scene after an accident
rows: Someone was injured and you left without helping
At least 1 year in prison or a fine of KRW 5 million to KRW 30 million
Fleeing after a death, or death after fleeing
Life imprisonment or at least 5 years in prison
Moving and abandoning the victim and fleeing (injury)
Only property was damaged and you did not take the required measures
Up to 5 years in prison or a fine of up to KRW 15 million
Only a parked or stopped vehicle was damaged and you did not give your details
A fine of up to KRW 200,000, short-term detention or a petty fine
table.note: Based on current law on the Korea Law Information Center (the government's official law database) as of October 2026. The duty to take measures after an accident also applies to accidents in places other than roads (Road Traffic Act Article 2, Item 26).

sections.title: Whether you fled depends on what you did before leaving
body: The Supreme Court has held that if you knew the victim was injured and left the scene without helping, it counts as fleeing even if you handed over materials identifying yourself (Supreme Court Decision 2004도250, March 12, 2004). The same decision said you do not always have to give help yourself, so whether you confirmed that someone else was helping before you left is also an important factor.

You should write down, in time order, how badly the victim was hurt, whether you were told they were fine, whether you contacted the police or your insurer, why you left, and how you were contacted afterward.

sections.title: A claim that you did not notice the accident is checked against objective evidence
body: If you did not know about the accident, you did not intend to flee or fail to take measures. However, investigators decide whether you were aware based on the force of the impact, the sound, the damage to the vehicles, dashcam footage, and what you did afterward, such as washing or repairing your car.

So it is a good idea to secure photos of the damaged parts of your car and the original dashcam footage right away. If you give a statement that differs from what the footage shows, your credibility drops sharply.

sections.title: Insurance and your license must be considered separately
body: If you fled, the special exception under the Act on Special Cases Concerning the Settlement of Traffic Accidents (교통사고처리 특례법) does not apply even if you have comprehensive insurance. Criminal proceedings continue separately from compensation through insurance, and a criminal settlement (형사합의) with the victim has a large effect on the outcome.

If your license is revoked because you injured someone and did not take the required measures or report the accident, you cannot get a new license for 4 years from the date of revocation, or 5 years if this is combined with drunk driving or similar offenses (Road Traffic Act Article 82(2)).

factors.title: Factors that affect the outcome and sentence
plus: Leaving even after seeing that the victim was badly hurt or had collapsed
Leaving to hide drunk driving or driving without a license
Changing or repairing the car to remove traces
Delaying your appearance after being contacted
minus: The impact was so slight that you may not have noticed the accident
You left your contact details after the victim said they were fine
You reported it to the police or your insurer yourself
A settlement with the victim and compensation for the harm

steps.title: How our Criminal Law Center handles your case

items.title: Reconstruct what happened
items.desc: We lay out, minute by minute, everything from the time of the accident to when you left the scene and how you were contacted afterward.

items.title: Secure footage and vehicle evidence
items.desc: We secure the original dashcam footage and photos of the vehicle damage, and check whether nearby CCTV footage is still kept.

items.title: Prepare for and attend questioning
items.desc: We rehearse with the questions the traffic investigation unit asks and attend the questioning with you.

items.title: Submit a legal opinion
items.desc: We submit a written opinion arguing whether you were aware of the accident and whether you took the required measures.

items.title: Compensation for the harm
items.desc: Separately from the insurance claim, we look at a criminal settlement or a criminal deposit (형사공탁) with the court.

checklist.title: Helpful documents to prepare before your consultation
items: Original dashcam footage (both front and rear)
Photos of the damaged parts of your car
Call and text records from the time of the accident
Your insurer's accident claim details
The text message from the police asking you to appear

faqs.q: Is it a hit-and-run if I left because the victim said they were fine?
faqs.a: If the victim was truly not injured and clearly said they were fine, that makes it hard to see your leaving as fleeing. However, if a medical certificate comes out later, the victim's condition at the time and what was said will be examined again, so write down in detail the circumstances in which you were told this.

faqs.q: Will it help if I contact the police first, even now?
faqs.a: If you report it yourself before the police contact you, it may be treated as voluntary surrender. Even after you have been contacted, appearing quickly and working to compensate the victim count in your favor for the outcome and sentence.

faqs.q: Insurance has covered everything. Can I still be criminally punished?
faqs.a: An insurance payout is civil compensation, and criminal liability is decided separately. In particular, if you injured someone and left, you can be indicted regardless of your insurance.

areaPages.title: Driving Without a License
areaPages.summary: Driving while your license is suspended or revoked also counts as unlicensed driving. If you cause an accident, it is hard to avoid criminal punishment even with insurance.
areaPages.lead: Driving without a license (무면허운전) covers not only people who never got a license, but also driving during a suspension or after revocation. The disqualification period (결격기간) often lasts longer than the punishment itself, so you also need to work out when you can apply for a license again.

seo.title: Driving Without a License in Korea: Penalties, Disqualification Period and Accidents | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: Driving while your license is suspended or revoked is unlicensed driving in Korea. Penalties for cars, motorbikes and e-scooters, cases where you did not know about the revocation, places that are not roads such as apartment complexes, unlicensed accidents and insurance, and the disqualification period before you can get a license again.

situations.title: When you may need advice
items: I thought my suspension had ended, but I was stopped while driving
I did not know my license had been revoked, but I am told I was driving without a license
I had a minor collision while driving without a license
I drove with an expired International Driving Permit
I rode a motorbike or e-scooter without a motorbike license
I have been caught driving without a license several times before

items.name: Road Traffic Act (도로교통법) Article 43 and Article 152, Item 1
items.text: Driving a car without a license or while your license is suspended is punishable by up to 1 year in prison or a fine of up to KRW 3 million. The same applies if you have no International Driving Permit or similar, if it has expired, or if you are banned from driving.

items.name: Road Traffic Act Article 154, Item 2 and Article 156, Item 13
items.text: Riding a motorized bicycle (motorbike) without a license is punishable by a fine of up to KRW 300,000 or short-term detention. Riding a personal mobility device such as an e-scooter without a license is punishable by a fine of up to KRW 200,000, short-term detention or a petty fine.

items.name: Road Traffic Act Article 82(2) (Disqualification Period)
items.text: If you drive without a license, you cannot get a license for 1 year from the date of the violation (6 months for a motorized bicycle license), or 2 years if it is your third time or more. If you injure someone while driving without a license and do not take the required measures or report it, the period is 5 years. If you receive a sentence lighter than a fine, a suspended sentencing (선고유예) or a suspension of indictment (기소유예), you can get a license even within this period.

sections.title: We first check whether you knew about the suspension or revocation
body: Unlicensed driving is an intentional crime, so you are only punished if you drove knowing your license was suspended or revoked. We check whether you received the notice of the decision, whether the notice was replaced by public notice because of a change of address or similar reason, and how you understood the last day of your suspension.
Driving on the last day of a suspension still counts as driving during the suspension. Miscalculating the period may be taken into account, but on its own it is unlikely to lead to an acquittal.

sections.title: If you drove somewhere other than a road, this can be disputed
body: The Road Traffic Act applies only some provisions, such as drunk driving, drugged driving and measures after an accident, to driving in places other than roads, and the unlicensed driving provision is not on that list (Article 2, Item 26). So if you were stopped inside an apartment complex or a building parking lot, the issue is whether that place was open for the general public to pass through.
Use photos and the building's management rules to show whether outside vehicles are controlled with a barrier and security staff, or whether anyone can come and go.

sections.title: An unlicensed accident is punishable even with insurance
body: An accident that injures someone while driving without a license is an exception under the Act on Special Cases Concerning the Settlement of Traffic Accidents (교통사고처리 특례법), so you can be prosecuted even if you have comprehensive insurance or the victim does not want you punished (Article 3(2), proviso, Item 7). A settlement with the victim often decides the outcome.

An employer who has an employee drive while knowing the employee has no license is also punished (Article 152, Item 2). Repeating the same violation is treated harshly at sentencing, and if you are on a suspended sentence (집행유예), the risk of actual imprisonment rises.

factors.title: Factors that affect the outcome and sentence
plus: Several prior convictions for unlicensed driving
Combined with drunk driving or an accident
Continuing to drive for work or other reasons while knowing about the suspension or revocation
Committing the offense during a suspended sentence
minus: A genuine mistake in calculating the suspension period
A short driving distance and unavoidable circumstances
Steps to make sure you will not drive again, such as selling the car
A settlement with the accident victim

steps.title: How our Criminal Law Center handles your case

items.title: Check the license decision
items.desc: We review the suspension or revocation notice, the decision date and how you were notified, to see whether intent can be disputed.

items.title: Clarify the place and circumstances
items.desc: We check whether the place you were stopped counts as a road, and set out why you drove and how far.

items.title: Prepare for and attend questioning
items.desc: We rehearse the questions about how you came to drive and your prior record, and attend the questioning with you.

items.title: Sentencing materials and legal opinion
items.desc: We turn the sale of your car, your public transportation plan and your financial circumstances into supporting documents and submit them with a written legal opinion.

checklist.title: Helpful documents to prepare before your consultation
items: The license suspension or revocation notice
Your driving record certificate or license status check result
Photos of the place you were stopped and documents on how it is managed
Any earlier judgment or summary order for unlicensed or drunk driving
If there was an accident, the insurance claim details and the victim's medical diagnosis

faqs.q: I only moved my car inside my apartment parking lot.
faqs.a: Unlicensed driving is only punished when it happens on a road. The answer can depend on whether outsiders and outside vehicles can freely enter that parking lot or whether access is controlled.

faqs.q: Can I get a new license right after I pay the fine?
faqs.a: Even after a fine becomes final, the disqualification period of 1 year from the date of the violation (6 months for a motorized bicycle license) must pass. If you receive a suspension of indictment or a suspended sentencing, you can get a license even within that period.

faqs.q: Is riding an e-scooter without a license also unlicensed driving?
faqs.a: To ride a personal mobility device, you need at least a motorized bicycle license. Riding without one is punishable by a fine of up to KRW 200,000, short-term detention or a petty fine.

areaPages.title: Retaliatory & Reckless Driving
areaPages.summary: Targeting a specific person is retaliatory driving (Criminal Act); creating traffic danger through several violations is reckless driving (Road Traffic Act).
areaPages.cardLaw: Criminal Act Articles 284 and 261, Road Traffic Act Article 46-3
areaPages.lead: Retaliatory driving (보복운전) is punished not under the Road Traffic Act but under the Criminal Act as special intimidation, special assault or special property damage. Because a car is treated as a dangerous object, the statutory penalties are heavy, and a separate license penalty also follows.

seo.title: Road Rage and Reckless Driving in Korea: Penalties and Dashcam Reports | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: Retaliatory driving in Korea, such as cutting in and braking suddenly or pushing another car, is punished as special intimidation or special assault. The difference from reckless driving, when a car counts as a dangerous object, reviewing dashcam footage, settlements and license penalties, and preparing for questioning.

situations.title: When you may need advice
items: I got angry when someone cut in, so I pulled in front and braked hard, and I was reported
I was accused of retaliatory driving for tailgating another car and honking
After an argument, I lightly pushed the other car with mine
I was asked to appear for reckless driving after someone reported me with dashcam footage
The other driver threatened me first, but only I was booked

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 284 (Special Intimidation), Article 261 (Special Assault), Article 369(1) (Special Property Damage)
items.text: Intimidating someone while carrying a dangerous object is punishable by up to 7 years in prison or a fine of up to KRW 10 million; assault, by up to 5 years in prison or a fine of up to KRW 10 million; and damaging property, by up to 5 years in prison or a fine of up to KRW 10 million. If someone is injured, it becomes special bodily injury (1 to 10 years in prison).

items.name: Road Traffic Act (도로교통법) Articles 46-3 and 151-2 (Reckless Driving)
items.text: Committing two or more violations in a row, or continuing or repeating one of them, such as running a red light, crossing the center line, speeding, not keeping a safe distance, illegal lane changes or sudden braking, or improper overtaking, so as to threaten others or create a traffic hazard is punishable by up to 1 year in prison or a fine of up to KRW 5 million.

items.name: Road Traffic Act Article 93(1), Item 10-2
items.text: Using a motor vehicle to commit special bodily injury, special assault, special intimidation or special property damage is grounds for revoking or suspending a driver's license.

sections.title: Retaliatory driving and reckless driving have different targets
body: Retaliatory driving means driving with the intent to frighten or harm a specific vehicle or person, so the Criminal Act's special intimidation and similar crimes apply. In a case where a driver reversed into another car to scare the other driver after an argument, the Supreme Court treated the car as a dangerous object (Supreme Court Decision 2010도10256, November 11, 2010).
Reckless driving (난폭운전) applies even without a specific target, if you commit the listed violations in a row or repeatedly and create a traffic hazard. Both charges are sometimes applied together.

sections.title: We look at the full dashcam footage before and after
body: Reported footage is usually cut to show only the problem scene. You need to check with your own original dashcam footage whether the other car cut in dangerously before that, whether your sudden braking was because of a car ahead or a traffic signal, and what the distances and speeds were.

Dashcams overwrite old footage over time, so as soon as you learn you were reported, remove the memory card and keep it safe. A claim that you had no intent to intimidate is only accepted with objective evidence like this.

sections.title: We prepare the settlement and the license penalty together
body: Special intimidation and special assault can be punished even if the victim does not want punishment, but a settlement has a large effect on the outcome and sentence. Settling the cost of repairing the other car or medical expenses first often makes an agreement easier.

A license revocation or suspension can be imposed separately from the criminal case. If there are grounds to challenge it, you should consider an administrative appeal or similar remedy within the deadline.

factors.title: Factors that affect the outcome and sentence
plus: Braking suddenly on an expressway or similar road, creating a high risk of an accident
Chasing and threatening several times, or getting out of the car and shouting abuse
An actual collision or injury
A similar prior record
minus: The other driver drove dangerously first
A single, brief act that stopped quickly
A settlement with the victim and payment for repairs
Completing a driving behavior correction course

steps.title: How our Criminal Law Center handles your case

items.title: Secure and analyze footage
items.desc: We secure your original dashcam footage, match it to the time of the reported footage, and check what happened before and after.

items.title: Clarify the charges
items.desc: In the consultation, we work out whether it is special intimidation or reckless driving, and whether both may apply.

items.title: Prepare for and attend questioning
items.desc: We rehearse the questions about why you braked, the distances and the speeds, and attend the questioning with you.

items.title: Legal opinion and settlement
items.desc: We submit a written opinion disputing intent and, if needed, look at ways to compensate and settle with the victim.

checklist.title: Helpful documents to prepare before your consultation
items: Your car's original dashcam footage (memory card)
The police text asking you to appear, or the details of the report
If there was a collision, the repair estimate and insurance claim details
Your driving history and documents about your livelihood

faqs.q: Is braking suddenly just once retaliatory driving?
faqs.a: Even a single sudden stop can raise special intimidation if you cut right in front of the other car and stopped to frighten the driver. On the other hand, if it was because of a car ahead or an unexpected situation, it is important to show this with footage.

faqs.q: The other driver also drove threateningly. Can I report them too?
faqs.a: If the other driver's conduct amounts to reckless or retaliatory driving, you can report it separately. However, use a counter-report as material to explain how your case happened, and prepare your defense against your own charge separately.

faqs.q: Can my license also be revoked for retaliatory driving?
faqs.a: Special intimidation, special assault and similar crimes committed with a car are grounds for revoking or suspending your license. The specific standards are set in the Enforcement Rules and depend on the outcome of your case.

areaPages.title: Breathalyzer Refusal
areaPages.summary: It is punished heavily regardless of your alcohol level. The key issue is whether it was objectively clear that you had no intention of taking the test.
areaPages.lead: Refusing a breathalyzer test (음주측정거부) is a crime punishable by 1 to 5 years in prison or a fine of KRW 5 million to KRW 20 million regardless of your actual blood alcohol level, which is heavier than the penalty for drunk driving below 0.2%. However, failing to blow properly a few times does not by itself make it a refusal, so what happened at the time must be examined closely.

seo.title: Breathalyzer Refusal in Korea: Penalties, When It Applies, License Revocation | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: Refusing a breathalyzer test in Korea is punishable by 1 to 5 years in prison or a fine of KRW 5 million to KRW 20 million, regardless of your level. Court standards for what counts as refusal, how it relates to asking for a blood test, cases where you were not driving, and license revocation and the disqualification period.

situations.title: When you may need advice
items: I blew into the breathalyzer several times, but I was booked for refusal because they said I did not blow properly
I protested that I had not been driving, and it was treated as refusing the test
I asked for a blood test instead of a breath test, and it was treated as a refusal
I left without blowing into the alcohol screening device
My license was revoked for test refusal and I am worried about my livelihood

items.name: Road Traffic Act (도로교통법) Article 44(2) and (3)
items.text: A police officer may test a driver by breath analysis when needed for traffic safety and to prevent danger, or when there is good reason to believe the person drove while intoxicated, and the driver must comply. A driver who disagrees with the result can be tested again, for example by a blood sample taken with consent.

items.name: Road Traffic Act Article 148-2(1), Item 1 and (2), Item 1
items.text: A person who there is good reason to believe is intoxicated, who drove a motor vehicle and does not comply with the test, is punishable by 1 to 5 years in prison or a fine of KRW 5 million to KRW 20 million. A repeat violation within 10 years from the date a sentence of a fine or heavier became final is punishable by 1 to 6 years in prison or a fine of KRW 5 million to KRW 30 million.

items.name: Act on Special Cases Concerning the Settlement of Traffic Accidents (교통사고처리 특례법) Article 3(2), proviso
items.text: If you cause an accident that injures someone and do not comply with a request for an alcohol test, you can be prosecuted regardless of comprehensive insurance or the victim's wish not to punish you. This does not apply if the driver requested or agreed to a blood test.

sections.title: Refusal requires that your unwillingness was objectively clear
body: The Supreme Court treats a failure to comply as a case where it is objectively clear that the driver had no intention of taking the test. This is judged by looking at your words and attitude at the time, how and why the officer asked for the test, documents such as the report on the detected intoxicated driver (주취운전자 적발보고서), and the reasons and time of the refusal as a whole (Supreme Court Decision 2016도16121, June 8, 2017).

The same decision held that refusing the earlier alcohol screening device test, while knowing that a breathalyzer test was to follow, can also count as test refusal. Do not assume it is fine because it was only a screening device.

sections.title: The order of the breath test and the blood test
body: A blood test is set out as a way to test again when you disagree with the breath test result. If you refuse the breath test itself and only ask for a blood test, there is a risk it will be treated as test refusal.

If lung disease or an injury made it hard for you to blow enough air, you need to explain this with a medical certificate and medical records. Also write down, in time order, how many attempts you made and whether the officer explained how to do it.

sections.title: We check whether you were driving and whether there was good reason
body: The crime of test refusal is limited to cases where you drove a motor vehicle, and there must be good reason to believe you were intoxicated. If you were not driving, or the alcohol was drunk somewhere else long after you finished driving, that premise can be disputed.

If you do not comply with the test, your license is always revoked (Road Traffic Act Article 93(1), Item 3), and you are excluded from reductions for those who drive for a living. The disqualification period is 1 year as a rule, but 2 years if you caused an accident or have two or more drunk driving or test refusal offenses (Article 82(2)).

factors.title: Factors that affect the outcome and sentence
plus: A drunk driving or test refusal record within 10 years
Refusing the test after causing an accident
Fleeing the checkpoint, or verbally abusing or assaulting an officer
Clearly stating a refusal several times
minus: A physical condition that made it hard to blow
Circumstances showing the test method was not explained well enough
A short driving distance and understandable circumstances
Efforts to prevent reoffending, such as selling the car or alcohol treatment

steps.title: How our Criminal Law Center handles your case

items.title: Reconstruct the stop
items.desc: We rebuild, in time order, when the test was requested, how many attempts were made and what the officer told you.

items.title: Check the records
items.desc: We check whether the intoxicated driver report and any footage of the stop exist, and look at how to obtain or review them through an information disclosure request or file inspection.

items.title: Prepare for and attend questioning
items.desc: We rehearse for leading questions about whether you meant to refuse, and attend the questioning with you.

items.title: Legal opinion and sentencing materials
items.desc: We submit a written opinion arguing that no refusal took place, or gather sentencing materials.

checklist.title: Helpful documents to prepare before your consultation
items: Documents you received at the checkpoint
Payment records from where you drank
Medical records showing why it was hard for you to blow
Dashcam footage and passengers' contact details
Any earlier drunk driving judgment or summary order (약식명령)

faqs.q: I blew into the device three times, but no reading came out.
faqs.a: Several attempts alone do not automatically count as refusal. However, if you are found to have deliberately blown weakly, it can be treated as refusal, so you need to explain the situation and your physical condition in detail.

faqs.q: I asked for a blood test. Is that a refusal?
faqs.a: A blood test is a way to test again when you disagree with the breath test result. If you did not take the breath test and insisted on a blood test from the start, it can be treated as test refusal.

faqs.q: Can test refusal end with a fine?
faqs.a: The statutory penalty includes a fine of KRW 5 million to KRW 20 million, so a fine can be imposed. However, if you have an alcohol-related record within 10 years, the statutory penalty goes up and a prison sentence becomes more likely.

areaPages.title: Accidents Involving the 12 Major Violations & Children's Protection Zone Accidents
areaPages.summary: Accidents under the 12 exceptions and accidents involving children in school zones are punishable even with insurance. A criminal settlement or deposit often decides the outcome.
areaPages.cardLaw: Act on Special Cases Concerning the Settlement of Traffic Accidents Article 3, Aggravated Punishment Act Article 5-13
areaPages.lead: Even if you injure someone in a traffic accident, prosecution is usually not allowed if you have comprehensive insurance or the victim does not want you punished. However, if the accident falls under one of the 12 exceptions (12대 중과실), such as running a red light, crossing the center line or hitting someone on a crosswalk, or happens in a children's protection zone (어린이보호구역, school zone), you can be indicted regardless of insurance.

seo.title: 12 Major Traffic Violations and School Zone Accidents in Korea: Penalties | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: In Korea, accidents under the 12 exceptions of the Act on Special Cases Concerning the Settlement of Traffic Accidents and accidents in children's protection zones are subject to criminal punishment even with comprehensive insurance. The 12 items, the serious injury exception, why keeping to the speed limit in a school zone may not be enough, criminal settlements and deposits, and preparing for questioning.

situations.title: When you may need advice
items: I entered an intersection on a yellow light, had an accident, and am told I ran the signal
I hit a pedestrian on a crosswalk
I hit a child in a children's protection zone, but I was within the speed limit
The victim says they need long-term treatment and is asking for a criminal settlement
My insurer handled the accident, but the police say I must be questioned as a suspect

items.name: Act on Special Cases Concerning the Settlement of Traffic Accidents (교통사고처리 특례법) Article 3
items.text: A driver who kills or injures a person in a traffic accident is punishable by imprisonment without labor for up to 5 years or a fine of up to KRW 20 million. For injury accidents, prosecution is not allowed against the victim's express wishes, but this does not apply to the 12 exceptions below, to fleeing, or to refusing an alcohol test.

items.name: Act on Special Cases Concerning the Settlement of Traffic Accidents Article 4
items.text: If you have comprehensive insurance or similar coverage, prosecution is not allowed. The exceptions are the 12 exceptions, cases where the victim's life was put in danger or the victim was left disabled or with an incurable or hard-to-cure illness, and cases where the insurer no longer has to pay.

items.name: Act on the Aggravated Punishment of Specific Crimes (특정범죄 가중처벌 등에 관한 법률) Article 5-13
items.text: Injuring a child under 13 in a children's protection zone by breaching the duty to drive safely is punishable by 1 to 15 years in prison or a fine of KRW 5 million to KRW 30 million. Causing death is punishable by life imprisonment or at least 3 years in prison.

table.title: The 12 exceptions under the Act on Special Cases Concerning the Settlement of Traffic Accidents
rows: Violating a traffic signal or a police officer's signal, or disobeying a no-entry or stop sign
Crossing the center line, or crossing, making a U-turn or reversing on an expressway or similar road
Exceeding the speed limit by more than 20 km/h
Violating rules on how, when or where overtaking is allowed, or illegally cutting in
Violating rules on crossing a railroad crossing
Breaching the duty to protect pedestrians on a crosswalk
Driving without a license (including while suspended)
Driving onto a sidewalk, or violating rules on crossing a sidewalk
Breaching the duty to prevent passengers from falling out
Injuring a child by breaching the duty to drive safely in a children's protection zone
Failing to secure cargo so it does not fall
table.note: Act on Special Cases Concerning the Settlement of Traffic Accidents Article 3(2), proviso, each item. Based on current law on the Korea Law Information Center (the government's official law database) as of October 2026.

sections.title: The first issue is whether the accident falls under the 12 exceptions
body: If the accident does not fall under the 12 exceptions and you have comprehensive insurance, the case should, as a rule, end with no right to prosecute (공소권 없음) even if the victim was injured. So facts such as when the signal changed, how far you were from the stop line and whether the pedestrian was on the crosswalk decide the outcome.

By matching the dashcam timestamps with the intersection's signal cycle and nearby CCTV, it is sometimes possible to dispute whether you ran the signal. Before accepting the violation the police first identified, check the footage frame by frame.

sections.title: School zone accidents can be a problem even if you kept to the speed limit
body: In a children's protection zone, besides following measures such as the 30 km/h speed limit, you have a duty to drive with care for children's safety (Road Traffic Act Article 12(3)). Even if you kept to the speed limit, you can be punished if you are found not to have watched the road ahead or slowed down enough.

On the other hand, if a child suddenly ran out from between parked cars and you could not avoid them, your negligence can be disputed. We also check whether the accident site was actually inside the protection zone and whether the child was under 13.

sections.title: A criminal settlement or deposit often decides the outcome
body: Even for accidents under the exceptions, a settlement with the victim (형사합의) has a large effect on whether you are indicted and on your sentence. First check whether your driver's insurance covers criminal settlement costs, and make sure the settlement agreement includes a statement that the victim does not want you punished.

If the victim demands an excessive amount or cannot be reached, we consider a criminal deposit (형사공탁) with the court. If the victim is seriously injured, the insurance exception does not apply even if the accident is not one of the 12 exceptions.

factors.title: Factors that affect the outcome and sentence
plus: Serious harm, or the victim is a child or an elderly person
Several violations at once (such as speeding and running a red light)
Delay in helping the victim after the accident
A traffic-related prior record
minus: The victim was partly at fault, for example by acting unexpectedly
A settlement with the victim or a criminal deposit
You helped the victim and reported the accident immediately
A long driving history and no prior record

steps.title: How our Criminal Law Center handles your case

items.title: Review the violation
items.desc: Using dashcam footage, the signal cycle and photos of the scene, we first check whether the accident really falls under the 12 exceptions.

items.title: Prepare for and attend questioning
items.desc: We rehearse with the questions the traffic investigation unit asks and attend the questioning with you.

items.title: Submit a legal opinion
items.desc: We set out in a written opinion that the violation is different or that you were not negligent, or the mitigating circumstances.

items.title: Settlement and deposit
items.desc: We check what your driver's insurance covers and look at a criminal settlement or a criminal deposit.

checklist.title: Helpful documents to prepare before your consultation
items: Original dashcam footage
Proof of insurance and the terms of your driver's insurance
The victim's medical certificate
Photos of the accident scene and the location of the signals
The police text asking you to appear

faqs.q: I have comprehensive insurance. Why am I facing criminal punishment?
faqs.a: The insurance exception only applies to accidents that do not fall under the 12 exceptions. If the accident falls under an exception, such as running a red light or hitting someone on a crosswalk, prosecution is allowed regardless of insurance.

faqs.q: A child suddenly ran out in front of me in a school zone.
faqs.a: If you kept to the speed limit and it was a sudden situation you could not avoid, you can dispute that you breached the duty to drive safely. It is important to use dashcam footage to check when the child became visible and when you braked.

faqs.q: The victim's injury is minor. Will I definitely be indicted because it was a school zone?
faqs.a: A children's protection zone accident is not excluded from punishment even if the injury is minor. However, the extent of the harm, any settlement and the degree of fault are reflected in whether you are indicted and in your sentence.

areaPages.summary: You can be punished even for writing true facts, and posting them online is treated more harshly under the Information and Communications Network Act.
areaPages.cardLaw: Criminal Act Article 307, Information and Communications Network Act Article 70
areaPages.title: Defamation & Online Defamation
areaPages.lead: In Korea, even if you wrote exactly what happened, it can be defamation (명예훼손) if you publicly lower someone's social reputation. Where you posted it, how many people read it and why you wrote it decide the outcome.

seo.title: Defamation and Online Defamation Complaints in Korea | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: Defamation by stating true facts and by stating false facts, and online defamation under the Information and Communications Network Act in Korea: statutory penalties, the issues of publicity, identifiability and intent to disparage, the public interest defense, the timing of a statement of no wish to punish and settlements, and how victims can request removal of posts.

situations.title: When you may need advice
items: I posted a review about how a business treated me, and I was sued for defamation
Something I said to a few coworkers spread, and I am told a criminal complaint was filed
I wrote about my ex on an online community and was asked to appear for questioning
False posts about me keep appearing from an anonymous account
Rumors about my child are spreading in a parents' group chat

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 307 (Defamation)
items.text: Publicly stating facts that damage a person's reputation is punishable by up to 2 years in prison or imprisonment without labor, or a fine of up to KRW 5 million. If the facts are false, the penalty is up to 5 years in prison, suspension of qualifications for up to 10 years, or a fine of up to KRW 10 million. Prosecution is not allowed if the victim does not want the offender punished (Article 312(2)).

items.name: Criminal Act Article 310 (Exclusion of Illegality)
items.text: Even defamation by stating facts is not punished if the facts are true and solely in the public interest.

items.name: Information and Communications Network Act (정보통신망법) Article 70 (Penalties)
items.text: Publicly revealing facts through an information and communications network with intent to disparage, and thereby damaging a person's reputation, is punishable by up to 3 years in prison or a fine of up to KRW 30 million. If the facts are false, the penalty is up to 7 years in prison, suspension of qualifications for up to 10 years, or a fine of up to KRW 70 million. Prosecution is not allowed against the victim's expressly stated wishes (paragraph 3).

table.title: Statutory penalties by type of defamation
rows: Up to 2 years in prison or imprisonment without labor, or a fine of up to KRW 5 million
Up to 5 years in prison, suspension of qualifications for up to 10 years, or a fine of up to KRW 10 million
Up to 3 years in prison or imprisonment without labor, or a fine of up to KRW 7 million
Information and Communications Network Act Article 70(1)
Up to 3 years in prison or a fine of up to KRW 30 million
Information and Communications Network Act Article 70(2)

table.note: The KRW 70 million maximum fine in Article 70(2) of the Information and Communications Network Act applies to acts committed after the amendment took effect on January 6, 2026 (Addenda Article 4). Based on current law on the Korea Law Information Center (the government's official law database) as of October 2026.

sections.title: You can be punished even for telling the truth
body: Many people think they are fine because they did not lie. However, Criminal Act Article 307(1) also punishes stating true facts, and the Constitutional Court has upheld this provision as constitutional (Constitutional Court Decision 2017헌마1113 and others, February 25, 2021).

However, if the facts are true and solely in the public interest, there is no punishment (Criminal Act Article 310). For posts related to the public interest, such as a review written to warn other consumers, the defense focuses on this point. Whether you wrote only verifiable facts such as dates, amounts and what was said, and whether you mixed in personal attacks, weigh heavily in the decision.

sections.title: What matters is whether it could spread, not how many people you told
body: Defamation requires publicity (공연성). The Supreme Court maintains that even if you told only one or two people, publicity can be found if those people were likely to pass it on to others (Supreme Court en banc Decision 2020도5813, November 19, 2020).

On the other hand, if you only told family members or someone in a relationship of confidentiality, the possibility of spreading may be denied. You need to set out specifically whom you told, in what setting and in what relationship.

sections.title: For online posts, intent to disparage is the key issue
body: Posts on blogs, online cafés, social media and review boards are often investigated under Article 70 of the Information and Communications Network Act. This provision punishes only where there is intent to disparage, and if the main motive of the post was the public interest, the decision may lean toward finding no such intent.

Even if you did not use a real name, the victim is considered identified if people around them can recognize who it is from the company name, job title, neighborhood or photos combined. Even if you deleted the post, screenshots usually remain, so secure the original text first.

sections.title: A statement of no wish to punish ends the case
body: Defamation under both the Criminal Act and the Information and Communications Network Act is a crime that cannot be prosecuted against the victim's wishes (반의사불벌죄). If the victim states that they do not want punishment, prosecution is not allowed. This can be done until the first-instance judgment is pronounced, and once stated it cannot be withdrawn (Criminal Procedure Act Article 232(3)).

If there is strong ground to dispute the charge, it may be wiser to first argue public interest and identifiability in a written opinion rather than rushing into a settlement. Which way to go is decided after looking at the original post and the surrounding circumstances.

factors.title: Factors that affect the outcome and sentence
plus: Posting facts you knew were false
Posting repeatedly in several places, or continuing after a removal request
Many views, and harm to the victim's job or livelihood
Revealing private life or sexual content
minus: Writing only about what you experienced, within what can be verified
A public interest reason for informing others
Deleting the post yourself right after posting and apologizing
The victim's statement of no wish to punish (처벌불원서)

steps.title: How our Criminal Law Center handles your case

items.title: Consultation with the managing partner
items.desc: Looking at the original post and how it came to be posted, we first decide whether it stated facts or falsehoods and whether public interest can be argued.

items.title: Organize the materials
items.desc: We put the post screen, comments, view counts and messages with the victim in date order and set the direction of your statement.

items.title: Prepare for and attend questioning
items.desc: We rehearse questions such as why you wrote the post and whom you had in mind, and attend the questioning with you.

items.title: Defense counsel's written opinion
items.desc: We submit an opinion arguing there was no publicity, identifiability or intent to disparage, or setting out grounds under Criminal Act Article 310.

items.title: Filing a complaint as a victim
items.desc: If you were harmed, we preserve the posts, draft and file the criminal complaint, and attend your interview as the complainant.

checklist.title: Helpful documents to prepare before your consultation
items: Screenshots of the original post or statement (showing the date and time it was written)
Where it was posted, and roughly how many views and comments it had
Contracts, receipts or chat records showing why you wrote it
The text asking you to appear, or a copy of the criminal complaint
Records of your communications with the other party

faqs.q: Is it defamation if I only used initials instead of a name?
faqs.a: Even if you only used initials or a nickname, the victim is considered identified if people around them can recognize who it is when combined with the rest of the post. On the other hand, if no one can tell who it is, defamation is hard to establish.

faqs.q: I heard the deadline for a complaint is 6 months. Is it over after that?
faqs.a: The 6-month complaint period applies only to crimes that can be prosecuted only upon complaint (친고죄). Defamation is not one of them; it is a crime that cannot be prosecuted against the victim's wishes, so a complaint can be filed even after 6 months, and an investigation proceeds as long as the statute of limitations has not run out.

faqs.q: I want false posts about me taken down first.
faqs.a: Under Article 44-2 of the Information and Communications Network Act, you can explain the infringement to the operator of the board and request removal or a temporary measure (임시조치), which lasts up to 30 days. Before requesting removal, capture the original text, its URL and the date and time it was written, so you have evidence for a complaint.

areaPages.summary: Insult can only be punished if a complaint is filed, so whether the complaint is withdrawn and when you settle have a large effect on the outcome.
areaPages.title: Insult (Group Chats, Games, Comments)
areaPages.lead: Many people in Korea face criminal complaints for swearing in group chats, in-game chat or online comments. Insult (모욕죄) requires publicity and identifiability, and because it can only be prosecuted upon complaint (친고죄), the case ends if the complaint is withdrawn.

seo.title: Insult Complaints in Korea: Group Chats, Online Games and Comments | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: For anyone in Korea facing, or planning to file, an insult complaint over a group chat message, in-game swearing or an online comment. The statutory penalty under Criminal Act Article 311, the complaint deadline for crimes prosecuted only upon complaint, how publicity and identifiability are judged, cases where only a nickname is shown, demands for settlement money, and the effect of withdrawing a complaint.

situations.title: When you may need advice
items: I swore during an argument in a group chat and was asked to appear for questioning for insult
I swore at someone in an in-game chat, and they gave their name and number and said they would file a complaint
I was told I had been sued over a comment on a news article
The other person is demanding several million won as settlement money
I keep being sworn at online and want to file a complaint

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 311 (Insult)
items.text: Publicly insulting a person is punishable by up to 1 year in prison or imprisonment without labor, or a fine of up to KRW 2 million.

items.name: Criminal Act Article 312(1) (Complaint and the Victim's Wishes)
items.text: Insult is a crime that can only be prosecuted if a complaint is filed.

items.name: Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 230(1) (Complaint Period)
items.text: For crimes prosecuted only upon complaint, a complaint cannot be filed once 6 months have passed from the day the victim learned who the offender was.

sections.title: In group chats, publicity depends on the number of members and their relationships
body: Like defamation, insult is only established when it is done where an unspecified or large number of people can learn of it. Group chats with several members are often found to meet this publicity requirement.

By contrast, swearing in a one-on-one chat with only the other person lacks publicity, so it is unlikely to be insult. For a small room of about three people, you need to consider the members' relationships and how likely the conversation was to spread outside.

sections.title: Where only nicknames are visible, identifiability can be disputed
body: If you swore at someone in a game or anonymous community based only on their username, it may be found that the victim was not identified if the people around them could not tell who that username belongs to in real life.

Recently there have also been reported cases where someone deliberately provokes swearing, then types their name and phone number in the chat and demands settlement money under threat of a complaint. Typing personal details in the chat does not automatically establish identifiability, so capture the entire chat flow.

sections.title: Swearing is different from rude criticism
body: An insult is an expression of contempt for a person without stating facts. There have been decisions holding that somewhat harsh or rude words were not an insult if they were not enough to lower the other person's social reputation.
The context matters as much as the words used. You need to show whether the other person provoked you first, whether it was a one-time remark, and what else was said in the same chat.

sections.title: If the complaint is withdrawn, the case ends
body: Because insult is a crime prosecuted only upon complaint, there can be no punishment if the complainant withdraws the complaint before the first-instance judgment is pronounced. A person who withdraws cannot file another complaint about the same case (Criminal Procedure Act Article 232).

There is no set standard for settlement amounts. The safer order is to first check whether the charge can be established, and to negotiate the amount only when it is likely to be. Be sure the settlement agreement includes a clause that the complaint will be withdrawn.

factors.title: Factors that affect the outcome and sentence
plus: Repeating it several times, or several people swearing together
Expressions targeting family, appearance or disability
Continuing with a different account after the victim blocked you
A similar prior conviction
minus: The other person provoked you or swore first
A one-time remark followed by an immediate apology
It was a space where only nicknames were visible
Withdrawal of the complaint or a settlement

steps.title: How our Criminal Law Center handles your case

items.title: Check whether the crime is established
items.desc: Looking at the number of chat members, how far nicknames were linked to real identities and when the complaint was filed, we check for issues of publicity, identifiability and the complaint deadline.

items.title: Secure the whole conversation
items.desc: We guide you to back up the entire conversation before and after, not just the one line at issue.

items.title: Attend questioning
items.desc: Before questioning, we rehearse the expected questions, then attend with you and raise objections to leading questions.

items.title: Written opinion or settlement
items.desc: If the case should be contested, we argue in a written opinion that there is no crime. If you admit it, we decide together when and how to settle, and Jisan Law handles settlement contact with the other party on your behalf.

checklist.title: Helpful documents to prepare before your consultation
items: Screenshots or an exported file of the entire chat
The number of chat members and how they know each other
Game IDs, chat logs and any reports made in the game
Messages from the other person threatening a complaint or demanding settlement money
The text asking you to appear

faqs.q: I swore in a game, and the other player gave me their name and number.
faqs.a: Typing a name and number in the chat does not automatically establish identifiability. The question is whether other users there could recognize that username as that real person. Before sending money out of fear, first check whether the crime is actually established.

faqs.q: Is online insult punished more heavily?
faqs.a: The Information and Communications Network Act has penalty provisions for defamation, but none that punish insult more heavily. Swearing online is also punished under Criminal Act Article 311, with the same statutory penalty.

faqs.q: Does a record remain if the complaint is withdrawn?
faqs.a: If the complaint is withdrawn, the case ends with a decision not to refer it to prosecutors (불송치) for lack of a right to prosecute at the police stage, or with dismissal of the prosecution (공소기각) after indictment, so no criminal record remains. However, a record that you were investigated stays in the investigative agencies' internal files.

areaPages.summary: If you take customer or employee data you learned through work or use it for other purposes, you can be punished personally, not just your company.
areaPages.cardLaw: Personal Information Protection Act Articles 59 and 71
areaPages.title: Personal Data Leaks & Misuse
areaPages.lead: Looking up a customer's details on your company's system and passing them to an acquaintance, or using contact details you received for work for personal purposes, violates the Personal Information Protection Act (개인정보 보호법). Sharing private conversations that have nothing to do with work is often covered by other laws.

seo.title: Personal Data Leaks and Misuse: Criminal Penalties in Korea | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: If you disclosed personal data learned through work, or looked it up or used it without authorization in Korea: the scope of punishment and who can be punished under Articles 59, 71 and 72 of the Personal Information Protection Act, the corporate joint liability provision, how this differs from sharing private screenshots, and how to prepare before questioning.
keywords: Personal Information Protection Act violation Korea

situations.title: When you may need advice
items: An audit found that I used the company system to look up an acquaintance's address for someone
I was sued for taking a file of customer contacts with me when I left the company
I think a hospital or government office employee gave my information to someone else
I posted residents' information I received while managing an apartment complex in a group chat
I am being investigated over a personal data leak at the company level

items.name: Personal Information Protection Act (개인정보 보호법) Article 59 (Prohibited Acts)
items.text: A person who handles or has handled personal information must not obtain personal information by improper means, disclose personal information learned through work, or use or leak another person's personal information without authorization.

items.name: Personal Information Protection Act Article 71 (Penalties)
items.text: A person who discloses personal information learned through work, provides it for others to use without authorization, or uses or leaks another person's personal information without authorization is punishable by up to 5 years in prison or a fine of up to KRW 50 million (Items 9 and 10).

items.name: Personal Information Protection Act Article 72 (Penalties)
items.text: A person who obtains personal information by deception or other improper means is punishable by up to 3 years in prison or a fine of up to KRW 30 million (Item 2).

sections.title: Individual employees can also be punished
body: Many duties under the Personal Information Protection Act are placed on personal information controllers, meaning institutions and companies that operate personal data files for business purposes. However, Article 59 applies to anyone who handles or has handled personal information.

The Supreme Court has also held that this provision is not limited to personal information controllers but includes anyone who has handled personal information learned through work (Supreme Court Decision 2015도8766, March 10, 2016). So even when a customer service agent or staff member takes information for personal reasons, they can be punished directly.

sections.title: What matters is whether you only looked it up, and to whom you passed it
body: Using or leaking another person's personal information without authorization carries up to 5 years in prison or a fine of up to KRW 50 million. In practice, investigators check one by one how many lookups appear in the access logs, who received the information and whether you were paid for it.

Whether you looked it up because your work required it or out of personal curiosity is also disputed. Matching the access records with the duties you had at the time can sometimes explain part of what happened.

sections.title: Sharing private screenshots raises other laws
body: The general view is that the Personal Information Protection Act is hard to apply to sharing unrelated to work, such as posting a contact number or conversation you received from a friend in a group chat. In such cases, whether it amounts to defamation or a breach of secrets under Article 49 of the Information and Communications Network Act (정보통신망법) is examined separately.

On the other hand, information received while performing a role, such as a club organizer or a building management office, is more likely to be treated as information learned through work. You first need to clarify in what capacity you received the information.

factors.title: Factors that affect the outcome and sentence
plus: Passing on information in exchange for payment
Many lookups or leaks over a long period
Secondary harm from the leaked information, such as stalking or fraud
Unique identifiers such as resident registration numbers, or health information, were included
minus: The lookup was related to your work
Only a narrow scope was passed on, and it was promptly retrieved or deleted
You apologized to the victim and made up for the harm
You have already been disciplined through the company's internal process

steps.title: How our Criminal Law Center handles your case

items.title: Establish the facts
items.desc: Based on the access records, your duties at the time and your relationship with the person who received the information, we determine which provisions are at issue.

items.title: Digital forensics response
items.desc: If your phone or work computer was seized, we apply to take part in the forensic examination so that data unrelated to the case is not handed over with it.

items.title: Attend questioning
items.desc: We attend questioning that goes through the access records one by one, and raise objections so the facts are not recorded inaccurately.

items.title: Submit a legal opinion
items.desc: At the decision stage, we submit an opinion setting out the connection to your work, the scope of the leak and your efforts to make up for the harm.

checklist.title: Helpful documents to prepare before your consultation
items: Audit results or a disciplinary notice from your company
Documents showing your duties and access rights at the time
Messages with the person who received the information
The summons to appear or a copy of the criminal complaint
The company's personal data handling guidelines or any pledge you signed

faqs.q: Will the company also be punished?
faqs.a: If an employee commits a crime under Articles 71 to 73 in connection with the company's business, the company can also be fined under the same provision (Article 74(2)). The company can avoid this if it exercised due care and supervision to prevent the violation.

faqs.q: Can I be punished for giving out an address just once because an acquaintance asked?
faqs.a: Passing information learned through work to someone else without authorization can fall under Article 71 even if it happened only once. However, the outcome varies greatly depending on the number of cases, the circumstances and whether secondary harm occurred.

faqs.q: Is it a problem if I take client contacts with me when I leave the company?
faqs.a: Taking the contact details of client staff you received for work without the company's permission and using them for other purposes can raise issues under the Personal Information Protection Act, and people are sometimes also sued for trade secret infringement or breach of trust in the course of business (업무상배임). You first need to check what kind of data you took.

areaPages.summary: Recording a conversation you take part in is allowed, but secretly recording a conversation between others carries only prison sentences, with no fine option.
areaPages.cardLaw: Communications Privacy Protection Act Articles 3 and 16
areaPages.title: Illegal Recording & Wiretapping
areaPages.lead: In Korea, whether a recording is illegal depends on whether the person who recorded it was a party to the conversation. Leaving a recorder running while you are out of the room, or hiding a recorder in your spouse's car, can lead to heavy punishment.

seo.title: Illegal Recording and Violations of the Communications Privacy Protection Act in Korea | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: When secret recording in Korea violates the Communications Privacy Protection Act. The difference between recording a conversation you are part of and recording others' conversations, the statutory penalty of 1 to 10 years in prison, disclosing or leaking recorded content, and the ban on using illegal recordings as evidence.

situations.title: When you may need advice
items: I suspected my spouse of having an affair, hid a recorder in the car, and was sued
I left the meeting room with my phone still recording
I put a recorder in my child's bag and recorded what was said in the classroom
I played a recording of my call with my boss to coworkers. Could that be a problem?
I think someone secretly recorded my conversation and spread it

items.name: Communications Privacy Protection Act (통신비밀보호법) Articles 3(1) and 14(1)
items.text: No one may intercept telecommunications or record or listen in on a private conversation between others except as provided by law, nor listen in using electronic devices or mechanical means.

items.name: Communications Privacy Protection Act Article 16(1) (Penalties)
items.text: A person who, in violation of Article 3, intercepts communications or records or listens in on a private conversation between others, or who discloses or leaks what they learned in that way, is punishable by 1 to 10 years in prison and suspension of qualifications for up to 5 years.

items.name: Communications Privacy Protection Act Articles 4 and 14(2)
items.text: Content obtained through illegal interception, or an illegal recording of a private conversation between others, cannot be used as evidence in a trial or disciplinary proceeding.

sections.title: The test is whether you were part of the conversation
body: What the Communications Privacy Protection Act prohibits is recording a conversation between other people. The Supreme Court has held that when three people are talking and one of them records it, that is not recording a conversation between others (Supreme Court Decision 2006도4981, October 12, 2006).

So recording a phone call you are on, or a meeting you take part in, does not violate this law. On the other hand, if the recording continued after you left, the part after that becomes a conversation between others.

sections.title: This crime has no fine option
body: Illegal recording and wiretapping carry 1 to 10 years in prison together with suspension of qualifications for up to 5 years, and there is no fine. If you are indicted, the argument is over a suspended sentence (집행유예) or suspended sentencing (선고유예) within the range of prison sentences.

The fact that you only recorded without listening, or deleted it right away, may be taken into account, but it does not erase the crime. Playing the recording to others or spreading it can be punished separately as disclosure or leaking.

sections.title: Illegal recordings are also hard to use as evidence
body: Even if you recorded to expose an affair or abuse, a secret recording of a conversation between others cannot be used as evidence in a trial or disciplinary proceeding. Trying to get evidence can end with you becoming the suspect instead.
If you need evidence, first consider lawful methods, such as recording a conversation you take part in yourself, or a court-ordered fact inquiry during a lawsuit.

factors.title: Factors that affect the outcome and sentence
plus: Hiding a device and recording over a long period
Spreading the recorded content to several people
Using the recording for threats or to demand settlement money
Buying a recording app or device in advance and installing it as planned
minus: You took part in only part of the conversation, or it is unclear whether you were a party
You did not disclose the recording and deleted it right away
You recorded in an urgent situation such as domestic violence
You settled with the victim and received a statement that they do not want you punished

steps.title: How our Criminal Law Center handles your case

items.title: Check how the recording was made
items.desc: Using the files, we check when the recording started and stopped and whether you were in the conversation during that time.

items.title: Take part in digital forensics
items.desc: If your phone or recorder is seized, we apply to take part in the forensic examination so that unrelated files are not handled along with it.

items.title: Attend questioning
items.desc: We attend questioning about why you recorded and whether you disclosed it, and help you separate the parts where you were a party from those where you were not.

items.title: Legal opinion and sentencing materials
items.desc: Because there is no fine option, we submit a written opinion with materials on the circumstances, compensation for the harm and your remorse.

checklist.title: Helpful documents to prepare before your consultation
items: A list of the recording files and when they were recorded
When the recording device or app was installed
Whom you sent the recordings to or played them for
The summons to appear or a copy of the criminal complaint
Materials showing why you came to record

faqs.q: Can I record a phone call without the other person knowing?
faqs.a: If you are a party to the call, recording it without the other person knowing does not violate the Communications Privacy Protection Act. However, spreading the recording to several people can raise other issues, such as defamation, depending on the content.

faqs.q: The home camera I installed also recorded sound.
faqs.a: If the recording function captured conversations between people other than your family, it can be an issue of recording conversations between others. The decision depends on why you installed it, how the recording function came to be on and who was recorded, so get advice before deleting any files.

faqs.q: Can I submit a secretly recorded file in my divorce case?
faqs.a: If it is a recording of a conversation you took part in, you can submit it as evidence. If it is a secret recording of a conversation between others, the law prohibits its use as evidence at trial, and submitting it can itself turn into a criminal matter.

areaPages.summary: Even if you knew the password, logging into someone else's account without permission can be punished as unauthorized intrusion into an information network.
areaPages.cardLaw: Information and Communications Network Act Articles 48 and 71
areaPages.title: Hacking & Account Takeover
areaPages.lead: Logging into a partner's social media with a password they once gave you, or logging into a company account after leaving the job, can be unauthorized intrusion into an information and communications network (정보통신망 침입). What you looked at and what you changed after logging in can add further charges.

seo.title: Hacking and Account Takeover Under the Information and Communications Network Act in Korea | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: If you secretly logged into someone else's account or read their messages in Korea: statutory penalties for network intrusion, infringement and leaking of secrets, breach of secrecy under the Criminal Act and computer fraud, logging into accounts between spouses or partners, accessing accounts after leaving a company, and how to respond to questioning.
keywords: Information and Communications Network Act Korea

situations.title: When you may need advice
items: I logged into my ex's Instagram with an old password
I unlocked my spouse's phone and took screenshots of their KakaoTalk messages, and I was sued
I downloaded files from my company's cloud account even after I left
I am accused of logging into someone else's game account and moving items
My account was hijacked and messages asking for money were sent to my contacts

items.name: Information and Communications Network Act (정보통신망법) Article 48(1) and Article 71(1), Item 11
items.text: Intruding into an information and communications network without legitimate access rights, or beyond the access rights granted, is punishable by up to 5 years in prison or a fine of up to KRW 50 million. Attempts are also punished (Article 71(2)).

items.name: Information and Communications Network Act Article 49 and Article 71(1), Item 14
items.text: Damaging another person's information processed, stored or transmitted through an information and communications network, or infringing, misusing or leaking another person's secrets, is punishable by up to 5 years in prison or a fine of up to KRW 50 million.

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 347-2 (Fraud by Use of Computers, etc.)
items.text: Obtaining a financial benefit by entering or changing information without authorization is punishable by up to 20 years in prison or a fine of up to KRW 50 million (as amended on December 23, 2025).

sections.title: Knowing the password does not give you permission
body: Network intrusion is judged by whether you had access rights. Even if your partner once gave you their password, it is hard to say you had legitimate rights if you logged in without permission after you broke up.

The same goes for company accounts. Logging in with an ID that still worked after your rights ended when you left the company, or going beyond the scope of your duties even while still employed, exceeds the access rights you were given.

sections.title: What you did after logging in can add charges
body: If you logged in and read and captured conversations, infringement of another person's secrets (Information and Communications Network Act Article 49) becomes an issue, and sending those screenshots to others raises leaking. If you unlocked a phone and looked at its records, breach of secrecy under Criminal Act Article 316(2) is also considered.

If you made payments with the account or moved items or points, it becomes computer fraud and the statutory penalty becomes much heavier. Investigators identify the number and timing of logins from IP addresses and log records, so avoid relying on memory and understating the number of times.

sections.title: There is no exception for family members or partners
body: A typical case is opening a spouse's phone to look for evidence of an affair. Being married does not exempt you from punishment, and a complaint is sometimes filed after the screenshots obtained this way are submitted in a lawsuit.

If you are the victim whose account was hijacked, first save the login records and password change alerts, report it to the platform, and then prepare a complaint. Jisan Law organizes these records, drafts the criminal complaint and attends your interview as the complainant.

factors.title: Factors that affect the outcome and sentence
plus: Logging in many times over a long period
Spreading what you read to others
Obtaining a financial benefit, such as making payments or transfers
Using malware or phishing to obtain the password
minus: Logging in once or twice with a password you were given in the past
Not saving or spreading what you saw
Settling with the victim and making up for the harm
No prior record

steps.title: How our Criminal Law Center handles your case

items.title: Clarify how you logged in
items.desc: In the consultation, we set out how you came to know the password, when and how many times you logged in, and what you saw.

items.title: Search, seizure and forensics response
items.desc: We attend the search and seizure of your phone or computer and apply to take part in the forensic examination so that data outside the warrant's scope is not used.

items.title: Attend questioning
items.desc: We attend questioning in which investigators present the log records, and object on the spot if the facts are being recorded inaccurately.

items.title: Legal opinion and compensation
items.desc: We set out in a written opinion any dispute over access rights, the circumstances and your efforts to make up for the harm.

checklist.title: Helpful documents to prepare before your consultation
items: Messages showing how the password was shared with you
The accounts you logged into and roughly when
A list of materials you captured or downloaded
The summons to appear and the list of seized items
If you left a company, your departure date and how your account was returned

faqs.q: I only logged in and did not look at anything.
faqs.a: Network intrusion can be established by logging in itself, and attempts are also punished. However, the fact that nothing was viewed or leaked is reflected in the outcome and sentence, so the login times and activity records should be checked together.

faqs.q: My husband's KakaoTalk was logged in on a tablet we share.
faqs.a: Even on a device that was left logged in, opening and capturing conversations can raise an issue of infringing secrets. How you came to share the device and whether viewing was normally allowed affect the decision.

faqs.q: My account was hijacked. Where do I report it?
faqs.a: First change your password and report the hijacking to the platform, then you can file a criminal complaint with the police or make a cybercrime report. Capturing login alerts, unusual payment records and the messages your contacts received will help the investigation.

areaPages.summary: Causing a scene at a shop, posting false reviews and filing repeated complaints can all be obstruction of business, and a settlement with the victim does not end the case automatically.
areaPages.title: Obstruction of Business
areaPages.lead: Obstruction of business (업무방해) is committed when someone interferes with another person's business by spreading false facts, by deception or by force. It can be a problem even without actual loss if there was a risk of interference, so the first step is to examine which method was involved.

seo.title: Obstruction of Business in Korea: Penalties and Complaints | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: For anyone in Korea facing, or planning to file, an obstruction of business complaint over a scene at a shop, a workplace dispute, false reviews and star ratings, or repeated complaints.
