The requirements of spreading false facts, deception and force under Criminal Act Article 314 and the statutory penalty, the difference from the minor offense of obstruction, and the effect of a settlement.

situations.title: When you may need advice
items: I raised my voice and pushed furniture at a bar, and I was reported for obstruction of business
I left a bad review on a delivery app, and the owner says they will sue me for obstruction of business
I protested in front of the office during a dispute with my company, and I was sued
A customer caused a scene in my shop for hours and I could not do business
A competitor spread false rumors and I lost my clients

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 314 (Obstruction of Business)
items.text: Interfering with a person's business by spreading false facts, by deception or by force is punishable by up to 5 years in prison or a fine of up to KRW 15 million. The same applies to interfering with business by entering false information or improper commands into a computer or other information processing device (paragraph 2).

items.name: Criminal Act Article 313 (Damage to Credit)
items.text: Damaging a person's credit by spreading false facts or by deception is punishable by up to 5 years in prison or a fine of up to KRW 15 million.

items.name: Minor Offenses Act (경범죄 처벌법) Article 3(2), Item 3 (Obstruction of Business)
items.text: Interfering with the business of another person, an organization or a public official on duty through mischief or similar conduct is punishable by a fine of up to KRW 200,000, short-term detention or a petty fine.

sections.title: We first look at which of the three methods is at issue
body: Force means power sufficient to suppress a person's free will, and conduct such as shouting and swearing, breaking furniture or blocking the entrance can fall under it. Deception means misleading the other party or taking advantage of a mistake, and spreading false facts means circulating false information.

The points to dispute differ depending on the method. You need to break it down specifically: whether an argument or protest went far enough to be considered force, and whether the content of a review was false.

The protected business only needs to be work you carry on as part of your job or social life, and it can qualify even without formalities such as a business license. On the other hand, interfering with a public official's duties is judged separately as obstruction of the performance of official duties, not obstruction of business.

sections.title: For reviews and star ratings, whether the content is true is the dividing line
body: A review describing what you actually experienced as a customer is unlikely to be obstruction of business even if the wording is harsh. The problem cases are reviews written without using the service, content that differs from the facts, and star-rating campaigns using multiple accounts.
Even if you wrote the truth, excessive wording can separately raise defamation or insult. Do not delete your order history, photos or conversations with the owner; keep them.

sections.title: You can be punished even after a settlement
body: Obstruction of business is not a crime that cannot be prosecuted against the victim's wishes, so the case does not end automatically even if the victim does not want punishment. However, compensation and a statement of no wish to punish weigh heavily when deciding on a suspension of indictment (기소유예) or the level of a fine.
If the scene happened while drinking, obstruction of business is often combined with property damage and assault. We respond to each charge separately, based on the facts it rests on.

factors.title: Factors that affect the outcome and sentence
plus: Repeatedly stopping the business for a long time
Breaking furniture or assaulting staff as well
Posting false reviews in an organized way with multiple accounts
Ignoring warnings or requests to leave
minus: A brief, unplanned disturbance
A review based on your actual experience
Compensation for the harm and a statement of no wish to punish
No prior record

steps.title: How our Criminal Law Center handles your case

items.title: Consultation with the managing partner
items.desc: We confirm which acts are alleged to be force or deception, and separate what to dispute from what to admit.

items.title: Secure footage and records
items.desc: We guide you to secure materials that disappear easily first, such as shop CCTV, the original review and order history.

items.title: Prepare for and attend questioning
items.desc: We put your actions at the time in time order, rehearse with you, and attend the questioning with you.

items.title: Legal opinion and compensation
items.desc: We set out in a written opinion that your conduct did not amount to obstruction of business, or the progress of compensation for the harm.

checklist.title: Helpful documents to prepare before your consultation
items: Video or photos from the scene
The original review or post and when it was written
Order and payment records
Communications with the business owner or company
The text asking you to appear

faqs.q: Is it obstruction of business even if the shop's sales did not fall?
faqs.a: Court precedent holds that obstruction of business can be established if a risk of interfering with the business arose, even without an actual drop in sales. However, the fact that the interference was minor is reflected in the outcome.

faqs.q: Is filing several complaints with the district office obstruction of business?
faqs.a: Filing a legitimate complaint is not obstruction of business. However, repeating the same complaint excessively, or mixing in false facts to the point of paralyzing the other party's work, can be a problem, so both the content and the number of complaints are examined.

faqs.q: How is the minor offense of obstruction different from obstruction of business under the Criminal Act?
faqs.a: Interfering with business at the level of mischief is handled under the Minor Offenses Act, with a fine of up to KRW 200,000 or similar. Using false facts, deception or force falls under Criminal Act Article 314, with up to 5 years in prison. Which law applies makes a big difference to the outcome.

areaPages.summary: Even pushing a police officer once can be obstruction of official duties, and the case continues even if the officer forgives you.
areaPages.title: Obstruction of Official Duties
areaPages.lead: In Korea, people who push or threaten police officers or paramedics on a call, often while swearing, are frequently arrested on the spot (현행범 체포) for obstruction of the performance of official duties (공무집행방해). The points to dispute are whether the officer was performing their duties lawfully and whether your act was serious enough to count as assault.

seo.title: Obstruction of Official Duties in Korea: Penalties and First Offenses | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: For anyone in Korea booked for obstruction of official duties after pushing or threatening a police officer, paramedic or other public official. The statutory penalty under Criminal Act Article 136 and special obstruction, the requirement of lawful performance of duties, the difference from drunken disturbance at a public office, the process after arrest in the act, and factors that affect the outcome.
keywords: special obstruction of official duties Korea

situations.title: When you may need advice
items: I was drunk, pushed a police officer who came to the scene, and was arrested on the spot
Obstruction of official duties was added because I shook off an officer's hand at a DUI checkpoint
I swore at a paramedic and pulled their arm
I was booked for shouting at a police substation, and I do not know if it is obstruction of official duties or drunken disturbance
The police restrained me excessively first, and it feels unfair that only I am being punished

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 136 (Obstruction of the Performance of Official Duties)
items.text: Assaulting or threatening a public official who is performing their duties is punishable by up to 5 years in prison or a fine of up to KRW 10 million.

items.name: Criminal Act Article 144 (Special Obstruction of Official Duties)
items.text: Obstructing official duties by showing the force of a group or many people, or while carrying a dangerous object, increases the penalty by up to one half. If a public official is injured, the penalty is at least 3 years in prison.

items.name: Minor Offenses Act (경범죄 처벌법) Article 3(3), Item 1 (Drunken Disturbance at a Public Office)
items.text: Behaving drunkenly with very rough words and actions or making a noise at a public office while intoxicated is punishable by a fine of up to KRW 600,000, short-term detention or a petty fine.

sections.title: The crime requires lawful performance of duties
body: Obstruction of official duties is only established when the official was performing their duties lawfully. If you resisted unlawful conduct, such as an arrest that did not meet the legal requirements or being dragged away without being told the reasons, the crime may not apply.
So what the officer was doing and saying at the time matters. You can only dispute this after checking the body camera footage, dispatch records and CCTV at the scene.

sections.title: Even a single push can be assault
body: Assault here is understood broadly as any use of physical force directed at the official. Pushing someone's chest or grabbing their collar, and in some cases shaking off their hand, can be an issue.

On the other hand, it must be distinguished whether it was a passive movement to free an arm that was being held, or a bump while falling. Matching each movement against the footage can change the outcome.

sections.title: The officer's wish not to punish is a mitigating factor
body: Obstruction of official duties is not a crime that cannot be prosecuted against the victim's wishes, so the case does not end even if the officer does not want you punished. However, an apology, the officer's statement of no wish to punish and compensation for any harm are taken into account in your favor when the outcome and sentence are decided.
Saying you cannot remember because you were drunk does not help. It earns more credibility to separate what you remember from what you do not, and to admit actions that can be confirmed on video.

factors.title: Factors that affect the outcome and sentence
plus: Hitting or kicking several times
The officer was injured
Holding a dangerous object or acting together with several people
A similar prior conviction, or committing the offense during a suspended sentence
minus: Only light physical force, such as a push or shaking off a hand
The officer was not injured
A sincere apology and the officer's wish not to punish
No prior record, and efforts to prevent recurrence such as alcohol treatment

steps.title: How our Criminal Law Center handles your case

items.title: Visit right after arrest
items.desc: If you were arrested on the spot, we visit you to hear what happened and decide the direction of your statement before questioning.

items.title: Pre-detention hearing
items.desc: If a detention warrant (구속영장) is requested, we attend the pre-detention hearing (영장실질심사) and explain your residence, family ties and why there is no risk of reoffending.

items.title: Check footage and attend questioning
items.desc: We check the body camera and scene footage, attend questioning with you, and raise points on the lawfulness of the officer's conduct and the degree of force.

items.title: Legal opinion and sentencing materials
items.desc: We gather materials that count toward the outcome, such as a letter of apology, a statement of no wish to punish and alcohol treatment records, and submit them with a written legal opinion.

checklist.title: Helpful documents to prepare before your consultation
items: The place and time of the incident, and who was with you
CCTV from the scene or phone videos
Documents you received at the time of arrest (such as the arrest notice)
If you were injured, a medical certificate and photos
Documents on your family relationships and job

faqs.q: If I am arrested in the act, how long can I be held?
faqs.a: If a detention warrant is not requested within 48 hours of the arrest, you must be released immediately (Criminal Procedure Act Article 213-2 and Article 200-2(5)). In obstruction of official duties cases, people are often released after questioning, but a warrant may be requested depending on the degree of violence and any prior record.

faqs.q: How is drunken disturbance different from obstruction of official duties?
faqs.a: If you only shouted while drunk at a public office, it is drunken disturbance under the Minor Offenses Act, with a fine of up to KRW 600,000 or similar. If you assaulted or threatened a public official, it becomes obstruction of official duties under the Criminal Act, and the punishment is much heavier.

faqs.q: The police officer restrained me excessively first.
faqs.a: If the officer's conduct was unlawful, obstruction of official duties may not be established, and you can separately raise the issue of excessive force. However, claims without footage are hard to get accepted, so securing the footage comes first.

areaPages.summary: A sworn witness who testifies against their own memory commits perjury, and if the aim is to harm someone, it becomes malicious perjury, which has no fine option.
areaPages.title: Perjury & Malicious Perjury
areaPages.lead: Perjury (위증죄) is committed when a witness who has taken an oath under the law makes a false statement. It is not enough that the testimony differs from the objective facts; the key is whether the witness said something contrary to their own memory.

seo.title: Perjury and Malicious Perjury in Korea: Complaints and Defense | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: For anyone in Korea accused of perjury after testifying in court, or wanting to file a complaint over a witness's false testimony. Statutory penalties for perjury and malicious perjury under Criminal Act Article 152, what testimony contrary to memory means, the difference between an honest mistake and perjury, reduced penalties for confessing or surrendering before the judgment becomes final, and inducing perjury.

situations.title: When you may need advice
items: I testified in a civil trial, and the other side filed a perjury complaint against me
An acquaintance asked me to say something untrue in court, and now I want to correct it
A witness for the other side lied in my criminal trial
I am accused of inducing perjury by asking someone to lie

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 152 (Perjury, Malicious Perjury)
items.text: A witness who has taken an oath under the law and makes a false statement is punishable by up to 5 years in prison or a fine of up to KRW 10 million. If the aim is to harm a defendant, suspect or person facing discipline in a criminal or disciplinary case, the penalty is up to 10 years in prison.

items.name: Criminal Act Article 153 (Confession, Voluntary Surrender)
items.text: If a person who committed perjury confesses or surrenders before the judgment or disciplinary decision in the case in which they testified becomes final, the penalty is reduced or waived.

sections.title: Only a sworn witness can commit perjury
body: Perjury applies only to a witness who took an oath and testified in court. Making a false statement as a witness during a police investigation, or a defendant lying in court in their own trial, is not perjury.

Witnesses in civil trials also take an oath, so they can commit perjury. Malicious perjury (모해위증) applies only in criminal and disciplinary cases where the aim is to harm the other party, and it has no fine option.

Before you go to court as a witness, it is a good idea to go back over messages or schedules from the time and organize your memory. For anything you are not sure about, do not state it as certain; saying "I do not remember exactly" reduces the risk of a perjury dispute.

sections.title: The test is whether you said something different from your memory
body: Court precedent consistently holds that a false statement in perjury means saying something different from what the witness experienced and remembers. Even if testimony does not match the objective facts, it is not perjury if the witness remembered it that way and said so.

Typical disputes include getting a date or amount wrong because the events were long ago, or answering a question after understanding it differently. So we start by obtaining the full witness examination record (증인신문조서) and comparing each question and answer line by line.

sections.title: Correcting it before the judgment becomes final reduces or waives the penalty
body: If you actually gave false testimony, confessing or surrendering before the judgment in the case in which you testified becomes final reduces or waives the penalty (Criminal Act Article 153). If you intend to correct it, timing matters above all.

A person who asked for false testimony can be punished for inducing perjury with the same penalty as the witness (Criminal Act Article 31(1)). The witness who was asked and the person who asked are often investigated together, so care is needed to keep statements from conflicting.

factors.title: Factors that affect the outcome and sentence
plus: The perjury changed the outcome of the trial or created a serious risk of doing so
Receiving something in return, or coordinating stories in advance
An aim to harm is found
Denying it to the end and hiding other evidence
minus: Circumstances suggesting a memory error or a misunderstood question
Correcting it yourself before the judgment became final
The testimony did not affect the outcome of the trial
No prior record

steps.title: How our Criminal Law Center handles your case

items.title: Check the witness examination record
items.desc: We check every question and answer in the testimony at issue and compare them with messages and documents from that time.

items.title: Decide the direction
items.desc: In the consultation, we decide whether the testimony reflected your memory or needs to be corrected.

items.title: Attend questioning
items.desc: We attend questioning on the perjury charge and help you calmly explain the basis for your memory.

items.title: Filing a complaint for you
items.desc: If you are filing a complaint over a witness's perjury, we organize the record and contrary evidence and draft the criminal complaint.

checklist.title: Helpful documents to prepare before your consultation
items: The witness examination record or a transcript of the testimony
The judgment or the status of the case in which you testified
Messages and documents from the time related to the testimony
The summons to appear or a copy of the criminal complaint

faqs.q: If the other side's witness is punished for perjury, will the judgment be overturned?
faqs.a: If testimony used as evidence for the original judgment is proven false by a final judgment, it can be grounds for a retrial (Criminal Procedure Act Article 420, Item 2; Civil Procedure Act Article 451(1), Item 7). However, other requirements, such as whether that testimony affected the judgment, must be examined separately.

faqs.q: Is lying during police questioning also perjury?
faqs.a: A false statement made as a witness to investigators is not perjury. However, if you manipulated evidence in someone else's case, for example by submitting false documents, a separate crime such as fabrication of evidence can arise.

faqs.q: Can I refuse to testify?
faqs.a: In cases set by law, such as when the testimony could expose you or a close relative to criminal punishment, you can refuse to testify. Check whether you have grounds to refuse before you testify.

areaPages.summary: The other person being cleared does not by itself make your report a false accusation; it must be proven that you knew the report was false.
areaPages.title: False Accusation
areaPages.lead: False accusation (무고) is committed when someone reports false facts to investigators or other authorities to get another person punished. It is a serious crime with a statutory penalty of up to 10 years in prison. Whether you are filing a counter-complaint or have been accused of false accusation, the key is how falsity and intent are proven.

seo.title: False Accusation in Korea: Requirements and Counter-Complaints | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: For anyone in Korea who was cleared after being accused and now wants to file a counter-complaint for false accusation, or who is accused of false accusation. The statutory penalty and requirements under Criminal Act Article 156, the difference between being cleared and a false accusation, how exaggeration differs from falsehood, reduced penalties for confessing or surrendering, and when to file a counter-complaint.

situations.title: When you may need advice
items: I was accused of sexual harassment and the police decided not to refer the case, and now I want to sue the accuser for false accusation
I filed a fraud complaint because I was not paid back, and the other person filed a counter-complaint for false accusation
I exaggerated in a report out of anger, and it is weighing on me
Someone made a false report about me to my company and got me disciplined

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 156 (False Accusation)
items.text: Reporting false facts to a public office or public official with the aim of having another person receive criminal or disciplinary punishment is punishable by up to 10 years in prison or a fine of up to KRW 15 million.

items.name: Criminal Act Article 157 (Confession, Voluntary Surrender)
items.text: If a person who made a false accusation confesses or surrenders before the judgment or disciplinary decision in the reported case becomes final, the penalty is reduced or waived (applying Article 153).

sections.title: Being cleared does not mean the accusation was false
body: The fact that the accused person received a decision of no charge (혐의없음) does not by itself make the complainant guilty of false accusation. The Supreme Court has held that the mere failure to prove the reported facts true does not immediately establish that they were false (Supreme Court Decision 2007도6406, October 11, 2007).

For false accusation to be found, it must be shown that the reported facts differ from the objective facts, and that the person who reported them knew this or at least recognized they might be false. The starting point is to find, in the original case record, where the complainant's account changed and where it conflicts with objective evidence.

sections.title: Partial exaggeration differs from a false report
body: Court decisions tend to hold that if the core of the report is true and only some parts were exaggerated or the legal assessment was wrong, it is hard to call it false accusation. A typical example is a fraud complaint over money not returned that ends up treated as a civil matter.

On the other hand, inventing something that never happened, or fabricating facts that decide whether a crime was committed, can be false accusation. Beyond reports to the police or the prosecution service (공소청), when a report is made to a supervisory body or a company to get someone disciplined at work, we also examine whether it counts as a report to a public office or public official.

sections.title: Decide on a counter-complaint after seeing the outcome of the original case
body: Filing a counter-complaint while the original case is still ongoing can look like an attempt to pressure a settlement, and the decision may be put off because the original case has not concluded. So many people file after a non-referral (불송치), non-indictment (불기소) or acquittal becomes final, using that record as the basis.

If you have been accused of false accusation, you need to show with evidence that you had grounds to believe what you reported at the time. If you did in fact make a false report, confessing or surrendering before the original case becomes final can reduce or waive the penalty.

factors.title: Factors that affect the outcome and sentence
plus: Falsely reporting a serious crime such as a sex crime
Fabricating false evidence
Serious harm, such as the other person being detained or investigated for a long time
Evidence of an aim to extract settlement money
minus: There were circumstances that gave reason to believe it at the time of the report
The core facts were true, with only some exaggeration
Confessing or withdrawing the complaint before the original case became final
Apologizing to the other person and making up for the harm

steps.title: How our Criminal Law Center handles your case

items.title: Review the original case record
items.desc: Based on the non-referral decision, the reasons for non-indictment or the judgment, we look for parts that reveal falsehood.

items.title: Inspect and copy records
items.desc: If needed, we inspect and copy the original case record and compare the complainant's changing statements with the objective evidence.

items.title: Filing a complaint for you
items.desc: If you decide to file a counter-complaint, we draft it around the facts that support falsity and intent, and attend your interview as the complainant.

items.title: Defense as the accused
items.desc: If you were accused of false accusation, we organize the grounds for your report, attend questioning with you and submit a written opinion.

checklist.title: Helpful documents to prepare before your consultation
items: The non-referral decision, notice of reasons for non-indictment or judgment in the original case
The complaint and statements filed in the original case
Messages or recordings showing where the complainant's account changed
Records of harm you suffered from the original case (discipline, leave of absence, medical records)

faqs.q: The decision clearing me says "insufficient evidence." Can I file a complaint for false accusation?
faqs.a: Insufficient evidence means the allegation was not proven, not that it was false, so this alone is unlikely to establish false accusation. First check whether there is other evidence that the complainant knew it was false.

faqs.q: If the accuser is convicted of false accusation, what happens to my original case?
faqs.a: A person who was convicted because of a false accusation can request a retrial once the false accusation is proven by a final judgment (Criminal Procedure Act Article 420, Item 3).

faqs.q: If I withdraw my complaint, does my liability for false accusation disappear?
faqs.a: Even if you withdraw the complaint, the fact that you made a false report remains, so the crime of false accusation does not go away. However, confessing or surrendering before the trial or disciplinary decision in the original case becomes final reduces or waives the penalty.

areaPages.areaName: Forgery & Use of Private and Public Documents
areaPages.summary: Making a document in a family member's name is forgery if you did not have their permission, and there is no special exception for relatives in document crimes.
areaPages.title: Forgery & Use of Private and Public Documents
areaPages.lead: Writing a power of attorney in a parent's name or stamping someone else's seal on an IOU often leads to a complaint for forgery of a private document (사문서위조). The first issue is whether you had authority to make the document and whether the named person gave permission.

seo.title: Forgery of Private and Public Documents and Their Use in Korea: Penalties | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: For anyone in Korea investigated for forging a power of attorney, IOU or contract in a family member's name, submitting forged documents or forging public documents. Statutory penalties for forgery and use of private documents and forgery of public documents, the issues of the named person's consent and the scope of authorization, why it is punished even between relatives, and how to respond to a complaint.

situations.title: When you may need advice
items: I signed loan documents in my mother's name, and my sibling filed a complaint against me
My business partner used my seal to make a contract
I altered my certificate of employment and submitted it to a bank
I am accused of making documents beyond the scope of what I was authorized to do
I am being investigated for editing and submitting documents issued by a government office

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 231 (Forgery or Alteration of Private Documents) and Article 234 (Use of Forged Private Documents)
items.text: Forging or altering another person's document concerning rights, duties or proof of facts, with the aim of using it, is punishable by up to 5 years in prison or a fine of up to KRW 10 million. Using such a document is punished by the same penalty.

items.name: Criminal Act Article 225 (Forgery or Alteration of Public Documents) and Article 229 (Use of Forged Public Documents)
items.text: Forging or altering a document of a public official or public office, with the aim of using it, is punishable by up to 10 years in prison. Using such a document is punished by the same penalty.

sections.title: The first issue is whether you had permission
body: Forgery means a person without authority making a document in someone else's name. If the named person gave permission in advance, it is not forgery, and implied consent, such as verbal permission or the person habitually leaving paperwork to you, can also be argued.

The scope of the permission also matters. If you were only entrusted with a loan application but also made surety documents, the part that went beyond the scope can be treated as forgery. The general view is that the named person giving permission afterward does not undo a forgery already committed.

sections.title: Making a document and submitting it are punished separately
body: Submitting a forged document to a bank, court or government office is a separate crime of using a forged private document, punished by the same penalty. If you borrowed money with that document, fraud can be added as well.

Public documents are punished much more heavily. Forgery of a public document carries only up to 10 years in prison, with no fine option, so cases involving altered resident registration cards or documents issued by government offices must be handled carefully from the start.

If you did not forge someone else's ID or public document but used it as if it were your own, the issue is improper use of a public document (공문서부정행사, Criminal Act Article 230). This carries up to 2 years in prison or imprisonment without labor, or a fine of up to KRW 5 million, which is lighter than forgery.

sections.title: You can be punished even within a family
body: The special rule for property crimes between relatives (친족상도례) does not apply to document crimes. Even for documents in a parent's or sibling's name, making them without permission is punishable.

Also, forgery of a private document is not a crime that cannot be prosecuted against the victim's wishes, so the case does not end automatically even if you settle with the named person. However, the named person's statement of no wish to punish and compensation for the harm weigh heavily in the outcome.

factors.title: Factors that affect the outcome and sentence
plus: Borrowing money or disposing of property with the forged document
Forging several documents repeatedly
Forging or using a public document
The harm has not been made good
minus: Circumstances suggesting the named person's implied consent
The document was not used, or no actual harm resulted
Settling with the named person and receiving a statement of no wish to punish
No prior record

steps.title: How our Criminal Law Center handles your case

items.title: Check the document and circumstances
items.desc: We look at the original or a copy of the document and how it was made, to see whether consent or the scope of authorization can be disputed.

items.title: Gather evidence of consent
items.desc: We collect messages with the named person and records showing you habitually handled paperwork on their behalf.

items.title: Attend questioning
items.desc: We attend questioning about who permitted what, and help keep your statements consistent.

items.title: Submit a legal opinion
items.desc: We submit a written opinion disputing that forgery was committed or, if you admit it, including materials on compensation and the named person's wish not to punish.

checklist.title: Helpful documents to prepare before your consultation
items: A copy of the document at issue
Messages and call records with the named person
Where the document was submitted
Documents showing family or business relationships
The summons to appear or a copy of the criminal complaint

faqs.q: If my mother, the named person, says she does not want me punished, is it over?
faqs.a: Forgery and use of a private document are not crimes that cannot be prosecuted against the victim's wishes, so the case does not end right away. However, if the named person states that she effectively gave permission, the forgery itself may not be established, and her wish not to punish is taken into account in the outcome.

faqs.q: I edited a scanned document file and sent it by email.
faqs.a: Whether this is treated as document forgery can depend on how the file was made and whether it was printed and submitted. Keep the original file and a record of how you sent it exactly as they are, and check this in a consultation.

faqs.q: What is the statute of limitations?
faqs.a: Forgery and use of a private document carry a maximum of 5 years in prison, so the statute of limitations is 7 years. Forgery and use of a public document carry a maximum of 10 years, so it is 10 years (Criminal Procedure Act Article 249). If the forgery and the use happened at different times, each is calculated separately.

areaPages.areaName: Harboring an Offender & Destruction of Evidence
areaPages.summary: If you say you were driving in place of a drunk driver or delete evidence in an acquaintance's case, the person who asked you can also be punished.
areaPages.title: Harboring an Offender & Destruction of Evidence
areaPages.lead: These are cases where people try to help family members or acquaintances and end up becoming suspects themselves. Here we explain what crimes arise from turning yourself in on someone else's behalf or throwing away their phone, and how far the special exception for relatives applies.

seo.title: Harboring an Offender and Destruction of Evidence in Korea: Penalties and the Relatives Exception | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: For anyone in Korea accused of harboring an offender or destroying evidence after swapping drivers in a drunk driving case, turning themselves in for someone else, or discarding an acquaintance's phone or files. Statutory penalties under Criminal Act Articles 151 and 155, the exception for relatives and cohabiting family members and its limits, and the liability of the person who asked for help for inducing the harboring of an offender.
keywords: false confession for someone else Korea

situations.title: When you may need advice
items: I told the police I was driving instead of my friend who drove drunk
I suggested saying I caused my husband's accident, and it was found out
I deleted server data on my company president's instructions, and I am told it is destruction of evidence
I arranged a place to stay for an acquaintance while they were on the run
I deleted KakaoTalk messages related to my own case. Is that a problem?

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 151 (Harboring an Offender and Special Exception for Relatives)
items.text: Hiding a person who committed a crime punishable by a fine or heavier, or helping them escape, is punishable by up to 3 years in prison or a fine of up to KRW 5 million. A relative or cohabiting family member who does so for that person is not punished.

items.name: Criminal Act Article 155 (Destruction of Evidence and Special Exception for Relatives)
items.text: Destroying, concealing, forging or altering evidence in another person's criminal or disciplinary case, or using forged or altered evidence, is punishable by up to 5 years in prison or a fine of up to KRW 7 million. A relative or cohabiting family member who does so for that person is not punished.

sections.title: Saying you were driving instead is harboring an offender
body: If you state that you were driving in place of the person who drove drunk or caused an accident, you have prevented investigators from finding the real offender, which is harboring an offender (범인도피). In most cases, the real driver is revealed through dashcam footage, parking lot CCTV or phone location data.
A relative or cohabiting family member who does this for the person is not punished. However, partners who are not legal spouses and friends are not covered by this exception.

sections.title: The person who asked commits inducement to harbor an offender
body: An offender who simply runs away is not punished for harboring an offender, but getting someone else to make a false confession is treated as an abuse of the right to defend oneself, and inducement to harbor an offender (범인도피교사) is established. The Supreme Court has held that this applies even if the person who falsely confessed is a family member who is not punished (Supreme Court Decision 2008도7647, November 13, 2008).

So if a family member steps in and it is discovered, the family member may escape punishment under the exception, but the person who asked them may face a heavier outcome because inducement to harbor an offender is added to the original case.

sections.title: Destruction of evidence applies to evidence in someone else's case
body: The crime of destruction of evidence (증거인멸) covers evidence in another person's criminal or disciplinary case, so deleting evidence in your own case does not by itself amount to this crime. However, getting someone else to delete evidence raises liability for inducement, and resetting your phone or deleting conversations is held against you as a risk of destroying evidence when deciding whether to detain you.

An employee who deletes data on the company's instructions can be punished for destruction of evidence if that data is evidence in a criminal case against the president or the company. The issues are how the instruction was given and whether the employee knew about the investigation at the time.

factors.title: Factors that affect the outcome and sentence
plus: The original case is serious and the investigation was greatly hindered
Several people coordinated their stories and destroyed evidence in an organized way
Giving or receiving something in return for a false confession
Continuing to make false statements even after being found out
minus: Correcting the facts right away
The investigation was not seriously hindered in practice
It was hard to refuse a superior's instruction
No prior record

steps.title: How our Criminal Law Center handles your case

items.title: Check the relationship and circumstances
items.desc: We check your relationship with the person in the original case and who suggested it first, to assess the relatives exception and liability for inducement.

items.title: Plan how to correct your statement
items.desc: If you have already made a false statement, we decide when and how to correct it and attend the questioning with you.

items.title: Search, seizure and forensics response
items.desc: In cases where deleted data is at issue, we attend the search and seizure and apply to take part in the forensic examination to keep it within its proper scope.

items.title: Submit a legal opinion
items.desc: At the decision stage, we submit a written opinion covering the extent of your involvement, the circumstances and your efforts to correct the record.

checklist.title: Helpful documents to prepare before your consultation
items: Details and status of the original case
Messages and call records of the request or instruction you received
A family relationship certificate (to check the relatives exception)
What kind of data was deleted and when
The summons to appear

faqs.q: My wife said she was driving instead of me. Will she be punished too?
faqs.a: Harboring an offender committed by a spouse for her husband is not punished under the relatives exception. However, if the husband asked her to do it, inducement to harbor an offender can be established against him.

faqs.q: Does the relatives exception apply to a common-law spouse?
faqs.a: The exception applies to relatives and cohabiting family members, so a common-law spouse who lives with you may be treated as a cohabiting family member. A partner who does not live with you is not covered.

faqs.q: Is it a crime if I delete evidence in my own case?
faqs.a: Destroying evidence in your own case yourself is not the crime of destruction of evidence. However, it can lead to a finding that there is a risk of destroying evidence at a detention warrant hearing, and getting someone else to delete it raises liability for inducement.

areaPages.summary: If it relates to someone's duties, it can violate the Anti-Graft Act even without a quid pro quo, and if a quid pro quo is found, it becomes bribery, with penalties rising sharply by amount.
areaPages.cardLaw: Criminal Act Articles 129 and 133, Anti-Graft Act Article 8
areaPages.title: Bribery & the Anti-Graft Act
areaPages.lead: These cases involve meals and gifts given to public officials, school staff or journalists. Depending on the connection to their duties, whether there was a quid pro quo and the amount received, outcomes range from an administrative fine to heavy punishment under the Act on the Aggravated Punishment of Specific Crimes.

seo.title: Bribery and Violations of the Anti-Graft Act (Kim Young-ran Act) in Korea | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: For anyone in Korea investigated for giving or receiving money or meals involving public officials. Statutory penalties for accepting and giving bribes and the increased penalties under the Aggravated Punishment Act, the Improper Solicitation and Graft Act thresholds of KRW 1 million per occasion and KRW 3 million per year, value limits for meals, congratulatory and condolence money and gifts, and the line between administrative fines and criminal punishment.
keywords: Improper Solicitation and Graft Act Korea

situations.title: When you may need advice
items: I sent a holiday gift to the official in charge of my permit, and now I am being investigated
A report was filed under the Anti-Graft Act over a gift card I gave my child's teacher
I played golf and had meals with an employee of a public company that is my client, and it was flagged in an audit
Money I received as a public official is suspected of being a bribe
I received notice of an administrative fine for making an improper request

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 129(1) (Acceptance of Bribes) and Article 133(1) (Offering of Bribes)
items.text: A public official who accepts, demands or agrees to accept a bribe in connection with their duties is punishable by up to 5 years in prison or suspension of qualifications for up to 10 years. A person who promises, gives or offers to give a bribe is punishable by up to 5 years in prison or a fine of up to KRW 20 million.

items.name: Act on the Aggravated Punishment of Specific Crimes (특정범죄가중처벌법) Article 2
items.text: If the bribe received is KRW 30 million or more, the penalty is at least 5 years in prison; KRW 50 million or more, at least 7 years; and KRW 100 million or more, life imprisonment or at least 10 years. A fine of 2 to 5 times the bribe amount is imposed in addition.

items.name: Improper Solicitation and Graft Act (청탁금지법) Article 8 and Article 22(1)
items.text: A public servant or other covered person who receives, demands or agrees to receive money or other valuables worth more than KRW 1 million at one time, or more than KRW 3 million in a fiscal year, from the same person is punishable by up to 3 years in prison or a fine of up to KRW 30 million, whether or not it relates to their duties. The same applies to the person who gave it.

table.title: Values allowed under the Anti-Graft Act (for social or ceremonial purposes)
rows: KRW 50,000 for wedding gifts or condolence money (KRW 100,000 for flower wreaths)
Gifts of agricultural or fishery products or processed products
KRW 150,000 (KRW 300,000 from 24 days before to 5 days after Seollal and Chuseok)
table.note: Enforcement Decree of the Improper Solicitation and Graft Act Article 17 and Attached Table 1 (as in force from June 30, 2026). Even when related to duties, these amounts are allowed for smooth performance of duties or for social or ceremonial purposes. Cash and securities are not included in gifts.

sections.title: The Anti-Graft Act does not ask whether there was a quid pro quo
body: If it relates to the recipient's duties, the Improper Solicitation and Graft Act prohibits money or valuables above the set limits even without a quid pro quo. Amounts of KRW 1 million or less per occasion or KRW 3 million or less per year lead to an administrative fine (과태료) of 2 to 5 times the amount received instead of criminal punishment (Article 23(5)).

Covered persons include not only public officials but also employees of public institutions, staff at schools at all levels and employees of media companies. This is why gifts from parents to homeroom teachers so often become an issue.

sections.title: For bribery, the key is connection to duties and a quid pro quo
body: Bribery is established only when a benefit is given or received in connection with a public official's duties and in return for them. Not only money but any benefit that satisfies a person's wants, such as entertainment, golf outings, debt forgiveness or job placement, can qualify.

We examine one by one whether it was a gift from a long-standing friendship, what duties the official had at the time, and whether the timing overlapped with a permit or contract. If the amount received exceeds KRW 30 million, the Aggravated Punishment Act applies and the penalty becomes much heavier, and the bribe received is confiscated or its value collected (Criminal Act Article 134).

sections.title: The giver is also punished
body: A person who gives a bribe is punished for offering a bribe, and a person who gives money or valuables above the Anti-Graft Act limits is punished by the same penalty as the official who received them. If the official reports the receipt and returns it, the case can end up focusing only on the giver.
Investigations proceed by matching bank records, card usage and work records. Before stating amounts or the number of occasions from memory, check the records first.

factors.title: Factors that affect the outcome and sentence
plus: Large amounts repeated several times
An improper decision or special favor actually followed
Demanding money or valuables first
Hiding traces with borrowed-name accounts or cash
minus: A customary gift arising from a long personal friendship
A weak connection to the official's duties
Returning it or reporting it right away
No prior record

steps.title: How our Criminal Law Center handles your case

items.title: Consultation with the managing partner
items.desc: Based on what was given and received and the duties at the time, we sort out whether it is an administrative fine matter, a criminal matter, or a matter likely to be contested as bribery.

items.title: Organize the records
items.desc: We match bank and card records with schedules to establish the exact amounts and number of occasions.

items.title: Search and seizure response
items.desc: If your office or home is searched, we attend the search and apply to take part in the forensic examination.

items.title: Attend questioning and legal opinion
items.desc: We attend questioning about the connection to duties and any quid pro quo, and set out the personal friendship and customary nature of the gift in a written opinion.

checklist.title: Helpful documents to prepare before your consultation
items: The dates and amounts of money, valuables or meals given or received
Bank transfer and card payment records
The official's duties at the time
Materials showing a long-standing friendship
Audit results or the summons to appear

faqs.q: It was a KRW 50,000 meal. Is that still a problem?
faqs.a: For smooth performance of duties or social or ceremonial purposes, meals up to KRW 50,000 are allowed. However, where the connection to duties is close, such as an official currently reviewing your permit, it may not be allowed even within the limit.

faqs.q: Can I give my child's homeroom teacher a gift on Teachers' Day?
faqs.a: Because a homeroom teacher evaluates and guides the student, a connection to duties is found, and the general interpretation is that even gifts within the value limits are not allowed. Only things accepted by social norms, such as flowers presented by a student representative, are treated as exceptions.

faqs.q: Is it all right if I received money and gave it back?
faqs.a: Under the Anti-Graft Act, an official who reports the receipt, returns or hands over the money or valuables, or states a refusal is excluded from criminal punishment. Bribery can be established once a bribe has been received, but returning it right away is meaningful for arguing there was no intent to accept it and at sentencing.

areaPages.summary: The statute of limitations is short, at 6 months after election day, trials move quickly, and the amount of a fine can void an election win.
areaPages.cardLaw: Public Official Election Act Articles 250, 257 and 268
areaPages.title: Election Law Violations
areaPages.lead: Not only candidates and campaign staff but also ordinary voters can be investigated for violating the Public Official Election Act (공직선거법) after accepting a meal or posting on social media. Because the statute of limitations and trial periods are short, you need to respond quickly from the start.

seo.title: Public Official Election Act Violations in Korea: Investigations and Trials | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: For candidates, campaign staff and voters in Korea under investigation by the election commission or the police. Statutory penalties for publishing false information, making donations and vote buying, the 6-month statute of limitations after election day, the 6-month first-instance trial period, the standard for voiding an election win, administrative fines for those who received money or valuables, and special rules for voluntary surrender.
keywords: Public Official Election Act lawyer Korea

situations.title: When you may need advice
items: I went to a meal arranged by a preliminary candidate's side and was contacted by the election commission
I shared a post about a rival candidate on social media and was reported for publishing false information
I am accused of giving campaign workers money on top of their allowance
I was indicted for an election law violation after winning, and I am worried my win will be voided
I am being investigated for sending text messages before the official campaign period

items.name: Public Official Election Act (공직선거법) Article 250 (Publishing False Information)
items.text: Publishing false information favorable to a candidate in order to get them elected is punishable by up to 5 years in prison or a fine of up to KRW 30 million. Publishing false information unfavorable to a candidate in order to prevent them from being elected is punishable by up to 7 years in prison or a fine of KRW 5 million to KRW 30 million.

items.name: Public Official Election Act Article 257(1) (Violation of Restrictions on Donations)
items.text: Violating the restrictions on donations by candidates and others, or by third parties, is punishable by up to 5 years in prison or a fine of up to KRW 10 million.

items.name: Public Official Election Act Article 268 (Statute of Limitations)
items.text: The statute of limitations for election crimes expires 6 months after election day (for crimes committed after election day, 6 months from the date of the act). It is 3 years if the offender fled, and 10 years if a public official committed the crime in connection with their duties.

table.title: Consequences of election crimes
rows: Sentenced to prison or a fine of KRW 1 million or more (Article 264)
Campaign manager or accounting officer, or the candidate's spouse, parents, grandparents, children or grandchildren
Sentenced to prison or a fine of KRW 3 million or more for vote buying, donations or similar acts (Article 265)
5 years after a fine of KRW 1 million or more becomes final, among others (Article 18)
People who received money, valuables or food
Value received of KRW 1 million or less (Article 261(9))
Administrative fine of 10 to 50 times the value received (up to KRW 30 million)
table.note: Based on the Public Official Election Act as in force from October 2, 2026. A person who received more than KRW 1 million faces criminal punishment, not an administrative fine.

sections.title: Both the limitation period and the trials are short
body: Because the statute of limitations for election crimes ends 6 months after election day, investigations are concentrated within that time. If you are indicted, the first-instance court must deliver its judgment within 6 months from the date of indictment, and the second and third instances each within 3 months from the judgment of the court below (Article 270).

That leaves little time to gather evidence and organize your statements. It is important to organize text messages, event photos and accounting records from the election commission investigation stage.

sections.title: The amount of the fine decides whether the win stands
body: If a winning candidate is sentenced to prison or a fine of KRW 1 million or more, the election win is voided. The candidate's win is also voided if someone close, such as the campaign manager or spouse, receives a prison sentence or a fine of KRW 3 million or more for vote buying or donations.

So in election cases, not only guilt or innocence but the amount of the fine itself is in dispute. Restrictions on holding public office and on voting rights also follow, so the consequences should be weighed before the sentence becomes final.

sections.title: Those who received something also pay administrative fines
body: Voters who received meals or gifts from a candidate's side can face an administrative fine (과태료) of 10 to 50 times the value received, up to KRW 30 million. If you return what you received to the election commission and voluntarily report it, the fine can be reduced or waived (Article 261(9)).

There is also a special rule that reduces or waives the penalty for people who received or agreed to receive money or valuables, or who handed them out on instructions, if they voluntarily surrender (Article 262). Decide on the timing and method of surrender in a consultation first.

sections.title: Social media posts can also be publishing false information
body: People are often reported for publishing false information even for sharing or reposting allegations about a rival candidate. The issues are whether you had grounds to believe the content was true, and whether it was an expression of opinion or a statement of fact.
Even when raising suspicions, it can be held against you if you cannot present supporting materials. Keep the articles and materials you checked at the time you posted exactly as they are.

factors.title: Factors that affect the outcome and sentence
plus: Large amounts of money or valuables given in an organized way
Directed by the candidate personally or the core of the campaign
False information spread widely enough to affect the election result
Repeating it even after a warning from the election commission
minus: A one-time act involving a small amount
There were grounds to believe the information was true
Voluntary surrender or returning what was received
No prior election law violations

steps.title: How our Criminal Law Center handles your case

items.title: Election commission investigation
items.desc: Before the election commission's question-and-answer interview, we organize the facts and materials and decide the direction of your statement together.

items.title: Attend questioning during the investigation
items.desc: If you are questioned by the police following a criminal report or a request for investigation, we rehearse with you and attend the questioning.

items.title: Search and seizure response
items.desc: If the campaign office or your home is searched, we attend the search and apply to take part in the forensic examination.

items.title: Trial
items.desc: If you are indicted, we prepare evidence and sentencing materials in advance to fit the short trial period, and defend you with the fine thresholds in mind.

checklist.title: Helpful documents to prepare before your consultation
items: The election commission's summons or interview record
The date, time, attendees and costs of the event or meal at issue
The original social media post and its supporting materials
The campaign office's accounting records
Messages within the campaign giving instructions or reports

faqs.q: Am I safe from punishment once 6 months have passed after the election?
faqs.a: The statute of limitations expires 6 months after election day. However, it is extended to 3 years if the offender fled or helped an accomplice or witness flee, and to 10 years if a public official committed the crime in connection with their duties. For acts after election day, it is counted from the date of the act.

faqs.q: I only went to a meal. Will I be fined?
faqs.a: If you received food provided by a candidate or their associates, you can also face an administrative fine. It depends on whether everyone paid their own share and who provided the meal, so check your receipts and transfer records.

faqs.q: If I am indicted for an election law violation together with another crime, are the fines combined?
faqs.a: If an election crime and another crime are indicted together, the sentences are pronounced separately (Article 18(3)). The fine amount that serves as the standard for voiding an election win is based only on the sentence for the election crime.

areaPages.areaName: Arrest, Detention and Search and Seizure
areaPages.title: Responding to Arrest, Detention & Search and Seizure
areaPages.lead: In Korea, a detention warrant (구속영장) must be requested within 48 hours of arrest, or the person must be released. During that time, the family and defense counsel work together to gather materials for the pre-detention hearing (영장실질심사).

seo.title: Arrest, Detention Warrants and Search and Seizure in Korea | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: If a family member has been arrested in Korea or a detention warrant has been requested, there are set things to prepare within 48 hours of the arrest. Materials for the pre-detention hearing, review of the legality of detention and bail, and what to check at a search and seizure, including the warrant's scope and taking part in the digital forensic examination.

situations.title: Contact us right away if
items: I was told a family member was arrested in the act and is in a police station holding cell
A detention warrant was applied for and the pre-detention hearing is set for tomorrow
During questioning, the investigator brought up detention
Investigators came to my home in the morning with a search and seizure warrant
They took company computers and documents, including materials unrelated to the case
My phone was seized and I have been told the date of the forensic examination

items.name: Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 200-2(5) and Article 200-4 (Deadline for Requesting a Warrant After Arrest)
items.text: To detain an arrested suspect, a detention warrant must be requested within 48 hours of the arrest. If it is not requested within that time, the suspect must be released immediately. The same applies to emergency arrests (긴급체포).

items.name: Criminal Procedure Act Articles 70 and 201 (Grounds for Detention)
items.text: A person can be detained when there is good reason to suspect they committed a crime and they have no fixed residence, or there is a risk they will destroy evidence or flee. The judge also considers the seriousness of the crime, the risk of reoffending, and any risk of harm to the victim or key witnesses.

items.name: Criminal Procedure Act Article 201-2 (Request for a Detention Warrant and Examination of the Suspect)
items.text: When a detention warrant is requested for an arrested suspect, the judge must examine the suspect by the day after the request, unless there are special circumstances. Defense counsel may attend the hearing and state their opinion.

items.name: Criminal Procedure Act Articles 215 and 219 (Search and Seizure)
items.text: Judicial police officers may search and seize only items that can be considered related to the case, under a warrant issued by a judge at the prosecutor's request. The warrant must be shown to the person subject to it (Article 118), and a list of seized items must be prepared and handed over (Article 129).

table.title: Time limits set by law, from arrest to indictment
rows: Request for a detention warrant after arrest
By the day after the request, unless there are special circumstances
Must be transferred to the prosecutor within 10 days of detention
Indictment within 10 days of transfer; one extension of up to 10 days with a judge's permission
Review of the legality of arrest or detention
Hearing within 48 hours of the petition being received
2 months, renewable twice for 2 months each at each level of court
table.note: Based on the Criminal Procedure Act as in force from October 2, 2026. The time from when the court receives the warrant request record until it returns it is not counted in the detention period (Article 201-2(7)).

sections.title: Materials to gather within 48 hours
body: An arrested person is held in a cell and cannot get documents or meet people on their own. In the end, the family has to gather the materials for the pre-detention hearing from outside. In a visit, defense counsel hears how the arrest happened and what was said during questioning, and tells the family what to bring and by when.

What the judge looks at is whether the person has a fixed residence, whether there is a risk of destroying evidence, and whether there is a risk of flight. So the materials are chosen to address these three points. Materials that directly rebut each ground are better than a large volume.
bullets: Residence: resident registration record (주민등록등본), lease agreement, family members living together
Risk of flight: certificate of employment or business registration certificate, family relationship certificate, circumstances of dependent family
Risk of destroying evidence: list of materials already submitted, record of complying with summonses
Compensation for harm: settlement agreement, repayment records, documents on a court deposit
Petitions: from family, coworkers and longtime neighbors

sections.title: The pre-detention hearing does not decide guilt or innocence
body: At the hearing, the judge calls the suspect in and asks questions directly. Even if the charge is supported to some degree, the warrant can be rejected if the grounds for detention are not established. So we write the written opinion separating the parts that dispute the charge from the parts that dispute the need for detention.

The suspect's answers at the hearing are recorded and later read during the investigation and trial. Out of a sense of injustice, people often explain the case at length and end up contradicting what they said during questioning. In a visit before the hearing, we go over what questions may come up and how far to answer.

sections.title: There are still ways to challenge detention after a warrant is issued
body: Not only the arrested or detained suspect, but also defense counsel, the spouse, parents, grandparents, children or grandchildren, siblings, family members, people living with the suspect and the employer can petition the court for a review of the legality of arrest or detention (체포·구속적부심사). The court examines the suspect within 48 hours of receiving the petition and may order release on the condition of posting a bond (Criminal Procedure Act Article 214-2).

After indictment, you apply for bail (보석). The court must grant bail unless, for example, the crime carries a maximum penalty of more than 10 years, the person is a repeat or habitual offender, or there is a clear risk of destroying evidence or flight (Criminal Procedure Act Article 95). If further questioning is scheduled during detention, we attend that questioning too.

sections.title: What to check during a search and seizure
body: You cannot stop a search carried out under a warrant. Physically blocking it or hiding materials creates new problems of obstruction of official duties or destruction of evidence. Instead, ask to see the warrant, check the scope of places and items, and object on the spot to any search beyond that scope so it is recorded.

A request to hand over items not listed in the warrant is a request for voluntary submission (임의제출). Items you hand over voluntarily can be seized without a warrant (Criminal Procedure Act Article 218), so decide what to hand over in consultation with your lawyer. When the search ends, get the list of seized items and check that nothing is missing from it.
bullets: The suspect, the charge, the place to be searched and the items to be seized as stated in the warrant
Whether permission for nighttime execution is stated (Criminal Procedure Act Article 125)
Whether you received the list of seized items, and whether it matches what was actually taken
Separately write down any objections you made at the scene and when you made them

sections.title: Seizure of phones and computers, and digital forensics
body: As a rule, for data storage media, investigators must define the scope of the necessary information and take it by printing or copying it, and may seize the device itself only when that is difficult (Criminal Procedure Act Article 106(3) and Article 219). If the whole device was taken, we take part in the later selection process to make sure information unrelated to the case is not passed on as evidence.

You can ask for the return of items that no longer need to be held, even before indictment. If the investigators refuse, you can ask the court for a decision ordering return or provisional return (Criminal Procedure Act Article 218-2). If the device is essential for your work, we ask for it to be returned first after a copy has been secured.

factors.title: Factors that decide whether you are detained
plus: Not actually living at your registered address, or no clear residence
A record of failing to respond to summonses without good reason
Signs of contacting accomplices or deleting data
Attempting to contact the victim or witnesses
A similar prior conviction, or committing the offense during the repeat offender period
Large-scale harm that has not been made good
minus: A fixed residence where you live with your family
A clear basis for your life, such as a job or business
A record of responding to summonses and attending questioning
Key evidence is already in the investigators' hands
Compensation or a settlement has been made
No prior record

steps.title: How our Criminal Law Center handles your case

items.title: 24-hour phone line
items.desc: We answer 02-6951-4097 at night and on weekends. We confirm the police station where the person was arrested, the time of arrest and the charge you were told.

items.title: Visit
items.desc: We meet the arrested person in person, hear how the arrest happened and what was said during questioning, and decide how far to go in later questioning and at the hearing.

items.title: Preparing materials with the family
items.desc: We tell the family which documents and petitions are needed for each ground for detention, and organize the materials we receive.

items.title: Written opinion and hearing
items.desc: We submit a written opinion, with supporting materials, showing there are no grounds for detention, and go over the questions likely to come up at the hearing in advance.

items.title: After a warrant is issued
items.desc: If a warrant is issued, we consider a review of the legality of detention or bail, and attend any further questioning during detention.

items.title: Search and seizure response
items.desc: We check whether anything was seized beyond the warrant's scope, and apply to take part in the forensic selection process for phones and computers.

checklist.title: Helpful documents to prepare before your consultation
items: The arrested person's name, date of birth and the police station where they were arrested
The time of arrest and the charge the police mentioned
Resident registration record and family relationship certificate
Certificate of employment or business registration certificate
A list of people who can write petitions
Photos of the search and seizure warrant and the list of seized items

faqs.q: If the detention warrant is rejected, is the case over?
faqs.a: No. Rejecting a warrant only means detention was not found necessary, and the investigation continues without detention. A warrant can be requested again for the same facts (Criminal Procedure Act Article 201(5)), so prepare for later appearances and statements as carefully as at the start.

faqs.q: If I am detained, will I be held until the trial ends?
faqs.a: During the investigation, the rule is 10 days with the police and 10 days with the prosecutor, which can be extended once by up to 10 days with a judge's permission. After indictment, the court's detention period is counted separately. In the meantime, you can still seek release through a review of the legality of detention or bail.

faqs.q: Can I refuse a search and seizure?
faqs.a: You cannot refuse a search carried out under a warrant, and physically blocking it can raise obstruction of official duties. However, you have no duty to comply with a search beyond the warrant's scope or a request to hand over items not listed in it. Objections you raise at the scene can later serve as grounds for challenging the admissibility of evidence.

faqs.q: When can I get my seized phone back?
faqs.a: Once the necessary information has been copied through forensics, there is often no longer a need to keep the phone. You can then ask for return or provisional return, and if the investigators refuse, you can ask the court for a decision (Criminal Procedure Act Article 218-2).

faqs.q: Can I see my arrested family member right away?
faqs.a: Family visits are sometimes not possible right away, depending on the holding cell's hours and the state of the investigation. Defense counsel, or someone intending to become defense counsel, can meet a detained suspect (Criminal Procedure Act Article 34), so it is quicker to check the situation through a lawyer first.

areaPages.title: Criminal Trials
areaPages.lead: If you have received an indictment (공소장) in Korea, you should inspect and copy the investigation record before the first trial date and separate what to dispute from what to admit. The deadline to appeal a first-instance judgment is 7 days from the date it is pronounced.

seo.title: Criminal Trial Defense, Sentencing Materials and Appeals in Korea | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: The steps of a criminal trial in Korea after you receive an indictment: inspecting and copying the record, giving opinions on evidence, witness examination and preparing sentencing materials. Also the 7-day deadline to request a formal trial after a summary order, the 7-day appeal deadline and 20-day deadline for the statement of grounds for appeal, the ban on a heavier sentence on the defendant's appeal, and bail.
keywords: formal trial request summary order Korea

situations.title: When you may need advice
items: I received a copy of the indictment and a notice about appointing a court-appointed defense counsel (국선변호인) from the court
My first trial date has been set and I do not know what to prepare
I received a fine through a summary order, but the amount is too high
I admit the charge but want to avoid actual prison time
The first-instance court gave me a heavier sentence than I expected
A family member is on trial while in detention

items.name: Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 266-3 (Inspection and Copying of Documents After Indictment)
items.text: The defendant or defense counsel can request to inspect and copy documents the prosecutor plans to submit as evidence, documents containing witness statements, and similar materials. If the prosecutor does not give notice of reasons for refusal within 48 hours, you can ask the court to allow inspection and copying.

items.name: Criminal Procedure Act Articles 358 and 343 (Period for Filing an Appeal)
items.text: An appeal must be filed within 7 days, counted from the date the judgment is pronounced.

items.name: Criminal Procedure Act Article 361-3 (Statement of Grounds for Appeal)
items.text: The appellant or defense counsel must submit a statement of grounds for appeal within 20 days from the date they receive notice from the appellate court that it has received the case record.

items.name: Criminal Procedure Act Article 368 (Prohibition of Change to the Defendant's Disadvantage)
items.text: In a case appealed by the defendant or on the defendant's behalf, the court cannot impose a heavier sentence than in the original judgment.

table.title: Deadlines you must not miss at trial
rows: Request for a formal trial against a summary order
7 days from the date you are notified of the summary order
7 days from the date of pronouncement
Submission of the statement of grounds for appeal
20 days from receiving notice that the case record was received
The other side's response to the statement of grounds for appeal
Final appeal against an appellate judgment
7 days from the date of pronouncement
table.note: If you miss a deadline by even one day, you lose that procedure. Based on the Criminal Procedure Act as in force from October 2, 2026.

sections.title: When you receive an indictment, look at the record first
body: The indictment states what the prosecutor intends to prove, and the basis is in the investigation record. Before the first trial date, we inspect and copy the record and check the suspect interrogation records (피의자신문조서), witness statements, seized items and forensic or appraisal results. This is also when you first see in full how your own statements during the investigation were written down.

After reviewing the record, we decide whether to consent or object to each piece of evidence the prosecutor has submitted. If you object to a written statement or interrogation record, the person who made it must appear in court as a witness, so which evidence you dispute changes the length and direction of the trial.

sections.title: Contesting the charges and admitting them require different preparation
body: If you contest the charges, the focus is on admissibility and credibility of the evidence. We examine whether evidence was collected illegally, whether statements changed over time and whether they match objective materials, and prepare questions for witness examination.

If you admit the charges, the issue at trial is the sentence. In setting a sentence, the court considers the offender's age, character and conduct, environment, relationship with the victim, the motive, means and result of the crime, and circumstances after the crime (Criminal Act Article 51). If you admit only part, you must clearly separate what you admit from what you dispute so the court is not confused.

sections.title: What to submit as sentencing materials
body: When the court imposes a sentence of up to 3 years in prison or a fine of up to KRW 5 million, it can suspend the sentence (집행유예) (Criminal Act Article 62). The closer a case is to the line between actual prison time and a suspended sentence, the more the content of sentencing materials matters. Materials that show who is writing, in what relationship and what they promise are read more closely than a large number of pages.
bullets: A settlement agreement and a statement of no wish to punish (처벌불원서), or a criminal deposit (형사공탁) if no settlement is reached
Records of compensation for the harm (repayment receipts, transfer records)
A letter of apology written by you
Petitions from family and coworkers
Certificate of employment and documents on dependent family members
Records of efforts to prevent reoffending, such as treatment or counseling

sections.title: If you received a summary order, decide within 7 days
body: When the prosecutor requests a summary order (약식명령), the court sets a fine based only on the documents, without holding a trial. If you disagree with the result, you must request a formal trial (정식재판) within 7 days from the date you are notified of the summary order.

In a formal trial requested by the defendant, the court cannot impose a heavier type of punishment than the summary order, such as prison instead of a fine. However, the amount can go up within the same type of punishment (a fine), and in that case the court must state the reasons in the judgment (Criminal Procedure Act Article 457-2). We decide whether to request one after looking at whether there are grounds to dispute and new materials to submit.

sections.title: After the first-instance judgment, 7 days is the deadline
body: The appeal period is counted from the date the judgment is pronounced, not the date you receive the written judgment. After hearing the result on the day of pronouncement, you decide whether to dispute errors of fact, errors of law or an unfair sentence, and file a notice of appeal. When you receive notice that the case record has been received, you submit the statement of grounds for appeal within 20 days.

If only the defendant appeals, the appellate court cannot impose a heavier sentence than the first instance. This principle does not apply if the prosecutor also appeals. New sentencing materials, such as a settlement or deposit, can also be submitted on appeal, so if compensation was made after the first instance, those materials become grounds for appeal.

factors.title: Factors that affect the sentence
plus: Serious harm that has not been made good
The crime was planned or repeated
A similar prior conviction, or committing the offense during the repeat offender period
Contacting or pressuring the victim even during the trial
Repeatedly changing explanations that conflict with the charges
minus: A settlement, a statement of no wish to punish, or compensation for the harm
A criminal deposit when no settlement can be reached
Admitting the crime and showing remorse
Understandable circumstances behind the crime
A stable job and dependent family
No prior record

steps.title: How our Criminal Law Center handles your case

items.title: Review the indictment and record
items.desc: We inspect and copy the record and check the basis for the charges and your statements during the investigation.

items.title: Client meeting and strategy
items.desc: We decide what to dispute and what to admit, and set out whether to consent to each piece of evidence.

items.title: Witness examination and evidence
items.desc: In contested cases, we prepare questions for witness examination and rebuttal materials.

items.title: Sentencing materials and compensation
