items.desc: We submit settlements, deposits, petitions and materials on preventing reoffending in line with the trial schedule.

items.title: Trial defense and post-judgment review
items.desc: We appear at trial, argue your case and submit a written summary of arguments. After the judgment, we immediately decide with you whether to appeal.

checklist.title: Helpful documents to prepare before your consultation
items: The copy of the indictment and all documents you received from the court
The summary order or first-instance judgment
Decisions and notices you received during the investigation
The status of settlement talks with the victim
Certificate of employment and family relationship certificate
If you have a prior record, the details of the earlier judgments

faqs.q: I have a court-appointed defense counsel. Can I also hire my own lawyer?
faqs.a: Yes. When a privately hired lawyer is appointed, the court-appointed counsel's appointment is usually cancelled. If there are grounds such as detention, being a minor or being 70 or older, the court appoints defense counsel on its own when there is none (Criminal Procedure Act Article 33).

faqs.q: Does a settlement with the victim during the trial count?
faqs.a: Yes. A settlement agreement submitted before the closing of arguments is reflected in sentencing. For crimes such as simple assault, where the victim's wish not to punish bars prosecution, the case ends with dismissal of the prosecution (공소기각) if that wish is submitted before the first-instance judgment is pronounced. If you settle after the first instance, you can submit it on appeal as sentencing material.

faqs.q: I am on trial in detention. Is there a way to be released?
faqs.a: After indictment, you can apply for bail (보석). The court must grant bail unless, for example, the crime carries a maximum penalty of more than 10 years, you are a repeat or habitual offender, or there is a clear risk of destroying evidence or flight (Criminal Procedure Act Article 95). Materials showing your residence and that you will attend court are submitted with the application.

faqs.q: Can my sentence get heavier if I appeal?
faqs.a: If only the defendant appeals, a heavier sentence than the first instance will not be imposed (Criminal Procedure Act Article 368). If the prosecutor also appeals, it can get heavier, so we check whether the prosecutor has appealed and decide how to respond.

areaPages.title: Filing a Criminal Complaint on Your Behalf
areaPages.lead: A criminal complaint (고소장) gets an investigation moving only when it sets out when, who and what happened in line with the elements of the crime. From October 2026, the police must decide whether to refer a complaint case to the prosecutor within 3 months from the date they accept it.

seo.title: Writing and Filing a Criminal Complaint and Objecting to Non-Referral in Korea | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: If you were harmed and want to file a criminal complaint in Korea, you need a complaint and evidence list that meet the legal requirements. What to check before filing, including the statute of limitations and the complaint period, the police's 3-month investigation deadline, the 3-month objection to non-referral and the 30-day appeal against non-indictment, and settlements and compensation.
keywords: how to file a criminal complaint Korea

situations.title: When you may need advice
items: Someone who borrowed money from me has cut off contact
I invested money and the operator has disappeared
I was assaulted and have obtained a medical certificate
I found signs that an employee embezzled company money
I filed a complaint, but the police decided not to refer the case
I have a complainant interview coming up and do not know what to say

items.name: Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 237 (Form of Complaints and Accusations)
items.text: A complaint or accusation must be made to a judicial police officer in writing or orally. This provision, amended on August 4, 2026 and in force from October 2, 2026, makes the judicial police officer the authority that receives complaints.

items.name: Criminal Procedure Act Article 238 (Investigation of Cases Based on Complaints)
items.text: When a judicial police officer investigates a crime based on a complaint or accusation, they must complete the investigation and decide whether to refer the case within 3 months from the date the complaint was accepted. This applies to cases accepted on or after October 2, 2026.

items.name: Criminal Procedure Act Article 245-7 (Objection by Complainants and Others)
items.text: A complainant notified of a decision not to refer the case (불송치) can file an objection with the head of the police agency within 3 months from receiving the notice, and once an objection is filed, the case is sent to the prosecutor. The 3-month deadline applies to notices given on or after October 2, 2026.

items.name: Criminal Act (형법) Article 156 (False Accusation)
items.text: Reporting false facts with the aim of having another person receive criminal or disciplinary punishment is punishable by up to 10 years in prison or a fine of up to KRW 15 million.

table.title: How to challenge the outcome
rows: Police decision not to refer the case
Objection (to the head of the police agency)
Appeal (to the head of the Regional Public Prosecution Office)
Petition for adjudication (to the competent High Court)
10 days from receiving notice of the dismissal
Appeal dismissed (where a petition for adjudication is not available)
30 days from receiving notice of the dismissal
table.note: Based on the Criminal Procedure Act and the Public Prosecution Service Act as in force from October 2, 2026. The objection period can be extended if there is good reason.

sections.title: Write the complaint to match the elements of the crime
body: Rather than writing at length about how unfairly you were treated, what matters is meeting each element of the crime one by one. For fraud, write in date order what the other person lied about and how, when and how much you sent because you believed them, and what loss resulted, and attach evidence for each fact.

Stating unconfirmed matters as certain or exaggerating the harm lowers the credibility of your statements during the investigation and, in serious cases, raises an issue of false accusation (무고). Separate what you know from what you suspect, and for suspicions, ask the investigators to confirm them.
bullets: The accused person's personal details (if unknown, clues to identify them, such as phone number, bank account number or nickname)
The facts of the complaint, set out in date order
A list of evidence matching each fact
The amount of loss and how it was calculated
Requests to the investigators (tracing bank accounts, securing footage, and so on)

sections.title: What to check before filing
body: If the statute of limitations has run out, or the complaint period for a crime prosecuted only upon complaint (친고죄) has passed, filing will not lead to punishment. For such crimes, you must file within 6 months from the day you learned who the offender was (Criminal Procedure Act Article 230), and under an amendment in December 2025, fraud and embezzlement between relatives can also only be punished if a complaint is filed.

Also decide in advance whether the other person may file a counter-complaint, and whether to pursue a civil lawsuit or provisional attachment (가압류) at the same time. A criminal complaint alone does not get your money back, so if recovery is your goal, the order of steps needs to be planned together.

sections.title: Changes to the complaint process from October 2026
body: With the abolition of the Prosecutors' Office (검찰청) and the launch of the Public Prosecution Service (공소청), prosecutors no longer investigate directly. You file the complaint with the police, and the police must complete the investigation and decide whether to refer the case within 3 months from the date they accept the complaint (Criminal Procedure Act Article 238, for cases accepted on or after October 2, 2026).

Once the case is referred, the prosecutor reviews the record, decides whether to indict, and asks the police for supplementary investigation where something is lacking. The complainant can request a meeting with the prosecutor to state their views, and the prosecutor decides whether to accept it based on need (Criminal Procedure Act Article 245-13). Supplementary written opinions after referral are prepared to fit this process.

sections.title: If the police decided not to refer the case
body: When the police decide not to refer a case, they must send the complainant the decision and information on how to object within 7 days (Criminal Procedure Act Article 245-6). The decision states the conclusion and reasons, such as no charge (혐의없음) or not a crime (죄가안됨), so start by reading which element they found lacking.

If you received the notice on or after October 2, 2026, file the objection within 3 months from receiving it; once you do, the case goes to the prosecutor. The objection should include new materials and legal arguments that fill the gaps the decision pointed out. If the prosecutor finds the non-referral unlawful or unjustified, they can also ask the police to reinvestigate (Criminal Procedure Act Article 245-8).

sections.title: We consider both punishment and compensation
body: If the offender is indicted, the victim can apply to testify in court as a witness and has the chance to state views on the harm suffered and the punishment (Criminal Procedure Act Article 294-2). The victim can also apply to inspect and copy the trial record (Article 294-4).

If a settlement offer comes during the investigation or trial, consider not only the amount but whether to write a statement of no wish to punish (처벌불원서), and, if payment is in installments, whether to write it only after payment is complete. For crimes that cannot be prosecuted against the victim's wishes, once you state that you do not want punishment, you cannot change your mind.

steps.title: How our Criminal Law Center handles your case

items.title: Analyze the harm and evidence
items.desc: We first check whether the facts meet the elements of the crime. If a complaint would not meet the requirements, we explain other options at this stage.

items.title: Draft and file the complaint
items.desc: We set out the facts in date order, attach an evidence list and file it with the competent police station.

items.title: Prepare for and attend the complainant interview
items.desc: We go over the rebuttals the other side is likely to raise and attend the complainant interview with you to help with your statement.

items.title: Monitor the investigation and supplementary opinions
items.desc: We check progress within the 3-month investigation deadline and submit supplementary opinions to the prosecutor after referral.

items.title: Challenges and compensation
items.desc: If the case is not referred or not indicted, we draft and file an objection or appeal. If the offender's side offers a settlement, we negotiate the amount and terms on the victim's side. After indictment, we also handle applications for a compensation order (배상명령) and the victim's written opinion.

checklist.title: Helpful documents to prepare before your consultation
items: Any information you know about the other person, such as name, phone number and bank account number
Transfer records or contracts
All messages exchanged (screenshots and original backups)
Medical certificates, photos and CCTV locations
The date you became aware of the harm
Any police decisions or notices you have already received

faqs.q: Do the police start investigating as soon as I file a complaint?
faqs.a: Once the complaint is accepted, the investigation begins, and the police must decide whether to refer the case within 3 months from the date of acceptance. However, if the complaint does not match the elements of the crime or the evidence is weak, questioning may be delayed or the case may end with non-referral, so the quality of the complaint you first submit matters.

faqs.q: Can I file a complaint without knowing the other person's name?
faqs.a: Yes. If you include clues that identify the person, such as a bank account number, phone number or nickname on the site where you dealt with them, the investigators will check them. Save the screens and keep the originals before those clues disappear.

faqs.q: What if I want to withdraw my complaint?
faqs.a: You can withdraw a complaint until the first-instance judgment is pronounced, but once withdrawn, you cannot file another complaint about the same case (Criminal Procedure Act Article 232). For crimes such as fraud or bodily injury, which are neither prosecuted only upon complaint nor barred by the victim's wishes, the investigation and trial can continue even after you withdraw.

faqs.q: Can I challenge a prosecutor's decision not to indict?
faqs.a: You can appeal to the head of the Regional Public Prosecution Office within 30 days from receiving notice of non-indictment (Public Prosecution Service Act Article 57). If the appeal is dismissed, you still have the option of filing a petition for adjudication (재정신청) with the High Court within 10 days to get the court's decision.

guides.stage: The police contacted me and told me to come in
guides.title: When the police ask you to appear for questioning
guides.lead: If you got a call or text asking you to appear, there are set things to do before the questioning date. Here, in order, is what to do today, what not to do, the rights you have in the interview room and what to check before you sign the record.

seo.title: Police Summons in Korea: How to Prepare for Questioning | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: Got a call or text from the Korean police asking you to appear? First check whether you are a suspect or a witness and what the allegation is. Step by step: rescheduling, the right to remain silent, having a lawyer present, time limits on questioning, and reviewing and correcting the record.

sections.title: What to do right away
body: There is not much to do on the day you are contacted. If you simply write down and gather the items below, in this order, you are halfway prepared for the questioning.
bullets: Write down the case number, the department, the investigator's name and contact number. If the call came from an unfamiliar number, call the police station's main number back to confirm it is genuine.
Ask what the allegation is and whether you are a suspect or a witness. The summons (출석요구서) must state the gist of the alleged facts (Investigation Rules (수사준칙) Article 19(3)).
Write what you remember on one page, in date order. Focus on dates and times, places, who was there and any money that changed hands.

Do not delete messages, call logs, transfer records or photos; save copies separately. CCTV at shops and car parks is usually overwritten within two weeks to a month, so if you need it, ask right away for it to be kept.
If the questioning date is too soon, call the investigator and set a new date.

sections.title: What not to do
body: When an investigator asks about the case over the phone, it is tempting to explain, even briefly. Phone conversations can also end up in an investigation report, so you can simply say you will explain in detail when you come in, and just agree on a date.
Do not contact the other party or anyone involved to get your stories straight. It can look like an attempt to destroy evidence. For the same reason, avoid changing your phone or leaving chat rooms.

sections.title: You can reschedule the questioning date
body: The investigator must agree the date, time and place of questioning with the suspect, and also with the suspect's lawyer if there is one. If the suspect asks for a postponement, the rules say the schedule should be adjusted unless there are special circumstances (Investigation Rules Article 19). If you changed the date by phone, ask for the new date to be confirmed by text as well.

However, if you keep failing to appear without a valid reason, an arrest warrant (체포영장) may be requested (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 200-2). If you need a postponement, give your reason in advance and offer two or three dates that work for you.

sections.title: Your rights in the interview room
body: Before questioning, the investigator must tell you that you may refuse to make statements, that refusing will not be held against you, that anything you do say may be used as evidence of guilt in court, and that you have the right to a lawyer's assistance (Criminal Procedure Act Article 244-3).

Your lawyer can take part in the questioning, sit next to you and take notes, and can object to improper questioning methods even while questioning is under way (Criminal Procedure Act Article 243-2; Investigation Rules Articles 13 and 14).
bullets: As a rule, there is no questioning between 9 p.m. and 6 a.m. (Investigation Rules Article 21)
Total time, including waiting, breaks and meals, must not exceed 12 hours (Investigation Rules Article 22)
Actual questioning time, excluding meals, breaks and reviewing the record, must not exceed 8 hours unless there are special circumstances
You cannot be questioned again until 8 hours have passed since the previous questioning ended

sections.title: Before you sign the record
body: You sign the suspect interrogation record (피의자신문조서) after reading it or having it read to you. If something was not written as you said it, or is not true, you can ask for it to be corrected or state your view, and the investigator must add that to the record (Criminal Procedure Act Article 244).

Do not skim through it because you are tired. The wording in the record is read as it stands when deciding whether to refer the case to prosecutors and whether to indict, and again at trial. In particular, check that times, amounts and expressions about what you knew, such as "I was aware," match what you actually said.

sections.title: After the questioning
body: Points you could not fully explain during questioning, or materials you found later, can be submitted with a written opinion. To be taken into account, they must be submitted before the police decide whether to refer the case to prosecutors (송치). You can apply to inspect and copy the record of your own statement (Investigation Rules Article 69(1)).

If the case started with a criminal complaint (고소), the police must decide whether to refer it within 3 months from the day they accepted the complaint (Criminal Procedure Act Article 238). You may be contacted for further questioning, so write down the questions you were asked and your answers as well as you remember them.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: A managing partner consults with you in person and reviews the summons and the materials you have. We draw up likely questions and practise the interview with you, go into the interview room with you, and raise objections on the spot to leading or improper questions. After the questioning, we submit a defense counsel's written opinion.
If a questioning date has already been set, tell us the date and the police station. 02-6951-4097 is answered 24 hours a day, including weekends and public holidays.

faqs.q: I've been asked to come in as a witness. Should I bring a lawyer?
faqs.a: A lawyer can also take part and assist when a witness (참고인) is questioned (Investigation Rules Article 13(3)). Someone questioned as a witness can become a suspect depending on what they say, so if you are also involved in the case, get advice before the questioning.

faqs.q: Will questioning take the whole day?
faqs.a: It varies by case, but as a rule total time is limited to 12 hours and actual questioning time to 8 hours. Reviewing the record also takes time, so leave plenty of room in your schedule.

faqs.q: If they ask me to hand over my phone during questioning, do I have to?
faqs.a: Without a warrant it is a request for voluntary submission, so you can decide for yourself whether to hand it over. Items handed over voluntarily can be seized without a warrant (Criminal Procedure Act Article 218), so first discuss with your lawyer whether you can limit what you submit.

guides.stage: Questioning is over and I'm waiting for the outcome
guides.title: After police questioning: waiting for the outcome
guides.lead: Even after questioning ends, the case is only closed once the police decide whether to refer it and the prosecutor decides whether to indict. Here is what to do while you wait, and a step-by-step outline of the procedure as changed in October 2026.

seo.title: After Police Questioning in Korea: Referral, Non-Referral and Indictment | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: How the Korean police decide to refer or not refer a case after questioning, and how prosecutors decide on referred cases. Covers the October 2026 changes: requests for supplementary investigation, requests for re-investigation, prosecutors hearing the facts, and when to submit a written opinion.

sections.title: What to do right away
body: When you walk out of questioning, the tension drains away and you may not feel like doing anything. Still, there are things to do in the next few days while your memory is fresh.
bullets: Write down the questions you were asked and your answers as well as you remember them. Mark separately any questions you could not answer or answered vaguely.
If any wording in the record bothered you, apply to inspect and copy the part containing your own statement (Investigation Rules (수사준칙) Article 69(1)).
Look for more materials that back up what you said in questioning. Download your transaction history as a PDF from your banking app, and keep both screenshots and the original files of conversations.
Submit anything further you want to explain in a written opinion before the decision on referral is made.
Do not delete texts from the police or the Public Prosecution Service (공소청), and note down the case number.

sections.title: What not to do
body: Calling the investigator often because you want to know the result does not help. Ask about progress only when you really need to, and if you have a lawyer, check through your lawyer.
Do not go to the victim to press for a settlement or pressure them to withdraw the complaint. It will count against you in the decision and, in some cases, can be a separate crime.

Also be careful not to write anything in a written opinion that differs from what you said in questioning. Changing your story without materials explaining why can lead to the view that your whole statement is hard to believe.

sections.title: The police decide to refer or not refer the case
body: If the police find that there are grounds to suspect a crime, they refer (송치) the case to a prosecutor at the Public Prosecution Service. If not, they send the file to the prosecutor with a document stating the reasons. A prosecutor who receives a non-referral (불송치) file must return it to the police within 90 days (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 245-5).

If the case started with a criminal complaint, the police must decide within 3 months from the day they accepted the complaint (Criminal Procedure Act Article 238). A written opinion must be submitted before this decision to be taken into account.

When the police decide to refer or not refer, both the complainant and the suspect are notified (Investigation Rules Article 53). This usually comes by text. If the case is referred, the text shows the case number and the Public Prosecution Service office the case went to, so do not delete it. If you are negotiating a settlement, the sooner you finalise it in this period, the easier it is for it to be reflected in the decision.

sections.title: Once referred, the prosecutor decides on the basis of the file
body: On October 2, 2026, the Prosecutors' Office (검찰청) was abolished and the Public Prosecution Service was launched. The prosecutor who receives a referred case does not investigate directly but decides whether to indict based on the file, and asks the police for supplementary investigation (보완수사) if more is needed. The police must carry out the supplementary investigation and report the result within 1 month of receiving the request (Criminal Procedure Act Article 197-2). When the prosecutor hears the suspect's views, the prosecutor must allow the lawyer's assistance, including letting the lawyer take part (Article 245-13(5)).

The prosecutor's decision falls broadly into three types: non-indictment (불기소), which means the case does not go to court; a request for a summary order (약식명령), seeking a fine through a trial on the papers; and indictment for a formal trial (공소 제기). Non-indictment includes no suspicion, not a crime, no right to prosecute and suspension of indictment (기소유예), among others (Investigation Rules Article 52). In a complaint case, the prosecutor must decide whether to indict within 3 months of the referral (Criminal Procedure Act Article 257).

sections.title: A case can be reopened even after non-referral
body: Even after a non-referral decision, the complainant can file an objection (for notices given on or after October 2, 2026, within 3 months of receiving the notice). Once an objection is filed, the case is referred to the prosecutor (Criminal Procedure Act Article 245-7). If the prosecutor finds the non-referral unlawful or unjustified, the prosecutor can request a re-investigation within 3 months of receiving the file (Article 245-8).

So do not throw away your materials just because you received a non-referral notice. If the complainant objects, the prosecutor will look at the file again, so prepare the views you would submit at that point in advance.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: If we sat in on your questioning, we write a written opinion straight away based on our notes from that day. If you were questioned alone, we first apply to inspect the record to see how it was written, and fill in what is missing with a written opinion. When the prosecutor hears your views to confirm the facts, your lawyer takes part with you.
If you received a referral text or a notice of the outcome, just show us the text as it is. Our consultation line, 02-6951-4097, is answered 24 hours a day.

faqs.q: I was told my case has been referred. Will I be questioned again?
faqs.a: The prosecutor does not investigate directly, but if supplementary investigation is requested, the police may question you further. The prosecutor may also hear your views to confirm the facts, and you can attend that together with your lawyer.

faqs.q: If I get a suspension of indictment, is it over?
faqs.a: It means the case is closed without going to court. However, the decision assumes the allegation has been made out, so if you dispute the allegation itself, you need to look at the decision and consider separately how to challenge it.

faqs.q: How long until there is a result?
faqs.a: Complaint cases have a 3-month deadline at the police stage, but how long the prosecutor takes after referral, or how long supplementary investigation goes on, varies by case. You can check progress with the investigator in charge or the Public Prosecution Service office the case was referred to; if you have a lawyer, your lawyer will check.

guides.stage: My home or workplace was searched
guides.title: When your home or office is searched
guides.lead: When investigators show up in the morning with a warrant, your mind goes blank. Here is what to check on the spot, what not to do, and how phone forensics and getting seized items back work.

seo.title: Police Search and Seizure in Korea: On-Site Response and Phone Forensics | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: If police come to search your home or office in Korea, first get a copy of the warrant and check the allegation and the scope of seizure. Covers your right to be present, the list of seized items, selection of phone data and attending forensics, voluntary submission requests, and asking for seized items back.

sections.title: What to do right away
body: When investigators hand you a warrant, take a breath first. You cannot stop the search, but what you check now becomes the basis for any challenge later.
bullets: Ask to see the warrant and get a copy. A search and seizure warrant (압수수색영장) must be shown to the person subject to it, and the suspect must be given a copy (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Articles 118 and 219).
Note the allegation, the items to be seized, the places to be searched and the validity period written on the warrant.
Contact a lawyer and ask the investigators to wait a moment until the lawyer arrives. The suspect and the lawyer may be present during the search (Article 121).
Check what each item being taken is, and when it is over, get the list of seized items (압수목록) (Article 129). If the list does not match what was taken, say so on the spot.
At a company, the CEO or the manager in charge should be present, and you can ask that copies of files essential for business be left behind.

sections.title: What not to do
body: Physically blocking investigators or hiding items can turn into obstruction of official duties or destruction of evidence. If you think they are going beyond the warrant, do not block them; state your objection in words and write it down.

Do not explain the case at length on the spot. What you say to investigators can be written into an investigation report. If you are asked to unlock your phone or give your password, talk to your lawyer before agreeing. Also avoid deleting remaining data after the search. Traces of deletion are often left too.

At a company, check the warrant to see whether employees' personal phones are also covered. If they ask for the device of someone not named in the warrant, ask whether it is a request for voluntary submission; that person decides whether to hand it over.

sections.title: As a rule, only the necessary data on a phone is taken
body: When seizing a phone or computer, the rule is to set the scope of information related to the allegation and print or copy only that. The whole device can be taken only when this is impossible or would make it extremely difficult to achieve the purpose of the seizure (Criminal Procedure Act Articles 106(3) and 219; Investigation Rules (수사준칙) Article 41).

If a device is taken, the police extract and sort the electronic data at the station in a forensic process. Investigators must respect the right of the person whose items were seized, or their lawyer, to be present throughout, and when sorting is finished they must hand over a list of the electronic data seized. Data not on the list must be deleted or returned (Investigation Rules Article 42). Also check whether data stored outside the device, such as cloud or messenger backups, is named in the warrant.

sections.title: What you can check by attending forensics
body: You are usually contacted separately about the forensics schedule. If you attend, you can see on the spot whether photos, conversations or work files unrelated to the allegation in the warrant are being selected. If they try to take unrelated data, object and have it noted in the record. When you attend, bring the warrant copy and the list of seized items, and judge against the allegation and the period stated in the warrant.
If you choose not to attend, you only learn later from the list what data was selected. Depending on the case, analysis can take quite a long time, and you will be without your phone in the meantime.

sections.title: Getting seized items back
body: If there is no need to keep holding an item, you can get it back (환부). Even an item to be used as evidence can be returned quickly on a provisional basis if the owner needs to keep using it, after its original state is preserved by photographs or similar (가환부; Criminal Procedure Act Articles 133 and 219). Consider this for a work laptop or phone. If you disagree with an investigator's decision on seizure or return, you can ask the court to cancel or change it (준항고; Article 417).
A search is usually followed by a request to appear for questioning as a suspect. The questions will be based on the seized materials, so it helps to sort out what was in them before the questioning.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: When you contact us, we attend the search to check the scope of the warrant and how items are seized. If a phone or computer was taken, we apply to attend the forensics and raise objections to data beyond the scope during selection.

For the questioning that follows, we practise likely questions with you and go in with you. If investigators are already at your door, call 02-6951-4097 right away. We answer on weekends and public holidays too.

faqs.q: What if they ask me to hand over my phone without a warrant?
faqs.a: Without a warrant it is a request for voluntary submission, so you can decide for yourself whether to hand it over. Once you hand something over voluntarily, it is seized without a warrant (Criminal Procedure Act Article 218). If you do submit it, first discuss with your lawyer how to set and record the scope of data you are handing over.

faqs.q: I was told they searched my home while I was out.
faqs.a: When searching someone else's home, investigators must have the occupant or someone in a similar position present, and if that is not possible, a neighbour or a local government official must be present (Criminal Procedure Act Articles 123 and 219). Start by getting the list of seized items and checking what was taken.

faqs.q: What should employees do if the company is searched?
faqs.a: The person in charge checks the warrant and is present during the search. Tell employees not to explain the case or move materials themselves, and ask that copies of files needed for work be left behind.

guides.title: How much should a settlement be?
guides.lead: There is no fixed going rate for a settlement in a criminal case. Here is what is weighed when setting the amount, how to write a settlement agreement and a statement of non-punishment, and what you can do if the victim refuses to settle.

seo.title: Criminal Settlement Amounts in Korea: Settlement Agreement, Non-Punishment Statement and Deposit | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: Settlement amounts in Korean criminal cases depend on the harm, medical costs, losses and the stage of the case. Learn how a settlement works depending on whether the offense requires the victim's wish for punishment, when to settle, what to put in the agreement and non-punishment statement, paying in instalments and criminal deposits.
keywords: offense not punishable against victim's wishes

sections.title: How a settlement changes the outcome depends on the offense
body: For offenses such as assault or threats, which cannot be punished if the victim does not want punishment, the case ends with "no right to prosecute" (공소권없음) once a statement of non-punishment (처벌불원서) is submitted (Criminal Act (형법) Articles 260(3) and 283(3)). For other offenses, such as fraud, embezzlement or bodily injury, a settlement does not end the case. Instead, it weighs heavily when deciding whether you get a suspension of indictment (기소유예), end with a fine, or receive a suspended sentence (집행유예).

For offenses that can only be punished on a complaint, the case ends when the complaint is withdrawn. Fraud or embezzlement between certain family members is an example (Criminal Act Articles 328, 354 and 361). So before starting settlement talks, first find out which type your case is. The same money can mean very different things.

sections.title: What the amount is based on
body: Treat "going rate" tables on the internet as a rough reference only. In practice, the amount is worked out by going through the items below one by one. Even if the victim's first figure is far from yours, do not cut off talks; asking what the figure is based on is how to keep the conversation going. If part of the harm is covered by insurance, as in a traffic accident, set the amounts so they do not overlap with that.
bullets: Medical costs, future treatment costs and the period of the medical diagnosis
Lost income from being unable to work, and the value of damaged property
For fraud or embezzlement, the amount lost and interest since then
Compensation for emotional distress
Whether the case is before a decision or already at trial

sections.title: When should you settle?
body: Settling before a decision is made improves the chance of ending with a suspension of indictment or a fine. Even after the case is referred, it is taken into account if it comes before the prosecutor decides, and even after indictment it is considered in sentencing. The later it is, the fewer options you have.

If you do not know the victim's contact details, ask the investigator in charge to pass on that you wish to settle. If the victim agrees, the investigator will give you the contact details or put you in touch. Going to the victim directly or pressuring them through family makes settlement harder and counts against you in the decision. A first contact that starts with an apology is more likely to be accepted. Bringing up money first tends to come across as trying to buy your way out.

sections.title: What to put in the settlement agreement and non-punishment statement
body: Submit the settlement agreement (합의서) and the statement of non-punishment to the investigator in charge while the case is with the police, to the Public Prosecution Service (공소청) after referral, and to the court after indictment. Send the settlement money by bank transfer so there is a record.
bullets: Names and contact details of both parties, and the case number
Which incident the settlement covers (date and details)
The settlement amount, how and when it will be paid
A sentence stating that the victim does not want the offender punished
If needed, a sentence stating that this settlement also ends any civil claim for damages
Date of signing, signatures and copies of ID

sections.title: If you agreed to pay in instalments
body: If you agree to pay in instalments, the victim usually wants to sign the statement of non-punishment only after receiving everything. This is because, for offenses not punishable against the victim's wishes, once the victim has said they do not want punishment, they cannot later ask for punishment again (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 232(3)).

If you really need the statement before the decision, write the payment schedule into the agreement and set an order, such as getting the signature after sending the first instalment. If you miss a promised date, the settlement may fall apart. After the final payment, getting a text confirming receipt can reduce disputes later.

sections.title: If the victim refuses to settle
body: If the victim refuses to the end, consider a criminal deposit (형사공탁). A defendant can make a deposit at the deposit office where the court handling the case is located, identifying the victim by the case number and similar details even without knowing the victim's personal information (Deposit Act (공탁법) Article 5-2). This special rule is for defendants who have been indicted and are on trial, so it is hard to use at the investigation stage.

A deposit is not the same as a settlement. If there is a deposit, the court must hear the victim's views before judgment (Criminal Procedure Act Article 294-6), and because the money was deposited against the victim's wishes, it is often given less weight than a settlement. Keep a record of the efforts you made toward the victim before depositing. Also be aware before deciding that, in principle, a deposit cannot easily be taken back once made (Deposit Act Article 9-2).

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: At the consultation we first explain whether your case is an offense not punishable against the victim's wishes, and what effect a settlement has at the current stage. Jisan Law handles contact and negotiation of terms with the victim's side on your behalf, reviews the wording of the settlement agreement and the statement of non-punishment with you, and sets out the settlement process and evidence of compensation in a defense counsel's written opinion. If the wording of the settlement has not yet been finalised, contact us at 02-6951-4097.

faqs.q: I paid the settlement, but the victim says they won't write a statement of non-punishment.
faqs.a: First check whether the agreement says the victim does not want punishment. If that sentence is in the agreement, you can submit the agreement to the investigators or the court. If only money changed hands without that sentence, it can still be used as evidence of compensation, but it does not end the case for offenses not punishable against the victim's wishes.

faqs.q: Can I get a criminal deposit back later?
faqs.a: In principle, a criminal deposit cannot be withdrawn. It can be withdrawn only if the victim consents or notifies the deposit office that they refuse to accept it, or if an acquittal becomes final or there is a non-indictment decision other than a suspension of indictment (Deposit Act Article 9-2).

faqs.q: If I settle, will I avoid a criminal record?
faqs.a: For offenses not punishable against the victim's wishes, if the case ends with no right to prosecute after a statement of non-punishment is submitted, there is no trial and so no criminal record. For other offenses, a criminal record remains if you are sentenced to a fine or a suspended sentence, even after settling. A suspension of indictment is not a criminal record, but it stays in investigation history records (수사경력자료) for a set period.

guides.title: I want to postpone my questioning date
guides.lead: If the questioning date clashes with a business trip, an exam or a hospital appointment, or you need more time to prepare, you can change it. Here is how to request a postponement, the rules behind it, and what happens if you simply do not show up.

seo.title: How to Postpone a Police Questioning Date in Korea | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: Want to change the date in a Korean police summons? Here is how to contact the investigator, what reasons and proof to give, the scheduling rule in Article 19 of the Investigation Rules, and why failing to appear without notice can lead to an arrest warrant request.
keywords: failure to appear arrest warrant Korea

sections.title: What to do right away
body: The date on a summons or text is often one the investigator picked first. If that day does not work, the most important thing is to get in touch before the date comes.
bullets: Find the investigator's name, department and case number on the summons (출석요구서) or text.
Sum up in one line why that date is difficult. If you have something to show, such as a business trip schedule, a text confirming a medical appointment or exam information, have it ready.
Pick two or three dates that work. Choosing only dates far in the future gives the impression you are trying to delay.
Call the investigator, explain your situation and set a new date.
After the call, ask for the new date and time to be confirmed by text as well.

sections.title: Changing the date is a procedure set out in the rules
body: When asking someone to appear, the investigator must allow enough time so that it does not disrupt their livelihood, and if the suspect asks for a postponement, the date must be adjusted unless there are special circumstances. The date, time and place of questioning must be agreed with the suspect, and also with the suspect's lawyer if there is one (Regulation on Mutual Cooperation between Prosecutors and Judicial Police Officers and General Investigation Rules (수사준칙) Article 19(1)(iii) and (2)).

The same article also says that taking statements by post or phone instead of in person should be considered first. For a simple check of facts, you can ask whether you may answer in writing. If you have a reason that makes it hard to come to the station, such as being in hospital, questioning can take place outside the police station (same article, (1)(i) and (5)). The same applies to witnesses.

sections.title: Reasons that are usually accepted
body: The more specific the reason, the better, and it helps further if you have proof. For the reasons below, investigators generally agree to change the date.
bullets: Hospital stay, surgery or treatment schedule (medical certificate or booking record)
Business trip or stay abroad (flight ticket, business trip order)
Exam, job interview or a court date already set
Family matters such as a funeral or childbirth
Time needed to hire a lawyer and review materials

sections.title: What happens if you miss it without notice
body: If a suspect fails to respond to a summons without a valid reason, or is likely not to respond, an arrest warrant (체포영장) can be requested (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 200-2(1)). Missing one date does not immediately lead to a warrant, but if you repeatedly let dates pass without contact, it is easy to conclude that you have no intention of appearing. Even in minor cases where the only penalties are a fine of 500,000 won or less, short detention or a petty fine, failing to appear without a valid reason makes you subject to an arrest warrant (proviso to the same paragraph).
So even if you postpone, it is important to leave a record of the reason and the new date each time. If you missed the investigator's call, at least send a text first.

sections.title: What to do with the extra time
body: The point of postponing is to prepare. In the extra time, write down what happened in date order and gather materials that support your account, such as messages and transfer records. Thinking ahead about likely questions and marking the parts that are hard to answer also shortens the consultation. If the case started with a complaint, ask the investigator what the other party is complaining about so you know the scope of the allegation first. Postponing without preparing only means going through the same anxiety twice.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: Once you retain us, your lawyer rearranges the questioning date directly with the investigator. During the extra time, a managing partner consults with you in person to organise the materials, practises likely questions with you, and goes into the questioning with you. If there are only a few days left before the date, contact us first at 02-6951-4097. We answer 24 hours a day.

faqs.q: How many times can I postpone?
faqs.a: The law does not set a number. The rules say the date should be adjusted on request unless there are special circumstances, but if you keep postponing without reason, it can be treated as refusing to appear and an arrest warrant can be requested. Each time you postpone, make the reason and the new date clear.

faqs.q: I'm in hospital. Do I still have to be questioned?
faqs.a: If treatment or similar makes it extremely difficult to go to the police station, questioning can take place outside the station (Investigation Rules Article 19(5)). Send a medical certificate and decide which works better: postponing until you recover, or being questioned at the hospital or elsewhere.

faqs.q: I simply can't get time off during weekday daytime.
faqs.a: As a rule, questioning must end before 9 p.m., so late-night questioning is difficult (Investigation Rules Article 21). You can ask the investigator whether an early time or a different day is possible; whether it works depends on the police station.

guides.title: Reviewing and correcting the interrogation record, and refusing to sign
guides.lead: When questioning ends, the investigator shows you the record and asks you to read and sign it. Here is how to read it, how to correct anything written differently, and what to do if it still is not corrected.

seo.title: Reviewing, Correcting and Refusing to Sign a Police Interrogation Record in Korea | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: What to check when reading a suspect interrogation record after Korean police questioning, how to request corrections under Article 244 of the Criminal Procedure Act, when to hold off signing, and how to fix a record you already signed through inspection and copying, a written statement or a written opinion.
keywords: refuse to sign police statement Korea

sections.title: What to check first
body: After hours of questioning, you may want to skim the record and sign. Even so, say that you will read the whole record yourself from start to finish. If it is shown on a screen, scroll through it slowly.
bullets: Check that your answer to the question about whether you will use the right to remain silent and the right to a lawyer was written correctly (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 244-3(2)).
Check that the time you arrived at the police station, and the start and end times of questioning, match what actually happened (Article 244-4).
Compare numbers such as dates, amounts and frequency, and people's names, one by one.
Check that expressions of awareness or admission, such as "I was aware" or "I admit," are exactly what you said.
Check that places where you said you do not remember have not been turned into "I did not do it" or "I did it."

sections.title: You can ask for anything written differently to be corrected
body: The investigator must let the suspect read the record or read it aloud, and must ask whether anything differs from what was said or from the facts. If the suspect asks for something to be added, removed or changed, or gives an opinion, the investigator must add that to the record, and the original part objected to must be left legible (Criminal Procedure Act Article 244(2)).

Visible corrections do not count against you. It is better to have a record of what was corrected and why. If a summarised sentence differs from what you said, dictate the sentence: "What I actually said was this."

sections.title: Do not sign because you are short of time
body: As a rule, questioning should end before 9 p.m., but reading a record that has already been prepared can continue until midnight (Investigation Rules (수사준칙) Article 21(1)). Time spent reading the record at your written request is an exception to the 12-hour limit on total questioning time (Article 22(1)(i)).
If a lawyer took part, the lawyer can also read the record after questioning and give an opinion, and any separate written opinion is filed in the case record (Investigation Rules Article 14(1)).

sections.title: If it still is not corrected
body: If there are no objections or comments, the suspect writes that in their own hand, stamps across the page joins and signs (Criminal Procedure Act Article 244(3)). If the part you asked to be corrected is not reflected, you can hold off signing and say why. In that case, ask for the reason you did not sign to be noted in the record or an investigation report.

Refusing to sign is a last resort, though. In most cases, it is settled by asking for your objection to be written at the end of the record, checking that it has been included, and then signing. If you have a lawyer, discuss it before signing.

sections.title: If you have already signed
body: You can apply to inspect and copy the parts containing your own statement (Investigation Rules Article 69(1)). The head of the police office must decide whether to disclose them within 10 days of the application, and an application for your own record made on the day of questioning must be reviewed without delay (Police Investigation Rules (경찰수사규칙) Article 87). Get a copy, mark the parts that are wrong, and correct them through further statements, a written statement or a written opinion. If what you want to say is complicated or you would rather set it out in writing, you can also submit a written statement (진술서) (Police Investigation Rules Article 39(3)). If the case has already been referred, submit a written opinion to the prosecutor at the Public Prosecution Service (공소청) handling the case.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: If we sit in on your questioning, we read the record with you sentence by sentence and ask on the spot for corrections and for your comments to be added where something was written differently. If you were questioned alone, we start by applying to inspect and copy the record to see how it was written, and add what is needed in a defense counsel's written opinion. If something in the record is bothering you, contact us at 02-6951-4097.

faqs.q: The record says "I admit the allegation and am remorseful," but I never said that.
faqs.a: If the investigator's summary differs from what you actually said, do not leave it; ask for it to be changed to your own words. Your request for correction and its content must be added to the record (Criminal Procedure Act Article 244(2)). A single summary sentence is read as it stands when deciding on referral and indictment.

faqs.q: Can't I just deny the contents of the record at trial?
faqs.a: A suspect interrogation record (피의자신문조서) prepared by the police only becomes evidence at trial if the defendant or their lawyer accepts its contents (Criminal Procedure Act Article 312(3)). Even so, if what you said in questioning differs from what you say in court, you will have to explain why it changed, and that difference affects whether your whole account is found credible. It is better to correct it at the questioning stage.

guides.title: Applying to have a lawyer present at questioning
guides.lead: For a lawyer to go into a suspect interview with you, an application must be submitted before the questioning. Here is who can apply, what the lawyer can do in the interview room, and how to challenge a restriction on the lawyer's presence.

seo.title: How to Have a Lawyer Present at Police Questioning in Korea | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: Submitting the application for counsel's participation and the letter of appointment, why family members can also apply, what a lawyer can do in the interview room (advice, notes, objections), restrictions on participation and how to challenge them, and the lawyer's role when a Public Prosecution Service prosecutor hears your views.

sections.title: What to do right away
body: If you only mention a lawyer verbally on the day of questioning, the schedule can easily get tangled. Prepare in advance in the order below.
bullets: Confirm the date and time of questioning, the police station and the investigator in charge.
Choose the lawyer who will go with you and prepare a letter of appointment of counsel (변호인 선임서).

Submit the letter of appointment and the application for counsel's participation (변호인 참여 신청서) to the investigator before the questioning (Police Investigation Rules (경찰수사규칙) Article 12(2)). The lawyer usually submits them directly.
Match the questioning date with the lawyer's schedule. If you have a lawyer, the investigator must also agree the date and time with the lawyer (Investigation Rules (수사준칙) Article 19(2)).

sections.title: Who can apply?
body: Not only the suspect but also the lawyer, a legal representative, the spouse, lineal relatives and siblings can apply. Once an application is made, the investigator must allow the lawyer to take part in the questioning unless there is a valid reason not to (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 243-2(1)). Family members often apply when the suspect has been arrested and is hard to reach.

A lawyer cannot be kept out on the grounds that it is just an informal interview rather than a suspect interview, and the same principle applies when questioning or interviewing others involved in the case, such as witnesses (Investigation Rules Article 13(2) and (3)).

sections.title: What the lawyer does in the interview room
body: The lawyer sits where they can actually help, such as next to the suspect, and may take notes for legal advice and consultation (Investigation Rules Article 13(1)). After questioning, the lawyer can read the record and give an opinion orally or in writing, and can also give an opinion during questioning with permission. The lawyer can object to improper questioning methods without permission, and opinions and objections are written into the record (Article 14). A record containing the lawyer's opinion is also read and signed by the lawyer. If there are two or more lawyers, the suspect chooses one to take part in the questioning (Criminal Procedure Act Article 243-2(2) and (4)).
bullets: If a question is unclear, talk to your lawyer before answering.
If the same question is repeated or you are being pushed toward an answer, the lawyer objects.
You and your lawyer decide together, on the spot, whether to decline to answer a question.
You check the wording together when reading the record.

sections.title: If the lawyer's participation is restricted
body: An investigator may restrict a lawyer's participation during questioning only when there is a concrete risk that the lawyer's presence will lead to evidence being destroyed or fabricated, or when it would seriously hinder the investigation, for example by obstructing questioning or leaking investigation secrets. In that case, the investigator must explain the reason, give a chance to respond and to bring in another lawyer, and must let the lawyer back in once the reason no longer applies (Police Investigation Rules Article 13).

If you disagree with a decision on the lawyer's participation, you can ask the court to cancel or change it (Criminal Procedure Act Article 417, quasi-appeal (준항고)). Matters concerning participation and restriction must be written into the record (Article 243-2(5)).

sections.title: Your lawyer is also with you at the Public Prosecution Service stage
body: From October 2, 2026, prosecutors no longer question suspects directly, but when they hear a suspect's views to decide whether to indict, they must allow the lawyer's assistance, including letting the lawyer take part (Criminal Procedure Act Article 245-13(5)). The same applies when a prosecutor meets the suspect to review a detention warrant (구속영장) requested by the police (Article 201(8)).

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: We submit the letter of appointment and the application for participation and arrange the schedule with the investigator. Before questioning, we practise likely questions with you; in the interview room, we sit beside you, raise objections right away to leading or improper questions, and make sure they are written into the record. We also attend questioning while you are under arrest. If a questioning date has been set, let us know at 02-6951-4097.

faqs.q: Won't the investigator be more suspicious if I bring a lawyer?
faqs.a: Having a lawyer's assistance is a right protected by law, and the investigator must tell you before questioning that you can have it (Criminal Procedure Act Article 244-3(1)(iv)). There is no rule allowing you to be treated less favourably because a lawyer takes part.

faqs.q: Can I call a lawyer in the middle of questioning?
faqs.a: Even during questioning, you can say that you want a lawyer's assistance. Whether you use the right to remain silent and the right to counsel is written into the record (Criminal Procedure Act Article 244-3(2)), so you can simply say you will not make a statement until your lawyer arrives.

guides.title: The police want me to come in as a witness
guides.lead: If you were asked to come in for questioning as a witness rather than a suspect, as a rule it is up to you whether to appear and whether to make a statement. Here is why you still should not take it lightly, and what to check before the questioning.

seo.title: Asked to Appear as a Witness by the Korean Police | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: Do you have to go when the Korean police ask you to appear as a witness? Covers the court witness examination that can follow a refusal, when a witness becomes a suspect, what to watch for when reading and signing the statement record, and bringing a lawyer.

sections.title: What to check first
body: If all you heard on the phone was "we have a few questions," ask about the points below first. You need to know what they want to ask in order to prepare.
bullets: Ask what the case is about, the case number, the offense and who the suspect is.

Make sure you know whether you are a witness (참고인) or a suspect. There are even separate summons forms for suspects and for people who are not suspects (Police Investigation Rules (경찰수사규칙) Article 34).
Ask which part of what you saw or heard they want to ask about.
Check whether you have messages, transfer records or photos related to it.
If your own conduct could also be in question, get advice before you appear.

sections.title: Appearing as a witness is not compulsory
body: If needed for an investigation, an investigator can ask a person who is not a suspect to appear and give a statement, and can video-record it with that person's consent (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 221(1)). This is a voluntary investigation, so you will not be punished or face an arrest warrant for not going. Arrest warrants are a tool designed for suspects.

However, if a person who is clearly found to know facts essential to the investigation refuses to appear or to make a statement, the prosecutor can ask a judge to examine that person as a witness before the first trial date (Article 221-2). In that case, you would have to appear in court as a witness. If the date simply does not suit you, you can reschedule just as a suspect can (Investigation Rules (수사준칙) Article 19(6)).

sections.title: When a witness becomes a suspect
body: The Supreme Court holds that a person becomes a suspect, who must be told of the right to remain silent, when investigators conclude there are grounds to suspect that person of a crime and take steps to start investigating them (Supreme Court Decision 2011도8125, November 10, 2011). Even if you were called as a witness, you become a suspect from the moment grounds for suspicion emerge during questioning and an investigation into you begins.

If the questions shift from what you saw to holding you responsible for what you did, ask what your status is now. If you have become a suspect, you must be told of the right to remain silent and the right to a lawyer. If needed, you can say you want to pause the questioning and consult a lawyer.

sections.title: What to be careful about when giving a statement
body: A witness's statement is kept as a statement record (진술조서) and can become evidence at trial if certain requirements are met (Criminal Procedure Act Article 312(4)). You may also later be called to court as a witness about the same matters.
bullets: Separate what you saw yourself, what you heard from others and what you are guessing.
If you do not remember something, say you do not remember.
Read the statement record to the end and ask for anything wrong to be corrected.
You can later apply to inspect and copy the parts containing your statement (Investigation Rules Article 69(1)).

sections.title: Witnesses can also bring a lawyer
body: The principles on a lawyer's participation and assistance also apply when questioning or interviewing others involved in a case, such as witnesses (Investigation Rules Article 13(3); Police Investigation Rules Article 14). If there is any chance you could become a suspect, it is safer to go with a lawyer than alone. The rules also allow people who are not suspects to be questioned by online video link with a statement record prepared that way, so if you live far away, ask whether that is possible (Police Investigation Rules Article 39(2)).

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: A managing partner consults with you in person, hears where you stand in the case, and first looks at whether there is a risk you could become a suspect. After deciding with you how far to go in your statement, we sit in on the questioning and raise objections on the spot if the questions turn to holding you responsible. If you have been asked to appear, call us first at 02-6951-4097.

faqs.q: I've been asked to appear as a witness in a case where a family member is the suspect.
faqs.a: Witness questioning is not compulsory, so you can decline to answer questions you do not want to answer. Even if you end up testifying in court, you can refuse to give testimony that might expose a relative to prosecution or a guilty verdict (Criminal Procedure Act Article 148). Rather than saying anything untrue, choose not to answer.

faqs.q: It's a witness interview, but they say they will record it on video.
faqs.a: A witness's statement can be video-recorded only with that person's consent (Criminal Procedure Act Article 221(1)). You can decide for yourself whether to agree, so ask why and then decide.

guides.title: Attending phone forensics and the data selection process
guides.lead: If your phone was seized under a warrant or you handed it over voluntarily, the police will run a forensic analysis at the station. Here is the order in which the analysis proceeds, how to apply to attend, and what to check while you are there.

seo.title: Attending Phone Forensics in Korea: Application and Data Selection | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: The forensic process for a seized or voluntarily submitted phone in Korea, how to apply to attend, what to check during data selection, the Supreme Court en banc ruling limiting the scope of voluntary submission, the list of seized electronic data, deletion of unrelated data, and getting the phone back.

sections.title: What to do right away
body: There are things to do in the first few days after you hand over your phone. You are usually contacted separately about the forensics schedule, so prepare before then.
bullets: Find out whether the phone was taken under a warrant or you handed it over voluntarily, and get a copy of the list of seized items or the voluntary submission form.
Tell the investigator in charge clearly that you want to attend the forensics, and if possible put it in a text.
If you are given a form asking whether you will attend, mark that you wish to attend. If you sign that you will not attend, you lose the chance to give your views during selection.
Make a note of what data is on the phone. Writing down where unrelated photos and work files are makes it easier to give your views during selection.
If the device is essential for work, also ask about the procedure for getting it back.

sections.title: How forensics proceeds
body: The rule is to select only the information related to the allegation, where the phone is, and print or copy just that. If that is impossible or would make it extremely difficult to achieve the purpose, investigators can copy everything and take the copy, or seal the original device in the presence of the person whose phone is seized and take it away (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Articles 106(3) and 219; Investigation Rules (수사준칙) Article 41).

Once taken, the process runs in this order: copying (imaging), searching, and selecting information related to the allegation. When selection is finished, investigators must hand over a list of the electronic data seized, and data not on the list must be deleted or destroyed, or returned, with a confirmation given to you. The right of the person whose items were seized, and their lawyer, to be present is protected throughout (Investigation Rules Article 42).

sections.title: Voluntary submission has limits too
body: The Supreme Court held that even for a phone handed over voluntarily, if the person's intention is not clear, only information related to the allegation that prompted the submission, and with at least minimal value in proving it, may be seized. Where a third party such as the victim hands over the suspect's phone, the scope must be read even more narrowly, and procedural rights such as the suspect's right to be present and to receive a list must be respected (Supreme Court en banc Decision 2016도348, November 18, 2021). When you submit something voluntarily (임의제출), make sure the form clearly states what scope of data you are handing over.

sections.title: What to check when you attend
body: The Supreme Court held that if investigators take a device and copy, search and print from it without giving a chance to attend or taking steps to prevent unrelated information from being copied, it is in principle unlawful (Supreme Court en banc Order 2011모1839, July 16, 2015). When you attend, look at the following.
bullets: Whether only data matching the allegation and period in the warrant or voluntary submission form is selected
What search terms and periods are used to look for data
Whether photos, conversations or work files unrelated to the case are kept off the list
Whether your views on relevance are written into the record (Investigation Rules Article 42(5))
Whether you receive the list and the confirmation of deletion or return after selection

sections.title: Passwords and getting the phone back
body: If you are asked to unlock the phone or give your password, talk to your lawyer before answering. What you open can change the scope of selection.

If there is no need to keep holding it, you can get it back, and for a device you need to keep using, you can ask for provisional return (가환부) (Criminal Procedure Act Articles 133 and 219). If you disagree with a decision on seizure or return, you can ask the court to cancel or change it (Article 417).

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: Right after the seizure, we apply to attend the forensics, go into the selection process with you, raise objections to data unrelated to the allegation, and make sure those objections are recorded. For the suspect questioning that follows, we prepare likely questions based on the selected data. If you have handed over your phone, contact us at 02-6951-4097 before the forensics date is set.

faqs.q: What happens if I don't attend the forensics?
faqs.a: Investigators must still use reliable methods even if you do not attend (Investigation Rules Article 42(4)). But you lose the chance to give your views on the spot about what data is being selected and why, and you only find out later from the list.

faqs.q: What if data about a different case turns up during analysis?
faqs.a: The Supreme Court held that if investigators come across information about a separate crime by chance while looking for information on the allegation, they must stop searching and obtain a separate warrant, and even then the right to be present and the delivery of a list are required (en banc Order 2011모1839). If you attend, you can see this process for yourself.

guides.title: I received a notice of a travel ban
guides.lead: If you received a travel ban notice during an investigation, or were stopped from leaving at the airport, first find out why and until when. Here are the periods of a travel ban for investigation purposes, how to object, and how to ask for it to be lifted.

seo.title: Travel Ban During a Criminal Investigation in Korea: Notice and Objection | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: The periods of a travel ban for criminal investigation in Korea (1 month, 3 months, the validity of a warrant), when notice can be delayed, objecting within 10 days of notice, requests to lift the ban and administrative lawsuits, emergency travel bans and departure suspension for foreign nationals.

sections.title: What to check first
body: A travel ban (출국금지) is a decision made by the Minister of Justice, and how to respond depends on the grounds. If you received a notice or were told about it, sort out the points below first.
bullets: Check the grounds and period stated in the notice. When a travel ban is imposed or extended, the grounds and period must be given in writing (Immigration Act (출입국관리법) Article 4-4(1)).
Write down the date you received the notice. The deadline for an objection is counted from that day.
Find out which agency requested it and which case it relates to.
Gather materials showing why you need to leave, such as a business trip order, contract schedule, letter of invitation or a family member's medical certificate.
Check whether there is any questioning still to come and whether the case has been referred to prosecutors.

sections.title: Periods of a travel ban for investigation
body: If leaving the country is found to be inappropriate for a criminal investigation, departure can be banned for up to 1 month. If the investigation has been suspended because your whereabouts are unknown, or it is difficult to proceed because of flight or similar, the ban can be up to 3 months; for a suspended case where a warrant has been issued, it can last for the warrant's validity period. These periods can be extended (Immigration Act Articles 4(2) and 4-2). While a criminal trial is pending, departure can be banned for up to 6 months (Article 4(1)).

Notice can be withheld if there is a risk of serious and obvious obstruction to the investigation, but you must be notified once the total period including extensions exceeds 3 months (Article 4-4(3)(ii)). This is why some people first learn of a ban at the airport.

sections.title: Object within 10 days
body: You can file an objection with the Minister of Justice within 10 days of the day you received notice of the travel ban or its extension, or the day you learned of it. The Minister must decide within 15 days and, if unavoidable, can extend this once by up to 15 days (Immigration Act Article 4-5).

In the objection, set out the specific reasons you need to leave, along with circumstances showing there is no risk you will flee. Useful materials include a fixed home and job, family in Korea, a record of faithfully responding to summonses so far, a short travel schedule and a return ticket.

sections.title: Requests to lift the ban and administrative lawsuits
body: When the grounds for a travel ban no longer exist, it must be lifted immediately, and the agency that requested it must also ask for it to be lifted (Article 4-3). If your questioning is over or the case has ended with non-referral or non-indictment, that is a basis for asking for it to be lifted. Another option is to ask the investigator to bring the questioning forward so that it is done before you leave.

A travel ban is an administrative decision, so it can also be challenged in an administrative lawsuit. A lawsuit to cancel it must be filed within 90 days of learning of the decision (Administrative Litigation Act (행정소송법) Article 20).

sections.title: Emergency travel bans and foreign nationals
body: If a person suspected of an offense punishable by imprisonment, with or without labor, for a maximum of 3 years or more poses a risk of destroying evidence or fleeing and there is an urgent need, investigators can ask for a travel ban on the spot at the airport. It is lifted if approval is not requested from the Minister of Justice within 6 hours, or not obtained within 12 hours (Immigration Act Article 4-6). For foreign nationals, departure is suspended (출국정지) under the same procedure, and the provisions on travel bans apply accordingly (Article 29).

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: At the consultation, we check the grounds and period of the travel ban and decide what to do first, looking at your investigation and your travel plans together. If questioning remains, we work to bring the investigation to a close sooner by preparing you and attending with you, and Jisan Law also writes and submits the travel ban objection with the supporting circumstances and materials. If the objection does not lift the ban, we continue on to an administrative lawsuit. If your departure date is close, contact us right away at 02-6951-4097.

faqs.q: Does a travel ban mean I'm about to be detained?
faqs.a: No. A travel ban is an immigration procedure that stops you going abroad during an investigation or trial. Detention is a separate procedure in which a court must examine the grounds for detention and issue a warrant.

faqs.q: Can I check in advance whether I've been banned from leaving?
faqs.a: As a rule you are notified, but notice can be delayed for investigation reasons (Immigration Act Article 4-4(3)), so if you have plans abroad, check with an immigration office in advance. If you are under investigation, it is safer to tell the investigator in charge about your travel plans and arrange the questioning schedule around them.

guides.title: After the case goes to the Public Prosecution Service (supplementary investigation requests after referral)
guides.lead: Once you get a text saying the police have referred your case, a prosecutor at the Public Prosecution Service decides whether to indict. Here is what the prosecutor does under the procedure changed on October 2, 2026, and what to prepare if the case comes back to the police through a request for supplementary investigation.

seo.title: After Referral to the Public Prosecution Service in Korea: Supplementary Investigation Requests | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: For cases referred on or after October 2, 2026: how a Public Prosecution Service prosecutor checks the facts, what supplementary investigation requests cover, the 1-month deadline and extensions, preparing for police re-questioning, extended detention in custody cases, and transitional rules for cases referred before the change.

sections.title: What to do right away
body: A referral text does not mean the outcome has been decided. There are things to do while the prosecutor reviews the file.
bullets: Note the Public Prosecution Service office (district office or branch) and the case number shown in the referral text.

If you have not yet seen the police-stage record, apply to inspect and copy the part with your own statement. You can apply even while the prosecutor is reviewing the case (Investigation Rules (수사준칙) Article 69(1)).
Set out in a written opinion the materials and explanations you could not give at the police stage, and submit it to the prosecutor.
If you are negotiating a settlement, the settlement agreement and statement of non-punishment now go to the Public Prosecution Service office handling the case.
Keep a record of any contact from the Public Prosecution Service or the police, together with the case number.

sections.title: The prosecutor decides based on the file
body: From October 2, 2026, prosecutors no longer investigate directly; they decide whether to indict (Public Prosecution Service Act (공소청법) Article 4). If needed for that decision, the prosecutor can confirm the facts by hearing the views of the suspect or others involved, or by receiving written opinions, either in person or by video or phone. When hearing the suspect's views, the prosecutor must inform the suspect of the right to remain silent and the right to a lawyer, and allow the lawyer to take part (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 245-13(1) and (5); Investigation Rules Article 65-3).

Statements and materials confirmed this way cannot be used as evidence at trial (Article 245-13(3)). Even so, they are what the decision to indict turns on, so do not treat them lightly. In a complaint case, the prosecutor must decide whether to indict within 3 months of referral (Article 257, for complaints accepted on or after October 2, 2026).

sections.title: When the case goes back to the police for supplementary investigation
body: If needed to decide whether to indict, the prosecutor asks the police for supplementary investigation (보완수사요구). It can cover the offender, the evidence, conditions for prosecution, sentencing materials, the charge and how the criminal facts are framed, and the request must be made in writing with specific reasons and content (Criminal Procedure Act Article 197-2(1) and (2); Investigation Rules Article 59(3)).
