The police must carry out the supplementary investigation and report the result within 1 month of receiving the request, and the prosecutor can extend this by up to 1 month. The result must be reported within 3 months of the request, but the prosecutor can ask for further supplementary investigation after receiving it, so the case may go back and forth several times (Article 197-2(4) and (6); Investigation Rules Article 60-3). If the supplementary investigation shows there are no grounds for suspicion, the police can also decide not to refer the case after consulting the prosecutor (Investigation Rules Article 60(7)).

sections.title: First find out what is being supplemented
body: A request for supplementary investigation does not mean you will be indicted. It may be because the evidence is insufficient, or simply to sort out sentencing materials or the charge. If the police contact you to appear again, ask the investigator what is being supplemented and prepare materials for that point. If you are questioned again, read your first record beforehand so your account does not change. If they ask for settlement or compensation materials, now is the time to submit them.

sections.title: If you are detained
body: The police and the prosecutor can each hold a person in detention for 10 days, and if supplementary investigation is needed to decide on indictment, a judge can, on the prosecutor's application, allow one extension of up to 10 days (Criminal Procedure Act Articles 202, 203 and 205). A separate period may also be set for supplementary investigation, so detention cases move faster (Investigation Rules Article 60(5)). At this stage, we also consider a review of the legality of detention (구속적부심).

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: Right after referral, we apply to inspect the record and write a defense counsel's written opinion for the prosecutor. When the prosecutor hears your views to confirm the facts, we take part as your lawyer, and if supplementary investigation leads to more police questioning, we prepare you and attend with you. If you received a referral text, just show us the text as it is. Our consultation line, 02-6951-4097, is answered 24 hours a day.

faqs.q: What about cases referred before October 2?
faqs.a: The amended rules on supplementary investigation requests also apply to cases the prosecutor had already received when the changes took effect (Addenda Article 2 of Act No. 21857). However, among cases prosecutors were investigating, those where it is unavoidable, such as the statute of limitations being close, can continue to be investigated under the previous rules for up to 90 days from the effective date (Addenda Article 12), so you need to check which applies to your case.

faqs.q: I want to meet the prosecutor and explain in person.
faqs.a: The law gives complainants and certain others the right to request a meeting with the prosecutor (Criminal Procedure Act Article 245-13(2)). A suspect can submit written opinions and materials, and if the prosecutor thinks it necessary, the prosecutor will hear your views in person, by video or by phone. If there is a reason your views need to be heard, convey it through your lawyer.

guides.title: The police did not refer my case, but the complainant objected
guides.lead: Sometimes, just as you breathe a sigh of relief at a non-referral notice, you hear that the complainant has filed an objection. Here is how the case proceeds after an objection and what the suspect should prepare.

seo.title: Complainant's Objection After Non-Referral in Korea: How the Suspect Should Respond | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: When a complainant objects to a non-referral decision in Korea, the case is referred to a prosecutor. Covers the 3-month deadline for notices from October 2026, the prosecutor's supplementary investigation and re-investigation requests, the complainant's access to records, and the suspect's written opinion and record access.

sections.title: What to check first
body: Gather the non-referral decision and any contact you received afterwards in one place, and check the following.
bullets: See whether the reason for non-referral (불송치) was no suspicion (crime not established, or insufficient evidence), not a crime, no right to prosecute, or dismissal (Investigation Rules (수사준칙) Article 51).
Check whether the non-referral notice was given before or after October 2, 2026. The objection deadline differs.
Find out which Public Prosecution Service (공소청) office the case was referred to because of the objection, and the case number.
Apply to inspect and copy the record of the non-referred case (Investigation Rules Article 69(2)).
For the complainant's objection, you can also apply to inspect and copy the parts about the allegations against you, stating why you need them (same article, (3)).

sections.title: Once an objection is filed, the case goes to the prosecutor
body: A complainant or similar person who receives a non-referral notice can file an objection with the head of the police office, and once filed, the police must refer the case to the prosecutor without delay (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 245-7(1) and (4)). A person who reported the crime without being the victim can file an objection only for certain offenses set by presidential decree, such as false accusation (paragraph (2)).

The deadline for an objection is 3 months from the day the notice was received, and with good reason it can be extended up to 6 months from the date the record was sent (paragraph (3)). This deadline applies to notices given on or after October 2, 2026 (Addenda Article 7 of Act No. 21857). For cases notified before then, there is no deadline, so an objection can come in even after quite some time.

sections.title: What the prosecutor can do
body: In a case referred because of an objection, the prosecutor can look at the file and indict or decide not to indict, and if further investigation is needed, ask the police for supplementary investigation (Criminal Procedure Act Article 197-2(1)(iii)). The prosecutor can also confirm the facts by hearing the views of the suspect or the complainant (Article 245-13). The prosecutor may find grounds for suspicion from the file alone, contrary to the police, so responding at this stage is no less important than before the non-referral.

Even without an objection, if the prosecutor finds a non-referral unlawful or unjustified, the prosecutor can request a re-investigation within 3 months of receiving the file, and the police must finish it within 3 months (Article 245-8). That is why you should not throw away your materials after a non-referral.

sections.title: The complainant can see the records
body: Complainants and similar persons can apply to inspect and copy investigation records to make an objection, and all or part may be allowed if found necessary. Access is limited where there are reasons such as risk to privacy, and handing records to others in breach of the purpose or conditions is punishable (Article 245-12). On the basis that part of your statement may be disclosed to the complainant, we respond by identifying what the complainant is disputing in the objection.

sections.title: What the suspect should prepare
body: The prosecutor decides by weighing the police file, the objection and both sides' views. Prepare the following and submit them to the Public Prosecution Service office the case was referred to.
bullets: A written opinion explaining why the reasons for non-referral should stand
Materials rebutting each claim in the objection
Any new materials obtained since the police stage
A review of your police-stage statements in case of further questioning
Not contacting the complainant directly. If it looks like pressure, it counts against you

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: We apply to inspect and copy the non-referral record and the objection to see what the complainant is disputing, and write a defense counsel's written opinion for the prosecutor. When the prosecutor hears your views, we take part as your lawyer, and if supplementary investigation leads to more police questioning, we attend with you. If you have heard about an objection, contact us at 02-6951-4097 with the non-referral decision to hand.

faqs.q: Is the suspect told when an objection is filed?
faqs.a: The police must notify the person who filed the objection of the outcome (Criminal Procedure Act Article 245-7(4)). Suspects often find out when the prosecutor contacts them to confirm facts or when they are summoned for supplementary investigation, so do not miss contact from the police or the Public Prosecution Service even after a non-referral.

faqs.q: If the prosecutor decides not to indict in the end, is it completely over?
faqs.a: The complainant can appeal to the head of the Regional Public Prosecution Office within 30 days of receiving the non-indictment notice (Public Prosecution Service Act (공소청법) Article 57), and can then challenge it with an application for a court ruling on prosecution (재정신청). Keep your materials until these procedures are over.

guides.title: A foreign national has become a suspect
guides.lead: When a foreign national is investigated in Korea, procedures such as interpretation and consular notification are added, and the criminal outcome can also affect their stay. Here is what the person and their Korean family should know first.

seo.title: Foreign National Suspect in Korea: Police Questioning, Interpretation and Visa Issues | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: For foreign nationals questioned as suspects by the Korean police: the legal basis for requesting an interpreter, having the record read back through the interpreter, consular notification on arrest, family members applying for a lawyer's participation, and how departure suspension and criminal outcomes affect deportation and permission to stay.

sections.title: What to do right away
body: Summonses come in Korean, so a Korean family member is often the first to read them. Start with the points below.
bullets: Tell the investigator in advance that an interpreter is needed, and say exactly which language you need.
Check the passport, alien registration card (외국인등록증), status of stay and its expiry date.
If arrested, the person can ask for the consulate to be notified.
If a spouse, lineal relative or sibling is in Korea, they can apply for a lawyer's participation on the person's behalf (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 243-2(1)).
If an extension of stay or a planned departure date is close, note that date as well.

sections.title: Interpretation is a procedure you can request
body: When questioning a foreign national, the police must provide interpretation in a language the person understands (Police Investigation Rules (경찰수사규칙) Article 91(1)). At trial too, statements by a person who does not understand Korean are interpreted by an interpreter (Criminal Procedure Act Article 180). If you are questioned without an interpreter because you can handle everyday conversation, questions involving legal terms may be understood differently.

Having a family member act as interpreter is not recommended. Interpretation by someone with an interest in the case may be seen as unreliable. Instead, where psychological stability and smooth communication are needed in light of nationality or similar factors, a person in a relationship of trust can sit in (Article 244-5(ii)).

sections.title: Check the Korean record again through the interpreter
body: The record is written in Korean. The investigator must let you read it or read it to you (Criminal Procedure Act Article 244(2)), so ask for the whole record to be read back to you from the start through the interpreter. If anything was rendered differently from what you said, ask for a correction on the spot and have your objection noted in the record. The most important thing is not to sign without understanding it.

sections.title: If arrested, the consulate can be notified
body: When arresting or detaining a foreign national, the police must explain that the person can freely meet and communicate with consular officers, within the limits of Korean law, and can ask for the consulate to be notified of the arrest or detention. If requested, the consulate concerned is notified without delay (Police Investigation Rules Article 91(2) and (3)).

sections.title: The criminal outcome is reviewed separately for immigration
body: A foreign national's departure can be suspended (출국정지) because of an investigation or trial, and the rules on travel bans for Korean nationals apply accordingly (Immigration Act (출입국관리법) Article 29). A person released after being sentenced to imprisonment without labor or a heavier sentence (금고 이상의 형) may be subject to deportation (강제퇴거); for permanent residents, this applies only in exceptional cases, such as insurrection or treason offenses or a sentence of 5 years or more of imprisonment (Article 46). If the violation of law is serious, permission to stay can also be cancelled or changed (Article 89). If a violation of the Immigration Act, such as overstaying, is found during an investigation, the official must report it to the immigration office (Article 84(1)).

How a fine or a suspension of indictment (기소유예) alone affects a person's stay is decided case by case by the immigration authorities. That is why reducing the level of the outcome matters even more than for Korean nationals. From the investigation stage onward, prepare materials showing compensation and settlement and the person's life in Korea.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: The person and their Korean family can come to the consultation together, and a managing partner hears about the case and the immigration situation in person. We attend the questioning to check that the interpreted questions and answers match what is written in the record, and if the person has been arrested, we visit them and make sure consular notification and access to counsel are in place. At the decision stage, we submit materials on compensation and life in Korea in a written opinion. To book a consultation, call 02-6951-4097.

faqs.q: I think the interpreter translated what I said differently.
faqs.a: Say so right away during questioning and ask for it to be interpreted again. When reviewing the record, ask for it to be read back to you through the interpreter; if you request a correction, it must be added to the record (Criminal Procedure Act Article 244(2)).

faqs.q: Can foreign nationals get a court-appointed lawyer?
faqs.a: The same criteria apply regardless of nationality. If you have no lawyer at a detention warrant hearing, the judge appoints a court-appointed lawyer (국선변호인) (Criminal Procedure Act Article 201-2(8)), and after indictment the court appoints one depending on factors such as whether you are detained and the statutory penalty for the offense (Article 33).

guides.stage: A family member has been arrested
guides.title: When a family member is arrested
guides.lead: When you hear of an arrest, it is hard to know where to start. Within 48 hours of the arrest, it is decided whether to request a detention warrant, so here is what the family should do in that time, in order.

seo.title: Family Member Arrested in Korea: What to Do in the First 48 Hours | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: If a family member has been arrested by the Korean police, confirm the time of arrest and the police station and arrange a lawyer's visit as soon as possible. Covers the 48-hour deadline for a detention warrant request, family visits versus lawyer visits, documents for the pre-detention hearing, review of detention and bail.

sections.title: What to do right away
body: When you hear about the arrest, your first instinct is to rush to the police station. Often you go and come back without even seeing them, so take care of the following first, in order.
bullets: Find out which police station and department, what the offense is and when the arrest took place. Within 24 hours of an arrest, the police must notify the lawyer or a family member or other person named by the suspect of these details in writing (Investigation Rules (수사준칙) Article 33).
Write down the time of arrest. The 48-hour deadline for requesting a detention warrant (구속영장) runs from then.
Apply right away for a lawyer to visit. A spouse, lineal relatives and siblings can appoint a lawyer independently of the person arrested (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 30(2)).

Gather documents showing the person's home, job and family ties, such as a resident registration abstract, family relationship certificate, certificate of employment or business registration certificate.
If they take any medication, bring the name of the medicine and the prescription and tell the police station.

sections.title: What not to do
body: If family members contact the victim or others involved to explain things or rush into a settlement, investigators may see it as an attempt to sway them or destroy evidence. Settle only after deciding the timing and method with the lawyer.
Do not tidy up or delete anything on the arrested person's phone or computer either. A risk of destroying evidence is one of the grounds for detention.

sections.title: What happens in the 48 hours after arrest
body: Questioning starts right after the arrest and may continue several times if needed. If unavoidable to decide whether to request a detention warrant, questioning can even take place at night (Investigation Rules Article 21(2)). Statements made in a state of panic stay in the record as they are and become material for the warrant decision.

If the police do not apply for a warrant, or the prosecutor who receives the application does not request it from the court, the person is released. If a warrant is not requested within 48 hours of the arrest, the person must also be released immediately (Criminal Procedure Act Articles 200-2(5) and 200-4).

The police must also tell the arrested person, and the person they name, that they can ask the court to review whether the arrest is lawful (Article 214-2(2)). If the arrest itself seems flawed, consider this procedure.

sections.title: The pre-detention hearing decides whether detention is needed
body: Once a warrant is requested, a judge calls the suspect in and questions them directly. An arrested person is questioned by the day after the warrant request unless there are special circumstances (Criminal Procedure Act Article 201-2(1)). The lawyer can attend and give views, and if there is no lawyer, the court appoints a court-appointed lawyer.

At this pre-detention hearing (영장실질심사), the judge looks at whether there are reasonable grounds to suspect a crime, whether the person has a fixed residence, and whether there is a risk they will destroy evidence or flee (Articles 70 and 201). It is not a hearing on guilt or innocence, so it is important to show in documents the person's ties to their life here and that they have cooperated with the investigation. The result usually comes out late that night or early the next morning.
bullets: Home: resident registration abstract, lease agreement
Job: certificate of employment, business registration certificate, salary records
Family: family relationship certificate, details of dependants
Compensation: settlement agreement or proof of repayment (if any)

sections.title: Even if detained, there are ways to be released
body: Once detained, a person can be held by the police for 10 days and by the prosecutor for 10 days, and with a judge's permission this can be extended once by up to 10 days (Criminal Procedure Act Articles 202, 203 and 205).

If the detention seems unjustified in the meantime, you can request a review of the legality of detention (구속적부심사). Family members, people living with the detainee and their employer can also request it; the court holds a hearing within 48 hours of receiving the request and may order release on condition of paying a security deposit (Article 214-2). After indictment, you can apply for bail (보석) (Articles 94 and 95).

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: When you contact us, we visit the arrested person to hear what happened first, and decide with them what to say in questioning and what to hold back. We also attend questioning while they are under arrest.

If a warrant is requested, we attend the pre-detention hearing to present our views and submit the documents the family gathered together with a written opinion. After detention, we continue to attend questioning and consider a review of detention and bail.
Arrests happen at night and on weekends too. If a lawyer's visit is urgent, let us know first at 02-6951-4097. We answer 24 hours a day.

faqs.q: Can I talk to my arrested family member on the phone?
faqs.a: An arrested person cannot use their phone, so it is hard for family to contact them directly. Confirm the arrest and location through the department in charge at the police station; hearing about the case through a lawyer's visit is quicker.

faqs.q: If family visit the police cell, can they hear about the case?
faqs.a: Family visits to the police cell are often restricted or kept short depending on the investigation, and what is said may become known, so it is hard to discuss the case. A lawyer, or someone about to become the lawyer, can visit an arrested or detained person (Criminal Procedure Act Article 34), so discuss the case during the lawyer's visit.

faqs.q: What if there is no news after 48 hours?
faqs.a: If a detention warrant is not requested within 48 hours of the arrest, the person must be released immediately. If a warrant has been requested, the judge notifies the suspect and the lawyer of the hearing date and place (Criminal Procedure Act Article 201-2(3)).

guides.title: If you were arrested in the act or under an emergency arrest
guides.lead: This guide is for people who were arrested on the spot without a warrant, or who were arrested and then released. Here is what happens in the 48 hours from the moment of arrest, and what to say and what to hold back in that time.

seo.title: Arrested in the Act or Under Emergency Arrest in Korea: How to Respond | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: The requirements for arrest in the act and emergency arrest in Korea, the rights you must be told of and family notification right after arrest, detention warrant requests and release within 48 hours, the prosecutor's pre-warrant meeting introduced in October 2026, and reviewing arrest documents and preparing for questioning after release.

sections.title: What to do right away
body: Right after an arrest, panic makes it easy to say whatever comes to mind. Take care of just these five things first.
bullets: Ask what you are suspected of and how you are being arrested. The police must tell you the gist of the alleged facts, the reason for arrest and that you can appoint a lawyer, give you a chance to explain, and also tell you of the right to remain silent (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 200-5; Investigation Rules (수사준칙) Article 32).
Remember the time of arrest. The 48 hours are counted from then.
Name a family member to be told of the arrest. If you have no lawyer, the family member or other person you name is notified in writing within 24 hours (Investigation Rules Article 33).
Say that you want a lawyer, and do not talk about the case at length before the lawyer arrives.
If you take medication or are hurt or unwell, say so right away.

sections.title: There are two kinds of arrest without a warrant
body: A person caught in the act (현행범인) is someone committing a crime or who has just committed one, and anyone can arrest them without a warrant. If a member of the public catches them, they must hand them over to the police immediately (Criminal Procedure Act Articles 211, 212 and 213). When making an arrest in the act, the police must consider whether there is an urgent need that makes immediate arrest unavoidable (Police Investigation Rules (경찰수사규칙) Article 52(1)).

An emergency arrest (긴급체포) is made when there are reasonable grounds to suspect an offense punishable by imprisonment, with or without labor, for a maximum of 3 years or more, there is a risk of destroying evidence or fleeing, and there is no time to get a warrant. The police must get the prosecutor's approval immediately and must request it within 12 hours. If approval is not given, the person is released immediately (Article 200-3; Investigation Rules Article 27).

sections.title: The 48 hours after arrest
body: To keep holding a person, a detention warrant (구속영장) must be requested within 48 hours of the arrest; otherwise the person must be released immediately (Criminal Procedure Act Articles 200-2(5), 200-4 and 213-2). A person arrested in the act is released right away if questioning shows there is no need for continued custody (Investigation Rules Article 28). During these 48 hours, questioning can take place even at night to decide whether to apply for a warrant (Article 21(2)).

From October 2, 2026, when the police apply for a detention warrant, the prosecutor can meet the suspect before requesting it, and must allow the lawyer's assistance at that meeting (Criminal Procedure Act Article 201(7) and (8)). If the arrest itself was unjustified, you can ask the court for a review of the legality of the arrest (체포적부심사) (Article 214-2).

sections.title: What to be careful about at the scene and in the cell
body: What you say at the scene is also written into the arrest report or an investigation report. Even if you feel wronged, explain the facts in the interview room with your lawyer. Swearing at or pushing a police officer can add a charge of obstructing official duties. Do not contact the victim or anyone who was with you either, as it may look like an attempt to destroy evidence.

sections.title: What to do after release
body: Release does not mean the case is over. In most cases the investigation continues without detention, and you will be summoned again. An arrested suspect or their lawyer can inspect and copy the arrest-in-the-act report or the emergency arrest report (Investigation Rules Article 69(4)), so start by checking what facts you were arrested for.

If you were released without a warrant after an emergency arrest, you cannot be arrested again without a warrant for the same criminal facts (Criminal Procedure Act Article 200-4(3)). If items such as your phone were taken at the time of arrest, get the list of seized items; if no warrant was issued, you can get them back (Article 217).

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: When contacted, we visit the arrested person to hear what happened and attend the questioning that continues while they are under arrest. If a warrant is applied for, we attend the pre-detention hearing (영장실질심사) to present our views, and after release we review the arrest documents and prepare for the next questioning. A family member can call 02-6951-4097 on your behalf. We answer 24 hours a day.

faqs.q: I was arrested in the act and released a few hours later. Is it over?
faqs.a: You were released because there was no need for continued custody; the investigation itself continues (Investigation Rules Article 28). You may soon be contacted for questioning as a suspect, so write down what happened that day in time order and secure any video from the scene and witnesses' contact details.

faqs.q: A shop owner caught me and handed me over to the police.
faqs.a: Anyone can arrest a person caught in the act without a warrant, but they must hand the person over to the police immediately, and the police must ask for the name and address of the person who made the arrest and the reason for it (Criminal Procedure Act Articles 212 and 213). If how the arrest happened is disputed, that person's statement and video from the scene become important.

guides.title: Preparing for the day of the pre-detention hearing
guides.lead: When a detention warrant is requested, a judge meets the suspect in person and decides whether to detain them. Here, in order, is the prosecutor's meeting before the hearing, what to bring on the day, the questions asked in court and where you wait for the result.

seo.title: Pre-Detention Hearing in Korea: How to Prepare and What Happens | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: From the notice of a pre-detention hearing to the prosecutor's pre-warrant meeting introduced in October 2026, what items and documents to bring, what the judge asks in the closed hearing, family statements, waiting for the result, and what happens after a warrant is issued or rejected.

sections.title: What to check first
body: The hearing date is set suddenly. If the suspect has been arrested, the rule is that the hearing takes place by the day after the warrant request, so there is only about a day to prepare (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 201-2(1)).
bullets: The hearing date, the court and the courtroom location. The judge notifies the suspect and the lawyer of the date and place (same article, (3)).

If the warrant was requested while the suspect was not under arrest, the court brings them in under a warrant to appear before questioning them (same article, (2)). Check the exact time and place with the investigator.
Check that the lawyer has reviewed the detention warrant request (구속영장청구서) and attached documents submitted to the judge (Criminal Procedure Rules (형사소송규칙) Article 96-21).
Pass the documents the family gathered on home, job and family ties, plus any medical certificates and settlement agreements, to the lawyer.
If there is no lawyer, the judge appoints a court-appointed lawyer on their own initiative (Article 201-2(8)).

sections.title: There is now a prosecutor's meeting before the request
body: From October 2, 2026, when the police apply for a detention warrant (구속영장), the prosecutor can meet the suspect or ask the police for their views to decide whether to request it. At the meeting, the suspect must be able to have a lawyer's assistance, including the lawyer taking part, and is told of the right to remain silent (Criminal Procedure Act Article 201(7) and (8); Investigation Rules (수사준칙) Article 29-2). The meeting is held in person, by video or by phone. If there were problems in the investigation or there are reasons why detention is not needed, raise them here first, before you see the judge.

sections.title: How the hearing proceeds
body: The hearing is not public. The judge tells the suspect the gist of the criminal facts in the warrant, and that they may refuse to make statements and may state facts in their favour. The judge then asks what is needed to decide whether detention is necessary, including personal matters such as career, family relationships and friendships (Criminal Procedure Rules Articles 96-14 and 96-16).

The judge looks at whether there are reasonable grounds to suspect a crime, whether the person has a fixed residence and whether there is a risk of destroying evidence or fleeing, and also considers the seriousness of the crime, the risk of reoffending and the risk of harm to the victim (Criminal Procedure Act Articles 70 and 201). The suspect can ask the lawyer for help even during the hearing.

sections.title: What to bring on the day and how to speak
body: If a warrant is issued, the suspect is held straight away, so prepare on the assumption that they will not go home.
bullets: Neat clothes, glasses, medication and prescriptions
Family and lawyer phone numbers written on paper (you may not be able to use your phone)
Short, consistent answers. Do not bring up anything new that differs from the record
Speak specifically about having cooperated with summonses, your home and job, and your plan to compensate the victim

sections.title: Where you wait for the result, and afterwards
body: After the hearing, the suspect usually waits for the result somewhere such as a police station cell, and the result often comes out late that night or early the next morning. If the warrant is rejected, the suspect is released and the investigation continues without detention. If it is issued, the police can detain for 10 days and the prosecutor for 10 days, and if a request for supplementary investigation or similar is needed, this can be extended once by up to 10 days with a judge's permission (Criminal Procedure Act Articles 202, 203 and 205).

Even after a warrant is issued, you can request a review of the legality of detention (구속적부심사) (Article 214-2). Prepare it around circumstances that have arisen since the warrant was issued, such as a settlement or compensation.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: We prepare for the prosecutor's meeting from the warrant application stage, attend the pre-detention hearing (영장실질심사) after reviewing the record to present our views, and submit the documents the family gathered with a written opinion. If the warrant is issued, we visit right away, attend questioning during detention and consider a review of detention. If you have been notified of a hearing date, let us know right away at 02-6951-4097.

faqs.q: Can family members go into the courtroom?
faqs.a: As a rule the hearing is closed, but the judge can allow relatives to observe if appropriate (Criminal Procedure Rules Article 96-14). A legal representative, spouse, lineal relatives, siblings, family, people living with the suspect and the employer can state their views with the judge's permission (Article 96-16(6)), so let the lawyer know in advance.

faqs.q: Can the hearing date be postponed?
faqs.a: The judge can change the date if there are special circumstances that make it impossible to hold the hearing on the set date (Criminal Procedure Rules Article 96-22). However, if the suspect is under arrest, time limits apply, so postponing is difficult.

faqs.q: If the warrant is rejected, can it be requested again?
faqs.a: It can be requested again for the same criminal facts, but the request must then state the purpose and reasons for requesting again (Criminal Procedure Act Article 201(5) and (6)). Even after a rejection, it is important to keep responding to summonses and not to contact the victim.

guides.title: Visiting a detained family member and what the family should do
guides.lead: When a family member is detained, visits, sending money and items, and sorting out work and household matters all come at once. Here is how visits work at police cells and detention centres, what you can send in, and what the family needs to take on.

seo.title: Visiting a Detained Family Member in Korea: Visits, Money and Items | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: How to visit a detained family member at a Korean police cell or detention centre, how often and for how long, how lawyer visits differ, sending money (custody funds), items and food, letters and bans on visits, and what the family should handle, such as hiring a lawyer and preparing documents.
keywords: what family should do detention Korea

sections.title: What to do right away
body: When you hear of the detention, you want to see them first. To avoid a wasted trip, check the following in order before you go.
bullets: Find out where they are now. At the police stage they are usually in a police station cell, and once the case is referred to the Public Prosecution Service (공소청), they are moved to a detention centre (구치소).
Call the custody department of the police station or the detention centre's public service office to ask about visiting hours and what to bring. Many detention centres require advance booking.
Bring your ID when you visit.
Make a list of things they need right away, such as a change of clothes, glasses, medication and prescriptions. What can be brought in differs by facility, so check first.
Arrange a lawyer's visit separately. Discuss the case during the lawyer's visit.

sections.title: Family visits (general visits)
body: Detained people can also see visitors from outside. A police station cell is treated as a pre-trial detention room of a correctional facility, and the same law applies (Administration and Treatment of Correctional Institution Inmates Act (형의 집행 및 수용자의 처우에 관한 법률) Articles 41 and 87). For people detained before a final judgment, general visits are once a day, for up to 30 minutes each, during working hours excluding public holidays (Enforcement Decree of the same Act, Articles 58 and 101).

General visits take place across a partition, and if there is a risk of destroying evidence or similar, a correctional officer can listen and take notes, or record audio or video. You are told in advance if it will be recorded (Act Article 41(4) and (5)). So during visits, it is safer not to talk about the victim, accomplices or the case itself.

sections.title: Lawyer visits are different
body: A lawyer, or someone about to become the lawyer, can visit a detained person and exchange documents with them (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 34). Correctional officers cannot be present at or listen to lawyer visits, there is no limit on time or frequency, and the meeting takes place without a partition (Administration and Treatment of Correctional Institution Inmates Act Articles 41(2) and 84). Lawyer visits also do not count toward the once-a-day limit on family visits.

sections.title: Sending money and items
body: Money held in custody for a detainee, commonly called yeongchigeum (영치금), is permitted when you apply to the facility to deliver it, unless it would threaten the safety or order of the facility (same Act, Article 27). With this money, the detained person buys food and daily necessities with the warden's permission (Article 24). Facilities also run a system where family members choose food or daily necessities at the detention centre's public service office to be delivered, commonly known as sasik (사식).

Each facility sets which items can be sent in and the limits, so check with the public service office. You can also exchange letters, which in principle are not censored, but do not write requests related to the case or anything about the victim (Article 43).

sections.title: What the family needs to take on
body: Apart from visits, there is a lot for the family to handle. Split the tasks among you.
bullets: Hiring a lawyer. A spouse, lineal relatives and siblings can appoint a lawyer independently of the detained person (Criminal Procedure Act Article 30(2)).
Contact their workplace or school to arrange leave. Making sure it is not treated as unauthorised absence also helps later when seeking release.
Gather a resident registration abstract, family relationship certificate, certificate of employment and lease agreement. These are used when requesting a review of detention or bail.
Do not contact the victim directly. Settle only after deciding the timing and method with the lawyer.
Family members, people living with the detainee and their employer can also request a review of the legality of detention (Article 214-2(1)).

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: We visit the detained person to hear about the case, and keep the family updated on progress as far as can be shared. We attend questioning that continues during detention and use the documents the family gathered to consider a review of detention or bail. If a visit is urgent, let us know first at 02-6951-4097. We answer on weekends too.

faqs.q: I was told visits have been banned.
faqs.a: If there is a risk of flight or destroying evidence, visits by anyone other than the lawyer can be banned. Even so, clothes, food and medical supplies cannot be stopped from being passed on (Criminal Procedure Act Articles 91 and 209). A visit ban ordered by the police lapses once the case is referred to prosecutors (Police Investigation Rules (경찰수사규칙) Article 59(3)).

faqs.q: Can friends visit too, not just family?
faqs.a: Visits from outside are not limited to family. But general visits are once a day, so it helps to decide in advance who will go. How many people can go in at once differs by facility.

faqs.q: Do they have to wear prison clothes to trial?
faqs.a: People detained before a final judgment can wear their own clothes when attending investigations or trials, except where there is a high risk of escape or a particular reason it is unsuitable (Administration and Treatment of Correctional Institution Inmates Act Article 82). The family can simply send in clean clothes.

guides.title: Review of detention and bail
guides.lead: Even after detention, there are ways to be released. Here is how a review of the legality of detention, requested before indictment, differs from bail, requested after indictment, who can request them and when, and what to prepare.

seo.title: Review of Detention vs Bail in Korea: Differences and How to Apply | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: The difference between a review of the legality of detention before indictment and bail after indictment in Korea, which family members can apply, the hearing within 48 hours and decision within 24 hours, exceptions to mandatory bail, security deposits and surety insurance, and preparing materials focused on changes since the warrant.
keywords: review of legality of detention Korea
release of suspect on deposit Korea

sections.title: What to check first
body: Which procedure to use depends on whether you are before or after indictment. If you have received an indictment (공소장), you have already been indicted.
bullets: Confirm the date of detention and the current stage (police, Public Prosecution Service (공소청) or court).
Get a certified copy of the detention warrant (구속영장). It must be provided on request to anyone who can apply for a review of detention (Investigation Rules (수사준칙) Article 34).
Calculate the remaining detention period: 10 days with the police, 10 days with the prosecutor and a 10-day extension (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Articles 202, 203 and 205).
Write down what has changed since the warrant was issued, such as a settlement, compensation, a place to live, a confirmation of return to work or deteriorating health.

sections.title: Review of the legality of detention (before indictment)
body: The detained suspect, their lawyer, legal representative, spouse, lineal relatives, siblings, family members, people living with them and their employer can apply to the court for a review of the legality of detention (구속적부심사). The court questions the suspect and examines the record within 48 hours of receiving the application and decides on release or dismissal; the decision is made within 24 hours of the end of the hearing (Criminal Procedure Act Article 214-2(1) and (4); Criminal Procedure Rules (형사소송규칙) Article 106). As a rule, the judge who issued the warrant cannot take part in the review.

The court can order release on condition of paying a security deposit and can attach conditions such as a restriction on residence. However, if there is a strong risk of destroying evidence or of harm to the victim or others, release on deposit is not ordered (same article, (5) and (6)). The decision cannot be appealed.

sections.title: Bail (after indictment)
body: The indicted defendant and the family members and others listed above apply to the court (Article 94). Once bail (보석) is requested, it must be granted unless one of the exceptions below applies (Article 95), and even if an exception applies, it can be granted if there is good reason (Article 96). Unless there are special circumstances, the court decides within 7 days of receiving the application (Criminal Procedure Rules Article 55).
bullets: Offenses punishable by death, life imprisonment, or imprisonment with or without labor for a maximum of more than 10 years
Repeat offenses or habitual offenses
When there is a strong risk of destroying evidence or fleeing
When the defendant's residence is unclear
When there is a strong risk of harm to the victim, witnesses or others

sections.title: Bail conditions and deposits
body: The court sets one or more conditions, such as a written pledge to appear, an agreement to pay a deposit, a restriction on residence, a ban on approaching the victim, a written undertaking by another person to secure the defendant's appearance (출석보증서), a pledge not to leave the country, or a deposit to compensate the victim (Article 98). Conditions the defendant cannot meet with their financial means cannot be imposed, and the deposit can be replaced by a surety document submitted by someone other than the defendant (Articles 99(2) and 100(3)).

If, after release, you fail to answer a summons without good reason or breach a condition, bail can be revoked and the deposit forfeited (Articles 102 and 103). Breaching a condition without good reason can also lead to an administrative fine or confinement.

sections.title: What to prepare
body: Resubmitting the same materials as when the warrant was issued rarely changes the result. Build your application around what has changed since then. If there is an urgent reason such as a serious illness or a family funeral, you can also consider a suspension of the execution of detention (구속집행정지), which pauses the detention for a time (Articles 101(1) and 209).
bullets: Home: resident registration abstract, lease agreement
Job: certificate of employment, business registration certificate, confirmation of return to work
Family: family relationship certificate, materials showing dependants
Compensation: settlement agreement, statement of non-punishment, deposit certificate
Health: medical certificate, medical records

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: We visit to hear the circumstances and first decide whether it is better to apply now or wait and apply once new circumstances are in place. We write the application, organise and submit the materials, and on the hearing date Jisan Law attends and presents our views (Criminal Procedure Act Article 214-2(9)). If your family is gathering documents, contact us at 02-6951-4097.

faqs.q: If the review of detention is dismissed, can I apply again?
faqs.a: If you apply again against the same detention warrant, it can be dismissed without a hearing (Criminal Procedure Act Article 214-2(3)(i)). The dismissal cannot be appealed either, so consider applying for bail after indictment.

faqs.q: Is bail possible before indictment?
faqs.a: Before indictment, you apply for a review of the legality of detention rather than bail, and as part of that the court can order release on condition of paying a deposit (Criminal Procedure Act Article 214-2(5)). This is what is often called "bail for suspects."

faqs.q: I was released after a review of detention. Can I be detained again?
faqs.a: A suspect released by a decision on review of detention will not be arrested or detained again for the same criminal facts unless they flee or destroy evidence. If released on a deposit condition, failing to answer a summons without good reason or breaching a condition are also exceptions (Criminal Procedure Act Article 214-3).

guides.title: When you receive an indictment
guides.lead: If the court has sent you a copy of the indictment, your trial has started. Here, in order, is the written opinion due within 7 days, reviewing the record, what happens at the first hearing and the deadline to appeal after sentencing.

seo.title: Received an Indictment in Korea: How to Prepare for a Criminal Trial | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: If you received a copy of an indictment from a Korean court, you must submit a written opinion within 7 days and apply to the Public Prosecution Service to inspect and copy the investigation record. Covers when a court-appointed lawyer is assigned, how the first hearing proceeds, preparing sentencing materials and the appeal deadline.

sections.title: What to do right away
body: When the envelope with the indictment arrives, check the date first. Deadlines are counted from the day you received it.
bullets: Write down the date you received the indictment (공소장). Within 7 days of that date, you must submit a written opinion to the court stating, among other things, whether you admit the charged facts (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 266-2).
Read the charge, the applicable provisions and the charged facts line by line, and mark anything that is not true.
Check whether the accompanying documents include information about a court-appointed lawyer (국선변호인). Decide whether to hire a lawyer or request a court-appointed one.
Get ready to apply to the Public Prosecution Service (공소청) to inspect and copy the investigation record. If you have a lawyer, the lawyer applies (Article 266-3).
If your address has changed, tell the court right away. If you miss a hearing because you did not receive the summons, it can count against you.

sections.title: What not to do
body: Do not write in the written opinion that you admit everything before you have seen the record. The opinion is also passed to the prosecutor (Article 266-2(2)). It is not too late to decide whether to admit the charges after seeing the record, and until then you can submit an opinion saying you will state your position after reviewing the record.
Do not contact the victim or witnesses to ask them to change their statements. It will count heavily against you in bail and sentencing decisions and can be a separate crime.

Do not decide on your own to put off a hearing or miss it without notice. The summons states that if you fail to appear without good reason, a detention warrant may be issued on the grounds that you may flee (Article 74).

sections.title: You need to see the record to know what to dispute
body: The indictment only states conclusions. To know which statements and evidence led to those conclusions, you need to look at the investigation record. The defendant or their lawyer can apply to inspect and copy the documents the prosecutor will submit as evidence, the list of witnesses and documents related to the defendant's arguments (Article 266-3). If the defendant has a lawyer, the defendant can only apply to inspect, not copy.

Once you have seen the record, you decide whether to consent to each piece of evidence. For statement records you do not consent to, the person who made the statement often has to appear and testify in court, so this choice sets the length and direction of the trial.

sections.title: When a court-appointed lawyer is assigned
body: If the defendant has no lawyer, the court appoints one on its own initiative when the defendant is detained, is a minor or aged 70 or over, has both hearing and speech impairments, is suspected of having a mental disability, or is charged with an offense punishable by death, life imprisonment, or imprisonment with or without labor for a minimum of 3 years or more (Criminal Procedure Act Article 33(1)).
In other cases, the court appoints one on request if the defendant cannot hire a lawyer because of poverty or similar reasons (Article 33(2)).

sections.title: What happens at the first hearing
body: The first hearing begins with notice of the right to remain silent and confirmation of identity. The prosecutor then reads out the charged facts, and the defendant and lawyer state whether they admit them. Next come views on the evidence, followed by the examination of evidence. As a rule, a criminal trial can only be held if the defendant appears (Article 276).

Where the charges are admitted, the hearing may close at the first session with sentencing at the next. Prepare materials to be considered in sentencing, such as a settlement agreement, proof of compensation, a letter of remorse and a certificate of employment, before the first hearing. The law does not set how long it takes to get to the first hearing; it depends on the court. If the victim applies, the court must call the victim as a witness and hear their views (Article 294-2), so in cases without a settlement, prepare for that testimony as well.

sections.title: 7 days after sentencing
body: To challenge the judgment, you must appeal within 7 days of the sentencing date (Article 358). After appealing, once you are notified that the record has been sent on, you must submit a statement of reasons for appeal within 20 days of that day (Article 361-3). If you miss these deadlines, you lose the chance to challenge the judgment, so write the dates down separately.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: Once you receive the indictment, we first apply to inspect and copy the record and review the records and evidence from the investigation stage. Points to dispute are disputed with evidence, and where the charges are admitted, we gather and organise compensation and sentencing materials. If we handled the case from the investigation stage, we build on the questioning records and written opinions from that time.
The written opinion is due within 7 days, so it is better to move quickly. If you have received an indictment, contact us at 02-6951-4097 and tell us the date you received it.

faqs.q: I received the indictment, but there is no date for the first hearing yet.
faqs.a: The copy of the indictment only needs to be served at least 5 days before the first hearing (Criminal Procedure Act Article 266), and the law does not set how long it takes to reach the first hearing. Once the date is set, the court will send a summons.

faqs.q: Do I have to attend the trial in person?
faqs.a: As a rule, a criminal trial cannot be held without the defendant (Criminal Procedure Act Article 276). Keep the hearing dates clear even if you have a lawyer. If you are ill or have an unavoidable reason, tell the court in advance and submit supporting documents.

faqs.q: I'm admitting everything. Do I still need a lawyer?
faqs.a: Where the charges are admitted, sentencing materials decide the outcome. It is important to set out in documents your progress in compensating the victim, your remorse and efforts to prevent reoffending, and your family and work situation; Jisan Law gathers these materials with the defendant and submits them as sentencing materials.

guides.title: When you receive a summary order imposing a fine
guides.lead: If the court has sent you a summary order, you need to decide within 7 days whether to request a formal trial. Here is what changes if you do, and when and how to pay the fine.

seo.title: Summary Order in Korea: 7 Days to Request a Formal Trial, and Paying the Fine | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: If you receive a summary order in Korea, you can request a formal trial within 7 days of notice. Step by step: whether the sentence can get heavier, withdrawing the request, the deadline for paying the fine and paying in instalments, applying for community service instead, and confinement in a workhouse.
keywords: no heavier type of sentence formal trial
community service instead of fine Korea

sections.title: A summary order is a fine decided on the papers
body: If the prosecutor considers a fine appropriate, they request a summary order (약식명령) instead of a formal trial. Without holding a hearing, the court looks only at the record, sets a fine, a petty fine or confiscation, and sends out a summary order (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 448). If you leave it, it becomes final and you will have a criminal record for a fine. If the court considers a summary order inappropriate, it may send the case to a formal trial (Article 450). Because the decision is made without giving the defendant a chance to speak in court, the written opinions and materials submitted at the investigation stage are what the decision rests on.

The summary order states the charge, the criminal facts, the amount of the fine and the period of confinement in a workhouse (노역장 유치) if the fine is not paid. Write down the date you received it first.

sections.title: Request a formal trial within 7 days
body: The defendant can request a formal trial (정식재판) in writing from the court that issued the summary order within 7 days of being notified of it (Criminal Procedure Act Article 453). The period is counted from the day after you receive it, and if the last day is a Saturday or public holiday, it runs to the next weekday (Article 66). If a family member living with you received the post on your behalf, that day may count, so check your post right away.
In a formal trial, you are tried again in court. It makes sense if there are facts to dispute, or if you have new materials to submit, such as a settlement reached after the summary order.

sections.title: The fine can also go up if you request a trial
body: In a case where the defendant requested a formal trial, the court cannot impose a heavier type of sentence than in the summary order, for example imprisonment instead of a fine (Criminal Procedure Act Article 457-2(1)). However, within the same fine, the amount can go up, and in that case the court must state the reasons in the judgment (same article, (2)).

So do not assume that requesting a formal trial will always reduce the fine. First work out what new materials you have and whether there are facts to dispute. A request for a formal trial can be withdrawn until the first-instance judgment is pronounced (Article 454); if you withdraw, the summary order becomes final as it is, and you cannot request again.

sections.title: What to weigh when deciding whether to request
body: A formal trial takes time and money. If it is hard to decide, one option is to first inspect and copy the investigation record to see what evidence the criminal facts were based on, and then decide. Go through the points below one by one.
bullets: Whether any of the criminal facts are written differently from what happened
Whether a settlement or compensation has been made since the summary order
Whether a fine affects your job or professional qualifications
Whether you can take time to attend each hearing
Whether disputing the case could bring new unfavourable facts to light

sections.title: You must attend a formal trial in person
body: As a rule, a formal trial also requires the defendant to attend. If a defendant who requested a formal trial fails to appear on the hearing date, and again fails to appear without good reason on the new date set, the court can give judgment without the defendant's statement (Criminal Procedure Act Articles 458(2) and 365).

If something comes up that prevents you from attending, apply to the court in advance to change the date and submit supporting documents such as a medical certificate or proof of a business trip. If a settlement was reached after the summary order, submit the settlement agreement before the first hearing.

sections.title: How to pay the fine
body: The fine must be paid within 30 days of the day the judgment becomes final (Criminal Act (형법) Article 69(1)). If paying in one go is difficult, apply to the execution department of the Public Prosecution Service for payment in instalments or a postponement (Public Prosecution Service Rules on the Execution of Property Penalties (재산형 등에 관한 공소청 집행사무규칙) Article 12). Those eligible include basic livelihood security recipients, some near-poverty households, people with disabilities, people receiving unemployment benefits, people with a decision to open individual rehabilitation, and people who themselves or whose household members need treatment for a month or more; the prosecutor decides based on their circumstances, the amount and whether they can actually pay. The period is up to 6 months and, if the reason continues, can be extended twice by 3 months each time.

If you cannot pay because of financial hardship, for a fine of 5 million won or less you can apply to do community service instead of workhouse confinement. Apply to the prosecutor at the District Public Prosecution Office with jurisdiction over your home within 30 days of the prosecutor's payment order; if you have permission to pay in instalments or postpone, you can apply within that permitted period (Act on Special Cases concerning Community Service for Persons Who Fail to Pay Fines (벌금 미납자의 사회봉사 집행에 관한 특례법) Article 4; Enforcement Decree Article 2). You cannot apply if you were sentenced to imprisonment along with the fine or are in custody for another case. If you never pay the fine, you may be confined in a workhouse for the period stated in the summary order (Criminal Act Articles 69(2) and 70).

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: At the consultation, we look at your summary order and tell you whether there is a reason to request a formal trial. If you request one, we apply to inspect and copy the investigation record to find what can be disputed, organise any new materials and prepare for trial. The 7-day deadline is short, so check the date you received the summary order and contact us at 02-6951-4097.

faqs.q: How do I write a request for a formal trial?
faqs.a: Submit it in writing to the court that issued the summary order. It is enough to state the case number, your name and that you are requesting a formal trial; you can give the detailed reasons at trial. Start by counting the days so you do not miss the 7-day deadline.

faqs.q: The criminal facts in the summary order are not true.
faqs.a: If it becomes final as it is, you will have been fined for those facts. To dispute the facts, request a formal trial within 7 days and inspect and copy the investigation record to see what evidence those facts were based on.

faqs.q: If I can't pay the fine, do I go straight to the workhouse?
faqs.a: If you do not pay within 30 days of the order becoming final, you will receive a reminder to pay, and if you still do not pay, workhouse confinement may be carried out. Before that, consider payment in instalments, a postponement or an application for community service.

guides.title: Court-appointed or privately hired lawyer: what is the difference?
guides.lead: If a notice about a court-appointed lawyer arrived with your indictment, you need to decide how you will be represented. Here is when a court-appointed lawyer is assigned, how to request one, and what to consider if you are thinking of hiring your own lawyer.

seo.title: Court-Appointed vs Private Defense Lawyer in Korea | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: When a Korean court appoints a defense lawyer on its own initiative and when you must request one, how their powers compare with a privately hired lawyer and what differs. Also covers asking to change a court-appointed lawyer, cancellation of the appointment when you hire your own, and the difference at the investigation stage.

sections.title: What to check first
body: When an indictment is sent, the court sends a defendant without a lawyer written information about court-appointed lawyers (Criminal Procedure Rules (형사소송규칙) Article 17). Take out the notice in the envelope first and check the following in order.
bullets: See whether the notice says it is a "case that cannot proceed without a lawyer." If so, the court will appoint a lawyer unless you hire one yourself.
If it is not such a case, consider whether you cannot afford to hire a lawyer. In that case, a lawyer is appointed only if the defendant requests one (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 33(2)).

If you plan to request one, prepare documents showing your financial situation, such as a certificate of benefit receipt, proof of health insurance premium payments or a certificate of income (Criminal Procedure Rules Article 17-2).
Check the date of the first hearing and work out whether there will be time for a lawyer to review the record before then.

sections.title: When the court appoints a lawyer automatically
body: If the defendant has no lawyer, the court appoints a court-appointed lawyer (국선변호인) on its own initiative when the defendant is detained, is a minor or aged 70 or over, has both hearing and speech impairments, is suspected of having a mental disability, or is charged with an offense punishable by imprisonment with or without labor for a minimum of 3 years or more (Criminal Procedure Act Article 33(1)).

Even in other cases, the court can appoint one if it considers it necessary in light of the defendant's age, intelligence and education, as long as the defendant does not object (same article, (3)). Also note that at the investigation stage, apart from the pre-detention hearing and reviews of the legality of arrest or detention, no court-appointed lawyer is assigned.

sections.title: Same powers, different starting point
body: A court-appointed lawyer, just like a privately hired lawyer (사선변호인), can inspect and copy the record, give views on evidence, examine witnesses and submit a closing brief. There is no difference in what they can do in court.

The difference lies in when they start and who chooses them. A court-appointed lawyer is assigned by the court after indictment, and the defendant cannot choose who it is. A privately hired lawyer can be retained before police questioning, so they can go into the questioning with you and submit a written opinion before the case is referred to prosecutors. Which suits you depends on whether you are disputing the case, how large the record is, and whether your job or professional qualifications are at stake.

If you are detained, how often the lawyer can visit is also worth considering. In cases with a large record and several witnesses, you need time between hearings to meet the lawyer and go over your account. Whether court-appointed or private, meet at least once before the first hearing to go through the indictment and the list of evidence together. If the defendant is detained, a spouse, lineal relatives and siblings can also hire a lawyer independently (Criminal Procedure Act Article 30(2)).

sections.title: If you want to change your court-appointed lawyer
body: A defendant cannot simply replace a court-appointed lawyer at will. However, you can ask the court for a change, and the court can cancel the appointment if it finds the request reasonable or considers that the lawyer is not performing their duties faithfully (Criminal Procedure Rules Article 18(2)).

Before asking for a change, first try contacting the lawyer at the number on the notice of appointment. Ask to meet before the hearing to go through the record together, and pass on a note of the points you want to dispute; this makes the conversation easier. If you hire a private lawyer, the court-appointed lawyer's appointment is cancelled (same article, (1)(i)).

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: Consultations are handled in person by a managing partner. We look at the indictment and the notice and tell you plainly whether your case qualifies for a court-appointed lawyer and what would change if you proceed with a private lawyer. If you decide to retain us, we start by reviewing the record, and we explain fees after the consultation. If your case is still at the investigation stage, we start by attending questioning with you and writing written opinions.

faqs.q: By when must I request a court-appointed lawyer?
faqs.a: The law does not set a deadline. However, the court-appointed lawyer needs time to review the record and consult with you, so it is better to request one as soon as you receive the notice. If the request is granted, the court will notify you of the appointment and who the lawyer is.

faqs.q: I was told a court-appointed lawyer was assigned, but they haven't contacted me.
faqs.a: The notice of appointment gives the lawyer's name and contact number. If the first hearing is close and you have not heard from them, call first to arrange a meeting. If you still cannot reach them, you can tell the court division handling your case.

guides.title: Preparing your views on evidence and your witnesses before the first hearing
guides.lead: At the first hearing, you must say whether you consent to each piece of evidence the prosecutor submitted, and that choice sets the length of the trial. Here is how to decide your views on evidence once you have the record, and the steps for preparing your own witnesses.

seo.title: Before the First Criminal Hearing in Korea: Consenting to Evidence and Preparing Witnesses | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: Before your first criminal trial hearing in Korea, you must decide whether to consent to each item of the prosecutor's evidence and prepare your own witnesses and materials. Covers the admissibility of police interrogation records, the effect of not consenting to witness statement records, the order of witness examination and pretrial preparation hearings.
keywords: consent to evidence criminal trial Korea

sections.title: What to check first
body: Once you have inspected and copied the record, start by keeping the list of evidence beside you and marking each item one by one.
bullets: Check the date, time and courtroom number on the summons and clear your schedule for that day.
Mark each number on the prosecutor's list of evidence as "admit," "dispute" or "unsure." Read the records containing your own statements line by line to see whether they match what you actually said.
List possible witnesses who support your account, and write one line on what each of them saw or heard directly.
Gather the documents you will submit, such as chat records, receipts and photos, and keep originals and copies separate.
On the day of the hearing, bring your ID, arrive early and check where your case falls in the day's order on the board outside the courtroom.

sections.title: Your view is decided separately for each piece of evidence
body: If the prosecutor and the defendant consent to a document or item being used as evidence and the court accepts it as genuine, it becomes evidence (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 318). Consent means "you may decide on the basis of this evidence," so if you carelessly consent to a document containing untrue statements, its contents become material for the judgment as they stand.

Your own suspect interrogation record (피의자신문조서) prepared by the police only becomes evidence if you accept its contents in court (Article 312(3)). If you do not consent to a record of someone else's statement, as a rule it only becomes evidence if that person appears in court, testifies that they said what is in the record, and you get a chance to cross-examine them (same article, (4)). So not consenting leads directly to witness examination.

sections.title: Your views differ depending on whether you admit or dispute the charges
body: If you admit all the charged facts, you usually consent to all the evidence and focus on sentencing materials. If you have nothing to dispute but refuse consent to the victim's statement record and make the victim come to court again, it is a burden on the victim and may not look good at sentencing.

If you dispute the charges, refuse consent only to the statements related to the points you dispute. If you admit only part, set out in your written opinion which facts you admit and which you dispute, so the court is not confused.

After the examination of evidence, the prosecutor and the defense lawyer may question the defendant about the charged facts and mitigating circumstances (Article 296-2), and at the end the defendant gives a final statement in person (Article 303). The final statement does not need to be long. If you prepare two or three sentences in advance about your thoughts on the victim and your plans, you will not be lost for words in court. Submit your own documents as copies with a list of evidence attached, and bring the originals to court so the judges can check them.

sections.title: Preparing your own witnesses
body: The defense can also call witnesses (Article 294). The side that called the witness asks questions first, and the other side asks afterwards (Article 161-2). Prepare your questions in advance and build them around what the witness experienced directly.

Do not tell witnesses what to answer or have them memorise answers. If they say something different from what they remember, it raises perjury issues, and they are easily shaken in cross-examination. It is safer to tell them only roughly when they need to come to court and what the case is about. In cases with many issues, the court may hold a pretrial preparation hearing (공판준비기일) to sort out evidence and witnesses in advance, and evidence not applied for at that point may be hard to submit later (Articles 266-7 and 266-13).

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: We take the record, decide our position on every item on the list of evidence, and set out the statements to be disputed and our grounds in a written opinion. If witness examination is needed, we prepare the questions and identify in advance the contradictions to raise in cross-examination. If we handled your case from the investigation stage, we compare against the questioning records from that time to see where statements changed.

faqs.q: Will the judge hold it against me if I don't consent to evidence?
faqs.a: Refusing consent when you have a reason to dispute something is the defendant's legitimate right. However, if the reason is unclear, for example admitting all the charged facts but refusing consent only to the victim's statement record so the victim has to come to court, it may be viewed unfavourably at sentencing. It is better to explain in a written opinion why you are not consenting.

faqs.q: Can a family member be a witness for me?
faqs.a: Family members can be witnesses. However, they testify under oath in court, so saying something different from what they remember raises the issue of perjury. Family members can refuse to answer questions that might expose themselves or a relative to punishment (Criminal Procedure Act Article 148).

guides.title: How to prepare a letter of remorse, petitions and sentencing materials
guides.lead: In a trial where you admit the charged facts, the materials used to decide the sentence drive the outcome. Here, in order, is what a letter of remorse should include, whom to ask for a petition, and when and how to submit them.

seo.title: Letters of Remorse, Petitions and Sentencing Materials in Korean Criminal Trials | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: What to include in a letter of remorse in a Korean criminal trial, whom to ask for a petition for leniency and how to write it, and the types and timing of sentencing materials such as settlement agreements, repayment receipts and treatment records. Also explains why they must be submitted before the hearing closes.
keywords: how to write a letter of remorse

sections.title: What to check first
body: Timing and content matter more than volume. Check the following before you start writing.
bullets: Confirm the case number and the court division (which single-judge criminal court or panel). Put these at the top of every document.
Write down the date of the next hearing. The hearing may close that day, so materials must be submitted before then.
Be clear about which charged facts you admit and which you dispute. A letter of remorse must not include anything admitting facts you dispute.
Sort out how far compensation has gone. Check whether you have a settlement agreement, transfer records or a deposit certificate.

sections.title: What to put in a letter of remorse
body: When deciding the sentence, the court takes into account factors such as the motive and consequences of the offense and the circumstances after the offense (Criminal Act (형법) Article 51). A letter of remorse (반성문) is the document in which you show those post-offense circumstances yourself. Rather than writing "I deeply regret it" over and over, explain in your own words what you did wrong and show that you understand the harm the victim suffered.

Reflect on why it happened and write specifically what you will change. If drinking was the cause, give the date you joined a sobriety group or started treatment; if it was a money problem, give your repayment plan. Blaming the victim or mixing in a sense of injustice makes the whole letter read like an excuse. Handwritten or printed is fine, but avoid sentences that obviously sound as if someone else wrote them.

sections.title: Whom to ask for a petition
body: A petition for leniency (탄원서) is written by someone who has known the defendant for a long time. Common writers are family members, a boss or colleagues, longtime neighbours, and people from a church or organisation the defendant belongs to. A few letters from people who know the relationship well are read more closely than a list of many signatures.

A petition should say who the writer is, how they know the defendant and for how long, give anecdotes showing what kind of person the defendant usually is, and include a promise of how they will help in future. Attach a copy of the writer's ID; if they are a colleague, submitting their certificate of employment as well makes it more credible.

If a family member writes the petition, it helps to say how they will look after the defendant from now on and what they will do together to stop the same thing happening again. There is no set format, but do not leave out the writer's name, contact details and signature.

sections.title: Objective materials worth submitting too
body: Documents carry more weight than words. Choose the ones that fit your case, make a list and submit them.
bullets: Settlement agreement and statement of non-punishment; if there is no settlement, a criminal deposit certificate and records of attempts to settle
Receipts for repayment of the harm, transfer records
Certificate of employment, family relationship certificate showing dependants
Records of treatment or counselling, certificates of completed courses
Records showing a change in your life, such as volunteer work certificates

sections.title: When and how to submit
body: Write the case number and court division on the materials and submit them at the court's public service office or send them by post. If you have a lawyer, it is better organised to submit everything at once with a list of materials attached. In cases where the charged facts are admitted, the hearing can close at the first session, so submit the basic materials before the first hearing and add anything that comes later.
Petitions submitted at the investigation stage may not be seen by the court unless the prosecutor submits them as evidence. It is safer to organise them again and submit them at the trial stage.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: We do not just bundle the materials together; in a defense counsel's written opinion, we explain one by one what each item shows. We read your draft letter of remorse with you and check that no sentence conflicts with the points you are disputing. If a hearing date has been set, we work out what to prepare first to meet that date.

faqs.q: How many times should I submit a letter of remorse?
faqs.a: There is no set number. Rather than submitting the same content several times, it is better to submit a new one when something has changed since the first. For example, write a new one when a settlement has been reached or you have started treatment.

faqs.q: Can I submit a petition just before the sentencing date?
faqs.a: Materials submitted after the hearing has closed may be hard for the court to reflect in the judgment. Submit them before the hearing in case it closes that day, and if a late item is essential, consider applying to reopen the hearing.

guides.title: Considering an appeal after the first-instance judgment
guides.lead: You have 7 days from the date of sentencing to appeal. That period often runs out before you even receive the written judgment, so you need to act from the day of sentencing. Here is the notice of appeal, the statement of reasons for appeal, and whether the sentence can become heavier.
