seo.title: Criminal Appeals in Korea: 7-Day Deadline, Statement of Reasons and the Ban on Harsher Sentences | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: To challenge a first-instance criminal judgment in Korea, file a notice of appeal with the original court within 7 days of sentencing and submit a statement of reasons within 20 days of being notified that the record was received. Covers grounds such as factual error and excessive sentence, and when a prosecutor's appeal can make the sentence heavier.
keywords: statement of reasons for appeal Korea
ban on harsher sentence on appeal

sections.title: What to do on the day of sentencing
bullets: Do not count the sentencing date as the first day; count 7 days from the next day. If the last day is a Saturday or public holiday, the period runs to the next weekday (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Articles 66 and 358).

Write down right away, as well as you remember, the order and the sentencing reasons the judge read out. The written judgment may come late, so this note is your first material for deciding whether to appeal.
Apply for a certified copy of the judgment (Article 45).
The prosecutor may also appeal, so check with the court after the 7 days have passed.
If you waive or withdraw an appeal, you cannot appeal again (Articles 349 and 354), so do not rush to sign a waiver right after sentencing.

sections.title: File the notice of appeal with the first-instance court
body: The notice of appeal (항소장) is filed not with the appellate court but with the first-instance court that gave the judgment (Article 359). It is enough for the notice to say you are appealing; you give the reasons later in a statement of reasons for appeal. If you are in a detention centre, submitting the notice to the warden within the period counts as meeting the deadline (Article 344).

When the record is sent to the appellate court, you receive a notice of receipt, and you must submit the statement of reasons for appeal (항소이유서) within 20 days of that day (Article 361-3). If you do not, the appeal is dismissed unless the notice of appeal stated reasons or there are grounds the court must examine on its own initiative (Article 361-4).

sections.title: What can you dispute?
body: Common grounds of appeal are factual error (the facts were found wrongly), violation of law (the law was applied wrongly), and excessive sentence (the sentence is too heavy) (Article 361-5). The appellate court decides mainly on the grounds stated in the statement of reasons (Article 364). Rather than repeating what you said at first instance, point out where the reasoning of the first-instance judgment was wrong.

If a settlement was reached or the harm repaid after the first instance, that in itself is a major ground for arguing the sentence is excessive. At the Supreme Court stage, you cannot argue that the sentence is excessive unless you were sentenced to 10 years or more of imprisonment with or without labor (Article 383), so for most cases the appeal is effectively the last stage at which the facts and the sentence can be disputed.

In the statement of reasons, cite the page and sentence of the first-instance judgment and explain with evidence why that finding was wrong. Even for the same argument, you need to show what the first instance missed to give the appellate court a reason to look again.

sections.title: Can the sentence become heavier?
body: In a case where only the defendant appealed, or an appeal was made on the defendant's behalf, the court cannot impose a heavier sentence than at first instance (Article 368). If the prosecutor also appealed, this limit does not apply and the sentence can become heavier.

If you withdraw the appeal, you cannot appeal again in the same case (Article 354). If you could not appeal within the period for reasons beyond your control, you can apply to restore the right of appeal (Article 345).

sections.title: What you can newly submit on appeal
body: On appeal, you can still apply to submit new evidence and file sentencing materials. If there was no settlement at first instance, keep trying to compensate the victim until the appellate judgment and keep a record of your efforts. In cases disputing the facts, first-instance witnesses may be called again or new witnesses applied for. A detained defendant may be moved to a detention centre near the appellate court after the notice of receipt of the record, so let the family know in advance (Article 361-2(3)).

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: We look at the reasoning of the first-instance judgment and the record together and first tell you whether anything could change on appeal. If you decide to appeal, we file the notice of appeal within the deadline and write a statement of reasons that addresses the first-instance findings point by point. Settlement or repayment materials obtained after the first instance are organised and submitted as well. If you are detained, we visit you to hear your views before deciding.

faqs.q: I haven't received the written judgment yet, and the 7 days are running out.
faqs.a: The appeal period is counted from the date of sentencing, not from the day you receive the written judgment (Criminal Procedure Act Article 343(2)). File the notice of appeal within the period first, and once you receive the judgment, argue your case in detail in the statement of reasons.

faqs.q: I got a suspended sentence. Is it safe to appeal?
faqs.a: If only the defendant appeals, the sentence cannot be heavier than at first instance. But if the prosecutor appeals, it could change to an actual prison sentence, so decide after looking at whether the prosecutor appeals and what grounds you have.

guides.title: When a suspended sentence comes with probation, community service or a mandatory course
guides.lead: If the order in a judgment imposing a suspended sentence includes probation, community service or a mandatory course, there are separate things to do once the judgment becomes final. Here are the reporting deadline, the conditions you must follow and what happens if you breach them.

seo.title: Suspended Sentence with Probation, Community Service or a Mandatory Course in Korea | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: If you received a suspended sentence with probation, community service or a mandatory course in Korea, you must report to the probation office within 10 days of the judgment becoming final. Covers maximum hours, conditions, warnings, compulsory appearance and revocation of the suspended sentence for breaches, and the effect once the suspension period ends.

sections.title: What to do right away
bullets: Confirm the date the judgment became final. It becomes final if neither the prosecutor nor the defendant appeals within 7 days of sentencing.

Within 10 days of that date, go in person to the probation office with jurisdiction over your home and report your residence, job and plans in writing (Enforcement Decree of the Probation and Parole Act (보호관찰 등에 관한 법률 시행령) Articles 16 and 39).
Check the order in the judgment for the suspension period, probation period and the hours of community service or the course, and write them down.
If you work, the schedule may clash with your job, so be ready to discuss scheduling with the probation office.
When you go to report, bring a copy of the judgment and your ID, and your work schedule if you have one.

sections.title: The three are different
body: Probation (보호관찰) means being guided and supervised by a probation officer during the suspension period. The court may also set a separate period within the suspension period (Criminal Act (형법) Article 62-2(2)). You must stay at your residence and work, respond when the probation officer calls you in or visits, and report in advance if you move or travel at home or abroad for a month or more (Probation and Parole Act (보호관찰 등에 관한 법률) Article 32(2)).

Community service (사회봉사) means doing unpaid work for the public good for the number of hours set by the court, and a mandatory course order (수강명령) means attending education for a set number of hours. The court sets community service at up to 500 hours and courses at up to 200 hours (same Act, Article 59). Both must be completed within the suspension period (Criminal Act Article 62-2(3)).

Course orders are often attached in cases where education to prevent reoffending is needed, such as drunk driving, sex offenses and domestic violence. You must attend the course on the schedule set by the probation office, and any hours you miss must be made up.

sections.title: If special conditions were attached
body: Depending on the offense, the court can attach additional conditions such as a night-time curfew, a ban on entering certain places, a ban on approaching the victim, a ban on drinking more than a certain amount, or efforts to repair the harm (same Act, Article 32(3)). You receive these in writing at sentencing, so keep them safe.
If a ban on approaching the victim has been attached, even contacting the victim to talk about a settlement can be a breach. If contact is truly necessary, go through a lawyer.

sections.title: What happens if you breach the conditions
body: If you breach a condition, the head of the probation office can first urge you to comply and give a warning (Article 38), and if you do not answer a summons or are likely to flee, you can be brought in under a judge's warrant to appear, requested by the prosecutor (Article 39).

If the breach is serious, the court can revoke the suspended sentence (Criminal Act Article 64(2)); revocation is requested by the prosecutor on application from the head of the probation office (Probation and Parole Act Article 47). If it is revoked, you actually serve the prison sentence that had been suspended. Missing community service sessions a few times can lead this far, so if something comes up, tell your probation officer in advance.

sections.title: When the suspension period ends
body: If the suspension period passes without the suspended sentence lapsing or being revoked, the sentence loses its effect (Criminal Act Article 65). Conversely, if during the suspension period you are finally sentenced to actual imprisonment with or without labor for a crime committed intentionally, the suspended sentence lapses (Article 63). During the suspension period, take care not to get caught up in even minor incidents.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: We read the order in the judgment and the special conditions with you and set out what you must do and by when. If revocation of the suspended sentence has been requested because of a breach, Jisan Law submits a written opinion explaining how the breach happened and your efforts to comply since, and attends the hearing.

faqs.q: Can I choose where or when to do community service?
faqs.a: The court can designate the field and place (Probation and Parole Act Article 59(2)); if it does not, the probation office decides. Mention your work or health situation when you report, and try to arrange the schedule.

faqs.q: I have a business trip abroad while on probation.
faqs.a: To travel at home or abroad for a month or more, you must report to your probation officer in advance (Probation and Parole Act Article 32(2)(iv)). Even for a shorter trip, it is safer to let them know your schedule in advance.

guides.title: When you cannot afford to pay a fine
guides.lead: A fine must be paid within 30 days of becoming final, and if it is never paid, you may be confined in a workhouse. Here is how the workhouse period is set, and the order in which paying in instalments and applying for community service work.

seo.title: Can't Pay a Criminal Fine in Korea? Instalments, Workhouse Confinement and Community Service | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: If you cannot pay a fine in Korea all at once, consider paying in instalments or postponing payment, and for fines of 5 million won or less, applying for community service. Covers how the workhouse period is calculated and reduced by partial payment, and the processing and completion deadlines after applying for community service.
keywords: community service instead of fine Korea

sections.title: What to check first
bullets: In the judgment or summary order, find the amount of the fine and the wording "if the fine is not paid, you will be confined in a workhouse for a period calculated at a set amount per day."
Work out when the 30-day period from the day it became final ends (Criminal Act (형법) Article 69(1)).
Check whether the fine is 5 million won or less and whether it was imposed together with imprisonment. This decides whether you can apply for community service.
Gather documents showing your financial situation, such as a certificate of benefit receipt, records of unemployment benefits or a medical certificate.

sections.title: The workhouse period is already set in the judgment
body: When imposing a fine, the court also sets the period of confinement in a workhouse (노역장 유치) if the fine is not paid (Criminal Act Article 70(1)). The period is between 1 day and 3 years (Article 69(2)), and for fines of 100 million won or more it must be at least 300 days, for 500 million won or more at least 500 days, and for 5 billion won or more at least 1,000 days (Article 70(2)).

If you pay even part of it, the days of confinement are reduced in proportion to the amount paid (Article 71). So even if you cannot pay it all at once, paying what you can first does not cost you anything. If you were held in custody before the judgment became final, those days may be credited against the fine, so check the order in the judgment as well.

sections.title: How to pay in instalments or postpone
body: You can apply to the execution department of the Public Prosecution Service (공소청) to pay in instalments or postpone payment. Those eligible include benefit recipients, some near-poverty households, people with disabilities, people receiving unemployment benefits, people with a decision to open individual rehabilitation, and people who themselves or whose household members need treatment for a month or more; the prosecutor decides whether to allow it (Public Prosecution Service Rules on the Execution of Property Penalties (재산형 등에 관한 공소청 집행사무규칙) Article 12). The period is up to 6 months and can be extended twice by 3 months each time.
Once allowed, if you miss two payments without good reason, the permission may be cancelled. Write the payment dates in your calendar, and if something comes up, tell the person in charge in advance.

sections.title: How an application for community service works
body: If a fine of 5 million won or less has become final and you cannot afford to pay it, you can apply for community service (사회봉사) to the prosecutor at the District Public Prosecution Office with jurisdiction over your home within 30 days of the prosecutor's payment order, or, if you have permission to pay in instalments or postpone, within that permitted period (Act on Special Cases concerning Community Service for Persons Who Fail to Pay Fines (벌금미납자의 사회봉사 집행에 관한 특례법) Article 4). The prosecutor decides within 7 days of the application whether to request it from the court, and the court decides within 14 days of the request whether to allow it (Articles 5 and 6).

If allowed, the number of hours is set to match the remaining fine, and you must finish within 6 months of the day it was allowed. With special reasons, this can be extended once by 6 months (Article 11). As a rule, no more than 9 hours are carried out per day (Article 10), and you can also end it partway by paying the remaining fine (Article 12). If not allowed, you must pay the fine within 15 days of being notified, and if you do not, you will be confined in a workhouse (Article 6(5)).

sections.title: If you simply do not pay
body: If you have not paid 30 days after the fine became final, you will receive a reminder to pay, and if you still do not pay, enforcement steps toward workhouse confinement begin. If you avoid contact, you may be taken into custody on the spot when you encounter the police over something else. If money is tight, it is better to contact the execution department first and apply for instalments or community service than to hold out.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: If the fine has not yet become final, we first look at whether there is room to dispute it through a request for a formal trial or an appeal. If it is already final, we decide which order of instalments, postponement and community service suits your situation and prepare the necessary documents with you. You can reach us first by phone for a consultation 24 hours a day.

faqs.q: If I pay after entering the workhouse, can I get out?
faqs.a: Paying the remaining fine deducts the corresponding days of confinement (Criminal Act Article 71), so once you pay the full remaining amount, the confinement ends. Family members can also pay on your behalf, so check with the execution department how to pay.

faqs.q: If the fine is over 5 million won, is community service not possible?
faqs.a: Only fines of 5 million won or less can be converted into community service (Enforcement Decree of the Act on Special Cases concerning Community Service for Persons Who Fail to Pay Fines, Article 2). For larger fines, first consider permission to pay in instalments or postpone.

guides.title: How long does a criminal record last?
guides.lead: Whether it is a fine or a suspended sentence, a record remains once the sentence is final. Here, in turn, is what records remain and where, what changes when a sentence expires, and whether companies or other people can see it.

seo.title: Criminal Records in Korea: When Sentences Expire and Criminal Record Certificates | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: In Korea, a fine expires 2 years after it is paid, and imprisonment of 3 years or less expires 5 years after it is served. Covers the difference between criminal history records and investigation history records, what is left off your own record certificate after expiry, and whether employers can check your record.
keywords: criminal record for a fine Korea

sections.title: What to check first
bullets: Confirm what outcome you received. The type of record and how long it lasts differ for a fine, imprisonment, a suspended sentence, a suspended sentencing and a suspension of indictment.
For a fine, note the date you finished paying; for imprisonment, the date you finished serving. The expiry period is counted from that date.
Check separately whether your job or professional qualifications have a disqualification period. It follows different rules from the expiry of a sentence.

sections.title: There are two kinds of records
body: Sentences of a fine or heavier, suspended sentencing (선고유예), probation, and community service or course orders imposed with a sentence are kept as criminal history records (범죄경력자료), which is what people usually mean by a criminal record (Act on the Lapse of Criminal Sentences (형의 실효 등에 관한 법률) Article 2(v) and (vii)). Other investigation history, such as non-referral or non-indictment decisions, is managed separately as investigation history records (수사경력자료) (same article, (vi)).

Once a sentence is final, it is also entered in the register of convicted persons (수형인명부) kept by the Public Prosecution Service (공소청) and in the convicted person card (수형인명표) kept by the city, district, town or township office of your place of family registration. However, only sentences of suspension of qualifications or heavier go on the register of convicted persons, so a fine remains only in the criminal history records.

Cases that did not go to trial, such as a suspension of indictment (기소유예) or non-referral for no suspicion, are not a criminal record; they remain as investigation history records and are deleted once the retention period set according to the statutory penalty has passed (same Act, Article 8-2).

sections.title: When sentences expire
body: If you do not receive another sentence of suspension of qualifications or heavier, a sentence expires (실효) after 10 years for imprisonment, with or without labor, of more than 3 years, 5 years for imprisonment of 3 years or less, and 2 years for a fine, counted from the day the sentence was fully served or remitted (same Act, Article 7(1)). Short detention and petty fines expire as soon as they are served.

For a suspended sentence (집행유예), if the suspension period passes without it lapsing or being revoked, the sentence loses its effect (Criminal Act (형법) Article 65), and a suspended sentencing is treated as an acquittal on procedural grounds (면소) once 2 years have passed (Article 60). A person who has served a prison sentence, compensated the victim and not received a sentence of suspension of qualifications or heavier for 7 years can also apply to the court for a declaration that the sentence has expired (Article 81).
If you paid a fine in instalments, the date you made the final payment is the date the sentence was served; if you were confined in a workhouse, it is the date confinement ended.

sections.title: What changes when a sentence expires
body: Once a sentence expires, the relevant entry in the register of convicted persons is deleted and the convicted person card is destroyed (Act on the Lapse of Criminal Sentences Article 8). When you request your own criminal record certificate, expired sentences, suspended sentencings treated as acquittals, and suspended sentences that have lost effect are left off unless you specifically ask for them (Enforcement Decree of the same Act, Article 7-2(2)).

That does not mean the record is completely erased from the Korean National Police Agency's data. It can be checked where there is a purpose set by law, such as an investigation or trial (same Act, Article 6(1)). On the other hand, ordinary companies cannot check criminal history without a legal basis, and no one may obtain this data for anything other than the purposes set out (same article, (3)).

sections.title: Job-specific disqualification periods are calculated separately
body: The expiry of a sentence and disqualification periods for jobs are separate. For example, a person cannot be appointed as a national public official until 5 years have passed since finishing an actual sentence of imprisonment without labor or heavier, or 2 years since the end of the suspension period of a suspended sentence of imprisonment without labor or heavier (State Public Officials Act (국가공무원법) Article 33). If your job requires a licence or permit, first check the disqualification provisions in the relevant law.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: If you are worried about your record, it is better to get advice before the outcome is decided. Even for the same incident, the record left behind and the impact on your job differ depending on whether the case ends in a suspension of indictment, a fine or a suspended sentence. From the investigation stage, we raise these circumstances in our written opinions.

faqs.q: I'm applying for a visa abroad and have been asked for a criminal record certificate.
faqs.a: A certificate you request yourself for entry to or residence in a foreign country leaves out expired sentences, sentences covered by a pardon or restoration of rights, suspended sentencings treated as acquittals, and suspended sentences that have lost effect (Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Lapse of Criminal Sentences, Article 7-2(3)). If the expiry period has not yet passed, the record will appear, so start by calculating the period.

faqs.q: Does a criminal record show on a family relationship certificate or resident registration abstract?
faqs.a: No. Criminal records are kept in the Korean National Police Agency's criminal history records, the Public Prosecution Service's register of convicted persons and the convicted person card at your place of family registration; they do not appear on family relationship documents or resident registration abstracts.

guides.title: When a public official, teacher or soldier is caught up in a criminal case
guides.lead: When a public official comes under investigation, their agency is notified, and disciplinary proceedings move separately from the criminal outcome. Here is which sentences lead to automatic dismissal, and when suspension from duty and disciplinary action become an issue.

seo.title: Public Officials and Teachers in Criminal Cases in Korea: Notice of Investigation, Discipline and Automatic Dismissal | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: When a Korean public official is investigated, their agency is notified within 10 days, and disciplinary proceedings can go ahead separately. Covers automatic dismissal for actual or suspended sentences of imprisonment without labor or heavier, fine thresholds for embezzlement and sex offenses, suspension from duty on indictment, and how teachers and soldiers differ.
keywords: notice of start of investigation Korea

sections.title: What to check first
bullets: Investigators notify the head of the official's agency within 10 days of starting and of finishing an investigation into a public official (State Public Officials Act (국가공무원법) Article 83(3)). Prepare on the assumption that your workplace will find out.
Find out what offense you are suspected of and whether it relates to your duties. The standard for automatic dismissal depends on the offense and its connection to your duties.
If your agency asks for a written explanation or statement, prepare it so that it does not conflict with what you told investigators before submitting it.
Gather your certificate of employment, career history and records of commendations for use in written opinions on the outcome.

sections.title: The type of sentence decides your status
body: An actual sentence of imprisonment without labor or heavier (금고 이상의 형), or a suspended sentence of that kind, is a ground for automatic dismissal (당연퇴직) (State Public Officials Act Articles 69 and 33(iii) and (iv)). This means that even a suspended prison sentence, not just an actual one, costs you your post. A suspended sentencing of imprisonment without labor or heavier leads to automatic dismissal only for certain offenses, such as bribery, embezzlement or breach of trust related to duties, and sexual violence.

A fine is in principle not a ground for automatic dismissal, but there are exceptions. If a fine of 3 million won or more becomes final for embezzlement or breach of trust related to duties while in office, or a fine of 1 million won or more for sexual violence or stalking offenses and similar, the official is automatically dismissed (Article 33(vi-2) and (vi-3)). So in cases involving public officials, the amount of a fine alone can change the outcome.

In cases involving public officials, the response must be planned from the start around what sentence the case will end with. Even for the same incident, if it ends with a suspension of indictment or a fine, there is room to keep your status, but if a suspended prison sentence becomes final, you are automatically dismissed.

sections.title: Suspension from duty and discipline move separately
body: If indicted in a criminal case, you may be suspended from duty (직위해제), except where a summary order has been requested (Article 73-3(1)(iv)). You may also be suspended while under investigation for serious misconduct such as financial misconduct or sex offenses (same paragraph, (vi)).

Discipline may not wait for the criminal outcome. The law only says disciplinary proceedings may be put on hold while an investigation is under way (Article 83(2)), so each agency decides differently. Even if you are acquitted, disciplinary grounds such as breach of the duty to maintain dignity are judged separately. The limitation period for discipline is 3 years for general grounds, 5 years for money-related grounds and 10 years for sex offenses (Article 83-2).

Before a disciplinary committee, be careful not to say anything different from your statements in the criminal proceedings. If you admit in disciplinary proceedings facts you are disputing in the criminal case, that statement can become unfavourable material at your criminal trial, and the reverse can also happen.

sections.title: How teachers and soldiers differ
body: For education officials, in addition to the disqualifications for national public officials, a final fine of 1 million won or more for sexual violence against an adult, or a final sentence for a sex offense against a minor, bars appointment and leads to automatic dismissal for those in office (Educational Officials Act (교육공무원법) Articles 10-4 and 43-2). Private school teachers are also automatically dismissed on the same grounds (Private School Act (사립학교법) Article 57).

Crimes by active-duty soldiers are in principle tried by military courts. However, in peacetime, sexual violence offenses, the underlying offenses in cases where a soldier died, and crimes committed before enlistment are handled by ordinary courts (Military Court Act (군사법원법) Article 2).

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: At the consultation, we look at the allegation and its connection to your duties and first identify which outcomes would affect your status. At the investigation stage, we attend questioning with you and, in written opinions on the outcome, set out the specific professional consequences and ask that they be taken into account. Jisan Law also writes your statement of explanation for the disciplinary committee so that it is consistent with the criminal record, and handles attendance at the disciplinary committee and an appeal to the appeals commission.

faqs.q: If I get a fine for drunk driving, can I keep my position as a public official?
faqs.a: A fine for drunk driving is not among the grounds for automatic dismissal. However, discipline proceeds separately, and heavy disciplinary action can be taken depending on your blood alcohol level, whether there was an accident and your history. Prepare explanatory materials for the disciplinary committee in advance.

faqs.q: Will I be suspended from duty if a summary order is requested?
faqs.a: Suspension on the grounds of indictment excludes cases where a summary order has been requested (State Public Officials Act Article 73-3(1)(iv)). However, this can change if a formal trial is requested or there is another ground for suspension.

guides.stage: I was harmed and want to file a criminal complaint
guides.title: When you have been harmed and want to file a criminal complaint
guides.lead: If you have decided to file a criminal complaint, some things have changed, starting with where and how you submit it. Based on the amended Criminal Procedure Act in force from October 2, 2026, here is everything from organising evidence and filing to notice of the outcome and how to challenge it.

seo.title: Filing a Criminal Complaint in Korea: Writing, Submitting and Objecting to Non-Referral | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: From October 2, 2026, criminal complaints in Korea are filed with the police. Step by step: organising evidence before filing, how to write a complaint, the police's 3-month deadline, objecting to delays, objecting to non-referral and accessing investigation records, and appealing a non-indictment decision.

sections.title: What to do right away
body: Gather evidence before writing the complaint. A lot of material gets deleted or disappears once the other party notices. Do not alter or edit what you collect; keep it in its original state.
bullets: Save conversations as screenshots and also as chat export files. Keep the other party's profile and account information too.
If you transferred money, download the transaction history as a PDF from your banking app. Keep original contracts, receipts and IOUs separately.
If you were injured, see a doctor right away to get a medical certificate and records, and take photos of the injuries with the date visible.
CCTV at the scene is usually deleted within two weeks to a month. Ask the shop or building management office to keep it, and if that is difficult, report right away and ask the police to secure it.
Write down when, where, who, what and how, in date order.

sections.title: What not to do
body: Do not exaggerate beyond the facts out of anger. If even part of it is untrue, the whole complaint becomes hard to believe, and filing a complaint based on false facts can be the crime of false accusation.

Do not go to confront the other party or post their real name online. You could face a counter-complaint for something else, such as defamation. Secretly opening the other party's phone to gather evidence is also a problem.

sections.title: File the complaint at a police station
body: From October 2, 2026, a criminal complaint (고소) is made to a judicial police officer, in writing or orally (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 237). With the Prosecutors' Office (검찰청) abolished and the Public Prosecution Service (공소청) created, the police are now the place that receives complaints. You usually submit it at the public service desk of the police station with jurisdiction over the other party's address or the place where the incident happened, and get a receipt.

The complaint (고소장) should include the other party's personal details (as much as you know), the facts you want punished and a list of evidence showing those facts. Write it briefly and in time order so the investigator can understand what happened after one read. Leave out emotions and guesses; putting the number of the supporting evidence next to each fact makes it easy to read. Attach copies of the evidence and bring the originals to show at the complainant interview.

sections.title: From filing to the police decision
body: The police must finish the investigation and decide whether to refer the case to prosecutors within 3 months of accepting the complaint (Criminal Procedure Act Article 238, for cases accepted on or after October 2, 2026). In the meantime, you will be contacted for a complainant interview. They will ask again about what you wrote and hear your response to the other party's claims. Before the interview, reread your complaint and make sure you do not state dates and amounts differently from it.

If more than 6 months pass after the investigation starts without real progress and without good reason, you can raise an objection with the head of the investigating office. Within 14 days, they must tell you what action they will take, such as changing the investigator or presenting an investigation plan, and if no action is taken or you disagree, you can ask a higher office to review it within 14 days (Article 245-11).

sections.title: If you receive a non-referral notice
body: If the police decide not to refer the case (불송치), they must notify you in writing of that decision and the reasons within 7 days, sending the decision together with information and a form for objecting (Article 245-6). If you were notified on or after October 2, 2026, an objection must be filed within 3 months of receiving the notice (Article 245-7(3)), and once you file, the case is referred to the prosecutor. In the objection, rather than saying you feel wronged, go through the reasons for non-referral in the decision and point out one by one where they are wrong, and submit any new evidence with it.

To rebut the reasons for non-referral, you need to see the record. You can apply to inspect and copy the investigation record for the purpose of objecting, and it is in principle allowed if found necessary (Article 245-12). After the case is referred, you can also request a meeting with the prosecutor to give your views (Article 245-13(2)). If the prosecutor decides not to indict, you can appeal to the head of the Regional Public Prosecution Office within 30 days of receiving the notice (Public Prosecution Service Act (공소청법) Article 57).

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: Before filing, we first examine whether it amounts to a crime. A complaint that does not meet the requirements only wastes time and can turn into a counter-complaint, so we screen for this at this stage. We write the complaint, attach the list of evidence and file it, and go with you to the complainant interview.
If you have received a non-referral notice, we first check the deadline and prepare the objection and record access. Organise the notice and your evidence and contact us at 02-6951-4097.

faqs.q: If I file a complaint, can I get my money back?
faqs.a: A criminal complaint is a procedure to seek punishment, which is separate from getting money back. In cases such as fraud, embezzlement or bodily injury, you can apply for a compensation order (배상명령) in the criminal trial (Act on Special Cases concerning Expedition of Legal Proceedings (소송촉진 등에 관한 특례법) Article 25), and the other party may offer repayment or a settlement to get a lighter outcome. If money is your goal, also consider civil proceedings.

faqs.q: Can I withdraw a complaint and file it again later?
faqs.a: A complaint can be withdrawn until the first-instance judgment is pronounced, but once withdrawn, you cannot file again for the same case (Criminal Procedure Act Article 232). Do not sign a withdrawal before you have received the full settlement.

faqs.q: Can a person who reported a crime also object to non-referral?
faqs.a: Complainants, victims and certain others can object. A person who reported a crime without being the victim can object only for offenses set by presidential decree where they have a direct interest comparable to a victim's, such as false accusation (Criminal Procedure Act Article 245-7(2)).

guides.title: When you are accused of fraud for not repaying a loan
guides.lead: Borrowing money and failing to repay it is not always fraud. Here is what investigators base their decision on, what to gather before questioning and what to be careful about during it, and what happens if you repay.

seo.title: Accused of Loan Fraud in Korea: How to Respond | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: If you have been accused of fraud in Korea for not repaying borrowed money, the test is whether you intended and were able to repay when you borrowed. Covers the higher statutory penalty for fraud from December 2025, materials to gather before questioning, what to be careful saying, and the effect of repayment and settlement.

sections.title: The test is the situation when you borrowed
body: In loan fraud cases, the first thing investigators look at is whether, when you borrowed the money, you intended and were able to repay it. If you could not repay because your business struggled or your income stopped after borrowing, it may remain a civil matter. On the other hand, if from the start you had no way to repay but said you did, or lied about what the money was for, it can be fraud (사기).

So what matters is not your current situation but your income and assets around the date you borrowed, your other debts and where the borrowed money actually went. If you borrowed several times, each loan is looked at separately. If you could repay the first loan but had no way to repay by the time of the last one, only that part may be a problem.

sections.title: Penalties have increased
body: The Criminal Act (형법) was amended on December 23, 2025, raising the statutory penalty for fraud to imprisonment of up to 20 years or a fine of up to 50 million won (Criminal Act Article 347). For acts committed before the amendment, the previous penalty of up to 10 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to 20 million won applies. If the amount gained is 500 million won or more, the Act on the Aggravated Punishment of Specific Economic Crimes (특정경제범죄 가중처벌 등에 관한 법률) applies and the penalty is heavier.

Most posts online saying fraud carries up to 10 years are based on the old rule. The statute of limitations for fraud is 10 years (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 249(1)(iii)), so people are sometimes accused belatedly over things that happened years ago.

sections.title: Materials to gather before questioning
body: Download the transaction history for the relevant period as a PDF from your banking app, and save the entire chat using the export function. Cutting out only the favourable parts actually raises suspicion. If the money was received in an account not in your name, you also need to be able to explain why.
bullets: Messages exchanged and any IOU from when you borrowed the money
Payslips, bank balances and asset records from around the time you borrowed
Transaction records showing where the borrowed money was actually spent
Records of repayments made so far (even partial)
Materials showing why you became unable to repay (business closure, job loss, illness, etc.)

sections.title: What to be careful saying in questioning
body: Saying things like "things were a bit tight then" or "I meant to pay it back somehow later" can be read as meaning you had no ability to repay when you borrowed. Do not guess at amounts or dates you do not remember exactly; say you will check the records and submit them separately.

First find out what the complainant says was a lie, for example what you are supposed to have said about the purpose, the repayment date or collateral; only then can you work out how to answer. If you bring a one-page table showing, for each date you borrowed, the amount, the purpose and how much you repaid, you can answer questions without being thrown.

sections.title: Be careful when contacting the complainant
body: If you are in touch with the complainant, do not send emotional messages. If you make a new promise to repay with a date you cannot meet, that promise can look like another lie. Put any repayment plan in writing, within what you can actually keep to. When replying to demands for payment, avoid wording that admits things that are not true.

The test is similar even when it is not a loan, such as payment for a second-hand sale or an investment. It looks at whether, when you received the money, you intended and were able to keep your promise, and whether you used the money as you said you would.

sections.title: Does repaying end the case?
body: Fraud is not an offense where the case ends just because the victim does not want punishment. Even if you repay in full and settle, you can be punished if the allegation is made out. However, compensating the victim weighs heavily in deciding the outcome and sentence, such as a suspension of indictment (기소유예), a fine or a suspended sentence (집행유예). A record of paying back little by little since before the complaint also shows that you intended to repay.

You can also repay while disputing the allegation. In that case, it is better to word the settlement agreement so that the repayment is not read as admitting wrongdoing. If it is a matter between family members, prosecution requires a complaint (Criminal Act Articles 328 and 354), so check the relationship first.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: At the consultation, we put together the materials from around the date you borrowed in time order and decide with you whether to dispute or admit the allegation. We practise likely questions with you and attend the questioning, and afterwards we submit a defense counsel's written opinion bringing together your repayment history and materials. If you have been summoned, contact us first at 02-6951-4097.

faqs.q: I definitely meant to pay it back, but I've been accused of fraud.
faqs.a: Intending to repay is not enough on its own; whether you had the ability to back up that intention is also considered. If you have records of your income and assets around the time you borrowed, or of borrowing from and repaying the same person before, put them together. Materials showing you used the money for the purpose you stated are also important.

faqs.q: I've paid it all back, but they won't withdraw the complaint.
faqs.a: Fraud is an offense where the investigation continues regardless of whether the complaint is withdrawn. Check whether you can get proof of repayment, a settlement agreement and a written statement that they do not want you punished, and submit them with a written opinion. They will be taken into account in deciding the outcome.

guides.title: Checking progress and viewing records after filing a complaint
guides.lead: After you file a criminal complaint, there can be long, frustrating stretches without any news. Here is how to check how far the case has gone, and what records a victim can see at each stage.

seo.title: Checking Criminal Complaint Progress and Victim Access to Records in Korea | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: How to check whether your complaint is now with the police, the Public Prosecution Service or the court in Korea, applying for victim notification, inspecting the record of your own statement, and after indictment applying to inspect and copy trial records and documents held by the prosecutor, stage by stage.

sections.title: What to check first
bullets: Check the receipt number, the police station handling the case and the investigation department shown on your complaint receipt. If you do not yet know the investigator's name and contact number, ask the department and write them down.
Check whether you can log in with identity verification to the Korea Information System of Criminal-Justice Services (형사사법포털, kics.go.kr) and look up the stage of the case.
Keep all post and texts you receive from now on in one place. Notices about referral, non-referral or indictment often state the deadline for the next step.
If you find new evidence, give it to the investigator in charge and keep a separate note of the date and what you submitted.

sections.title: How to check at the police stage
body: The police must finish the investigation and decide whether to refer the case to prosecutors within 3 months of accepting the complaint (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 238, for cases accepted on or after October 2, 2026). There is also a rule that the police should make efforts to keep those involved appropriately informed of progress (Investigation Rules (수사준칙) Article 12), but investigators often do not get in touch first. If you want to know, briefly ask the investigator in charge what stage the case is at and whether there is anything more you should submit.

You can apply to inspect and copy the records of your own statements and the documents you submitted, even during the investigation (Investigation Rules Article 69(1)). This is how to check how what you said in the interview was written down. To see the other party's statements too, you generally have to wait until the objection stage after a non-referral decision, or until after indictment.

If more than 6 months pass after the investigation starts without real progress and without good reason, there is also a procedure for raising an objection with the head of the investigating office (Criminal Procedure Act Article 245-11).

sections.title: After referral, apply for notification
body: When the prosecutor indicts or decides not to indict in a complaint case, the complainant must be notified in writing within 7 days (Criminal Procedure Act Article 258). If it is a non-indictment, the prosecutor must explain the reasons in writing within 7 days if the complainant asks (Article 259).

If the victim applies, the prosecutor must promptly notify them of whether the case is indicted, the date and place of trial hearings, the trial result, and custody matters such as the offender's detention or release (Article 259-2). If you want to attend the trial or know whether the offender has been released, it is a good idea to apply for this notification.
When applying, give the case number and the exact address and mobile number for notifications. If you move, tell them your new address so the notifications do not stop.

sections.title: After indictment, you can see the trial records
body: While the trial is under way, the victim, a family member they have authorised, or their lawyer can apply to the presiding judge to inspect and copy the case records. The judge must allow it if needed for the victim's remedies or right to make a statement, and must give reasons if refusing or attaching conditions (Article 294-4). You can also apply to the prosecutor to inspect and copy the documentary evidence the prosecutor will submit to the court (Article 294-5).

Seeing the records tells you what the offender is disputing in court, which makes it easier to prepare a written opinion or testimony. The victim can apply to testify as a witness, and can then also give views on the harm suffered and on punishment (Article 294-2). Do not post what you read online or pass it around to others.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: In complaints we file on your behalf, we stay in touch with the investigator to check progress and submit any additional materials needed. If a non-referral notice arrives, we apply to inspect the record and write the objection, and after indictment we inspect and copy the trial records and submit a victim's written opinion that responds to the offender's arguments. In cases involving victims of sex crimes, Jisan Law acts as the victim's lawyer, attending victim interviews and trial hearings to state the victim's views (Act on Special Cases Concerning the Punishment of Sexual Crimes (성폭력범죄의 처벌 등에 관한 특례법) Article 27).

faqs.q: Can I find out whether the offender was detained and then released?
faqs.a: If the victim applies, the prosecutor must give notice of custody matters such as the suspect's or defendant's detention or release (Criminal Procedure Act Article 259-2). If you are worried about retaliation, apply for notification to the Public Prosecution Service (공소청) office handling the case, and if you need personal protection, ask the police in charge as well.

faqs.q: Can the other party see the complaint I filed?
faqs.a: A suspect can also apply to inspect and copy the complaint by showing why they need it. However, access is limited to the parts about the allegations against the suspect, and other people's personal information, evidence and attached documents are left out (Investigation Rules Article 69(3)).

guides.title: How to apply for a compensation order in a criminal trial
guides.lead: Once the offender has been indicted, you can seek compensation for your losses in the criminal trial itself, without a separate civil lawsuit. Here are the cases and deadlines for applying, when applications are dismissed and what your options are afterwards.

seo.title: Compensation Orders in Korean Criminal Trials: How to Apply, Deadlines and Dismissal | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: In Korean criminal trials for offenses such as fraud, embezzlement, bodily injury and sex crimes, victims can apply for a compensation order without paying stamp fees until the close of hearings at first or second instance. Covers what losses can be claimed, when applications are dismissed, enforcement after finality and the relationship with civil lawsuits.
keywords: compensation order Expedition of Legal Proceedings Act

sections.title: What to check first
bullets: Check whether the offender has been indicted and a trial has begun. You cannot apply for a compensation order at the police or Public Prosecution Service (공소청) stage.

Check the case number, the court division and the next hearing date. The prosecutor may also send you a notice that you can apply for compensation (Act on Special Cases concerning Expedition of Legal Proceedings (소송촉진 등에 관한 특례법) Article 25-2).
Check whether you have already filed a civil lawsuit for the same loss that is still ongoing. If so, you cannot apply for compensation (Article 26(7)).
Gather transfer records, receipts, medical certificates and medical bills showing the amount of your loss.

sections.title: Cases in which you can apply
body: When giving a guilty verdict for offenses such as bodily injury, aggravated bodily injury, assault causing injury, negligent injury, rape or indecent assault, theft or robbery, fraud or extortion, embezzlement or breach of trust, and property damage, the court can order compensation on the victim's application or on its own initiative. Certain offenses under the Sexual Violence Punishment Act and the Act on the Protection of Children and Youth against Sex Offenses are also included (Article 25(1)). Compensation covers direct material losses caused by the crime, medical costs and compensation for emotional distress (위자료).

Even for offenses not on the list, such as simple assault or threats, if the defendant and the victim have agreed on an amount of damages, the court can order compensation for that agreed amount (same article, (2)).
Even if the case was indicted together with other crimes, you can apply for the part of the loss caused by an offense eligible for a compensation order.

sections.title: Deadline and how to apply
body: Apply to the court handling the case before the hearings at first or second instance close. No stamp fee is attached to the application (Article 26(1)). State the case number, the names and addresses of the applicant and the defendant, what is to be compensated and the amount claimed, and submit as many copies as there are defendants. If you appear in court as a witness, you can also apply orally there and then (same article, (5)).

When the copy of the application is served on the defendant, the court can hide the applicant's name and address, so if you are worried about your address being revealed, ask for this too (Article 28). Since you cannot know when the hearings will close, it is safer to apply around the first hearing.

Break the amount claimed down by item and attach the supporting evidence. For fraud, attach a calculation of the money you sent minus any money returned, with the transfer records; for bodily injury, attach the medical certificate, receipts for medical costs and materials showing the period you could not work. This makes it easier for the court to determine the amount.

sections.title: When applications are dismissed, and what next
body: No compensation order is made when the victim's name or address is unclear, the amount of loss cannot be determined, it is not clear whether or to what extent the defendant is liable, or the compensation order would significantly delay the trial (Article 25(3)). This is why applications are often dismissed in cases with several accomplices whose share of responsibility differs.

If an application is dismissed or only partly granted, the applicant cannot challenge it or make the same application again (Article 32(4)). Instead, you can bring a separate civil lawsuit. Once a compensation order (배상명령) becomes final, it can be enforced like a civil judgment (Article 34(1)), and you cannot claim the same amount again through other proceedings within the amount granted (same article, (2)).
A compensation order can be declared provisionally enforceable (Article 31(3)); if so, you can start enforcement even before it becomes final.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: Jisan Law matches the amount of your loss against the evidence item by item, and writes and files the compensation application with the court. If the case is likely to be dismissed, we prepare civil proceedings alongside from the start. If the offender's side proposes a settlement, we negotiate the amount and terms on the victim's behalf, and also consider how to include the agreed amount in a compensation order.

faqs.q: If I get a compensation order, will the money come in straight away?
faqs.a: No. A compensation order is only a ruling that the money must be paid, so if the offender does not pay voluntarily, you must enforce it against their assets using an authenticated copy of the judgment. If the offender has no assets, recovery may be difficult, so it helps to find out about their assets in advance.

faqs.q: What happens to the compensation order if the offender is acquitted on appeal?
faqs.a: If the guilty verdict is overturned on appeal and an acquittal, acquittal on procedural grounds or dismissal of prosecution is given, the original compensation order is also cancelled (Act on Special Cases concerning Expedition of Legal Proceedings Article 33(2)). However, this does not apply to a compensation order made at first instance for an agreed amount (same article, (3)).

guides.title: When you are notified that the offender has made a criminal deposit
guides.lead: If you refused to settle and then receive a court document saying a deposit has been made, it is easy to be thrown. A deposit is not a settlement, and there are separate things to consider about how to state your views as the victim and whether to accept the money.

seo.title: Criminal Deposit Notice for Victims in Korea: Response, Refusal and Accepting with Reservation | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: When an offender makes a criminal deposit in Korea, the court must hear the victim's views before sentencing. Covers what to write in your written opinion, the difference between accepting, refusing and consenting to withdrawal of the deposit, and accepting it as part of damages with a reservation, and how that relates to civil claims.

sections.title: What to check first
bullets: Check the deposit number, deposit office, amount and date of deposit on the notice.
See whether a request for your views from the court or prosecutor came with it, and when the reply is due.
Put a figure on your total losses and compare it with the deposit. List medical costs, losses from time off work, the value of property and emotional harm separately.
Check when the next hearing or sentencing date is. Your views only matter if they are in before sentencing.
Note the dates of any texts and calls in which the offender's side proposed a settlement before depositing.

sections.title: A deposit is not a settlement
body: Even without knowing the victim's personal details, the offender can make a deposit at the deposit office where the trial court is located, identifying the victim by the case number and similar details (Deposit Act (공탁법) Article 5-2). Because this can be done without the victim's consent, the fact that a deposit was made does not mean the victim has forgiven the offender.

If the defendant deposits money, the court must hear the victim's views before pronouncing judgment (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 294-6). Your views are obtained through a request sent via the prosecutor or the victim's lawyer, or in writing, by phone or by text, and they are used only in deciding the sentence, not as evidence that the crime was committed (Criminal Procedure Rules (형사소송규칙) Article 134-13).
If the deposit is far smaller than the harm, or was suddenly made just before sentencing, you can also say so in your written opinion to let the court know.

sections.title: Three options
body: You need to decide whether to accept the deposit, decline it and make your refusal known, or consent to the offender withdrawing the money. In principle, an offender cannot withdraw a criminal deposit (형사공탁), but they can if the victim consents to withdrawal or notifies the deposit office that they refuse to accept it (Deposit Act Article 9-2(1)). Consenting to withdrawal or notifying refusal shows clearly that you want punishment, but it lets the offender take the money back, so you may lose the chance to receive it later.

If you want severe punishment but would still like to receive the money later, one option is not to notify the deposit office, and instead state in your written opinion to the court only that you will not accept it for now and that you want punishment. The right to collect a deposit expires 10 years after it can first be exercised (Article 9(3)).

sections.title: If you decide to accept it
body: If you accept the deposit without saying anything, you are treated as accepting it on the terms on which it was deposited, which can make it hard to dispute the rest of your damages. On the application to collect the deposit, write a reservation (이의유보) stating that you are accepting it as part of the damages. Even so, the money received may be deducted from civil damages later.

To collect it, you need a certificate confirming you are the named depositee, issued by the court or the Public Prosecution Service (Deposit Act Article 5-2(4)). Take the case number and deposit number and ask the relevant office how to get it issued.

If you have not yet decided whether to accept it, there is no need to rush. Give your current view in reply to the court's request, and decide separately about collecting the deposit after the judgment.

sections.title: What to put in your written opinion
body: Set out specifically why you refused to settle, how the deposit compares with your actual losses, how your life has changed since the incident, and how and how often the offender contacted you. Attaching materials showing the harm, such as medical certificates, medical records or confirmation of leave from work, helps the court understand your situation.

As the victim's lawyer, Jisan Law writes and submits your written opinion on the deposit to the court, and once you decide whether to accept the deposit, handles the documents for the deposit office as well. If you need advice, take photos of the notice and the request for your views and contact us.

faqs.q: If I accept the deposit, will the offender get a lighter sentence?
faqs.a: The deposit and whether the victim accepted the money are circumstances taken into account in sentencing. If you accept it, it is more likely to be seen as partial compensation; if you decline and ask for severe punishment, that is also considered. Either way, the court decides, so it is important to state your wishes clearly in your written opinion.

faqs.q: Can I still collect the deposit after the trial is over?
faqs.a: If you did not consent to withdrawal or notify refusal, you can collect it even after the judgment. However, the right expires 10 years after you first could collect it (Deposit Act Article 9(3)).

guides.title: What to watch for when signing a settlement as the victim
guides.lead: If the offender's side has sent you a settlement form, read the wording before you sign. From the victim's side, here is what a non-punishment sentence does, the order in which to receive the money, and what a sentence ending civil claims too really means.

seo.title: Settlement Agreements for Crime Victims in Korea: Non-Punishment Statements and Instalments | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: When a victim signs a criminal settlement agreement in Korea, check the effect of the non-punishment sentence, signing only after the payment arrives, acceleration clauses and notarised deeds for instalments, the scope of wording that waives civil claims, and exposure of personal information.

sections.title: What to check first
bullets: Check what offense the case is. For offenses not punishable against the victim's wishes, such as assault or threats, stating that you do not want punishment ends the case; for offenses such as fraud or bodily injury, it only affects the level of punishment.
List your losses by item. Separate medical costs so far, future medical costs, losses from time off work, the value of property and compensation for emotional distress.
Look at who you are settling with. If a lawyer contacted you, check whether the offender personally signs the agreement or whether there is a power of attorney.
When you receive a draft agreement, do not sign it straight away; take a day or two to read it.

sections.title: A settlement agreement, a non-punishment statement and a withdrawal of complaint are different
body: A settlement agreement (합의서) sets out the money and conditions; a statement of non-punishment (처벌불원서) tells the investigators or the court that you do not want the offender punished; and a withdrawal of complaint (고소취소서) withdraws a complaint you filed. If a settlement agreement contains the sentence "I do not want the offender punished," it can have the same effect as a statement of non-punishment, so look at the sentences, not the title.

Once you withdraw a complaint, or state for an offense not punishable against the victim's wishes that you do not want punishment, you cannot file again or ask for punishment again (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 232). If you hand over a document with this sentence before receiving all the money, there is no way back through the criminal process even if payments stop.

Conversely, if the agreement is only about receiving money and does not say you do not want punishment, state that clearly in the document. That way, there will be no differing interpretations of the wording later.

sections.title: The order in which to receive the money
body: If you are paid in one go, the rule is to hand over the signed settlement agreement and statement of non-punishment only after confirming the payment has arrived. If you exchange them in person, confirm the bank transfer before handing over the documents.

If you agree to instalments, write into the agreement the amount and date of each instalment and a sentence that if any payment is late, the whole remaining balance becomes due immediately. Another option is to have a notary prepare a notarised deed containing consent to compulsory enforcement, so the remaining money can be enforced (Civil Execution Act (민사집행법) Article 56(iv)). It is safest to sign the statement of non-punishment after receiving the last payment; if you must sign it earlier because of the offender's timetable, decide knowing the risk.

sections.title: Check the scope of any sentence ending civil claims
body: If you sign a sentence saying "I will raise no civil or criminal objection whatsoever," it may become difficult to claim additional medical costs even if after-effects appear later. If your treatment is not finished, state what this settlement money covers and leave it on record that future medical costs will be settled separately.

You do not have to put the last digits of your resident registration number or your home address in the agreement. If a copy of your ID must be attached, cover the last digits, and if you are worried about your address being revealed, exchange documents through a lawyer.

sections.title: When and where to submit them
body: Submit the settlement agreement and statement of non-punishment to the investigator in charge while the case is with the police, to the Public Prosecution Service (공소청) after referral, and to the court after indictment. The offender's side usually submits them, but the victim can also submit them directly. For offenses not punishable against the victim's wishes, the wish not to punish must be stated before the first-instance judgment is pronounced to end the case (Criminal Procedure Act Article 232(3)).
Sometimes the offender's side takes the documents and submits them late or not at all, so keep copies of what you signed and check that they were submitted.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: Jisan Law acts for the victim in settlement negotiations with the offender's side. We identify the sentences in the draft agreement that need changing and rewrite them, and negotiate the order of payment and when to hand over the statement of non-punishment. Documents are exchanged through Jisan Law so your contact details and address do not reach the offender's side.

faqs.q: If I change my mind after taking the money and signing a non-punishment statement, can I ask for punishment again?
faqs.a: For offenses not punishable against the victim's wishes, once you have said you do not want punishment, you cannot take it back (Criminal Procedure Act Article 232(3)). For other offenses, you can later submit a petition for severe punishment, but the settlement agreement already submitted and the money received will also be taken into account.

faqs.q: The offender is paying only part of the settlement and says the rest will come after the trial.
faqs.a: Unless the agreement states when and how the rest will be paid and you obtain a notarised deed, it may be hard to collect after the trial. It is safer to make it a condition that you will sign the non-punishment sentence only after receiving the rest.

guides.title: Support available when you are a victim of crime
guides.lead: If you were injured or lost a family member because of a crime and cannot get compensation from the offender, there is a system under which the state pays relief. Here are the requirements and deadlines for crime victim relief, and where to get help with medical costs, psychological support and legal support.

seo.title: Crime Victim Relief in Korea: Eligibility, Deadlines, Medical and Psychological Support | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: If a crime in Korea caused death, disability or serious injury and you have not been compensated, you can apply for crime victim relief. Covers the 3-year and 10-year deadlines, the definition of serious injury, grounds for limiting payment and emergency relief, and where to get help with medical costs, psychological treatment and legal support.
keywords: apply for crime victim relief Korea

sections.title: What to do right away
bullets: Get treatment first. Do not throw away medical certificates, medical bills or hospital admission confirmations; keep them together.

Ask the investigator in charge for information about victim support. The state must inform victims about relief payments and support organisations during investigations and trials (Crime Victim Protection Act (범죄피해자 보호법) Article 8-2).

If you are struggling emotionally, contact a Smile Center (스마일센터), a state-run centre providing psychological care for victims of violent crime, or a Crime Victim Support Center (범죄피해자지원센터) and ask for counselling.
If you have received money from the offender or insurance payouts, note the amounts and dates. These are deducted when relief is decided.
If you feel unsafe because your home address has been exposed, ask the police in charge whether you can get personal protection.

sections.title: Who can receive relief?
body: It covers people who died or suffered a disability or serious injury from a crime against life or body and were not compensated for all or part of the harm, and people harmed because they gave statements or submitted materials in an investigation or trial (Crime Victim Protection Act Article 16). Harm caused by negligence is excluded, so ordinary traffic accidents are not covered (Article 3(1)(iv)).

A serious injury means one of the following that takes 2 months or more to treat: damage to major organs, amputation or serious deformation of part of the body, a similar injury requiring hospital admission of 1 week or more, or a serious mental illness requiring admission of 3 days or more (Enforcement Decree of the same Act, Article 3). Relief is divided into relief for bereaved families, disability relief and serious injury relief (Article 17).

sections.title: Deadlines and procedure
body: Apply to the Crime Victim Relief Committee (범죄피해구조심의회) of the District Public Prosecution Office with jurisdiction over your address, place of residence or the place where the crime occurred (Articles 24 and 25(1)). You cannot apply once 3 years have passed since you learned of the harm or 10 years since it occurred (Article 25(2)).

If the decision may be delayed because the degree of disability or serious injury is not yet clear, you can first apply for emergency relief (Article 28). If your application is rejected or only partly granted, you can apply for a review within 2 weeks of receiving the original decision (Article 27).

sections.title: When relief is reduced or not paid
body: If at the time of the crime the offender was your spouse, a lineal blood relative, a relative within the fourth degree or a relative living with you, relief is in principle not paid (Article 19(1)). If the victim provoked the crime or made the harm worse, all or part of it may not be paid.

If you received damages from the offender, that amount is deducted (Article 21(1)), and if you can receive state compensation or benefits under other laws, relief is not paid to that extent (Article 20). The state takes over the claim for damages against the offender up to the amount of relief it paid (Article 21(2)).

sections.title: Medical, psychological and legal support
body: The state and local governments must put in place measures such as counselling, medical care including help with medical costs, legal aid and housing support (Article 7). Medical costs and emergency living expenses are often applied for through a Crime Victim Support Center, and victims of violent crime and their families can receive psychological assessment and treatment at a Smile Center.

Legal advice is available from the Korea Legal Aid Corporation (대한법률구조공단, call 132 without an area code). Victims of sexual violence can appoint a lawyer, and if they do not have one, the prosecutor can appoint a state-appointed victim's lawyer (Act on Special Cases Concerning the Punishment of Sexual Crimes (성폭력범죄의 처벌 등에 관한 특례법) Article 27). If the offender has been indicted, also look into applying for a compensation order (배상명령) in the criminal trial.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: As the victim's lawyer, Jisan Law writes the criminal complaint, goes with you to the complainant interview and submits a victim's written opinion at trial. We also handle compensation order applications, civil claims and settlement negotiations with the offender's side, and at the consultation we decide with you which routes to use, including crime victim relief, and in what order.

faqs.q: Can I receive relief even if the offender is unknown or has not been caught?
faqs.a: Relief is paid when the harm has not been compensated, so cases where you cannot get compensation because the offender is unknown can also qualify. The deadline runs regardless of whether the offender is caught, so do not let more than 3 years pass from when you learned of the harm.

faqs.q: Can I sue the offender in a civil court after receiving relief?
faqs.a: Yes, but the claim for damages up to the amount of relief paid by the state passes to the state (Crime Victim Protection Act Article 21(2)). The victim can claim the remaining losses directly.

guides.title: When you are caught drink-driving
guides.lead: If you are caught in a drink-driving check, criminal punishment and action on your licence proceed separately. Here are the statutory penalties by blood alcohol level, heavier penalties for repeat offenses, refusing a test, how long until you can get a licence again, and the materials to prepare before questioning.

seo.title: Caught Drink-Driving in Korea: Police Questioning, Penalties and Licence Disqualification | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: If you are caught drink-driving (DUI) in Korea, criminal punishment and administrative action on your licence proceed separately. Covers statutory penalties by blood alcohol level, heavier penalties for repeat offenses within 10 years, penalties for refusing or obstructing a test, licence disqualification periods and sentencing materials to prepare.

sections.title: Criminal punishment and licence action run separately
body: The reading taken at the checkpoint starts two separate procedures. One is the criminal procedure that decides a fine or imprisonment; the other is the administrative procedure that suspends or revokes your licence. The licence decision often comes before the criminal case is decided, and any challenge to it must be made within its own deadline, separately from the criminal case.

The standards for licence action are set out in Annex 28 of the Enforcement Rules of the Road Traffic Act (도로교통법 시행규칙 별표 28). A blood alcohol level of 0.03% or more but under 0.08% means 100 penalty points and a suspension, with each point generally counting as one day; 0.08% or more, causing an accident that injures someone while drunk, or refusing a test leads to revocation. If you have been caught drink-driving before and are caught again, your licence is revoked even if this reading is only at suspension level (Road Traffic Act (도로교통법) Article 93(1)(ii)).

sections.title: Statutory penalties for a first offense
body: Statutory penalties are set by blood alcohol level band (Road Traffic Act Article 148-2(2) and (3)).
bullets: 0.03% or more but under 0.08%: imprisonment of up to 1 year or a fine of up to 5 million won
0.08% or more but under 0.2%: imprisonment of 1 to 2 years or a fine of 5 million to 10 million won
0.2% or more: imprisonment of 2 to 5 years or a fine of 10 million to 20 million won
Refusing a test: imprisonment of 1 to 5 years or a fine of 5 million to 20 million won

sections.title: Getting caught again within 10 years is heavier
body: If you offend again within 10 years of the date a sentence of a fine or heavier became final for drink-driving or refusing a test, the aggravated bands apply. This is the case even if the earlier sentence has since expired (Road Traffic Act Article 148-2(1)).

For 0.03% or more but under 0.2%, the penalty is imprisonment of 1 to 5 years or a fine of 5 million to 20 million won; for 0.2% or more, imprisonment of 2 to 6 years or a fine of 10 million to 30 million won; for refusing or obstructing a test, imprisonment of 1 to 6 years or a fine of 5 million to 30 million won. If someone was injured, dangerous driving causing injury under the Act on the Aggravated Punishment of Specific Crimes (특정범죄 가중처벌 등에 관한 법률) may also be an issue.

sections.title: Refusing a test makes things worse
body: It is easy to think that refusing a test means there is no reading, so you will get off lightly. If there are reasonable grounds to believe you were drunk and you refuse to be tested, that is the offense of refusing a test, and its penalty is heavier than the 0.08% to under 0.2% band. Drinking more after driving to make testing difficult is also punished separately (Road Traffic Act Articles 44(5) and 148-2(2)(ii)).

If you do not accept the breath test result, you can be retested, for example by a blood sample, with your consent (Article 44(3)). If you want to dispute it later, you must ask for this at the scene.

sections.title: What to prepare before questioning
body: In drink-driving cases, the reading and your history are already fixed, so most cases have little to dispute. What remains open is how well you have prepared the materials considered when deciding the outcome and sentence. Also keep, and do not throw away, any documents about the test result you were given at the checkpoint.
bullets: A time-ordered account of how far you drove and why (designated driver call records, etc.)
Efforts to prevent reoffending, such as selling your car or using public transport
A certificate of completing a drink-driving prevention course
Materials showing family dependants and job circumstances
If there was an accident, the victim's settlement agreement and insurance records

sections.title: When you can get a licence again
body: If your licence is revoked for drink-driving, you cannot get a new one for a set period: 1 year from revocation for a first offense; 2 years if you have offended twice or more or caused a traffic accident while drink-driving; 3 years if you have caused two or more drink-driving accidents; and 5 years if you injured someone and left without taking the necessary steps, or caused a fatal accident (Road Traffic Act Article 82(2)).

However, if the criminal case ends with a final sentence lighter than a fine, a suspended sentencing (선고유예) or a suspension of indictment (기소유예), you can get a licence again even within this period (proviso to the same paragraph).
