The end of the disqualification period does not mean you can drive straight away; you must go through the required training and tests again.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: At the consultation, we check how the test was done, the reading and your history, and set out which sentencing materials are likely to be accepted. Before police questioning, we practise likely questions with you, attend the questioning, and submit a defense counsel's written opinion before the decision. If you have been summoned after a drink-driving check, contact us at 02-6951-4097.

faqs.q: My reading was 0.07, it's my first time and there was no accident. How much will the fine be?
faqs.a: The statutory penalty is imprisonment of up to 1 year or a fine of up to 5 million won (Road Traffic Act Article 148-2(3)(iii)). The actual amount depends on how far you drove, the circumstances and materials showing remorse, so it is hard to say in advance. Licence action proceeds separately from the criminal process.

faqs.q: Will a criminal record for a drink-driving fine affect getting a job?
faqs.a: Once a fine becomes final, it stays in your criminal history records. Ordinary companies cannot check criminal records at will, but for appointment as a public official and some qualifications and occupations, laws separately set out disqualifications or a basis for checking, so check the rules for the field you want to work in.

faqs.q: Can I challenge a licence revocation?
faqs.a: Licence revocation is an administrative decision, so it is challenged by an administrative appeal or administrative lawsuit. The deadlines are separate from the criminal case, so note the date you received the decision. If you depend on driving for your livelihood, an objection seeking a reduction is filed with the head of the provincial police agency within 60 days of the decision, but you are not eligible for a reduction if your blood alcohol level exceeded 0.1% or you have a drink-driving record within the past 5 years. You need to look at whether there is anything to dispute in the test procedure or reading, and whether the decision follows the standards.

guides.title: When you are reported for assault
guides.lead: When an argument ends in shoving or an exchange of punches, both people are often booked. Here is the difference between assault and bodily injury, why self-defense is rarely accepted, when to settle and how to prepare for questioning.

seo.title: Reported for Assault in Korea: Mutual Assault, Self-Defense and Settlement | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: If you have been reported for assault in Korea, first check whether the other person submitted a medical certificate and whether it was a mutual fight. Covers statutory penalties for assault, bodily injury and special assault, why self-defense is hard to establish, non-punishment statements and when to settle, and preparing for questioning.

sections.title: What to check first
body: The first few days after a report are your window to gather evidence. If police came to the scene, their dispatch record and what you said then are in the case file, so write down what you said as well as you remember. Take care of the following first.
bullets: Find out whether the other person submitted a medical certificate. If they did, the case may be investigated as bodily injury rather than assault.
Secure CCTV and dashcam footage from the scene, and the contact details of people nearby. Footage from shops and car parks is usually deleted within two weeks to a month.
If you were hit too, see a doctor right away and take photos of your injuries.
Write down in time order who spoke first and who touched whom first, and how many times and in what way.

sections.title: Assault, bodily injury and special assault carry different penalties
body: Assault (폭행) is punishable by imprisonment of up to 2 years, a fine of up to 5 million won, short detention or a petty fine, and cannot be punished if the victim does not want punishment (Criminal Act (형법) Article 260). If an injury results, it becomes bodily injury (상해), punishable more heavily by imprisonment of up to 7 years, suspension of qualifications of up to 10 years or a fine of up to 10 million won, and a settlement does not end the case (Article 257).

Hitting someone while holding a dangerous object such as a phone or a bottle is special assault (특수폭행), punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years or a fine of up to 10 million won (Article 261). Special assault can be punished even if there is a statement of non-punishment. If the other person submits a medical certificate later, the charge can change, so do not relax just because of the allegation you first heard.

sections.title: I hit back after being hit. Why isn't that self-defense?
body: Self-defense (정당방위) is accepted when an act to prevent a present, unlawful attack is reasonable in degree (Criminal Act Article 21). In a fight where punches were exchanged, the courts view attack and defense as mixed together and rarely accept self-defense.

The assessment differs depending on whether you pushed the other person away in the moment to block an attack, or struck back after the attack was over. This distinction turns on the details of the footage and statements, so secure the footage before questioning and set out the exact order of movements. If your intention to defend yourself was clear and you did not go too far, as when pushing away someone holding a weapon to escape, it may be worth arguing.

sections.title: When to settle
body: Simple assault ends with "no right to prosecute" (공소권없음) once a statement of non-punishment (처벌불원서) is submitted. If you settle at the police stage, the case can end with non-referral, so the sooner the better. In mutual assault cases, it is often resolved by both sides exchanging statements of non-punishment.

Once someone says they do not want punishment, it cannot be undone (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 232(3)), so the other person will also be careful about signing. Set the settlement amount based on medical costs, losses and how the incident happened, and send the money by bank transfer to keep a record. Even if the other person asks for an excessive amount, do not angrily cut off talks; ask for supporting evidence such as medical receipts and then negotiate.

sections.title: What to say in questioning
body: Explain what happened before and after in time order; describing accurately what you did is more convincing than listing the other person's faults at length. Check movements such as whether you pushed or hit, and how many times, against the footage.

If you were injured, submit the medical certificate and photos, and if you are also a victim, give a separate statement about that part. Decide whether to ask for the other person to be punished together with your approach to settlement.

sections.title: What not to do
body: Going to the other person or contacting them repeatedly can turn into threats or stalking, let alone a settlement. If you do not know their contact details, pass on your wish to settle through the investigator.
Saying you do not remember because you were drunk does not help the outcome. Separate what you remember from what you do not, and tell the truth.

Swearing at or pushing police officers who came to the scene can add a charge of obstructing official duties. If that has already happened, it is better to tell the truth and apologise in questioning than to hide it.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: At the consultation, we look at the footage, medical certificates and statements to see first whether it is assault or bodily injury and whether there is room to argue self-defense. We practise questioning with you and attend it, and if a settlement is needed, Jisan Law handles contact with the other party on your behalf. The settlement process and materials are set out in a defense counsel's written opinion. If you have just been reported, securing footage is urgent, so contact us at 02-6951-4097.

faqs.q: If the medical certificate says 2 weeks, is it automatically bodily injury?
faqs.a: With a medical certificate, cases are often investigated as bodily injury, but there are court rulings that did not treat extremely minor harm that heals by itself without treatment as bodily injury. The certificate needs to be looked at together with the actual medical records.

faqs.q: The other person hit me first, but I was reported too.
faqs.a: Having been hit first can be taken into account, but it alone does not let you avoid punishment. At the consultation, decide whether to seek punishment as a victim yourself or for both sides to exchange statements of non-punishment.

guides.title: I've been accused of insult over something I said in a group chat
guides.lead: When a single remark in a group chat brings a call from the police, your first worry is whether you will end up with a criminal record. Here, in order, is whether the offense of insult actually applies, and when and how to settle.

seo.title: Accused of Insult Over a Group Chat Message in Korea: What to Do | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: If you have been accused of insult over a group chat message in Korea, first back up the entire conversation and check the number of people, whether the target was identifiable and when the complaint was filed. Covers how publicity is judged, the effect of withdrawing a complaint for an offense requiring one, dealing with settlement demands and preparing for questioning.

sections.title: What to do right away
body: If you received a text asking you to come in, you usually have a few days before the questioning date. There is not much to do in that time, but the order matters.
bullets: Back up the whole group chat using export or screenshots. Keep at least a full day of conversation before and after the line in question.
Write down who was in the chat at the time and how they are related to one another.
Check when the other person learned who you were and when they filed the complaint. A complaint for insult cannot be filed once 6 months have passed since the person learned who the offender was.
Do not leave the chat or delete messages. Traces of deletion remain, and conversations that help you disappear too.

sections.title: Three things are needed for the offense of insult
body: First, it must have been visible to a number of people (publicity, 공연성). The more people in a group chat, the more easily publicity is accepted; in a one-to-one chat with the other person, it is hard for the offense of insult (모욕죄) to apply.

Second, others must be able to tell who the remark was about (identifiability, 특정성). Even if you did not use a name, identifiability is accepted if everyone could tell from the flow of conversation. Third, the expression must be contemptuous of the other person. Even harsh words may not count as insult if they were simply a complaint or criticism.

sections.title: What not to do
body: Contacting the other person directly to argue, or posting an explanation in the same chat, can lead to a new complaint. Asking other members to take your side also undermines the credibility of statements later.

Also avoid sending whatever settlement amount the other person names out of fear. First check whether the offense even applies, and if you do pay, do it at the same time as receiving a settlement agreement and a withdrawal of the complaint.

sections.title: Settlement and withdrawal of the complaint
body: Insult is an offense that requires a complaint (친고죄), so if the complainant withdraws the complaint before the first-instance judgment is pronounced, the case ends. If it is withdrawn at the police stage, the case is not referred on the grounds of no right to prosecute; if after indictment, it ends with a judgment dismissing the prosecution, and no criminal record remains.

There is no going rate for a settlement. It is based on how severe the expression was, whether it was repeated and the harm suffered by the other person, and if whether the offense applies at all is in dispute, there is little reason to rush to settle. Put the amount, wording that the complaint will be withdrawn, and a statement that no civil claim will be made over the same matter in the settlement agreement.

sections.title: What to say in questioning
body: What you said is preserved in screenshots, so rather than denying it, it is better to explain the circumstances before and after that led you to say it. Whether the other person criticised you first, whether it was a one-off and whether you apologised right away are reflected in the outcome.

If you are disputing identifiability or publicity, give specific facts supporting that, such as the number of people in the chat, how nicknames were displayed and the fact that members did not know who each other were.

sections.title: What happens after questioning
body: After questioning, if the police do not find grounds for the allegation, they decide not to refer the case; if they do, they refer it to the Public Prosecution Service (공소청). Insult cases that are referred often lead to a request for a summary order (약식명령) imposing a fine, and if the court issues one, you receive it by post.

If you do not agree with the fine in the summary order, you can request a formal trial within 7 days of being notified (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 453). Requesting a formal trial will not change the outcome to a heavier type of sentence than the summary order, so if you have grounds to dispute it, do not miss this period.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: A managing partner looks at the whole conversation personally and first assesses whether the offense of insult applies. If the case is worth disputing, we practise likely questions with you before questioning, go into the questioning with you and submit a written opinion. If settlement is the better course, we decide the timing and terms with you. If your questioning date is close, contact us first at 02-6951-4097.

faqs.q: There were only three people in the group chat. Is there still publicity?
faqs.a: Even with few people, publicity can be accepted if there is a possibility they would pass the conversation on elsewhere. The relationships among the members and the nature of the chat need to be looked at together.

faqs.q: Once the complaint is withdrawn, do I need to submit anything to the police?
faqs.a: The complainant can submit a withdrawal of complaint directly, or a document stating the intention to withdraw the complaint can be submitted with the settlement agreement to the investigator handling the case or to the court. Be sure to check that it has been submitted.

guides.title: I want to file a counter-complaint for false accusation
guides.lead: After being wrongly accused and cleared, you may want the other person punished for false accusation. Here is why being cleared is not enough on its own to establish false accusation, and the steps for preparing a counter-complaint.

seo.title: Counter-Complaint for False Accusation in Korea: Preparation and Timing | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: For those who were wrongly accused in Korea, received a non-referral or no-suspicion decision, and want to file a complaint for false accusation. Covers the difference between being cleared and false accusation, materials showing falsity and intent, when to file, how to obtain the original case records and what to put in the complaint.

sections.title: What to check first
body: It is tempting to file a counter-complaint while your anger is at its height, but false accusation (무고) is a case in which the complainant has a lot to prove. Start by gathering materials in the order below.
bullets: Confirm the outcome of the original case. See whether you have a non-referral decision, a notice of reasons for non-indictment or an acquittal judgment.
Distinguish whether the reason for the decision was "insufficient evidence" or that facts contrary to the complaint came to light.
Mark the parts of what the other person said in the complaint and in questioning that conflict with objective materials.
Set out the harm the original case caused you (disciplinary action, leave from work, treatment, legal fees).

sections.title: Being cleared is not the same as false accusation
body: When investigators find no suspicion, it often means the allegations in the complaint were not proven. The Supreme Court held that the fact that the reported facts could not be accepted as true is not, on its own, enough to conclude that they were false (Supreme Court Decision 2007도6406, October 11, 2007).

For false accusation to be established, it must be shown that what the other person reported differs from the objective facts and that they knew this. You need materials such as records showing the other person was somewhere else on the day, bank records showing they received money they claimed not to have received, or a message to an acquaintance saying "it isn't true, but I filed a complaint."

sections.title: When should you file?
body: If the original case is still ongoing, it is usually better to wait for the outcome. A counter-complaint during the investigation can look like pressure to force a settlement, and the false accusation investigation effectively stalls until the original case is decided.

The complainant can object within 3 months of receiving a non-referral notice, and the case is then referred to the Public Prosecution Service (공소청) to be decided again (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 245-7). It is safer to file after confirming the original case has been finally resolved. The statute of limitations for false accusation is 10 years, so you will not lose the chance by waiting.

sections.title: How to obtain the original case records
body: Most of the grounds for a false accusation complaint lie in the original case records. As the former suspect, you can apply to inspect and copy your own statement records and the materials you submitted, and you may get part of other documents, such as the complaint, through a freedom of information request (정보공개 청구). They often come with personal information blacked out.
Once you have the records, set out in date order how the other person's statements changed from one interview to the next. If their account changed on key points, that is a clue showing falsity.

sections.title: How to write the complaint
body: Rather than describing at length how you were wronged, a complaint for false accusation works well when it sets the sentences the other person reported side by side with the actual facts. Write it item by item, for example: "On [date], the other party stated X, but the bank records for the same day show Y."

You must also show separately that the other person knew it was false. Circumstances showing it could not have been a mistake because they experienced it directly, things they said before and after filing the complaint, and signs they demanded settlement money are materials that show intent.

sections.title: What not to do
body: Telling people on social media or acquaintances that the other person is a false accuser can turn into defamation. Using a false accusation complaint as leverage to demand money from the other person can raise extortion issues.

If you file a counter-complaint on weak evidence, it ends with no suspicion, and the other person may even accuse you of false accusation in turn. Only write facts that have been confirmed in the complaint.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: A managing partner personally reviews the decision and records of the original case and first tells you whether there are grounds worth pursuing as false accusation. If you decide to file, we write the complaint around the facts that show falsity and intent and go with you to the complainant interview. If the grounds are insufficient, we also consider other options such as a civil claim for damages. Consultations are available 24 hours a day at 02-6951-4097.

faqs.q: If I file a false accusation complaint, will the other person be punished right away?
faqs.a: False accusation goes through a police investigation and the Public Prosecution Service's decision on indictment like any other case. Because falsity and intent must be proven, the investigation can take longer than the original case.

faqs.q: Is it still false accusation if the other person withdrew the complaint?
faqs.a: Even if they withdrew it after making a false report, the offense of false accusation is complete at the moment of reporting. However, if they confess or turn themselves in before the original case becomes final, the sentence is reduced or waived.

faqs.q: Besides false accusation, can I also get damages?
faqs.a: If you suffered harm from a false complaint, you can claim damages such as compensation for emotional distress and legal fees in a civil case. A guilty verdict for false accusation makes this easier to prove.

guides.title: I got into a physical struggle with a police officer
guides.lead: Being arrested for obstructing official duties after pushing a police officer who came to the scene, or shaking off their grip, is more common than you might think. Here is what to do first after release and what is taken into account in the outcome.

seo.title: Physical Struggle with Police in Korea: Responding to an Obstruction of Official Duties Charge | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: If a scuffle with a police officer during a drunken dispute or a check led to a charge of obstructing official duties in Korea, securing footage, apologising and preparing for questioning come first. Covers the procedure after arrest, whether the officer's duty was lawful, what a non-punishment statement means and what affects the outcome.
keywords: obstruction of official duties first offense

sections.title: What to do right away
body: If you were released after questioning, there is time before the next questioning or referral. Here, in order, is what to do in that time.
bullets: Write down what happened that day in time order, as well as you remember. Separate the time the police arrived, what was said first, and the moments of physical contact.
Check where CCTV cameras are at nearby shops and buildings, and if anyone with you filmed it, get the original footage.
If you were injured, see a doctor right away and take photos.
Keep the documents you were given at the arrest and the list of any seized items.

sections.title: What happens after arrest
body: If you are arrested in the act, you are questioned at the police station, and if no detention warrant (구속영장) is requested within 48 hours of the arrest, you are released. If the violence was minor and you have a fixed address, you are often released after questioning, but if the officer was injured or you have a criminal record, a warrant may be requested.

After release, there is further questioning and the case is referred to the Public Prosecution Service (공소청), where the prosecutor decides on a suspension of indictment (기소유예), a request for a summary order (약식명령) or a formal indictment. What you prepare during this process decides the outcome.

sections.title: Points that can be disputed
body: Obstruction of official duties (공무집행방해) only applies if the officer was carrying out their duties lawfully. If the officer tried to take you away by force without meeting the legal requirements, or to arrest you without telling you why, resisting that may not be this offense.

The degree of force also matters. Whether you were trying to pull your arm free or using force against the officer is settled by the footage. Do not rush to admit or deny anything before checking the body camera and surrounding CCTV.

sections.title: What an apology and a non-punishment statement mean
body: For obstruction of official duties, the case does not end even if the officer does not want punishment. Still, a sincere apology and a statement that the officer does not want punishment weigh heavily in deciding the outcome.

Going to see the officer in person or contacting them repeatedly can be a burden on them. Consider conveying your apology through the investigator in charge or in writing. If drinking was behind it, records of joining a programme to cut down on alcohol or of counselling also serve as materials showing you will not reoffend.

sections.title: When other charges are added
body: If there was a separate incident that brought the police out, such as a fight while drinking, drink-driving or a disturbance at a shop, it is investigated together with the obstruction. Settling with the victim of the original incident and apologising to the officer need to be handled separately.

If the officer was injured and has a medical certificate, bodily injury becomes an issue, and if you were holding a dangerous object, it becomes special obstruction of official duties, with the sentence increased by up to half. Depending on what charges the case ends up with, even whether a fine is possible changes, so it is important to put the facts straight before referral.

sections.title: What not to do
body: Simply saying you were drunk and do not remember does not help. Denying actions caught on footage makes you look unremorseful.
Also be careful about posting on social media criticising the police for overreacting. If it is untrue, it raises defamation issues, and it may also be read against you when the outcome is decided.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: If you are under arrest, we visit to decide on your approach to the statement before questioning, and if a warrant is requested, we attend the pre-detention hearing (영장실질심사). After release, we practise questioning with you against the footage and statements, go into the questioning with you, and submit a written opinion with materials on your apology and steps to prevent reoffending. If a family member has been arrested, let us know first at 02-6951-4097.

faqs.q: If it's a first offense, will it end with a fine?
faqs.a: There are cases where a first offense limited to pushing ends with a suspension of indictment or a fine, but if the officer was injured or a dangerous object was involved, it can go to a formal trial. The outcome depends on the degree of force and how you respond afterwards.

faqs.q: I'm preparing for the civil service exam. Will this affect it?
faqs.a: A sentence of imprisonment without labor or heavier, or certain suspended sentences, can disqualify you from appointment as a public official. Whether it ends with a fine or a suspension of indictment matters, so mention this from the start and plan your response around it.

guides.title: I've been accused of defamation over a review I posted
guides.lead: More and more often, people who post a review of something they experienced are accused of defamation by the business or the other person. Here is why you can be accused even when you wrote the truth, and what to prepare to clear yourself.

seo.title: Accused of Defamation Over a Review in Korea | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: If you have been accused of defamation in Korea over a business review, hospital review or post about your experience in an online community, first preserve the original post and your supporting evidence. Covers defamation by stating true facts and public interest, how intent to disparage is judged, deleting the post and when to settle, and preparing for questioning.

sections.title: What to do right away
body: Many people first wonder whether to delete the post, but there are things to preserve before you do.
bullets: Take screenshots of the post showing the date and time it was written, the view count and the comments.
Put contracts, receipts, photos and chat records supporting the facts in your post into one folder.
If there are other people's reviews or news articles about the same business, save them too.
Keep any deletion requests or complaint messages exchanged with the business or the other person exactly as they are.

sections.title: Why can you be accused even if you wrote the truth?
body: Korean law also punishes damaging someone's reputation by publicly revealing true facts, and posts made online are often investigated under the Information and Communications Network Act (정보통신망법). So the fact that you did not lie does not, on its own, make the allegation disappear.

However, the Information and Communications Network Act only punishes where there was intent to disparage, and under the Criminal Act (형법), stating true facts solely for the public interest is not punished. For a review meant to warn other consumers so they do not suffer the same harm, this is the core of the defense.

sections.title: The same experience can be judged differently depending on how you write it
body: A post that sets out verifiable facts such as dates, amounts and what was said, and leaves the judgment to readers, is more likely to be accepted as serving the public interest. On the other hand, attacking someone's character with words like "con artist" or "subhuman," or stating unconfirmed guesses as fact, can be seen as showing intent to disparage, and the offense of insult may also become an issue.
In questioning, you will be asked why you wrote the post. Your answer as to whether it was to pressure them for a refund or to inform others drives the decision, so think it through in advance.

sections.title: Delete the post or settle?
body: Taking the post down is not in itself an admission of the allegation, and it can be taken into account as a step to stop the harm from growing. But be sure to keep the original before deleting it.

Defamation is an offense not punishable against the victim's wishes, so if the other person does not want punishment, the case ends. If there is good room to argue public interest, the usual order is to dispute it first through a written opinion rather than rush to settle, and to consider settling if the post included false statements or went too far.

sections.title: What happens next
body: Once a complaint is filed, the police first interview the complainant, then ask the writer to appear. After questioning, if they find no grounds, the case ends with non-referral; if they find grounds, they refer it to the Public Prosecution Service (공소청), where the prosecutor decides on a suspension of indictment (기소유예), a request for a summary order (약식명령) or a formal indictment.

Separately from the criminal complaint, the business may also sue for damages. If public interest is accepted in the criminal case, it also helps in the civil case, so it is better to prepare your written opinions and materials at the criminal stage with the civil case in mind too.

sections.title: What not to do
body: Posting again about being accused, or continuing to mention the business, can lead to a new complaint. Also avoid copying the same content to other platforms.

Contacting the business to complain emotionally, or setting conditions such as "I'll delete the post if you refund me," can also be interpreted against you. If you need to talk, keep it short and in a form that leaves a record.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: A managing partner looks at the original post together with your supporting materials and assesses whether arguments about public interest and intent to disparage can be made. Before questioning, we practise questions about how you came to write the post and about each expression, attend the questioning with you and submit a defense counsel's written opinion with the supporting materials attached. If you have been summoned, contact us at 02-6951-4097.

faqs.q: I didn't use the business name; I only wrote "a certain restaurant in a certain neighbourhood."
faqs.a: If people could tell which shop it was from information such as the neighbourhood, type of business or photos, the victim is considered identified. To dispute identifiability, it must be shown that the shop could not be recognised from that information alone.

faqs.q: The business says it will also file a complaint for obstruction of business.
faqs.a: A review that truthfully describes your actual experience as a customer is unlikely to amount to obstruction of business (업무방해). If you wrote it without having used the business, or it contained untrue statements, obstruction of business may also become an issue.

guides.title: Can I use a secret recording as evidence?
guides.lead: Many people have made, or are thinking of making, recordings to prove verbal abuse, an affair or mistreatment. Here is which recordings count as evidence, which can actually get you punished, and what to do if you have already recorded something.

seo.title: Using Secret Recordings as Evidence in Korea and the Protection of Communications Secrets Act | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: Wondering whether you can submit a secret recording as evidence in Korea? First check whether you were a party to the conversation. Covers punishment for recording other people's conversations under the Protection of Communications Secrets Act and the ban on using them as evidence, how to store and submit recordings, and alternatives to recording.

sections.title: What to check first
body: Before you submit a recording anywhere, check the points below. If you skip this, you may end up facing a complaint yourself while trying to submit evidence.
bullets: Check whether you took part in the recorded conversation from start to finish.
Listen through by time to see whether recording continued during any stretch when you were not there.
Check whether it was made by hiding a recorder or installing an app on someone else's phone.
Think back to whether you have already sent the file to or played it for anyone else.

sections.title: Conversations you took part in can be used as evidence
body: What the Protection of Communications Secrets Act (통신비밀보호법) prohibits is recording a non-public conversation between other people. The Supreme Court held that when one of three people in a conversation records it, that is not a recording of a conversation between others (Supreme Court Decision 2006도4981, October 12, 2006).

So secretly recording verbal abuse your boss directed at you, or what someone said to you on a call, does not violate this law and can be submitted as evidence in court. However, spreading the recording can cause other problems such as defamation depending on its content, so submit it only where it needs to go.

sections.title: If you recorded a conversation between other people
body: Recording a conversation between others, for example with a recorder left running while you were away, a recorder hidden in a car or room, or a recorder put in a child's bag, can be punished by imprisonment of 1 to 10 years and suspension of qualifications of up to 5 years, with no fine available. Disclosing or leaking the content carries the same penalty.

Recordings obtained this way cannot be used as evidence in a trial or disciplinary proceedings. In a case where a parent put a recorder in their child's bag to record classroom conversations, the Supreme Court did in fact deny the recording's admissibility (Supreme Court Decision 2020도1538, January 11, 2024).

sections.title: How to store recording files
body: Leave the original file on your phone as it is, and back up a copy separately. If only an edited or trimmed file remains, you will be suspected of tampering.
When submitting to a court, it is usual to submit a transcript together with the recording. Noting the date, place and participants separately makes it easier to explain later.

If your recording app automatically uploads to the cloud, check where the original is stored. If you do not move the original before changing or resetting your phone, information such as when the file was created may be lost.

sections.title: Alternatives to recording
body: In cases such as an affair or abuse where you cannot be part of the conversation yourself, first look for materials you can obtain lawfully, such as text and messenger records, card statements, medical certificates and statements from people around you. If you are in a lawsuit, you can also obtain materials through the court, by a request for fact-finding or an order to produce documents.
If you have already recorded a conversation between other people, do not send or submit the file to anyone; get advice first.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: A managing partner personally hears how the recording was made and listens to the file, then separates the parts you can submit as evidence from the risky parts. If you have already been accused because of a recording, we respond by preparing you for questioning, attending with you and submitting written opinions, and if your phone is seized, we apply to attend the forensics. Consultations are available 24 hours a day at 02-6951-4097.

faqs.q: I left a recording running during a meeting and stepped out briefly.
faqs.a: The recording while you were there is fine, but conversations between others recorded while you were away may count as recording other people's conversations. Do not use that section; keep the original file as it is and get advice.

faqs.q: Do I have to tell the other person I'm recording a call?
faqs.a: If you are a party to the call, recording it without telling the other person does not violate the Protection of Communications Secrets Act. However, depending on how you make the recording public, other problems may arise.

guides.title: When you are reported for stalking
guides.lead: When a stalking report is made, measures such as a ban on approaching or contacting the person are often imposed before any questioning. Here, in order, is what to comply with and what to prepare from the day you receive the decision.

seo.title: Reported for Stalking in Korea: Provisional Measures and Police Questioning | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: If you have been reported for stalking in Korea, first check the scope of any emergency or provisional measures. Covers what contact to avoid, the 7-day deadline to appeal, what can be disputed in questioning such as justifiable reasons and repetition, the effect of a settlement, and course orders and later procedures.

sections.title: What to do right away
body: The duration and how to challenge it differ depending on whether the document you received right after the report is a police emergency measure (긴급응급조치) or a court provisional measure (잠정조치). Check in the order below.
bullets: Write down the name of the document, the decision date and the date you were notified. An appeal against a provisional measure must be filed within 7 days of notice.

Check the scope of what is prohibited. For a ban on approaching, check who is covered (the person, people living with them, family) and where (home, workplace); for a ban on contact, check whether calls, texts, messenger apps and social media are all included.
Do not delete any messages exchanged with the other person; back them all up. Records of the other person contacting you first also matter.
If there are shared belongings, money matters or children involved, do not contact them directly; list these issues instead.

sections.title: Whatever you do, do not do these
body: The most common mistake is getting in touch to explain because you feel wronged. Apology texts, offering to return belongings, asking a friend to pass on a message, messages from a new number or another account, and comments or reactions on the other person's social media can all be treated as prohibited contact.

Do not reply even if the other person contacts you first. If you run into them by chance, do not speak to them and leave right away; noting the time, place and why you were there helps later in explaining that it was not deliberate.

sections.title: What happens next
body: The police interview the victim and analyse the contact records, then question the suspect, and if they find grounds, they refer the case to a prosecutor. The prosecutor decides whether to indict and, if needed, asks the police for supplementary investigation.

Among provisional measures, bans on approach and contact cannot exceed 3 months, but can be extended twice by 3 months each. If the prosecutor decides not to indict, the provisional measure lapses. If the decision contains errors of fact or circumstances have changed, you can apply to the court to cancel or change it.

sections.title: What can be disputed in questioning
body: A stalking offense is committed when someone continuously or repeatedly contacts or approaches another person against their will and without a justifiable reason, causing them anxiety. The number and period of contacts, when you learned they did not want contact, whether you had a reason to get in touch, and whether what you said was threatening are each examined.

Courts look not so much at whether the other person actually felt anxious as at whether the conduct was objectively likely to cause anxiety. So materials showing the full flow of the conversation are more persuasive than claiming "the other person was fine with it."

sections.title: If you are thinking about settling
body: Stalking offenses can be punished even if the victim does not want punishment, but a settlement weighs heavily in a suspension of indictment (기소유예) or the sentence. If approach and contact are banned, you must not convey your wish to settle directly either; you need to go through a lawyer. If you have started counselling or a treatment programme on your own, submit those records as well.

If found guilty, you may be ordered, along with the sentence, to complete a course of up to 200 hours or a stalking treatment programme. Counselling records from beforehand serve as evidence that the risk of reoffending is low, and it also helps to set out steps you have taken to avoid running into the person again, such as deleting their contact details or moving.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: At the consultation, we read the scope of the decision with you and separate what you must comply with from what can be disputed. We judge within the deadline whether an appeal or an application to cancel or change it is needed, practise likely questions before questioning and attend with you. We also submit a defense counsel's written opinion organising the contact records. If you want to settle, Jisan Law handles contact with the victim's side on your behalf so you do not breach the ban on approach and contact. If you have received a decision, contact us at 02-6951-4097.

faqs.q: Can I be punished for breaching an emergency measure from the police too?
faqs.a: Failing to comply with an emergency measure can be punished by imprisonment of up to 1 year or a fine of up to 10 million won. However, this does not apply if the prosecutor did not request after-the-fact approval or the judge did not approve it.

faqs.q: We live in the same neighbourhood, so I can't avoid running into them. Do I have to move?
faqs.a: The basic rule is not to enter the distance and places set in the decision. If your daily lives overlap so much that it is hard to comply, you can consider applying to the court to change the measure.

guides.title: When the police came because of domestic violence
guides.lead: When the police are called over a fight between spouses or family members, you may be barred from going home from that very night. Here is what you must comply with after the police leave, and what procedures follow.

seo.title: Police Called for Domestic Violence in Korea: Temporary Measures and Procedures | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: If the police came because of domestic violence in Korea, first check what emergency temporary measures and temporary measures were imposed. Step by step: when you must leave home, contact about children, referral and domestic protection cases, the effect of the victim not wanting punishment, and what to do if both sides were hurt.
keywords: police called over marital fight Korea

sections.title: What to do right away
body: First sort out the documents you were given and what you were told at the scene. The measures imposed that night are the starting point for what follows.
bullets: If you received an emergency temporary measure decision (긴급임시조치결정서) or a notice, check whether it orders you to leave the home, not to come within 100 metres, or not to call or text.
If you must leave the home, decide where you will stay for a few days, and ask the police to accompany you to collect essential belongings.
If you were also hurt, see a doctor right away and take photos of your injuries.
Note how the fight started and when, the time of the 112 emergency call, and which family members were there.

sections.title: Whatever you do, do not do these
body: Contacting your spouse to ask them to withdraw the report, or getting other family members to persuade them, can look like a breach of the ban on approach or pressure on the victim. Also avoid going near the home after drinking. Failing without good reason to comply with temporary measures such as removal from the home, a ban on approach or a ban on contact can be punished by imprisonment of up to 1 year, a fine of up to 10 million won or short detention.

If some contact is truly necessary, such as taking children to and from school or living expenses, do not do it directly; first look for a way through a lawyer, or apply to the court to change the measure.

sections.title: How the case proceeds
body: If a judicial police officer imposed an emergency temporary measure, a temporary measure (임시조치) is requested from the court within 48 hours and a judge decides on it. Temporary measures such as removal from the home and a ban on approach cannot exceed 2 months, but can be extended up to twice.

When the police finish the investigation, they refer the case to a prosecutor and can give their view on whether it should be handled as a domestic protection case. The prosecutor can indict for a criminal trial, send the case to the family court as a domestic protection case, or suspend the indictment on condition of counselling.

sections.title: If the case is sent as a domestic protection case
body: A domestic protection case (가정보호사건) is a procedure that imposes protective dispositions, such as restrictions on approach, course orders, probation or referral to counselling, instead of criminal punishment. There will be an interview with a court investigator and a hearing date, and you can appoint a lawyer as your assistant. Records of counselling you started on your own, the family's views and a plan to prevent recurrence are taken into account in deciding the disposition.

A case can be handled as a domestic protection case even if the victim does not want punishment. Conversely, if there is bodily injury or repeated violence, it is more likely to go to a criminal trial.

sections.title: If you were hit too, and if you are considering divorce
body: If both sides used their hands, both can be treated as perpetrators and victims of domestic violence. You need medical records and photos of the harm you suffered too, so that the full course of events is set out in a balanced way.

If you are also thinking about divorce or custody, what you say in the criminal proceedings and the outcome can be used as material in the family case as well. Stating only the facts, focusing on dates and actions, works better in both proceedings than emotionally blaming the other person.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: At the consultation, we start by setting out the scope of the temporary measures and what you must comply with, and consider applying to cancel or change them if needed. We practise likely questions before police questioning and attend it with you, and submit a written opinion either arguing that a domestic protection case is appropriate or disputing the allegation. If the case is sent as a domestic protection case, Jisan Law acts as your assistant, submitting written opinions and attending hearings. If some contact is essential during the temporary measures, we also work out which route is safe. Even the day after the police came, contact us at 02-6951-4097 before a questioning date is set.

faqs.q: If my spouse withdraws the report, does the case end?
faqs.a: For simple assault, criminal punishment can be avoided if the victim does not want punishment, but even then the prosecutor can handle it as a domestic protection case. Bodily injury or special assault can be indicted regardless of whether the victim wants punishment.

faqs.q: Can I also report the part where I was hit?
faqs.a: If both sides used violence, each can report their own harm, and the investigation proceeds together. It is important to get medical records and photos quickly.

faqs.q: Can I challenge a temporary measure decision?
faqs.a: If the decision violates the law, involves a serious error of fact or is plainly unjust, you can appeal within 7 days of being notified.

guides.title: When the police contact you after you left an accident scene
guides.lead: Many people drive off after a minor collision thinking it was nothing, only to be asked by the police a few days later to come in. The offense that applies, and how to respond, differ greatly depending on whether someone was injured or only property was damaged.

seo.title: Police Contact After Leaving an Accident Scene in Korea (Hit-and-Run) | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: If the police contacted you after you left the scene of an accident in Korea, first find out whether it is being treated as hit-and-run causing injury or failure to take measures after an accident. Covers securing dashcam footage, what not to do, arguing you did not know about the accident, compensation and settlement, and what to explain in questioning.
keywords: leaving after property damage accident Korea
failure to take measures after accident Korea
leaving scene of minor collision Korea

sections.title: What to check first
body: When the police call, panic makes it easy to say whatever you remember. On the call, just agree a date to appear, and first check the points below.
bullets: Ask whether the other party says they were injured or only that the car or property was damaged. This decides which offense applies.
Take out the dashcam memory card right away and keep the original. The accident footage could be overwritten.
Before repairing scratches or dents on your car, take photos with the date visible.
Write down your route and times on the day of the accident, any passengers and your call records.
Report the accident to your insurer and get the claim number.

sections.title: Whatever you do, do not do these
body: Rushing to repair or wash your car before you appear raises suspicion that you tried to remove traces. Deleting or formatting the dashcam is an even bigger problem.

Also avoid contacting the other party emotionally or pressing them to withdraw the report. If contact is needed, keep it to calmly passing on the insurance claim and your apology, and it is better to settle after the facts have been sorted out.

sections.title: Which offense is at issue
body: If someone was injured and you left without helping them, hit-and-run causing injury (도주치상) under the Act on the Aggravated Punishment of Specific Crimes (특정범죄 가중처벌 등에 관한 법률) is at issue, with a statutory penalty of imprisonment for a fixed term of 1 year or more, or a fine of 5 million to 30 million won. According to court rulings, leaving an injured person behind can count as fleeing even if you handed over your contact details.

If only property was damaged and you did not take the necessary measures, it is failure to take measures after an accident (사고후미조치) under the Road Traffic Act (도로교통법), punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years or a fine of up to 15 million won. If you only scratched a parked car and did not leave your contact details, it is much lighter: a fine of up to 200,000 won, short detention or a petty fine.

sections.title: What to explain in questioning
body: If you did not know about the accident, you need to show with the dashcam footage and photos how light the impact was, whether there was a noise and whether the damage to the car was noticeable. If you knew but left, set out truthfully why you left, how you judged the victim's condition and whether you tried to get in touch afterwards.

Filling in parts you are not sure about with guesses will count against you later when they do not match the footage. It is better to say you do not know what you do not know. Read the whole record, and if anything is written differently from what you said, ask for it to be corrected before signing.

sections.title: Compensation and settlement
body: Criminal proceedings go ahead separately from the insurance claim, so a settlement with the victim greatly affects the outcome. If someone was injured, consider a criminal settlement while checking on their recovery, and if settlement is difficult, consider a criminal deposit (형사공탁).

If your licence is revoked for injuring someone and failing to take the necessary measures and report it, you cannot get a licence again for 4 years from revocation, or 5 years if combined with drink-driving. If you drive for a living, you also need to look within the deadline at whether there are grounds to challenge the licence decision, alongside the criminal outcome.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: At the consultation, we look at the dashcam footage and photos with you and first judge whether there is room to dispute that you fled, or whether the case will be treated as failure to take measures after an accident. We practise likely questions before questioning, attend the questioning at the traffic investigation unit with you, and submit a defense counsel's written opinion on what happened and the compensation made. If a date to appear has been set, contact us at 02-6951-4097.

faqs.q: Can I postpone the date to appear?
faqs.a: If you have a valid reason, you can agree a new date with the investigator in charge. However, repeatedly postponing without reason can look bad, so only adjust it as much as you need to prepare.

faqs.q: I was told no one was hurt. Could a medical certificate turn up later?
faqs.a: Sometimes a medical certificate is submitted a few days after an accident. In that case, you need to check whether the diagnosis fits the force of the impact and what the victim said and did at the time.

guides.title: When you are reported for child abuse
guides.lead: Whether it is a parent's discipline or guidance at a daycare centre or school, once a child abuse report is made, an investigation by the district office and a police investigation start almost at the same time. Here is what to do, and what to avoid, in the first few days.

seo.title: Reported for Child Abuse in Korea: What Parents, Teachers and Childcare Workers Should Do | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: If you have been reported for child abuse in Korea, first secure CCTV and records of what happened. Covers the difference between the district office's child abuse investigation and the police investigation, why you must not contact the child or parents directly, the exception for teachers' guidance and the superintendent's opinion, and later outcomes.
keywords: childcare worker reported for abuse Korea
teacher reported for child abuse Korea

sections.title: What to do right away
body: The time right after you learn of the report is when you can gather materials. Do the following before your memory fades.
bullets: Write down what happened on the day in question in time order, including what the child did, what you said and did, and who else was there.
If there is CCTV at the daycare centre or classroom, ask the institution to preserve it. It is deleted once the retention period passes.
If you are a teacher, check what was reported to the school and the education office, and the procedure for the superintendent of education to submit an opinion.
Record the dates of contact from the district office or police, the person in charge and the materials requested.

sections.title: Whatever you do, do not do these
body: However wronged you feel, avoid explaining yourself directly to the parents or asking the child about that day again. You may be suspected of trying to change their account, and the case becomes more complicated by questions about the child's statement having been contaminated.

If it is a case involving a parent, do not criticise the person who reported it or blame the child in front of the child. Emergency or temporary measures may be imposed to protect the child, so if there are any, comply exactly with their scope.

sections.title: The investigation runs on two tracks
body: A child abuse officer at the city, county or district office can require you to appear, make statements and submit materials to protect the child and assess the case, while the police investigate it as a criminal case. The two procedures have different purposes, but your statements will be compared, so you must give a consistent account of the same facts.

Child abuse (아동학대) can be established once there is a risk of harm to the child's health or normal development, and according to court rulings it is enough that the person was aware of that risk as a possibility (dolus eventualis). So rather than your intentions, be ready to explain specifically what you actually said and did, how often, and the context at the time.

sections.title: What teachers and childcare workers should check
body: Legitimate educational activities and student guidance by kindergarten, elementary, middle and high school teachers are not regarded as child abuse. If conduct during educational activities is reported, the superintendent of education with jurisdiction can give an opinion, and the police and prosecutor must file that opinion in the case record and take it into account.

Childcare workers and teachers are mandatory reporters, so if found guilty, their sentence can be increased by up to half, and even a fine alone is, as a rule, accompanied by an order restricting employment at child-related institutions. From the start, you need to respond with this in mind as well as the allegation itself.

sections.title: The outcome can take several forms
body: When the police finish the investigation, they refer the case to a prosecutor and can give their view on whether it should be handled as a child protection case. If the prosecutor finds no grounds, they decide not to indict; even if there are grounds, considering the nature of the case, the relationship with the child, the potential for change and the wishes of the child's side, they can suspend the indictment on condition of counselling, treatment or education, or send the case to court as a child protection case (아동보호사건).

In a child protection case, protective dispositions such as restrictions on approach, restrictions on exercising parental authority, course orders or probation are imposed instead of criminal punishment. Which route the case takes makes a big difference to employment restrictions and professional consequences, so it is a good idea to make this point clear in a written opinion before referral.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: At the consultation, we set out the reported scene and its context, and look with you at whether it can be explained as falling within legitimate guidance. We practise likely questions before questioning, attend the police questioning with you and submit a defense counsel's written opinion based on CCTV and records. If you have been summoned, contact us at 02-6951-4097.

faqs.q: I only hit my child once. Will I be punished?
faqs.a: If even a single incident can be seen as physical abuse, it is subject to investigation. In cases involving parents, taking into account keeping the child in the family, the indictment is sometimes suspended on condition of counselling or education, or the case is handled as a child protection case.

faqs.q: Do I have to attend the district office's investigation too?
faqs.a: Unless you have a valid reason, you must comply with a child abuse officer's request to appear, make statements and submit materials. However, it is a good idea to work out in advance what to say and how, together with your preparation for police questioning.

guides.title: When you are reported for road rage
guides.lead: If the other driver submits dashcam footage after a dispute on the road, the police get in touch a few weeks later. Retaliatory driving is dealt with as offenses such as special intimidation under the Criminal Act and may not end lightly, so start by securing footage and setting out what happened.

seo.title: Reported for Road Rage in Korea: Dashcam, Questioning and Settlement | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: If you have been reported for road rage in Korea, first secure your own original dashcam footage. Covers the difference between special intimidation and reckless driving, what not to do, explaining the reason for braking and distances in questioning, compensation and settlement, licence action and what happens next.

sections.title: What to do right away
body: If you have been summoned, gather your own materials before setting a date.
bullets: Take out your dashcam memory card and keep it. Footage older than the report may already have been deleted, so copy every file that remains.
Write down the date and place of the incident, where you were driving from and to, and any passengers.
If the other driver cut in dangerously or threatened you first, mark the minute and second where that happens.
If the cars collided, gather photos of both cars and your insurance claim details.

sections.title: Whatever you do, do not do these
body: Going to see or contacting the driver who reported you to argue can turn into intimidation. Posting the other car's licence plate or footage in online communities can also create other problems such as defamation.

If you make up plausible details in questioning for parts you do not remember, they will not match the footage and you will lose credibility. Explain things based on facts that can be checked on the footage. If you want to apologise to the other driver, it is safer to convey that through the investigators or your lawyer.

sections.title: Which allegation is at issue
body: If you cut in front of a particular car and braked suddenly, or tailgated it closely to frighten the driver, special intimidation (특수협박) is at issue; if there was an actual collision, special assault or special property damage is at issue. Court rulings treat a car as a dangerous object in such situations. Even if you were not targeting anyone in particular, committing a series of violations such as running red lights, speeding and sudden braking that created danger is reckless driving (난폭운전).

Special intimidation carries imprisonment of up to 7 years or a fine of up to 10 million won, while reckless driving carries imprisonment of up to 1 year or a fine of up to 5 million won, a big difference in statutory penalty. Which allegation the case ends up as changes the outcome greatly.

sections.title: What to explain in questioning, and what happens next
body: Explain, matched to the timestamps on the footage, whether you braked because of the car in front, a signal or road conditions, what the distance and speed relative to the other car were, and how many seconds it lasted. If the other driver threatened you first, submit that footage too.

After police questioning, if they find grounds, the case is referred to a prosecutor, who decides whether to indict. Separately from the criminal process, special intimidation and similar offenses committed with a car are grounds for licence revocation or suspension, so if you receive notice of a decision, consider within the deadline whether to challenge it.

sections.title: Compensation and materials showing it won't happen again
body: If the cars collided, conveying an apology and a willingness to compensate the other driver, separately from the insurance claim, is the starting point for a settlement. If the other driver claims to have been hospitalised, check whether the diagnosis matches the force of the impact, but it is better to keep that dispute separate from your apology.

If you drive for a living, prepare a certificate of employment and income records, and if you have taken anger management counselling or traffic safety education on your own, submit those records too. Showing with materials that the same thing will not happen again is taken into account in deciding the outcome.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: At the consultation, we look at the reported footage and your own dashcam together and separate what can be disputed as special intimidation from what should be admitted. We practise likely questions before questioning, attend the questioning with you, and submit a defense counsel's written opinion setting out the circumstances showing there was no intent and the compensation made. Dashcam footage needs to be checked before it is deleted, so if the police have contacted you, call us at 02-6951-4097.

faqs.q: If I settle, does the case end?
faqs.a: Special intimidation and special assault can be punished even if the victim does not want punishment, so a settlement alone does not end the case. However, settlement and compensation weigh heavily in the decision to indict and the sentence.

faqs.q: I don't have dashcam footage. What can I do?
faqs.a: You can fill in what happened with statements from passengers, footage from nearby cars or road CCTV, and navigation records. It is important to gather as much material as possible showing the situation before and after, so the decision is not based on the reported footage alone.

guides.title: When the police contact you as a voice phishing cash courier
guides.lead: If you collected and passed on cash thinking it was a part-time job, and the police then contacted you about a voice phishing case, what you protect and gather before your first questioning greatly affects the outcome. Here it is, in order.

seo.title: Police Contact as a Voice Phishing Cash Courier in Korea: What to Do Before Questioning | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: If you passed on cash for a high-paying part-time job and the Korean police contacted you as a voice phishing cash collector, preserving chat records and setting out the extent of your involvement come first. Covers what not to do, what you will be asked in questioning, what to do if you are worried about detention, and how to compensate victims.
keywords: voice phishing courier police questioning Korea
voice phishing cash collector contacted by police
high-paying part-time job police summons Korea

sections.title: What to check first
body: Take care of these one by one from the day you are contacted. The records that remain now are the most important materials for showing later that you were used.
bullets: Check the offense, case number and investigator in charge in the summons text
Do not delete Telegram or KakaoTalk conversations; save them as screenshots and with the chat export function
Gather the job advertisement, any company materials you received and the account records showing your pay
Note down, by date, where and from whom you received how much, and how you passed it on
Stop following instructions, and keep any money or items you still have exactly as they are

sections.title: What not to do
body: If you reset your phone or leave the chat rooms out of fear, you will be suspected of trying to destroy evidence. Telling the organisation that the police have contacted you causes the same problem.

Putting off the date and cutting off contact is also dangerous. Couriers who met victims in person are easy to identify, so if you do not appear, an arrest warrant (체포영장) may be requested. If you need to change the date, explain your situation to the investigator and set a new one.

sections.title: What you will be asked in questioning
body: The investigator will start with how you found the job, then ask in turn whether there was an interview, how the work was explained to you, how much you were paid and how, who you were told to say you were when collecting cash, and how you passed the money on. They will also always ask when you started to feel something was wrong.

Do not guess at dates or amounts you do not remember; say you will check the records and submit them. Inconsistent statements undermine the credibility of saying you did not know. Equally, hiding unfavourable facts that then conflict with your bank records has the same result.

sections.title: If you are worried about arrest or detention
body: If you made several collections or the amounts were large, you may be arrested without a summons first. If a family member has been arrested, find out which police station they are at and ask first for a lawyer's visit. If a detention warrant (구속영장) is requested, at the pre-detention hearing (영장실질심사) we show that you have a fixed home and job, a clear intention to appear and no risk of destroying evidence. A certificate of employment, family relationship documents and the chat records you have already preserved are used at this point.

sections.title: Compensating victims and reduced sentences
body: Taking part in voice phishing is an offense where the investigation and trial continue even if the victim does not want punishment, but compensating victims weighs heavily in the outcome and sentence. If there are several victims, consider a settlement or criminal deposit (형사공탁) for each one.

From September 8, 2026, if during an investigation or trial you provide statements or materials revealing crimes by other members of the organisation, or tip off investigators about catching offenders or the proceeds of crime, your sentence can be reduced or waived (Special Act on the Prevention of Telecommunications Financial Fraud and Refund for Damage (전기통신금융사기 피해 방지 및 피해자산 환급에 관한 특별법) Article 17-2). It also applies to cases already under way at that time, so if you have any information, consider organising it with your lawyer and submitting it.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: A managing partner sets out with you, in date order, everything from your recruitment to your last collection, and practises questions about intent with you. We attend the questioning and raise objections on the spot to leading questions, and if your phone has been seized, we apply to attend the forensics. If you have been arrested, we respond by visiting you and attending the pre-detention hearing. If you have been contacted, let us know first at 02-6951-4097. We answer 24 hours a day.

faqs.q: Can I be detained even if I only did it once?
faqs.a: Even once, detention may be considered if the amount was large or you pretended to be someone else. Conversely, even with several collections, some cases proceed without detention when the person has a fixed home, has preserved evidence and appears faithfully, so showing cooperation with appearing and submitting materials from the start is important.

faqs.q: Do I have to give back the daily pay I received?
faqs.a: Pay obtained through crime can be confiscated or its value collected. Keep an accurate record of the amount you received, and decide with your lawyer whether to use it to compensate victims.

guides.title: When your company says it will file an embezzlement complaint
guides.lead: If your company is raising embezzlement, demanding a signed pledge or repayment, or telling you it will file a criminal complaint, confirm the amount before you sign or send any money. Here is what to do before and after a complaint.

seo.title: When Your Employer Threatens an Embezzlement Complaint in Korea | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: If your company in Korea is demanding a pledge or repayment and threatening a complaint for occupational embezzlement, check the transactions and amounts it is disputing before you sign anything. Covers organising materials, what to be careful about when talking to the company, repayment and settlement, and unpaid wages.

sections.title: What to check first
body: Without knowing what the company is claiming and on what basis, you can neither admit nor rebut anything. Sort things out in the order below.
bullets: Ask the company to give you in writing the period, the list of transactions and the amounts it is disputing
Do not sign a pledge or confirmation right away; get a copy of the wording
Download your own bank account and card statements for that period
Gather materials you legitimately hold, such as approval records and messages with instructions from your superiors
If you have unpaid salary or severance, list it separately

sections.title: When talking to the company
body: If you start by apologising when you speak to or meet someone from the company, it may be taken as admitting everything. Even if there is something to admit, first pin down which transactions are meant before saying anything.

Taking large amounts of company materials without permission to use as evidence can become another dispute. Start with materials you legitimately held for your work, and for accounting records that only the company has, ask for them to be produced during the investigation.

sections.title: How to dispute the amount
body: Break the amount the company claims into a table by transaction, and next to each, note what it was actually used for and the supporting evidence. Once business expenses, advances the company knew about and allowed, amounts already settled and amounts used personally are separated, it becomes clear what to dispute and what to admit. If the company relies on an internal audit report, also check what materials it was calculated from and whether any settlement records were left out.

Occupational embezzlement (업무상횡령) is punishable by imprisonment of up to 10 years or a fine of up to 30 million won (Criminal Act (형법) Article 356), and if the amount gained is 500 million won or more, the Act on the Aggravated Punishment of Specific Economic Crimes (특정경제범죄법) applies and the penalty becomes much heavier. So how the amount is calculated ties directly to the level of punishment.

sections.title: Repayment and settlement
body: If there is an amount you admit, repaying early helps the outcome. However, sending whatever the company names before the amount is settled, or making instalment promises you cannot keep, leaves disputes for later.

The settlement agreement should include the amount repaid, how it is paid, a statement that the company does not want you punished, and that no further civil claims will be made. Occupational embezzlement is an offense where the investigation can continue even if the complaint is withdrawn, so the aim is to have the non-punishment wording taken into account in the outcome.

sections.title: Wage issues are dealt with separately
body: Sometimes a company withholds salary or severance on the grounds of the embezzled money. Unpaid wages can be dealt with through separate procedures such as a petition to the Ministry of Employment and Labor, so keep this separate from the embezzlement case. Conversely, taking company money first because of unpaid wages can itself become an embezzlement issue. When combining severance settlement and repayment of embezzled money in one agreement, state each amount separately.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: A managing partner reviews the company's claims transaction by transaction and looks at the wording of any pledge or settlement agreement with you. If a complaint is filed, we practise likely questions about the flow of funds with you, attend the questioning, and submit a written opinion with supporting evidence for the amounts in dispute. If the company has contacted you, get advice at 02-6951-4097 before you sign anything.

faqs.q: The company says it will file a complaint right away unless I sign a pledge.
faqs.a: Signing a pledge does not stop a complaint, and it may even be used like a confession in the investigation. Get the wording, check the amount and content, and then decide whether to sign.

faqs.q: I think the company has inflated the loss.
faqs.a: The amount the company submitted is only the complainant's claim. If you submit materials matching each transaction to its use and supporting evidence, investigators will look at the amount again.

guides.title: When you are accused of fraud over a second-hand sale
guides.lead: If you have been accused because you took payment in a second-hand sale and did not send the item, how to respond depends on whether there is one case or several. Here is what to do now, what not to do and the order for repaying buyers.

seo.title: Accused of Fraud Over a Second-Hand Sale in Korea | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: If you have been accused of fraud in Korea for taking payment in a second-hand sale and not sending the item, preserving transaction records and listing the buyers come first. Covers asking for cases to be combined when several police stations contact you, when it counts as fraud, and how to repay and settle.
keywords: used goods marketplace fraud police questioning Korea
accused of fraud on resale app Korea

sections.title: What to do right away
body: In second-hand sale cases, the trading app records are practically everything. Start by preserving the records and working out the scale.
bullets: Take screenshots of the listings, chat rooms and payment records, and do not delete your account
Write the police stations that contacted you, the investigators and the case numbers on one page
Make a table of each buyer with the date, item, amount and whether you refunded
Send whatever items you can, and refund right away whatever you can
If several police stations have contacted you, ask the investigator to bring the cases together in one place

sections.title: What not to do
body: Posting new listings to raise refund money looks like robbing Peter to pay Paul and becomes grounds for finding habitual fraud. Deleting your account or receiving money into an account in someone else's name also suggests you were trying to hide something.
If you make a new promise to a buyer to send the item by a certain date and miss that date again, the promise looks like another lie. Only give dates you can keep.

sections.title: If there are several cases
body: Buyers file complaints where they each live, so at first you will be contacted by several police stations. If you repeatedly fail to respond to summonses, an arrest warrant (체포영장) may be requested, which can lead to a wanted notice, so do not ignore them because they are far away. Tell the investigator about the other cases and ask to be questioned in one place.

Once the cases are combined, buyers who have not yet filed complaints are sometimes identified. If you have made your own list of victims, it is easy to check against the investigation record, and you can base your repayment plan on the full scale.

sections.title: When it counts as fraud
body: The test is whether, when you posted the listing, you actually had the item and intended to send it. If the item you had was damaged or something suddenly came up so that you could not send it, there is room to see it as a civil matter of failing to keep a contract. The date the photos of the item were taken, the purchase receipt and courier booking records support this.

Following the amendment of December 23, 2025, fraud (사기) is punishable by imprisonment of up to 20 years or a fine of up to 50 million won; for transactions before the amendment, the statutory penalty at the time applies. If it is found to be habitual, the sentence is increased by up to half (Criminal Act (형법) Articles 347 and 351).
