sections.title: Repayment and settlement
body: Fraud is an offense where the investigation continues even if the victim does not want punishment, but compensating victims weighs heavily in the outcome. If there are several victims, settling with only some has limited effect, so make a plan aimed at repaying everyone, starting with the smaller amounts if necessary. For buyers you cannot reach, consider a criminal deposit (형사공탁).

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: A managing partner uses the transaction records to separate what may be seen as fraud from what is a trading dispute, and looks with you at how to bring together cases from several police stations. We practise likely questions before questioning, attend the questioning with you, and submit a defense counsel's written opinion setting out your progress in repaying buyers. If you have been summoned by several police stations, contact us first at 02-6951-4097.

faqs.q: I've refunded everyone. Do I still have to go to the police station?
faqs.a: Even after refunds, a case in which a complaint was filed is concluded only after questioning. If you get proof of the refunds and statements from buyers that they do not want you punished, they will be reflected in the outcome.

faqs.q: The police station is too far away for me to go.
faqs.a: If you hold out and do not go, an arrest warrant may be requested. Explain your situation to the investigator and ask whether the case can be moved closer to your address or whether you can be questioned together with your other cases.

faqs.q: A buyer is demanding a settlement far larger than the price of the item.
faqs.a: There is no fixed standard for settlement amounts; they are agreed through negotiation. If the demand is excessive, you can make a criminal deposit of an amount equivalent to the loss, and that will also be considered in the outcome.

guides.title: When your account is frozen after lending it to someone
guides.lead: If you sent your debit card or lent your bank account to get a loan, and suddenly receive a text saying payments are suspended and a call from the police, you need to deal with both the risk of punishment and restrictions on financial transactions.

seo.title: Bank Account Frozen After Lending It in Korea: Payment Suspension and Police Contact | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: If you lent your debit card or bank account and then received a payment suspension text and a summons for violating the Electronic Financial Transactions Act in Korea, first preserve your conversations with the other person. Covers what to do right away, the standard for punishment, objecting to payment suspension and restrictions on financial transactions.
keywords: Electronic Financial Transactions Act violation summons

sections.title: What to do right away
body: If you received a payment suspension (지급정지) text, it means a report has been made that your account was used in a crime. Act in the order below.
bullets: Contact the bank that suspended payments and find out when and because of which transaction
Report the card and OTP device you handed over to the bank as lost or compromised, and change your passwords
Save the texts, KakaoTalk messages, call logs and courier waybills exchanged with the other person
Gather any business registration certificate, business card or loan information the other person sent you
If you have been summoned by the police, check whether the offense is a violation of the Electronic Financial Transactions Act or extends to aiding fraud

sections.title: What not to do
body: Even if the other person offers to clear up the misunderstanding and asks for more verification codes or a photo of your ID, do not comply. Trying to withdraw money that came into your account, or sending it on to another account as instructed, makes the allegation heavier, as an accomplice to fraud.
Also avoid deleting your conversations because you feel wronged. Records of the other person impersonating a financial company show that you believed it was a genuine loan.

Borrowing an account in someone else's name because the account for your living expenses is frozen can create another problem. If your salary account is frozen, tell your employer and the bank and discuss what to do.

sections.title: The standard for punishment
body: Transferring access media such as a debit card, password or certificate, lending them in exchange for a promised benefit, or lending them knowing they will be used in a crime is punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years or a fine of up to 30 million won (Electronic Financial Transactions Act (전자금융거래법) Article 49(4)).

The Supreme Court has held that the chance to get a loan can also count as a benefit (Supreme Court Decision 2017도16946, June 27, 2019). So questioning centres on what the other person promised to do for you, whether you were supposed to get the card back, and whether it was reasonable to believe it was a normal loan procedure. If you sent several cards or encouraged others to lend their accounts, brokering may also be an issue.

sections.title: Payment suspension and restrictions on financial transactions
body: There is a procedure for objecting to a payment suspension. You show with objective materials that the account was not one used for fraud or that you received the money legitimately, and there is a deadline (Telecommunications Fraud Refund Act (통신사기피해환급법) Article 7), so check with the bank that notified you right away. However, it will not be accepted if you are found to have known it would be used for fraud or to have failed to know through gross negligence.

If you receive a fine for transferring or lending access media in connection with voice phishing, you may be designated as a person restricted from electronic financial transactions until 3 years have passed, or 5 years for a prison sentence (same Act, Article 13-2). This is why the aim at the investigation stage is a no-suspicion decision or a suspension of indictment (기소유예).

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: A managing partner sets out with you, using the chat records, how the card came to be handed over, and practises questions about benefits and awareness of the crime with you. We attend the questioning with you, and before the decision we submit a written opinion on why you believed it was a normal loan and other circumstances to be considered. If you received both a payment suspension text and a summons, call 02-6951-4097 to ask for a consultation.

faqs.q: Can't I use even my own money left in the account?
faqs.a: Payment suspension applies to the whole account suspected of being used for fraud, so your own money may be frozen too. If the money came in legitimately, consider the objection procedure, showing this with supporting materials.

faqs.q: I was deceived by the other person, so I'm a victim too.
faqs.a: If the other person impersonated a financial company and made you believe it was a normal procedure, that can be grounds for a no-suspicion decision or a suspension of indictment. However, if you were promised a benefit, you may be punished, so it is important to show with materials what you were told when you sent it.

guides.title: When the police contact you about theft from an unstaffed shop or supermarket
guides.lead: If the police have contacted you about items you did not pay for at an unstaffed shop or supermarket, you have usually already been identified from footage and payment records. Here is the order in which to get the facts straight and compensate the shop.

seo.title: Police Contact Over Shoplifting at an Unstaffed Shop or Supermarket in Korea | Jisan Law Criminal Law Center
seo.description: If the Korean police contacted you about theft over items you did not pay for at an unstaffed shop or supermarket, check exactly what and when is at issue and prepare to compensate the shop. Covers what to do when the owner demands a settlement, what to be careful about in questioning, and likely outcomes.

sections.title: What to do right away
body: First you need to know exactly what is at issue. If you talk from memory and guesswork, it may not match the footage.
bullets: Ask the investigator for the date, place and items at issue
Find your payment records for that day in your card app and mobile payment history
If you still have the items you took, do not use them; keep them as they are
Work out for yourself whether you went to the same shop on other days
If the date to appear is difficult, call the investigator to adjust it

sections.title: If it was a mistake, find evidence of that
body: If you did not realise a barcode had not scanned at a self-checkout, or thought someone with you had paid, you can argue that you had no intention to steal. Records of paying for other items the same day, an error screen at the checkout and messages with the person you were with support this. However, if the footage shows you hiding something, this argument is hard to accept, and denying it regardless only hurts you.

sections.title: When the owner demands a settlement
body: Sometimes the shop demands far more than the value of the goods. Settlement is not mandatory; it is agreed through negotiation based on the loss and the circumstances. Do not get emotional when in contact, and keep it to text messages.

If the demand is so excessive that settlement is difficult, you can make a criminal deposit (형사공탁) of an amount equivalent to the loss. If you sign a settlement agreement, state both the amount received and that the owner does not want you punished.
If the owner asks you to come to the shop to talk or demands a written apology, do not agree an amount there and then; get the terms by text and decide afterwards.

sections.title: What to be careful about in questioning
body: In questioning, you will be asked what time you went in, what items you took, why you did not pay and whether you have done this before. Explanations that differ from the footage undermine your credibility, so for anything you are unsure of, say you will answer after checking the records.
If the investigator also asks about other days, first check your payment records for those dates. If you admit everything at once and it turns out to be inaccurate, it is hard to correct.

sections.title: How the outcome is decided
body: Theft (절도) is punishable by imprisonment of up to 6 years or a fine of up to 10 million won (Criminal Act (형법) Article 329). For a first offense involving a small amount where the loss has been made good, the case sometimes ends with a suspension of indictment (기소유예) or a fine, but if it was repeated several times at the same shop or you have a criminal record, the outcome is heavier.

If it has been an impulsive, repeated behaviour, records of starting counselling or treatment serve as materials showing your efforts not to reoffend. A suspension of indictment is not a criminal record, but it stays in investigation history records for a set period. If you get a record of the dates and content of your counselling sessions, it can be attached directly to a written opinion.

sections.title: How Jisan Law helps
body: A managing partner matches your payment records against the allegation to separate what to admit from what to dispute, and practises questions about the circumstances and motive with you. We attend the questioning with you and, before the decision, submit a written opinion with materials on compensation, remorse and treatment. If you have been contacted and are worried, call us first at 02-6951-4097.

faqs.q: It was only worth a few thousand won. Do I still have to be questioned by the police?
faqs.a: Even for a small amount, once theft is reported, it goes through questioning. However, the amount, the number of times and whether the loss was made good are reflected directly in the outcome, so it is important to get the facts exactly right.

faqs.q: My child, who is a minor, took something from an unstaffed shop.
faqs.a: Children under 14 are not criminally punished, but from age 10, juvenile protection proceedings may be an issue. It is important for the parent to compensate the shop together with the child and show a plan to prevent it happening again.

moreFaqs.q: I was told someone filed a complaint against me. Can I find out what it says in advance?
moreFaqs.a: The request to appear (출석요구서) states the gist of the alleged facts, and if you were contacted by phone or text, you can ask the investigator in charge what you are accused of. In many cases you cannot see the full criminal complaint before questioning, so we prepare likely questions based on the allegations you were told.

moreFaqs.q: I got a text telling me to come in, but I'm not sure it's really from the police.
moreFaqs.a: Rather than replying to the number in the text, call the police station's main number and confirm that the investigator and the case are real. Investigators do not ask for money transfers or account details over the phone.

moreFaqs.q: I've already been questioned once on my own. Is there any point in hiring a lawyer now?
moreFaqs.a: Yes. We first check how your statement was recorded, then fill in anything missing or misunderstood with an additional statement or a written opinion. If the decision on referral or indictment has not yet been made, there is still room to affect it.

moreFaqs.q: The police are asking me to voluntarily hand over my phone.
moreFaqs.a: If the request comes without a warrant, you can decide for yourself whether to hand it over. Items handed over voluntarily can be seized without a warrant (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 218), so talk with a lawyer before handing it over about whether you can submit only what is needed.

moreFaqs.q: The police are asking me all sorts of questions about the case over the phone. Do I have to answer?
moreFaqs.a: You don't have to answer on the phone right away. The call can be written up in an investigation report, and if you answer from memory without your materials, it is easy to get dates or amounts wrong. Say you will explain the details when you come in, and just set a date.

moreFaqs.q: Can my lawyer answer for me in the interview room?
moreFaqs.a: You must make your own statement. The lawyer can sit next to you, give legal advice and take notes, object on the spot to improper questioning methods, and give an opinion when questioning ends (Criminal Procedure Act Article 243-2; Investigation Rules (수사준칙) Articles 13 and 14).

moreFaqs.q: I read the statement record, and it's different from what I said.
moreFaqs.a: Before you sign, you can ask for corrections or state an objection, and the investigator must write this in the statement record (Criminal Procedure Act Article 244). If it is not corrected, talk with your lawyer before signing. If you have already signed, we put together the points to correct and submit them as an additional statement or written opinion.

moreFaqs.q: Can I see the statement record of my statement later?
moreFaqs.a: In a case under investigation, you can apply to inspect and copy the parts containing your own statement and the documents you submitted (Investigation Rules Article 69(1)). If you apply right after questioning, you can check the exact wording when writing a written opinion.

moreFaqs.q: My child, a minor, has been asked to appear. Can a parent go in too?
moreFaqs.a: If, considering age and other factors, emotional stability and smooth communication are needed, a person in a relationship of trust such as a parent can sit in (Criminal Procedure Act Article 244-5; Investigation Rules Article 24). Ask the investigator before questioning. A lawyer can also take part.

moreFaqs.q: If we collect lots of petitions, can we avoid detention?
moreFaqs.a: Petitions (탄원서) are not required, and a larger number does not change the result. The judge looks at whether the person has a fixed residence and whether there is a risk of destroying evidence or fleeing. A letter from the family with specific commitments to take care of the person's daily life and court appearances, along with residence and work documents, is better than many pro forma petitions.

moreFaqs.q: If someone is detained, do they stay locked up until the trial ends?
moreFaqs.a: Before indictment, detention is 10 days with the police and 10 days with the prosecutor, extendable once by up to 10 days with a judge's permission (Criminal Procedure Act Articles 202, 203 and 205). After indictment, the detention period is 2 months and can be renewed twice for 2 months each at each level of trial (Article 92). The person may be released in the meantime through a review of the legality of detention (구속적부심사) or bail (보석).

moreFaqs.q: Does bail have to be paid in cash all at once?
moreFaqs.a: The court can allow the deposit to be replaced with a surety bond submitted by someone other than the defendant (Criminal Procedure Act Article 100(3)). Besides the deposit, conditions such as residence restrictions, a pledge to appear and a ban on approaching the victim may also be attached (Article 98).

moreFaqs.q: Will I still be questioned by prosecutors after October 2026?
moreFaqs.a: No. From October 2, 2026, prosecutors belong to the Public Prosecution Service (공소청) and handle indictments; they do not investigate directly. Investigations are handled by investigating agencies such as the police, and prosecutors decide on indictment by reviewing the referred records, requesting supplementary investigation or hearing views when needed.

moreFaqs.q: My case was referred, but I was told it came back to the police with a request for supplementary investigation.
moreFaqs.a: It means the prosecutor sees something more to check before deciding whether to indict. The police must carry out the supplementary investigation and send the results to the prosecutor within 1 month of receiving the request (Criminal Procedure Act Article 197-2(4)). You may be contacted for more questioning, so find out what is being supplemented and prepare materials on that point.

moreFaqs.q: We reached a settlement after the case was referred. Is it too late to submit it now?
moreFaqs.a: It is not too late if the prosecutor has not yet made a decision. Submit the settlement agreement and the statement that the victim does not want punishment (처벌불원서) to the Public Prosecution Service office handling the case. For crimes that cannot be punished against the victim's wishes (반의사불벌죄), the case ends with no right to prosecute (공소권없음); for other crimes, it is taken into account in deciding on a suspended indictment (기소유예) or a summary order (약식명령). If you have already been indicted, submit it to the court.

moreFaqs.q: If I get a suspended indictment, where is it recorded?
moreFaqs.a: A suspended indictment is a decision without a trial, so it does not appear in your criminal record (범죄경력자료). It does remain in your investigation history records (수사경력자료), and it is deleted 5 or 10 years after the decision depending on the statutory penalty (Act on the Lapse of Criminal Sentences (형의 실효 등에 관한 법률) Article 8-2(2)). If you were a juvenile at the time of the decision, it is 3 years from the decision (Article 8-2(3)). These records can be checked only in cases set by law.

moreFaqs.q: The police decided not to refer my case. Is it completely over now?
moreFaqs.a: If the complainant or victim files an objection, the case is referred to the prosecutor. For cases notified on or after October 2, 2026, the objection must be filed within 3 months of receiving the notice (Criminal Procedure Act Article 245-7). The prosecutor may also request reinvestigation if they find the decision not to refer (불송치) unlawful or unjust, so keep your materials.

moreFaqs.q: It's been over a month since I was questioned, and I haven't heard anything.
moreFaqs.a: No news does not mean the case is over. Often the police are waiting to question others involved or for replies to information requests. For complaint cases filed on or after October 2, 2026, the police must decide whether to refer within 3 months of accepting the complaint (Criminal Procedure Act Article 238). If you want to know, ask the investigator in charge once what stage it is at.

moreFaqs.q: Does a fine count as a criminal record?
moreFaqs.a: A fine is also a punishment imposed by a final guilty judgment or summary order, so it remains as a criminal record. If you received a summary order and there are facts or amounts to dispute, consider within 7 days of being notified whether to request a formal trial.

moreFaqs.q: I'm on a suspended sentence, and now I'm caught up in another case.
moreFaqs.a: If, during the suspension period, you receive a final sentence of imprisonment without labor or heavier for an intentional crime, the suspended sentence (집행유예) loses effect and you also serve the earlier sentence (Criminal Act (형법) Article 63). If the new case ends in a fine, the earlier suspended sentence does not lapse. However, in principle you cannot receive another suspended sentence for a crime committed during the suspension period (Criminal Act Article 62(1), proviso). This is possible only if the earlier suspension period ended without lapse or cancellation before the new judgment (Supreme Court Decision 2006도6196, February 8, 2007). So first calculate how much of the suspension period is left, and focus from the start of the new case on lowering the level of the outcome.

moreFaqs.q: Can anyone apply for a court-appointed defense counsel?
moreFaqs.a: The court appoints one on its own when, for example, the defendant is detained, is a minor or is 70 or older, or is indicted for an offense carrying a minimum of 3 years' imprisonment (Criminal Procedure Act Article 33(1)). In other cases, one is appointed on request if you cannot hire a lawyer because of poverty or similar reasons. A court-appointed defense counsel (국선변호인) is not appointed for ordinary police questioning, but for the pre-detention hearing and the review of the legality of arrest or detention, the court appoints one if there is no lawyer (Articles 201-2(8) and 214-2(10)).

moreFaqs.q: I don't know how to contact the victim. How do I start settlement talks?
moreFaqs.a: Ask the investigator in charge to pass on to the victim that you want to settle. If the victim agrees, the investigator will give you their contact details or put you in touch. Do not try to find the victim's address and visit them. After indictment, you can make a criminal deposit (형사공탁) even without the victim's personal details (Deposit Act (공탁법) Article 5-2).

moreFaqs.q: Can I make a criminal deposit during the police investigation stage?
moreFaqs.a: The special rule allowing a criminal deposit without the victim's personal details is for defendants who have been indicted and are on trial, and the deposit is made at the deposit office where the court handling the case is located (Deposit Act Article 5-2). This method is hard to use during the investigation stage, so attempts to settle through the investigator, and records of those attempts, matter more.

moreFaqs.q: If the complainant withdraws the complaint, does the case end?
moreFaqs.a: For crimes that cannot be punished if the victim does not want punishment, such as assault and threats, and crimes that can be punished only on a complaint, the case ends with no right to prosecute. For other crimes, the investigation continues even after withdrawal, but it counts in your favor in the decision and sentence. A complaint can be withdrawn until the first-instance judgment is pronounced, and once withdrawn it cannot be filed again (Criminal Procedure Act Article 232).

moreFaqs.q: The offender's side contacted me about settling. Should I accept?
moreFaqs.a: Settling itself is not a problem, but check the terms. Decide whether they are also asking for a statement that you do not want punishment, and if payment is in installments, whether you will sign it only after receiving the full amount. For crimes that cannot be punished against the victim's wishes, such as assault and threats, once you state that you do not want punishment, you cannot later ask for punishment again.

moreFaqs.q: Do I file a criminal complaint with the police or the Public Prosecution Service?
moreFaqs.a: From October 2, 2026, complaints are made to a judicial police officer (Criminal Procedure Act Article 237). The Public Prosecution Service does not accept complaints, so file it at the police station with jurisdiction over the other party's address or the place where it happened, and get a receipt.

moreFaqs.q: It's been more than six months since I filed my complaint, and the investigation seems to have stopped.
moreFaqs.a: If more than 6 months have passed since the investigation began with no real investigation and no good reason, you can raise an objection with the head of the investigating agency. Within 14 days, they must tell you what action they will take, such as replacing the investigator or setting an investigation plan, and if there is no action or you disagree, you can request a review by the higher agency within 14 days (Criminal Procedure Act Article 245-11). This applies to cases where the investigation began on or after October 2, 2026.

moreFaqs.q: I don't accept the reasons for non-referral. Can I see the investigation records?
moreFaqs.a: To prepare an objection, you can apply to the police or prosecutor to inspect and copy the investigation records, and if found necessary, all or part must be allowed (Criminal Procedure Act Article 245-12). Access may be limited for reasons such as concerns about invading privacy. If you were notified on or after October 2, 2026, the 3-month deadline for an objection keeps running, so don't miss it while waiting for the records.

moreFaqs.q: The prosecutor decided not to indict. Is there any other way to challenge it?
moreFaqs.a: Within 30 days of receiving notice of non-indictment, the complainant can appeal (항고) to the head of the regional public prosecution office through the district public prosecution office the prosecutor belongs to (Public Prosecution Service Act (공소청법) Article 57). If the appeal is dismissed, you can file an application for a ruling (재정신청) with the high court within 10 days of receiving notice of the dismissal (Criminal Procedure Act Article 260).

moreFaqs.q: How are legal fees set?
moreFaqs.a: The work involved depends on the type of case, its stage and the issues to be disputed, so we explain fees after the consultation. We first hear about your case in the consultation, then tell you what work we would take on along with the fee.

moreFaqs.q: Can I just have a consultation without hiring you?
moreFaqs.a: Yes. In the consultation, we first lay out what you should and should not do at this stage. You can decide whether to hire us after hearing that.

moreFaqs.q: My case is being handled by a police station outside Seoul.
moreFaqs.a: Consultations are available at our main office in Seoul and our branch offices in Incheon, Hongseong and Songpa. Tell us where the police station is and when the questioning is scheduled, and we will set the dates for mock questioning and sitting in during the consultation.

moreFaqs.q: Do you take consultation calls at night or on weekends?
moreFaqs.a: 02-6951-4097 is answered 24 hours a day, including weekends and public holidays. If the matter is urgent, such as an arrest or a search and seizure, call us at any hour.

moreFaqs.q: My questioning is tomorrow. Will it still help to contact you now?
moreFaqs.a: Yes. We fit the remaining time to cover the questions you must be ready for and how to answer them. If we judge that you are not prepared enough, we also consider adjusting the date and time with the investigator (Investigation Rules Article 19).

moreFaqs.q: Who handles the first consultation?
moreFaqs.a: The managing partner consults with you in person. It is not handed off after an office manager or associate lawyer hears you first, so we can set the direction of the case right away based on what we hear in the consultation.

moreFaqs.q: I only stated facts. Can that still be defamation?
moreFaqs.a: If you publicly state facts that damage another person's reputation, you can be punished even if they are true (Criminal Act Article 307(1)). However, if the facts are true and stated solely in the public interest, it is not punished, so put together, with supporting materials, why you wrote or said it.

moreFaqs.q: I've been accused of insult, and the other person is demanding far too much to settle.
moreFaqs.a: There is no set standard for settlement amounts in insult cases. If publicity or identifiability is in dispute, first check whether the crime is made out before settling, and even if you settle, send the money at the same time as you receive the written withdrawal of the complaint.

moreFaqs.q: Posts attacking me keep appearing online. Can I file a complaint without knowing who wrote them?
moreFaqs.a: You can file a complaint without knowing the author, and investigators will request data from the platform to identify them. Save the post URLs, posting times and screenshots, and keep in mind that it may be hard to obtain data from overseas platforms.

moreFaqs.q: Can I record my boss's verbal abuse and submit it to the labor office?
moreFaqs.a: If you recorded verbal abuse that you heard as a party to the conversation, it does not violate the Protection of Communications Secrets Act and can be submitted as evidence. Leave out any parts that recorded conversations only among other employees.

moreFaqs.q: A former coworker gave my personal information to someone else.
moreFaqs.a: If the coworker passed on information learned through their work, they may face up to 5 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 50 million under Article 71 of the Personal Information Protection Act. If it was information learned privately and unrelated to work, whether another law applies must be considered separately.

moreFaqs.category: Public Duties and the Justice System
moreFaqs.q: I told the police I was driving when it was actually my family member who drove drunk. Can I still correct it now?
moreFaqs.a: In principle, correcting it is to your advantage. Harboring an offender (범인도피) is not punished when done by a relative or a family member living with the offender for that person's sake, but the family member who asked you to do it can be charged with instigating it, so first get advice on how to correct your statement.

moreFaqs.category: Public Duties and the Justice System
moreFaqs.q: I found out later that my testimony in court was wrong.
moreFaqs.a: If you testified as you remembered, it is not perjury even if it turned out to be wrong. If you knowingly said something different, the sentence is reduced or waived if you confess or turn yourself in before that trial's judgment becomes final, so it is better to act quickly.

moreFaqs.category: Public Duties and the Justice System
moreFaqs.q: The election commission contacted me for a question-and-answer interview.
moreFaqs.a: Depending on the results of the election commission's inquiry, it may lead to a criminal accusation or a referral for investigation, so your first statement matters. Organize materials on the date and time of the event or meal, who attended and who paid, and then attend.

moreFaqs.category: Public Duties and the Justice System
moreFaqs.q: I pushed a police officer, but the officer says it's fine. Does the case end?
moreFaqs.a: Obstruction of the performance of official duties (공무집행방해) does not end even if the officer does not want punishment. However, an apology and the officer's wish not to punish count in your favor when deciding the outcome, such as a suspended indictment (기소유예).

moreFaqs.q: The police are asking me to come with them to the station. Do I have to go?
moreFaqs.a: You can refuse voluntary accompaniment (임의동행) without a warrant, and even if you go, you can leave partway or walk out of the place at any time. The police must tell you this when asking you to come along (Investigation Rules (수사준칙) Article 20). An arrest in the act or an emergency arrest is different, as it is a compulsory procedure, so first ask what they are doing right now.

moreFaqs.q: A prosecutor from the Public Prosecution Service contacted me to ask about the facts by phone.
moreFaqs.a: From October 2, 2026, to decide whether to indict, prosecutors can hear a suspect's views in person, by video or by phone (Criminal Procedure Act (형사소송법) Article 245-13; Investigation Rules Article 65-3). They must inform you of your right to remain silent and your right to a lawyer, and a lawyer can take part. Statements made here cannot be used as evidence at trial but do become material for the indictment decision, so rather than answering right away, set a date and respond after preparing.

moreFaqs.q: Questioning is dragging on. Can I ask to take a break?
moreFaqs.a: Yes. When questioning runs long, a break of at least 10 minutes must be given every 2 hours unless there are special circumstances, and if the suspect or lawyer asks for a break, one must be given considering how long questioning has gone on and the suspect's health. If something is wrong physically, the suspect must be allowed to see a doctor or rest (Investigation Rules Article 23).

moreFaqs.q: Can I send letters to a family member who is detained?
moreFaqs.a: Yes, and in principle the contents are not censored. However, letters can be inspected if there is a censorship decision under the law or content suspected of violating criminal laws, and sending or receiving can be banned if the content raises concerns about destroying evidence (Administration and Treatment of Correctional Institution Inmates Act (형의 집행 및 수용자의 처우에 관한 법률) Article 43). Don't write about the case or the victim.

moreFaqs.q: I was released after an emergency arrest. Can I be arrested again?
moreFaqs.a: A person released after an emergency arrest because a detention warrant was not requested or not issued cannot be arrested again for the same alleged crime without a warrant (Criminal Procedure Act Article 200-4(3)). They can be arrested if the court issues an arrest warrant, so it is important to respond properly to requests to appear even after release.

moreFaqs.q: I'm detained and very ill. Is there a way to get out?
moreFaqs.a: A detained person can receive medical treatment from a doctor, and the lawyer can have a doctor examine them (Criminal Procedure Act Articles 34 and 89). If there is substantial reason, such as a serious illness, the court can suspend the execution of detention on condition of entrusting the person to family or others or restricting residence (Article 101(1) and Article 209). First gather medical certificates and medical records.

moreFaqs.q: I received a no-contact order, but I want to settle. What can I do?
moreFaqs.a: During a no-approach or no-contact period, even passing on that you want to settle directly can be a violation. First consider doing it through a lawyer or telling the investigators that you want to settle. Once Jisan Law is appointed, we handle settlement contact with the victim's side on your behalf.

moreFaqs.q: Can I choose whether my case goes as a domestic protection case or a criminal trial?
moreFaqs.a: The prosecutor decides whether to send it as a domestic protection case (가정보호사건), considering the nature, motive and result of the case and the offender's character and conduct, and must respect the victim's wishes. The suspect cannot choose, but can submit an opinion and materials showing that a domestic protection case is appropriate.

moreFaqs.q: Can a crime with no fine option, such as special injury, end with a summary order?
moreFaqs.a: A summary order (약식명령) can impose only a fine, a petty fine or confiscation, so a crime with no fine in its statutory penalty cannot end with a summary order. If you are indicted, you will face a formal trial, so it is important to dispute the charge and the outcome at the investigation stage.

moreFaqs.q: If I'm arrested in the act for domestic violence, will I be detained right away?
moreFaqs.a: If a detention warrant is not requested within 48 hours of the arrest, you must be released. If a detention warrant is requested, at the pre-detention hearing (영장실질심사) we explain that there are no grounds for detention, pointing to your residence, work, family relationships and plan to prevent reoffending.

moreFaqs.q: After an accident, the police are asking for my dashcam footage. Do I have to hand it over as is?
moreFaqs.a: If it is a request for voluntary submission, you can decide whether to hand it over, but if a seizure warrant is issued, it can be taken by force. Before handing it over, copy the original and check first what scenes it contains.

moreFaqs.q: What happens if I drove without a license and was also drunk?
moreFaqs.a: Unlicensed driving and drunk driving are separate crimes and are punished together, and if there was an accident, both fall under the exceptions in the Act on Special Cases Concerning the Settlement of Traffic Accidents (교통사고처리 특례법). The period before you can get a license again also becomes longer.

moreFaqs.q: My accident involves one of the 12 serious-negligence categories, and the victim is demanding too much to settle.
moreFaqs.a: A settlement weighs heavily in the decision and sentence, but you don't have to accept an unreasonable amount. Check what your driver's insurance covers, and if settlement is difficult, consider showing your willingness to make up for the harm through a criminal deposit (형사공탁).

moreFaqs.q: I'm a teacher reported for child abuse. Do I also need to explain separately to the education office?
moreFaqs.a: If conduct during educational activities is reported, the superintendent of education with jurisdiction can submit an opinion, which is filed in the investigation records for reference. Any written account you submit to the school and the education office must be consistent with your statements to investigators.

moreFaqs.q: Unknown money came into my account and the account was immediately frozen.
moreFaqs.a: Voice phishing rings sometimes send victims' money to an unrelated account to get it frozen, then demand money in exchange for unfreezing it. Even if someone contacts you, do not send money. Tell the bank what happened, and look into the objection procedure where you show, with documents, that your account was not used for fraud.

moreFaqs.q: Money was sent to my account by mistake, and I spent it on living expenses.
moreFaqs.a: Spending money sent to you by mistake instead of returning it can be embezzlement (Supreme Court Decision 2010도891, December 9, 2010). If the bank or the sender asks for it back, return it right away, and if you have already spent it, make a repayment plan and contact them.

moreFaqs.q: Is the statute of limitations different for each property crime?
moreFaqs.a: It depends on the maximum statutory penalty. Fraud, computer fraud, occupational embezzlement, extortion and nighttime burglary are 10 years; theft, simple embezzlement and stolen goods are 7 years; and embezzlement of lost property, property damage and gambling under the Criminal Act are 5 years (Criminal Procedure Act Article 249). If the gain is KRW 500 million or more, the Specific Economic Crimes Act applies and the period changes.

moreFaqs.q: Can someone be punished for taking money or property from a family member?
moreFaqs.a: With the amendment to the Criminal Act on December 31, 2025, theft, fraud, embezzlement and similar crimes between family members are no longer exempt from punishment and can be punished if the victim files a complaint. The complaint must be filed within 6 months of learning who the offender is, and this special rule may not apply where a financial institution is seen as the victim, as with bank transfers.

moreFaqs.q: There are several victims. Does it help to settle with only some of them?
moreFaqs.a: Whatever you settle is reflected in the decision and sentence. However, each victim is assessed separately, so the part involving victims you did not settle with remains. For victims you cannot reach or find it hard to settle with, it is a good idea to consider a criminal deposit (형사공탁) to come as close as possible to making up for all the harm.

moreFaqs.q: Can my phone or car be confiscated if it was used in the crime?
moreFaqs.a: Items used or intended for use in a crime can be confiscated if they belong to the offender, and if they cannot be confiscated, their value can be collected instead (Criminal Act (형법) Article 48). Confiscation is decided by the court, so you can dispute how closely the item was related to the crime.

moreFaqs.q: I want to repay the money while still disputing the charge.
moreFaqs.a: That is possible. However, so that repayment is not read as admitting wrongdoing, it is better to state in the settlement agreement or the transfer memo which points you dispute and what the repayment means. Decide which way to go before questioning so your statement stays steady.

moreFaqs.q: Can I be punished just because there are records of me putting money into a gambling site?
moreFaqs.a: Deposit records alone are not enough; it must be shown that you actually bet money and gambled. Investigators match account records with the site server's betting and cash-out records, so check how far your records go before giving a statement.

moreFaqs.q: When can I get a suspended sentencing?
moreFaqs.a: When the court imposes imprisonment of 1 year or less, suspension of qualifications or a fine, and there are clear signs of remorse, it can defer pronouncing the sentence itself (선고유예). This is not available if you have a prior record of suspension of qualifications or a heavier sentence (Criminal Act Article 59). Once 2 years pass from the date of the suspended sentencing, the case is deemed dismissed (면소) (Article 60).

moreFaqs.q: Does my criminal record go away when the suspended sentence period ends?
moreFaqs.a: If the suspension period passes without lapse or cancellation, the sentence loses effect (Criminal Act Article 65), and it is also removed from the criminal record certificate you request about yourself (Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Lapse of Criminal Sentences Article 7-2). However, it remains in investigative agencies' records and can be checked for purposes set by law, and for appointment as a public official, the disqualification lifts only 2 years after the suspension period ends (State Public Officials Act Article 33, item 4).

moreFaqs.q: How do I get a copy of the judgment?
moreFaqs.a: Apply for a certified copy of the judgment to the court that pronounced it and pay the fee (Criminal Procedure Act Article 45). The 7-day appeal period runs from the date of sentencing, not the date you receive the judgment, so don't miss it while waiting for the judgment.

moreFaqs.q: I want to know when the offender's trial will be held.
moreFaqs.a: If the victim requests it, the prosecutor must notify them of whether the case was indicted, the date, time and place of trial hearings, the outcome of the trial, and whether the offender was detained or released (Criminal Procedure Act Article 259-2). Request notification from the Public Prosecution Service office handling the case, and once the trial begins, you can also apply to inspect and copy the trial records.

moreFaqs.q: I have to testify as a witness, but I'm afraid of facing the offender.
moreFaqs.a: If there is concern that the victim will be very anxious, the court can let a person in a relationship of trust sit next to them (Criminal Procedure Act Article 163-2), and if facing the offender is likely to cause serious psychological distress, it can set up a screen or examine the witness through a video link (Article 165-2). If privacy or personal safety needs protecting, you can also request a closed hearing (Article 294-3). Ask the prosecutor or the court in advance before you appear.

moreFaqs.q: I was told my case has been referred to criminal mediation.
moreFaqs.a: Before deciding whether to indict, the prosecutor has sent the case to the Criminal Mediation Committee to try to resolve the dispute between the parties through mediation (형사조정) (Crime Victim Protection Act (범죄피해자 보호법) Article 41). In mediation you can discuss terms for making up for the harm, and you don't have to agree if the terms don't work for you. The prosecutor can take the mediation outcome into account in the decision (Article 45(4)).

moreFaqs.q: Can victims also get a state-appointed lawyer?
moreFaqs.a: If a victim of a sexual crime has no lawyer, the prosecutor can appoint a state-appointed lawyer for victims (국선변호사), and must do so for victims under 19 and certain others (Act on Special Cases Concerning the Punishment of Sexual Crimes (성폭력범죄의 처벌 등에 관한 특례법) Article 27(6)). Victims of other crimes can check whether they qualify for legal counseling and aid from the Korea Legal Aid Corporation (대한법률구조공단, 132). Separately from a state-appointed lawyer, victims can also hire their own lawyer, and Jisan Law, as the lawyer the victim hires, handles everything from writing the criminal complaint to presenting the victim's views at trial.
